Title: Selfhood is a grand illusion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Monima Chadha is Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of Oxford. A leading figure in cross-cultural philosophy, her work brings classical Indian traditions into dialogue with contemporary epistemology and the philosophy of mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Monima Chadha unpacks the ancient Buddhist argument that the self does not exist, and offers a suggestion of what morality looks like for the Buddhist, without a self to blame, punish, or with which to be angry.

Title: The secret to quantum gravity is randomness, with Jonathan Oppenheim
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jonathan Oppenheim is a Professor of Quantum Theory at UCL, renowned for developing “post-quantum” models in which spacetime remains classical, but interacts consistently with quantum matter.
Synopsis & Topics: Physicist Jonathan Oppenheim offers a radical new way to rethink the problem of reconciling quantum theory and gravity: we must think of spacetime as classical, but randomly fluctuating.

Title: The edge of the world
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Erling Kagge, Maria Balaska, Steven Mithen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist and one of Granta's Best Young British Novelists. Erling Kagge is a Norwegian explorer, philosopher, and writer. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole, and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. Steven Mithen is an archaeologist whose work explores the evolution of human intelligence, creativity, and social behaviour. Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work explores subjectivity, ethics, and the limits of experience. HOST: Sophie Scott-Brown
Synopsis & Topics: As the Earth is mapped, knowledge is only a click away, and human adventurousness declines, is the end of the unknown changing what it means to be human? Erling Kagge, Joanna Kavenna, Steven Mithen and Maria Balaska debate.

Title: The hype and limits of AI
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski, Audrey Borowski, Michael Wooldridge
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Wooldridge is an Oxford computer scientist and one of the world’s foremost authorities on AI. His book The Road to Conscious Machines argues that the hype around AI distracts us from the more immediate risks that the technology poses. Audrey Borowski is a Leverhulme Early Career Fellow at Cambridge specialising in the philosophy of AI. Her research argues that data and algorithmic systems have become a new form of ideology, undermining democratic politics. Tipped by The Times as "the next Einstein," Sabrina Pasterski is a theoretical physicist specializing in celestial holography. Based at the Perimeter Institute, she founded and leads the Celestial Holography Initiative, aimed at uniting our understanding of spacetime with quantum theory. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist account of the relationship between language and the world. He extends the same principles to artificial intelligence, with radical implications for what machines can and cannot do.
Synopsis & Topics: The world is consumed with the power and potential of AI.  Leading tech names like Altman and Musk have claimed it threatens humanity’s future. All while trillions of dollars are being invested.  The extraordinary success of Large Language Models, initiated by the 2017 breakthrough transformer/attention coding principles, is seen as just the beginning.  More data, more computing it is assumed will deliver ever more powerful AI. But a growing number of critics argue these models are in fact unintelligent word calculators that have already reached their peak as human training data has been exhausted. To be intelligent they would have to interact with the world, while language models merely find patterns in human text predicting what comes next and nothing more.

Title: The dangerous urge to punish
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Andy West is the author of The Life Inside and the Executive Producer of the acclaimed BBC adaptation of that book Waiting for the Out.
Synopsis & Topics: Most of us see punishment as a necessity, even as a moral good needed to prevent bad actors in society and rehabilitate wrongdoers. But what if the urge to punish has darker, more sinister roots?

Title: The institutions that failed Gaza
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Norman Finkelstein is one of the most high-profile controversial political scientists writing today. He has spent decades as a leading critic of Israeli policy. His 2025 book, Gaza’s Gravediggers, turns his scrutiny on the institutions he accuses of complicity in Gaza’s destruction.
Synopsis & Topics: Norman Finkelstein and Roger Hearing discuss the failure of international institutions to prevent the destruction of Gaza.

Title: Why we should embrace cybersex, with Trudy Barber
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr. Trudy Barber is a fine artist, sexual futurologist, and pioneer of cybersex research who created one of the first virtual reality sex environments in the early 1990s. Her work focuses on the intersection of human desire and technology, spanning virtual reality, AI, sex robotics, and the posthuman future of intimacy.
Synopsis & Topics: Artist and futurologist Trudy Barber argues that the advent of cybersex is forcing us to reimagine the boundaries between the human and the robotic.

Title: The reckless and the rational
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the few few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold. Zachary Karabell is an author and columnist, writing on economics, investing, history and international relations. He has taught at several leading universities, including Harvard and Dartmouth, and is the author of twelve books. Paul Johnson is an economist currently serving as Provost of Queen's College Cambridge, having spent fourteen years as Director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies analysing tax, spending, and public policy across successive governments.
Synopsis & Topics: Are economic bubbles a necessary part of growth, or do they pose an unacceptable economic risk? Zachary Karabell, Paul Johnson, and Gillian Tett debate.

Title: When compassion turns dangerous
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and author who rose to prominence as a central figure in debates over sex, gender, and truth—resigning from the University of Sussex in 2021 and entering the public discourse. Author and broadcaster, Mary Ann Sieghart is a former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Kathleen Stock in debate with Mary Ann Sieghart on the ethics of assisted dying.

Title: Carlo Rovelli on the impossibility of a theory of everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli is a pioneer of theories like Loop Quantum Gravity, White Holes, and the relational interpretation of quantum mechanics. His books include Seven Brief Lessons on Physics, which has been translated into 41 languages and sold over a million copies, as well as the bestselling Reality Is Not What It Seems (2015) and White Holes (2023). He was named one of the 100 most influential thinkers in the world by Foreign Policy magazine, and is Emeritus Professor at the Centre de Physique Théorique of Marseille, as well as holding positions at the Santa Fe Institute and the Perimeter Institute.
Synopsis & Topics: Theoretical physicist and best-selling author Carlo Rovelli argues that our theories can only describe parts of our multifaceted relationship to the universe, rather than attempt a theory of everything.

Title: One giant conflict for mankind
Guests & Speakers: Kishore Mahbubani, Adam Frank, Laura Grego
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Adam Frank is an American astrophysicist, writer, and public intellectual who serves as Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester. Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar, former President of the UN Security Council, and one of Asia's most influential voices on geopolitics and the historic return of Asia to the global centre stage. Laura Grego is an astrophysicist and director of the Global Security Programme at the Union of Concerned Scientists, specialising in space policy and nuclear safety and security. Philip Ball hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is space a new military battleground? Kishore Mahbubani, Laura Grego, and Adam Frank ask if space exploration can still benefit all humanity, or if the strongest will make the rules.

Title: Spacetime and the framework of the world
Guests & Speakers: Avshalom Elitzur, Ivette Fuentes, Jonathan Oppenheim
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. Jonathan Oppenheim is a Professor of Quantum Theory at UCL, renowned for developing “post-quantum” models in which spacetime remains classical, but interacts consistently with quantum matter. Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton whose work considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Bjørn Ekeberg hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the idea of spacetime inherently incompatible with quantum mechanics? Quantum physicists Jonathan Oppenheim, Ivette Fuentes, and Avshalom Elitzur debate.

Title: The rise and fall of the educated elite
Guests & Speakers: Thangam Debbonaire, Daniel Susskind, Michael Gove
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Gove is Editor of The Spectator and served in cabinet across five government departments for more than a decade. Most consequentially as Secretary of State for Education, where he steered through the biggest changes to English schooling in decades. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour life peer and former MP for Bristol West who served as Shadow Secretary of State for Culture under Keir Starmer. Her work in the Lords spans arts, cultural diplomacy, AI and copyright. Daniel Susskind is a leading economist, Professor of Business at Gresham College, and a member of the UK Government's Expert Panel on AI and the Future of Work. His new book What Should My Children Do explores how AI is changing the future of education. Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist, author, and public intellectual committed to dismantling the invisible yet powerful bias she calls “the authority gap.”
Synopsis & Topics: Should we conclude that the educated are no longer winning, and that the future will favour the skilled and the self-taught? Daniel Susskind, Michael Gove, and Thangam Debonnaire debate.

Title: There can be no ultimate map of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: A transformative encounter with a German Sufi philosopher in Cairo set Jenann Ismael on her way to becoming the leading philosopher of physics that she is today. Her work confronts the tension between what physics tells us about reality, and how the world actually seems to us in our conscious experience of it. She tries to ground free will in the nature of thermodynamics, and argues that reality is fundamentally unpredictable.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Jenann Ismael, whose work is at the leading edge of trying to connect the theories of physics to our conscious experiences of reality, argues that there can be no complete map or model of physical facts.

Title: Desire and danger in the age of self-love
Guests & Speakers: Trudy Barber, Maureen Dowd, Minna Salami
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Trudy Barber is an academic exploring the social and cultural implications of emerging technologies. Barber also developed one of the first virtual reality sex environments in 1992. Maureen Dowd is an American journalist and columnist known for her incisive political commentary in The New York Times . Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology and argue for a more embodied approach to understanding the world. Claudia Canavan hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Humans are increasingly turning to AI partners and sex toys as sex with other people declines. Is this a threat to happiness, society and birth rates, or a new path to independence and pleasure? Trudy Barber, Maureen Dowd and Minna Salami debate.

Title: The democracy emergency and the collapse of critical thinking, with Louisa Munch
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Louisa Munch is a critical theorist, PhD researcher, and influencer reaching over 200,000 people on social media, translating complex ideas into clear commentary on politics, culture, and power.
Synopsis & Topics: Louisa Munch argues that a media-driven decline in critical thinking has turned anger at deindustrialisation and housing costs toward scapegoats like migration, and explains why accessible education is the answer.

Title: The future of the AI economy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sebastian Mallaby is a journalist, author, and economic commentator. He is the Paul A. Volcker Senior Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and the author of The Infinity Machine , which tells the inside story of Demis Hassabis and the race to build superintelligence. Martin Wolf is chief economics commentator for the Financial Times , widely recognised as one of the world’s most influential financial journalists. His most recent book T he Crisis of Democratic Capitalism sets out a bold vision to fix the drift between capitalism and democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Pulitzer Prize finalist Sebastian Mallaby in conversation with Martin Wolf on the future of AI superintelligence and its economic effects.

Title: Mysticism, Heidegger, and the future of philosophy, with Simon Critchley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Critchley is a leading continental philosopher and Hans Jonas Professor at The New School for Social Research whose more than twenty books span ethics, tragedy, mysticism, and the meaning of life. Host of the Apply-degger podcast, he works to make Heidegger's philosophy more accessible.
Synopsis & Topics: Speaking to the IAI, Simon Critchley argues that we must work to undo Heidegger's reputation as an inpenetrable and obscure philosopher, and bring phenomenology to bear on the everyday.

Title: The philosophy and dangers of fame
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sarah Wilson is a New York Times bestselling author whose most recent book, I Eat the Stars , is a guide to finding meaning in a world that seems to be falling apart. Jordan Stephens is best known as one half of chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, and as a mental health advocate. His latest book, Avoidance, Drugs, Heartbreak explores the struggles of a young man rising to fame.
Synopsis & Topics: Jordan Stephens and Sarah Wilson explore identity, public image and the idea of a true self in an age of curated online personas.

Title: Democracy and the weaponisation of law
Guests & Speakers: Philippe Sands, James Orr, Marlène Laruelle, Christopher Steele
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Orr is a Cambridge philosopher and theologian. He is admired by JD Vance, who once described him as his "British sherpa." Christopher Steele is a former MI6 officer who ran the Russia desk from 2006 to 2009 and later compiled the "Steele dossier"—intelligence reports alleging ties between Donald Trump and Russia. Marlène Laruelle is a historian, sociologist and political scientist at The George Washington University, where she is directs the Illiberalism Studies Programme. Philippe Sands is a writer and lawyer at University College London whose work in international law has taken him from the trial of Pinochet to the prosecution of Nazi war criminals.
Synopsis & Topics: Is law a safeguard of democracy, or a political weapon that undermines it? James Orr, Christopher Steele, Marlène Laruelle, Philippe Sands debate.

Title: The power of moral shaming, with Kenneth Roth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kenneth Roth is an American attorney, human rights activist, and writer, as well as the former Executive Director of Human Rights Watch.
Synopsis & Topics: Kenneth Roth argues that moral shaming deters abuses of power even in countries which disdain human rights treaties.

Title: Liberalism's fight for survival
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Ignatieff is a Canadian author, academic and former politician who served as leader of the Liberal Party and leader of the Opposition from 2008 until 2011. Known for his work as a historian, Ignatieff has held senior academic posts at the universities of Cambridge, Oxford, Harvard, and Toronto.
Synopsis & Topics: Today, under relentless attack, it is beginning to feel inevitable that liberalism will die - but Michael Ignatieff argues that it simply needs to win our loyalty back.

Title: Science and art are not separate, with Sheila Atim
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sheila Atim MBE is an actress, singer and playwright, best known for her Olivier Award–winning stage work and roles in The Woman King and Bruised.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning actress and playwright Sheila Atim reflects on the similarities between art and science, the relationship between authorship and audience, and the future of the arts sector.

Title: Language and the illusion of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research. A major theme in Enfield’s work is how language operates not just as a system of signs but as a form of social action embedded in time. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher known for his theory of 'Closure', he is an outspoken critic of philosophical realism, and is Editorial Director of the IAI.
Synopsis & Topics: Join linguistic anthropologist, Nick Enfield, in conversation with anti-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson, as they explore why language excels at persuasion but falters at faithfully representing reality.

Title: Gutenberg vs Zuckerberg
Guests & Speakers: Mary Harrington, Cory Doctorow, Jimmy Wales
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jimmy Wales is the founder of Wikipedia, the world’s largest collaborative encyclopedia, which is run by the non-profit Wikimedia Foundation. Cory Doctorow is a Canadian-British author and digital rights activist who has served as European Director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. He is the author of several books including Enshiffication. Mary Harrington is an author and contributor editor for UnHerd and runs her own weekly Substack, Reactionary Feminist, a term she coined.
Synopsis & Topics: Fewer young people enjoy reading today than at any point in the past twenty years, and OECD data show literacy stagnating across the developed world. If the literate mind shaped the modern world, what kind of world will the post-literate mind create?

Title: You are not your brain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martine Nida-Rümelin is a German philosopher and professor of philosophy at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. Her work develops and defends what she calls subject-body dualism.
Synopsis & Topics: Conscious beings such as ravens, dolphins and human beings stand in sharp contrast to mere things. Join Martine Nida-Rümelin as she argues for her distinctive subject-body dualism, which is not obscurantist but a demand for intellectual honesty.

Title: Curtis Yarvin challenged on his argument for benevolent monarchy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy.
Synopsis & Topics: We tend to think that liberal democracy, for all its flaws, is ultimately a just and functioning form of government. Controversial figure Curtis Yarvin, here challenged by the IAI's Alexis Papazoglou, argues that we are wrong on both counts

Title: Reason and revolution
Guests & Speakers: Susan Neiman, Rowan Williams, Cornel West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cornel West is an American philosopher and public intellectual whose landmark work Race Matters established him as one of America's most prominent voices on race, democracy, and political philosophy. He ran for president in 2024. Rowan Williams is the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury and one of the world's leading theologians, whose work spans theology, spirituality, and philosophy. Susan Neiman is a philosopher pressing for a renewed commitment to Enlightenment morality and politics. She is Director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam and author of Left Is Not Woke.
Synopsis & Topics: We often see reason as providing a solid basis for our theories. But critics of reason argue that it is equally a vehicle of destruction. Should we see reason as a double-edged sword?

Title: Consciousness is biology's biggest blunder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University who developed the first mathematical model of the working heart and has since become one of the world's leading critics of neo-Darwinian orthodoxy in biology.
Synopsis & Topics: Denis Noble argues that consciousness in the biological world is grounded in randomness that the silicon molecules, and therefore artificial intelligence, cannot emulate.

Title: The not so blind watchmaker
Guests & Speakers: Denis Noble, Samir Okasha, Eva Jablonka
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University. He developed the first mathematical model of the working heart and has since become one of the world's leading critics of neo-Darwinian orthodoxy in biology. Eva Jablonka is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life. Her book Evolution in Four Dimensions helped pioneer the extended evolutionary synthesis. Samir Okasha is Professor of Philosophy of Science at the University of Bristol and winner of the Lakatos Prize for outstanding contributions to the philosophy of science. Philip Ball hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is evolution a blind process or does life actively reshape itself? Denis Noble, Eva Jablonka, and Samir Okasha debate.

Title: The hostile takeover of philosophy, with Christoph Schuringa
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Christoph Schuringa is a British philosopher and Associate Professor of Philosophy at Northeastern University London, whose research focuses on German philosophy and the history of ideas.
Synopsis & Topics: Christoph Schuringa challenges philosophy's self-image as a neutral, rational enterprise, arguing instead that it is deeply rooted in capitalist liberalism and shaped by its struggle against Leftist engagement.

Title: The crisis of attention is a crisis of meaning
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Gloria Mark is a Professor of Informatics at the University of California, Irvine, where she studies how digital technology impacts attention, productivity, and well‑being. Trained in psychology and computer science, her research combines empirical data with human‑centred insights to understand how people manage focus in an always‑on environment.
Synopsis & Topics: We often describe distraction as a failure of focus, but what if it is also a crisis of meaning? Drawing on decades of research, Gloria Mark explores how our cognitive, emotional, and social capacities are being reshaped by environments that never allow the mind to rest.

Title: Gender equality and the freedom trap
Guests & Speakers: Minna Salami, Kathleen Stock, Mary Harrington, Lucy Jones
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology. Mary Harrington is an author and contributing editor for UnHerd and runs a weekly Substack, Reactionary Feminist, a term she coined. Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and author, best known for her work on sex and gender, who resigned from the University of Sussex in 2021 to become a prominent public voice in the debate. Lucy Jones is a writer and journalist whose book Matrescence draws on neuroscience, evolutionary biology, and cultural history to argue that the transition into motherhood is one of the most profound biological transformations in human life. Chine McDonald hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Does the freedom to choose deliver deliver gender equality, or will gender always define work and family roles?  Lucy Jones, Minna Salami, Kathleen Stock and Mary Harrington debate.

Title: Activists don't need to win in order to achieve their aims, with Sophie Scott-Brown
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Scott-Brown is a historian of anarchism, Honorary Research Fellow at the University of St Andrews, and the author of The Radical Fifties: Activist Politics in Cold War Britain .
Synopsis & Topics: Historian of anarchism Sophie Scott-Brown argues that the disorganized methods of fringe activists are surprisingly effective at achieving political change.

Title: The metamodernist turn
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Jason Ānanda Josephson Storm, Linda Martín Alcoff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of objective truth. Best known for his theory of Closure, which goes beyond postmodernism to provide a new account of the relationship between language and reality. Linda Martín Alcoff is an award-winning philosopher whose work interrogates who gets to define what’s real, and whose knowledge counts as knowledge. Professor of Philosophy at City University, New York, in 2021 she was ranked the third-most influential philosopher in the world. Jason Ānanda Josephson Storm is a leading proponent of metamodernism. His work puts forward a philosophical programme, and a guide to what a world beyond postmodernism might look like. He is Chair of Science & Technology Studies and Professor of Religion at Williams College. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we embrace metamodernism as a way out of the paralysing scepticism of postmodernity and the naivety of traditional realism? Hilary Lawson, Linda Martín Alcoff and Jason Ānanda Josephson Storm debate.

Title: Memories are not stored in the brain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher, researcher, and writer who challenges the dominance of reductive materialism in contemporary thought. Working across philosophical psychology, metaphysics, and the history of ideas, she seeks to recover a deeper, more expansive understanding of the human soul.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher of time Victoria Trumbull argues that the brain enables memory but does not store it like a hard drive: instead, memories exist only in time itself.

Title: Patriotism, populism, and the fate of nations
Guests & Speakers: James Orr, Michael Ignatieff, Gillian Tett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Orr is a Cambridge philosopher and theologian and former Head of Policy for Reform UK. He is admired by JD Vance, who once described him as his "British sherpa." Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. One of the few few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is nationalism and national identity a vehicle for intolerance and the resort of demagogues and tyrants, or are open borders an elitist fantasy? Gillian Tett, James Orr, and Michael Ignatieff debate.

Title: The thoughts computers can't think
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of Britain’s most influential psychologists, Simon Baron-Cohen is renowned for his pioneering research on autism, empathy, and the cognitive differences between individuals. Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work brings together continental philosophy, ethics, psychoanalysis, and political thought.
Synopsis & Topics: Join clinical psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen and philosopher Maria Balaska to explore how modern education and technology are reshaping how we think, and what is at risk when we mistake a computer's appearance of thought for thought itself.

Title: The future of the Left
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Faiza Shaheen is an economist, author, and activist whose work exposes the structural forces that uphold inequality. She is Executive Director of Tax Justice UK, a Visiting Senior Fellow at the London School of Economics' International Inequalities Institute, and the author of Know Your Place. Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020 and later co-founded Your Party.
Synopsis & Topics: Firebrand economist Faiza Shaheen and leader of “Your Party” Jeremy Corbyn discuss why the Left requires ideas that match the scale of the crises society faces.

Title: Pragmatism and the pursuit of truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Edmonds is a British philosopher, and a radio feature maker at the BBC World Service. With Nigel Warburton he produces the popular podcast series, Philosophy Bites One of the most influential contemporary pragmatist philosophers, Cheryl Misak is known for reviving and reshaping the American pragmatist tradition for the 21st century.
Synopsis & Topics: David Edmonds and Cheryl Misak discuss the legacy of the WWI-era Vienna Circle, which argued that political and ethical statements can never be objectively true, and are nothing more than expressions of human desires and preferences.

Title: Physics has misunderstood time
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory.
Synopsis & Topics: Quantum physicist Avshalom Elitzur challenges the orthodoxy among physicists that time's flow is illusory, exploring sub-quantum research which shows time may be the universe's most fundamental ingredient.

Title: The age of the illiberal democracy
Guests & Speakers: Kishore Mahbubani, Michael Ignatieff, Marlène Laruelle
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar, former President of the UN Security Council, whose work examines the geopolitics of Asia's return to the global centre stage. Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. Marlene Laruelle is a historian, sociologist and political scientist at George Washington University, where she directs the Illiberalism Studies Programme.
Synopsis & Topics: Kishore Mahbibani, Michael Ignatieff, and Marlene Laruelle debate the rise of the illiberal democracy - where democratic majorities have endorsed crackdowns on human rights and civil liberties - and whether it is here to stay.

Title: The self has no center, with Julian Baggini
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The author of best-sellers such as The Pig That Wants to Be Eaten and How the World Thinks, Julian Baggini is a leading philosopher and the co-founder of The Philosopher’s Magazine.
Synopsis & Topics: Julian Baggini draws on philosopher Derek Parfit's ideas to describe a complex, ever-changing, many-sided self, which is still.

Title: In defense of democracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. Oli Dugmore is a political journalist and executive digital editor at the New Statesman .
Synopsis & Topics: Michael Ignatieff, in conversation with Oli Dugmore, explores the destruction of democratic culture, and whether liberalism still has the intellectual and moral resources to sustain and defend itself.

Title: The future of the tech crisis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cory Doctorow is a Canadian-British author and digital rights activist who has served as European Director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. He is the author of several books including Enshittification.
Synopsis & Topics: Cory Doctorow, author of Enshittification, makes the case that monopoly and weak regulation have caused the degredation of the internet, arguing that users, not platforms, need to start seting the terms.

Title: Economists don't understand the nature of power, with Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven is a Senior Lecturer in International Development at King’s College London, founder of the blog Developing Economics and a leading thinker in heterodox economics.
Synopsis & Topics: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven argues that the discipline of economics fails to understand its dependence on global power structures shaped by imperialism, class, and inequality.

Title: Buddhism and the emptiness of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Founder of the Journal of Hindu Studies whose research translates classical Indian philosophy into terms that engage contemporary debates on metaphysics and ethics.
Synopsis & Topics: Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier explains the Buddhist metaphysics of emptiness, and its consequences for our understanding of ethics.

Title: Consciousness has evolutionary roots, with Eva Jablonka
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eva Jablonka is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
Synopsis & Topics: Biologist Eva Jablonka advances an evolutionary account of origins of consciousness, arguing that sheer level of complexity it requires to develop is beyond the capacity of artificial intelligence, just as it is for plants and fungi.

Title: Rethinking the global orthodoxy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism, have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
Synopsis & Topics: Former President of PEN International John Ralston Saul argues that a global overreliance on borderless institutions has hollowed out local economies, weakened democratic accountability, and fractured civic trust.

Title: Why Plato matters now
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Angie Hobbs is the chair for the Public Understanding of Philosophy at Sheffield, and a frequent contributor to the BBC’s In Our Time, Night Waves and The Forum. She is the author of Plato and the Hero and is currently working on a new edition of Plato’s Symposium.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor Angie Hobbs argues that Plato's philosophy can help us understand a host of modern problems, including fake news, autocracy, cancel culture and the limits of wealth.

Title: Time's great mystery
Guests & Speakers: Ivette Fuentes, Tim Maudlin, Wahida Khandker, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University. Wahida Khandker is a philosopher and co-chair of the Society for European Philosophy. Her work is at the cutting-edge of the philosophy of process and the philosophy of biology. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Ivette Fuentes is a physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. Her work and previous collaboration with Roger Penrose considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity.
Synopsis & Topics: Is time part of the essential structure of the universe, an object we can measure, or something else entirely? Tim Maudlin, Ivette Fuentes, Wahida Khandker and Hilary Lawson debate.

Title: Globalisation has failed the Left, with Maurice Glasman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman founded the Blue Labour movement in 2009.
Synopsis & Topics: Maurice Glasman, founder of the Blue Labour movement, argues that the Left needs to reject open borders, globalisation and the rule of capital, and embrace a conservative strand of socialism that champions tradition, community, and civic association.

Title: Free will is real
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading physicist George Ellis argues that free will can emerge from complex systems, and that scientific accounts of causality have wrongly dismissed it.

Title: The return of the grand narrative
Guests & Speakers: Steve Fuller, Shini Somara, Michael Shermer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve Fuller is a Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick and founder of the research programme of social epistemology, best known for his work on the post-truth condition and the politics of knowledge. Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society. Dr. Shini Somara is an award-winning media broadcaster and a highly accomplaished British mechanical engineer specialising in Computational Fluid Dyanmics. Jack Symes hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Rather than replacing the old religious grand narratives, has science just conjured up new versions? Steve Fuller, Michael Shermer, and Shini Somara debate.

Title: Quantum measurement influences the past, with Avshalom Elitzur
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avshalom Elitzur is a theoretical physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research, whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, theoretical physicist Avshalom Elitzur argues that quantum physics alters our conception of time and causation: a measurement done in the present influences not only the future, but the past.

Title: Education has lost its way
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Guy Standing is a trailblazing economist and long-standing advocate for Universal Basic Income. He is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network.
Synopsis & Topics: Economist Guy Standing argues that the modern education system has been corrupted by market logic, which encourages AI use and erodes student skills. In this talk, he proposes a new democratic alternative.

Title: Beyond the sci-fi myths of AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Mirowski is the Carl Koch Professor of Economics and the History and Philosophy of Science at the University of Notre Dame. He is a leading historian and philosopher of economic thought, known for his trenchant critiques of neoliberalism, the commercialisation of science, and the epistemology of economics.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher and historian of economic thought Philip Mirowski argues that artificial intelligence is reshaping what counts as legitimate knowledge and fundamentally altering what it means to be a scientist.

Title: The end of the great alliance
Guests & Speakers: Jeremy Corbyn, Gillian Tett, Michael Ignatieff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020. He is co-founder and interim leader of Your Party. Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights have established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. One of the few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold . Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: As the US-Europe alliance breaks apart, what next for the global balance of power? Michael Ignatieff, Jeremy Corbyn, and Gillian Tett debate.

Title: Disloyalty is not betrayal
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown writes a weekly opinion column for The i Paper, focusing on British politics, social justice, and cultural issues. She is an award-winning journalist and was named Broadsheet Commentator of the Year at the Media Freedom Awards. Alibhai-Brown was also the founder of the British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown argues that we need to reclaim the courage to be disloyal to the political movements, communities, and identities we support rather than retreating behind the rhetoric of solidarity.

Title: The return of Malcolm X
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kehinde Andrews is the first Black Studies professor in the UK, currently working at Birmingham City University. He is the director of the Centre for Critical Social Research, founder of the Harambee Organisation of Black Unity, and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
Synopsis & Topics: Malcolm X is often written off as a slogan or a threat. Join the first Black studies professor in the UK, Kehinde Andrews, as he restores Malcolm X's radical clarity.

Title: The key to the cosmos
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Dean Rickles, Sarah Hart
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sarah Hart is the first female Professor of Geometry at Gresham College and the author of Once Upon a Prime. Her research focuses on the cutting-edge of group theory. Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Hosted by Jay Shapiro: an award-winning filmmaker, writer, and podcaster.
Synopsis & Topics: Can mathematics provide an ultimate description of reality? Sarah Hart, Dean Rickles, and Hilary Lawson debate.

Title: The idea of progress is a dangerous lie, with John Gray
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Gray, hailed as "Britain's best philosopher," is a leading critic of liberalism and the Enlightenment. He has long challenged the belief in inevitable progress, predicting both the 2008 financial crisis and the rise of populism. Jonny Thomson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: John Gray argues that the belief in civilizational progress is both false and dangerous—a secular myth that blinds us to the recurring conflicts of history.

Title: The science of creativity
Synopsis & Topics: But Sheila Atim, Olivier Award–winning actor, argues that the divide between art and science is a myth that limits both creativity and scientific innovation

Title: New rebels and a failed establishment
Guests & Speakers: Thangam Debbonaire, Eric Kaufmann, Louisa Munch
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change. Louisa Munch is a critical theorist, PhD researcher, and influencer reaching over 200,000 people on social media, translating complex ideas into clear commentary on politics, culture, and power.
Synopsis & Topics: Since the French Revolution, the young have rebelled left, but now France, Germany and the US are showing a shift to the far-right in young voters. Should these new rebels be listened to as a challenge to a failed establishment?

Title: Science and the unknowable universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought. Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. HOST: Philip Ball is a British science writer. For over twenty years he has been an editor of the journal Nature for which he continues to write regularly. He now writes a regular column in Chemistry World.
Synopsis & Topics: Can science ever fully grasp reality? Avshalom Elitzur and Lera Boroditsky explore whether science is a window onto the world — or a refleciton of the mind's limits.

Title: What 50 days of silence can teach you, with Erling Kagge
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Erling Kagge is a Norweigian explorer, philosopher, and writer who has spent his life testing the limits of the physical world and human mind. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. He has also sailed across the Atlantic twice, rounded Cape Horn, and sailed to Antarctica and back. After his record-breaking feat, Kagge founded a publishing house which went on to acquire one of Norway's oldest publishing companies. In 2021, Kagge sold his publishing company and in 2025 he left his position as publisher. His writing on exploration and philosophy has appeared in the Financial Times, The New York Times, and the Guardian.
Synopsis & Topics: Explorer and philosopher Erling Kagge argues one way to find meaning is to deliberately make your life harder. In this interview, he explains the origins of gratitude, talks about his encounter with a polar bear, and explains what he learnt from 50 days of silence in Antarctica.

Title: Pride and prognosis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Charlotte Blease is a philosopher of medicine whose research focuses on the ethical, psychological and social dimensions of healthcare innovation, particularly the use of digital and artificial intelligence technologies in clinical settings.
Synopsis & Topics: AI now outperforms clinicians in detecting certain cancers, predicting risks, and spotting patterns no human eye can see. So why are so many doctors resisting it?  Philosopher of medicine Charlotte Blease outlines the costs of clinging to tradition.

Title: The mystery of the self and the body
Guests & Speakers: Slavoj Žižek, Federico Faggin, Martine Nida-Rümelin, Monima Chadha
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a Senior Researcher at the University of Ljubljana and the author of more than fifty books applying Lacanian psychoanalysis and Hegelian philosophy to politics, film, and culture. Monima Chadha is Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of Oxford. A leading figure in cross-cultural philosophy, her work brings classical Indian traditions into dialogue with contemporary epistemology and the philosophy of mind. Martine Nida-Rümelin is a German philosopher and professor of philosophy at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. Her work develops and defends what she calls subject-body dualism. Federico Faggin is an Italian-American physicist and engineer who led the design of the world's first commercial microprocessor at Intel in the 1970s, earning him the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
Synopsis & Topics: Are the self and the physical body fundamentally distinct substances? Join Slavoj Žižek, Monima Chadha, Martine Nida-Rümelin, and Federico Faggin debate the merits and drawbacks of dualism.

Title: Immunity and impunity in a lawless world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philippe Sands is a writer and lawyer known for his work in international law and human rights. His books chart the use of international law to hold to account violations of international law from Chile's Pinochet to Nazis who fled to avoid the Nuremberg trials. He has emerged as a leading defender of the rule of law around the world in an age where populism and conflict threaten to send the world into anarchy. He is currently a Professor of Laws and the Director of the Centre on International Courts and Tribunals at University College London. He has appeared as a counsel and advocate at the International Court of Justice, the European Court of Justice, the European Court of Human Rights and the International Criminal Court. His most recent book, 38 Londres Street, charts the trial of Pinochet, the first national leader to be tried under international law, and the efforts to hold Nazi officers responsible for the holocaust to account.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading international lawyer Philippe Sands argues that combating impunity — the ability of the powerful to escape accountability for atrocities — is more essential now than ever.

Title: Neurodiverse pattern-seeking drives human invention, with Simon Baron-Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of Britain’s most influential psychologists, Simon Baron-Cohen is renowned for his pioneering research on autism, empathy, and the cognitive differences between individuals. Professor of Developmental Psychopathology at the University of Cambridge, Baron-Cohen has challenged conventional views of the human mind with a body of work that spans theories of mind, systemizing-empathizing, and the biological basis of social cognition. He is the author of The Essential Difference , Mindblindness , Zero Degrees of Empathy , and The Pattern Seekers , as well as a frequent contributor to the Guardian , Scientific American , and academic journals worldwide. Baron-Cohen’s rigorous research and thought-provoking theories continue to shape contemporary debates on neurodiversity, education, and the nature of human cognition.
Synopsis & Topics: Simon Baron-Cohen argues that pattern-seeking, or "if-and-then" thinking, fuelled human invention, and is markedly stronger in autistic minds.

Title: Marx, Raymond Williams, and the climate crisis
Synopsis & Topics: John Merrick explores how Raymond Williams’ Marxist critique of industrial capitalism and its extractive systems are newly relevant in helping to understand and solve the climate crisis.

Title: Warfare in the academy
Guests & Speakers: Minna Salami, John Ralston Saul, James Cleverly
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Cleverly is a Conservative politician who has served as Foreign Secretary, Home Secretary, and Education Secretary, as well as Party Chairman. He is currently Shadow Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government. Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology and argue for a more embodied approach to understanding the world. John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism , have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
Synopsis & Topics: Can education ever be devoid of politics, or should we acknowledge it as a permanent ideological background? John Ralston Saul, Minna Salami, and James Cleverly debate our options.

Title: Evolution beyond genes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eva Jablonka, Professor at the Cohn Institute for the History and Philosophy of Science and Ideas at Tel Aviv University, is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
Synopsis & Topics: Is evolution truly random, or does it have purpose? Eva Jablonka, author of Evolution in Four Dimensions, challenges the standard story to ask whether living systems can be genuinely goal-directed

Title: The philosophy of the senses: our inner worlds
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Barry C. Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. As founding director of the Centre for the Study of Senses, he has created a platform for collaborative research between philosophers, psychologists and neuroscientists.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher of the senses Barry C. Smith reveals how internal signals from heart, lungs, and gut secretly shape our moods, decisions, and sense of self.

Title: Cosmology in crisis
Guests & Speakers: Claudia de Rham, George Ellis, Bjørn Ekeberg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics. Claudia de Rham is a Swiss theoretical physicist at Imperial College London whose theory of massive gravity proposes that the graviton carries a nonzero mass—offering an alternative account of the universe's accelerating expansion. Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
Synopsis & Topics: New findings—including unexpectedly fast cosmic expansion and mature early galaxies—are challenging our standard cosmology. Do we patch the model, or does this signal a deeper crisis requiring new physics? George Ellis, Claudia de Rham and Bjørn Ekeberg debate

Title: Rebalancing the global order
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar. A former President of the UN Security Council, his work examines the geopolitics of Asia's return to the global centre stage.
Synopsis & Topics: Kishore Mahbubani tracks a new shift in global power: Asia is regaining its historical weight, and the West's refusal to accept this reality is fuelling growing conflict.

Title: The language we speak shapes the way we think, with Lera Boroditsky
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought.
Synopsis & Topics: Cognitive scientist Lera Boroditsky shows how language molds perception of space, time, colour, and causality - and why losing languages is such a pressing problem.

Title: The hidden philosophy of food
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Julian Baggini is a philosopher and author renowned for translating deep philosophical questions into engaging, practical insights. Co-founder of The Philosopher’s Magazine and author of best-sellers such as The Godless Gospel , How the World Thinks , The Virtues of the Table , and The Ego Trick , Baggini defends Enlightenment values and champions reason, scepticism, and humanism in a complex world.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Julian Baggini explores how food shapes identity, ethics, and meaning across cultures—from Japanese precision to Italian conviviality—arguing that understanding humanity starts at the plate.

Title: Everything we knew about economics is wrong
Guests & Speakers: Faiza Shaheen, Maurice Glasman, Paul Johnson, Llŷr Powell, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Faiza Shaheen is an economist, author, and activist whose work analyses the structural forces behind inequality. She is Executive Director of Tax Justice UK, and the author of Know Your Place . Llŷr Powell is a member of Reform’s shadow cabinet in the recently elected Senedd, where he is responsible for Business and is also Chief Whip. Maurice Glasman is the founder of Blue Labour and a life peer whose political thought draws on Jewish socialism, Christian democracy, and guild association to make the case for a conservatism rooted in working-class culture. Paul Johnson is an economist currently serving as Provost of Queen's College Cambridge, having spent fourteen years as Director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies analysing tax, spending, and public policy across successive governments.
Synopsis & Topics: Is economic nationalism a credible theory, or just a set of incoherent policies touted by populist governments? Faiza Shaheen, Maurice Glasman, Llŷr Powell, and Paul Johnson debate.

Title: Reality doesn't care what you think
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading sceptic Michael Shermer argues that abandoning the idea of an objective truth is a disastrous mistake.

Title: Why you should ignore the Economics Nobel Prize, with Cahal Moran
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist and Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and the creator of the YouTube channel Unlearning Economics.
Synopsis & Topics: Cahal Moran says economics' "physics envy" for mathematical rigor leaves it detached from reality, masking real declines in living standards, and calls for refocusing on people's needs

Title: The simulation matrix
Guests & Speakers: Steve Koonin, John Ioannidis, Paulette Clancy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paulette Clancy is a Johns Hopkins engineering professor and leading computational materials scientist, pioneering atomic-scale modelling and ML-driven materials discovery. John Ioannidis is a Stanford professor and one of the world’s most-cited scientists, known for reshaping debates on evidence, bias and reproducibility. Steve Koonin is a NYU physicist and former US Undersecretary of Science, known for scrutinising political claims about climate change. Adviser to major science and defence agencies, and author of the controversial Unsettled (2021). Bahar Gholipour hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are simulations revealing truth or just reflecting their creators' biases? John Ioannidis, Paulette Clancy, and Steeve Koonin debate.

Title: Memes, minds and the myth of control
Guests & Speakers: Victoria Trumbull, Tony D. Sampson, Sylvie Delacroix
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tony D. Sampson is an academic and author whose research connects digital culture, media theory, and political philosophy. Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher and writer working across the philosophy of mind and the philosophy of time, whose recent work argues that memory unfolds in time rather than being stored in the brain. Sylvie Delacroix is a scholar and philosopher reimagining how communities might govern shared digital resources in ways that promote fairness, accountability, and trust in the age of AI. Jonny Thomson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Do ideas genuinely originate in individuals, or are we merely vessels or hosts for "social contagions"? Tony D. Sampson, Sylvie Delacroix, and Victoria Trumbull debate.

Title: Memory is a construction
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Charan Ranganath is Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience and Director of Dynamic Memory Lab at the University of California, Davis, where he spent more than 25 years investigating how the brain encodes, stores and retrieves memories. He is the author of Why We Remember: The Science of Memory and How It Shapes Us .
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscientist Charan Ranganath draws on new research to show that memory is a dynamic, purposeful system which actively reconstructs the past, present, and future.

Title: Rationality can't decide everything for us, with Miriam Schoenfield
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist.
Synopsis & Topics: Should you abandon beliefs shaped by your culture? Epistemologist Miriam Schoenfield argues that every belief system relies on unprovable assumptions.

Title: The economics of the new world order
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Formerly a lead research economist at the World Bank, Branko Milanović is one of the world’s leading experts on income inequality and globalization. He is a senior scholar at the Stone Center on Socio-economic Inequality at the City University of New York and is best known for the “Elephant Curve,” a visual representation of how different income groups benefit unevenly from globalization, which has shaped debates on economic development and social justice. Milanović has brought rigorous data analysis and historical insight to some of the most pressing questions of our time. His new book, The Great Global Transformation, examines the decline of neoliberalism and the rise of a new economic order shaped by nationalism, trade conflicts, and shifting power. Drawing on original research, Milanović examines how Asia’s economic growth is reshaping income patterns and the uncertainties facing the global order.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading economist Branko Milanović argues that neoliberalism is ending, replaced by nationalism, tariffs, and trade blocs - and explores the place of the new global middle class within this system.

Title: The pathology of everyday life
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Moncrieff, Anna Lembke, Sarah Wilson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert, best known for her bestselling book, Dopamine Nation. Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at UCL and was the lead author of a landmark scientific study into the theory of serotonin and depression. She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, and philanthropist. She founded the global ‘I Quit Sugar’ movement.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we see mental health issues as primarily social rather than medical? Anna Lembke, Joanna Moncrieff, and Sarah Wilson debate.

Title: The James Webb Telescope's threat to cosmology
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. He holds a Ph.D. in philosophy of science from the University of Victoria (Canada) and has combined rigorous academic inquiry with creative and practical ventures. Ekeberg’s philosophical writing spans cosmology, metaphysics, and the limits of scientific knowledge, exemplified by his book Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe, which critiques assumptions in modern physics and invites fresh perspectives on how we understand the universe.
Synopsis & Topics: Bjørn Ekeberg examines new observations from the James Webb Space Telescope that challenge the standard cosmological story.

Title: Marx, Trump, and a new vision for the Left with Bhaskar Sunkara
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bhaskar Sunkara is the founding editor of Jacobin , the president of the Nation , and the author of The Socialist Manifesto: The Case for Radical Politics in an Era of Extreme Inequality .
Synopsis & Topics: Jacobin founder Bhaskar Sunkara analyzes the modern left, Trump's tariffs, and why defending liberal democracy is a strategic necessity for socialists.

Title: Evidence in the dock
Guests & Speakers: Genia Schönbaumsfeld, Nick Enfield, Timothy Williamson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research. He is the author of Language vs Reality. Analytic philosopher and author of Knowledge and Its Limits, Timothy Williamson is a Senior Research Fellow at New College, Oxford and former Wykeham Professor of Logic. Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton and the author of several books – most recently, Wittgenstein on Religious Belief. In 2023, Genia was awarded a highly prestigious ERC Advanced Grant for her project entitled ‘The Ethics of Doubt – Kierkegaard, Scepticism and Conspiracy Theory’. Jay Shapiro hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can evidence be objectively truthful, or is it merely a persuasive argument in favour of a given theory or narrative? Nick Enfield, Timothy Williamson, Genia Schönbaumsfeld debate.

Title: The Big Bang miracle
Guests & Speakers: Priyamvada Natarajan, Phil Halper, Joseph Silk, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Phil Halper is a science communicator and Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society. His recent book, Battle of the Big Bang, explores alternative theories of the universe’s birth, especially those often dismissed for challenging established cosmological ideas. Joseph Silk is a cosmologist and the Savilian Professor of Astronomy Emeritus at the University of Oxford, whose work investigates the early universe, dark matter, and galaxy formation. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and was named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Despite its central role in modern cosmology, the Big Bang theory originated from religious thought. But do religious assumptions still have a hidden impact on the science? Phil Halper, Joseph Silk, and Priya Natarajan discuss.

Title: Privacy is power
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carissa Véliz is a philosopher and Associate Professor at Oxford Univeristy, specialising in AI ethics, privacy and political philosophy. She explores how data and algorithmic prediction shape power, autonomy and democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Political philosopher and AI ethicist Carissa Veliz argues that control over information is control over people: every piece of personal data handed over gives someone else the power to shape your choices, your habits, and even your future.

Title: To save democracy we need fewer elections, with Hélène Landemore
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dedicated to reimagining democracy as a system that truly empowers people, Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and Professor at Yale University. As founder of Yale’s Citizens’ Assemblies research program and a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI, she blends deep theoretical insight with practical innovation. Landemore challenges traditional electoral democracy by arguing for a more inclusive, deliberative model—one that better captures collective intelligence and democratic reason. Her work, including advising OpenAI’s Democratic Inputs to AI program, explores how democratic institutions can become more stable, representative, and capable of addressing today’s complex political and technological challenges.
Synopsis & Topics: Landemore argues true democracy needs fewer elections, not more. Random citizen selection—like jury duty—would break elite capture and reconnect governance to ordinary people, drawing on Athenian precedent that populism gestures toward but misapplies.

Title: The rise and fall of the city
Guests & Speakers: Luís Bettencourt, Kiran Sidhu, Joanna Kavenna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Luís Bettencourt is a physicist, author, and urban systems researcher, currently Professor at the University of Chicago and External Professor at the Santa Fe Institute. Kiran Sidhu is an evocative and honest writer known for blending personal insight with lyrical storytelling. She regularly writes for Prospect magazine about rural life and the philosophical implications of this change in her life. Joanna Kavenna is a novelist and travel writer whose work explores themes of place, displacement, and the contrasts between urban and rural existence. She's held the Alistair Horne Fellowship at St Antony’s College Oxford and the Harper-Wood at St John’s College Cambridge.
Synopsis & Topics: The long urban dominance in elections is fading as a resurgent rural vote reshapes politics. Could remote work and the internet make this shift permanent? Kiran Sidhu, Luís Bettencourt, and Joanna Kavenna discuss.

Title: The patriarchy in question
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Hakim, Mary Ann Sieghart, Paul Dolan, Nick Fletcher
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and happiness expert at LSE, widely known for his research on wellbeing, decision-making, and human motivation. Nick Fletcher is a former Tory MP for Don Valley known for his opinions on gender equality, trans issues and immigration. He was chair of the Men and Boys All-Party Parliamentary Group. Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specialising in women's employment and women's issues, known for inventing the concept of "erotic capital". Mary Ann Sieghart is an author, broadcaster and former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are feminist gains under threat? As boys are outperformed by girls at every school level, and women in their 20s out-earn men, there are increasing signs of anti-feminist backlash on the Right. Catherine Hakim, Mary Ann Sieghardt, Paul Dolan, and Nick Fletcher debate the consequences.

Title: Iain McGilchrist on why the mind is not a machine
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Iain McGilchrist is a distinguished British neuroscientist, psychiatrist and philosopher. A former Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, he has also worked as a consulting psychiatrist, and is known for his influential work on the relationship between the structure of our brains, human cultures and our understanding of the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Iain McGilchrist argues that explaining the mind in purely mechanistic terms is a profound mistake, rooted in materialist and reductionist assumptions.

Title: How to sue your government, with Jolyon Maugham
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jolyon Maugham KC is an activist barrister, founder of the Good Law Project, and thorn in the side of the government. Jolyon has sought to challenge the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid and transgender rights. He has written for the Telegraph, Guardian and New Statesman on the legal implications of Brexit.
Synopsis & Topics: Jolyon Maugham, the barrister who took on Boris Johnson, argues that laywers need to intervene in a legal system which too often fails to hold those in power to account.

Title: Imagination and the real
Guests & Speakers: Karl Friston, Maria Balaet, Nadine Dijkstra
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nadine Dijkstra is Principal Investigator at UCL’s Queen Square Institute of Neurology, where she leads the Imagine Reality Lab in exploring how the brain constructs our sense of reality. Karl Friston is a world-leading neuroscientist and Professor at UCL, best known as the architect of the influential Free Energy Principle and a Principal Research Fellow with the Wellcome Trust. Maria Balaet is a leading voice in psychedelic research, using advanced neuroimaging at King’s College London to uncover how these substances transform consciousness. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscience increasingly suggests that perception and imagination share the same brain processes. Does this mean that reality and hallucination are indistinguishable? Neuroscientists Karl Friston, Maria Balaet, and Nadine Dijkstra discuss.

Title: Love is more than magic
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alain de Botton is the bestselling philosopher redefining how we understand love, work, and meaning in the modern world. He first rose to prominence with Essays in Love, a novel-philosophy hybrid that became an international bestseller. He has since authored several bestselling works that blend literary elegance, psychological insight, and philosophical depth.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Alain de Botton explores how romantic ideals mislead us and why emotional maturity, not chemistry, holds the key to enduring intimacy.

Title: Navigating the unknown
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Jessica Frazier, Graham Priest
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Graham Priest is Professor of Philosophy at City University of New York. He is well known for his work on non-classical logic and Buddhist Philosophy. Jessica Frazier is an Oxford philosopher who works on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. She is also a frequent consultant for the BBC and speaker on In Our Time. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything , has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Shini Somara hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: If science builds models rather than revealing truth — as Heisenberg and Hawking argued — and they still work, what does that say about our grasp on reality? Graham Priest, Jessica Frazier and Hilary Lawson debate.

Title: Where quantum meets gravity, with Ivette Fuentes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and an Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. She earned her PhD in physics from the University of Nottingham and completed postdoctoral research at the University of Vienna, where she worked extensively on quantum optics and relativistic quantum information theory. Fuentes has since established herself as a leading figure in the study of quantum gravity, focusing on how quantum phenomena behave in curved spacetime — bridging quantum mechanics with general relativity.
Synopsis & Topics: Can smaller, cheaper experiments unlock quantum gravity? Physicist Yvette Fuentes thinks so — and she's building one, inspired by Roger Penrose's ideas on gravitational wave function collapse.

Title: Technology is always political, with Sheila Jasanoff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sheila Sen Jasanoff is an Indian-American academic in the field of Science and Technology Studies. In 2021 she was elected to the American Philosophical Society. Her research has been recognized with many awards, including the 2022 Holberg Prize "for her groundbreaking research in science and technology studies."
Synopsis & Topics: Groundbreaking science and technology theorist Sheila Jasanoff argues that technology isn't neutral or inevitable: our social choices actively create the technological world we inhabit.

Title: In the name of reason
Guests & Speakers: Steve Fuller, Miriam Schoenfield, Dan Sperber
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dan Sperber is a distinguished anthropologist and philosopher who is the author of several critically-acclaimed books, including The Enigma of Reason. Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the author of dozens of books, including Post-truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist. Jack Symes is a public philosopher and writer. He is the producer of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast and editor of the Bloomsbury series Talking about Philosophy. He is currently Teacher and Researcher at Durham University, UK.
Synopsis & Topics: Reason doesn't always free us from bias — it can sharpen our ability to justify existing beliefs, making educated people more prone to groupthink. But can it be reclaimed as a tool for critical resistance rather than tribal conformity? Dan Sperber, Steve Fuller, and Miriam Schoenfield discuss.

Title: The world after liberalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman is the founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Co-founder of Compact magazine and author of Tyranny, Inc., Sohrab Ahmari is a celebrated journalist and cultural critic.
Synopsis & Topics: Maurice Glasman and Sohrab Amari diagnose the roots of the current crisis of liberalism and explore possibilities for what lies beyond it.

Title: Riches and rags
Guests & Speakers: Yaron Brook, Thangam Debbonaire, Ingrid Robeyns
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ingrid Robeyns is a philosopher and economist best known for developing limitarianism, the case for placing ethical limits on personal wealth. She holds the Chair of Ethics in Institutions at Utrecht University. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur and political commentator, best known as chairman of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of The Yaron Brook Show. He co-authored the bestseller Free Market Revolution. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we prioritise eradicating poverty or is wealth equality essential for justice? Join Yaron Brook, Ingrid Robeyns, and Thangam Debbonaire in debate.

Title: Science beyond the physical
Guests & Speakers: Lisa Feldman Barrett, Michael Levin, Adam Frank
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lisa Feldman Barrett is among the most cited scientists in the world for her research on the psychology and neuroscience of emotions. Adam Frank is an astrophysicist who explores the origins of stars, civilizations and consciousness, and is a leading figure in astrobiology and the search for alien life. Michael Levin is a synthetic biologist whose pioneering work in regenerative biology involves building biological robots to probe the nature of life, intelligence and evolution. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Science has long assumed reality is purely physical — but could materialism actually be holding back progress on neuroscience, quantum gravity, and the origin of life? Lisa Feldman Barrett, Michael Levin, and Adam Frank discuss.

Title: The fight for the AI economy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Transhumanist thinker and former US presidential candidate, Zoltan Istvan is known for promoting life extension and emerging technologies in politics. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian .
Synopsis & Topics: Two visions of the AI future collide in this head-to-head debate: Zoltan Istvan's tech-optimist 'Automated Abundance Economy' and Aaron Bastani's 'Fully Automated Luxury Communism.'

Title: The end of woke
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change.
Synopsis & Topics: Where did woke culture come from—and is it finished? Prof. Eric Kaufmann traces its roots and argues the left needs a new political framework to survive.

Title: The only freedom which deserves the name
Guests & Speakers: Yascha Mounk, Curtis Yarvin, Minna Salami
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Expert on the challenges facing liberal democracy in the 21st century, Yascha Mounk is a political scientist and Professor at Johns Hopkins University. Writer, social critic, and thought leader Minna Salami is known for fusing feminism, philosophy, and political thought. She is the author of Can Feminism Be African?.
Synopsis & Topics: Minna Salami, Yascha Mounk, and Curtis Yarvin debate whether liberalism can still claim the moral high ground, or whether it is just one partisan worldview among many.

Title: Mental health and the chemical imbalance myth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, and a consultant psychiatrist for the NHS.
