She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Her most recent book is Chemically Imbalanced: The Making and Unmaking of the Serotonin Myth.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychiatrist Joanna Moncrieff argues that the chemical imbalance theory of depression lacks scientific support, despite prompting the widespread use of antidepressants.

Title: The OnlyFans paradox, with Farha Khalidi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker and OnlyFans model with 1.7 million followers on TikTok.
Synopsis & Topics: Feminist cultural commentator Farha Khalidi argues that the moral panic over OnlyFans conceals centuries of double standards over sex work.

Title: The mirror
Guests & Speakers: Dean Rickles, Joanna Kavenna, Winsome Pinnock
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Winsome Pinnock is a British playwright and dramaturge, known for her pioneering contributions to contemporary theatre. Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. She is the author of six books and has written for The New Yorker, The Guardian and London Review of Books. Hosted by Jessica Frazier.
Synopsis & Topics: The mirror has long symbolised art and the mind's relationship to reality - but can we, or should we seek to copy the world at all? Dean Rickles, Winsome Pinnock, and Joanna Kavenna discuss.

Title: Mysticism vs modernity
Guests & Speakers: David Pearce, Naomi Goulder, Rupert Sheldrake
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Transhumanist philosopher David Pearce, author of Philosophy of Action Naomi Goulder, and world-renowned biologist Rupert Sheldrake debate mysticism and modernity. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
Synopsis & Topics: David Pearce, Naomi Goulder, and Rupert Sheldrake debate whether the battle between science and spirituality will ever truly be resolved.

Title: The Enlightenment under fire, with John Gray and Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of Britain’s most provocative thinkers, John Gray is a political philosopher famous for dismantling liberalism and exposing the illusions of human progress. Former Professor of European Thought at the London School of Economics, Gray has challenged orthodoxy across the political spectrum with a body of work that ranges from critiques of Enlightenment rationalism to meditations on the limits of secular humanism. He is the bestselling author of Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals , and Seven Types of Atheism as well as a frequent contributor to The Guardian , New Statesman, and The Times Literary Supplement . Gray’s sharp insights and contrarian stance continue to shape contemporary debates on ethics, politics, and the future of humanity.
Synopsis & Topics: Join John Gray and Hilary Lawson in conversation on the power of philosophy as a disruptive force and the growing challenges to the liberal belief in progress.

Title: Global challenge and global action
Guests & Speakers: Kai Heron, James Bacchus, Leah Downey
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Bacchus is a professor of Global Affairs and Director of the Global Economic and Environmental Opportunity Centre at the University of Central Florida. With a long and storied career in Congress and the World Trade Organisation (WTO), his most recent work argues that we need global democracy in order to have true, sustainable development. Leah Downey is a political theorist, a junior research fellow at St. John’s College, Cambridge and a lecturer at Kings College London. She has published research on the macroeconomics of the green transition and is the author of Our Money: Monetary Policy as if Democracy Matters . Kai Heron is a political organiser, trade unionist, and Lecturer in Political Ecology at Lancaster University. He is the co-editor of the De Gruyter Degrowth Handbook , has published widely on the politics of green energy and is the co-author of Radical Abundance: How to Win a Green Democratic Future . Adrienne Buller hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Liberal democracies face mounting climate failures as emissions rise and political will wavers. Can they adapt, or does the crisis demand an entirely new political model? James Bacchus, Leah Downey, and Kai Heron discuss.

Title: Our future theories of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on black holes, Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and physicist. In recent years, he has investigated the relationship between physics and the mind, famously arguing that quantum mechanics plays an essential role in solving the mysteries of human consciousness. Penrose has made numerous appearances on media such as BBC, Closer to Truth, and The Joe Rogan Experience. In 1994, he was knighted for his services to science. Famed for his poetic take on the cosmos, physicist and broadcaster Brian Cox has become one of the world’s most recognizable voices in science communication. A former musician turned particle physicist, Cox has played a key role in major experiments at CERN and the Large Hadron Collider, while also captivating millions through BBC series such as Wonders of the Universe, The Planets, and Forces of Nature. Cox has been showered with praise for his contributions, appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE), and is the recipient of the Institute of Physics Kelvin Medal and the Michael Faraday Prize. Beyond his work as a Royal Society professor of physics at the University of Manchester, Cox advocates for public scientific literacy and political responsibility in science funding. His style blends rigorous physics with a deep sense of awe — bringing relativity, entropy, and quantum theory into living rooms around the globe. His rare ability to fuse clarity with wonder has earned global acclaim.
Synopsis & Topics: Roger Penrose & Brian Cox explore whether flaws in foundational scientific theories—from the Big Bang to consciousness—are insurmountable or can be overcome to reshape our understanding of reality.

Title: Democracy in the ruins of neoliberalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Wendy Brown is one of the most influential political theorists of her generation, known for her penetrating analyses of power, neoliberalism, democracy, and the fate of the public good in contemporary political life. Brown is currently the UPS Foundation Professor in the School of Social Science at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton and Professor Emerita of Political Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Hosted by Sophie Scott-Brown.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosophers Wendy Brown and Sophie Scott-Brown explore how antidemocratic politics and neoliberal economics intertwine.

Title: The wealth cap
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ingrid Robeyns is a political philosopher known for her work on economic justice, the capability approach, and limits on extreme wealth.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Ingrid Robeyns proposes the idea of limitarianism to address soaring inequality, setting a hard cap on the wealth of the ultra-rich.

Title: The price of populism, with Jason Furman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jason Furman is a prominent American economist known for his extensive contributions to public policy, academia, and economic analysis. He currently serves as the Aetna Professor of the Practice of Economic Policy at Harvard University. He served as the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) under President Barack Obama from August 2013 to January 2017. In this role, he acted as a principal economic advisor to the President.
Synopsis & Topics: Ex-Obama advisor Jason Furman argues that the line between business and government is becoming increasingly blurred under the Trump administration.

Title: I forget therefore I am
Guests & Speakers: Oliver Hardt, Iain McGilchrist, Catherine Loveday
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Oliver Hardt, Professor of Psychology at McGill University, Catherine Loveday, Author of The Secret World of the Brain, and Iain McGilchrist, famed neuroscientist, philosopher and psychologist at the University of Oxford as they clash over what it means to be human. Hosted by Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier.
Synopsis & Topics: Forgetting may matter more than memory: it shapes identity, enables decisions, and supports wellbeing. Those unable to forget show its vital role — but should therapy focus on letting go rather than recovering the past?

Title: How to reclaim the body
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic. She came to prominence with the book Fat Is A Feminist Issue, and was therapist to Diana, Princess of Wales.
Synopsis & Topics: Psycholanalyst and author of Fat is a Feminist Issue, Susie Orbach, argues that society needs to revalue bodily autonomy and redefine the self beyond appearance.

Title: AI and the mysteries of reality
Guests & Speakers: Roman Yampolskiy, Steve Fuller, Suzanne Livingston
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Computer scientist Roman Yampolskiy, philosopher Steve Fuller, and co-curator of AI: More than Human Suzanne Livingston debate whether AI can make novel scientific discoveries. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: While some argue that AI will produce a new golden age of scientific discovery, critics claim that it cannot independently define problems or create truly novel insights. Will AI ever truly discover on its own? Roman Yampolskiy, Steve Fuller, and Suzanne Livingston discuss.

Title: Thinking isn't only in the brain, with Barbara Tversky
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Barbara Tversky is an active Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. Her research has spanned memory, categorization, language, spatial cognition, event perception and cognition, diagrammatic reasoning, sketching, creativity, design, and gesture. The overall goals have been to uncover how people think about the spaces they inhabit and the actions they perform and see and then how people use the world and the things in it. Her 2019 book, Mind in Motion: How Action Shapes Thought, provides an overview of some of that work. She has collaborated widely, with linguists, philosophers, neuroscientists, computer scientists, chemists, biologists, architects, designers, and artists.
Synopsis & Topics: Cognitive psychologist Barbara Tversky argues that thinking is spatial and embodied, not merely verbal: gestures shape thought, and abstract ideas are rooted in bodily experience.

Title: Peace, passion and adventure
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Alenka Zupančič, Paul Bloom
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Janne Teller was formerly a UN macroeconomist specialising in developing economies. She has since become a bestselling author of novels, essays, and short stories. Alenka Zupančič is a leading Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica. Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. He is Professor Emeritus at Yale and a professor at the University of Toronto. Bloom’s work explores human nature, morality, and pleasure.
Synopsis & Topics: Is peace actually a virtue, or does it lead to stagnation? Explore the dark side of serenity with Janne Teller, Alenka Zupančič, and Paul Bloom as they debate if we need enemies to find meaning.

Title: The iron fist vs the invisible hand
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Hélène Landemore, Curtis Yarvin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described by the Guardian as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain’. Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and professor at Yale University, and is also a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI.
Synopsis & Topics: Does democracy hinder economic growth? Curtis Yarvin, Aaron Bastani, and Hélène Landemore debate if authoritarian models like China are the future of global wealth.

Title: There is no fundamental basis to reality, with James Ladyman and Susan Schneider
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind. She is the founding director of the Center for the Future Mind at Florida Atlantic University and holds the Baruch S. Blumberg NASA/Library of Congress Chair in Astrobiology, Exploration, and Scientific Innovation. Schneider is best known for her exploration of post-biological intelligence and the philosophical implications of machine consciousness. In her widely discussed book Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind, she examines whether machines could ever truly possess consciousness, and whether humans should merge with them. James Ladyman is a pioneering philosopher renowned for combining rigorous natural science with deep metaphysical inquiry. A leader in philosophy of science and physics, he champions ontic structural realism, the view that reality is fundamentally relational, and defends a naturalised metaphysics that aligns with our best scientific understanding, challenging inherited intuitions that mislead us about the nature of the universe. In Everything Must Go: Metaphysics Naturalized, Ladyman argues that many common metaphysical assumptions—about objects, causation, or essence—are relics incompatible with modern science. Ladyman’s fusion of analytic clarity with scientific insight reshapes how we think about reality—revealing a cosmos that is stranger and more beautiful than our unexamined instincts suggest.
Synopsis & Topics: Why the "bottom" of reality might not exist. James Ladyman and Susan Schneider debate the nature of existence and why we are losing the competition with AI goals.

Title: Dreams of the future
Guests & Speakers: Daniel Markovits, Eric Kaufmann, Thangam Debbonaire
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Markovits is the Guido Calabresi Professor of Law at Yale Law School and the author of the best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap . Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, chair of the Labour Women's Network, and a leading voice on cultural policy. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at The University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. Hosted by Jack Symes.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we give up on the notion that the future will be better than the past? In a time when such optimism seems to be fading, Daniel Markovits, Eric Kaufmann and Thangam Debbonaire discuss the value of the future.

Title: Materialism and emergence can't explain consciousness, with Alex O'Connor
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alex O’Connor is a YouTuber, public speaker, writer, and host of the Within Reason Podcast. He first began posting videos to his YouTube channel "CosmicSkeptic" before taking his degree in philosophy and theology at St John's College, Oxford. He has since grown his following to over 1.5 million subscribers with his rigorous yet accessible philosophy videos. O’Connor has appeared on television programmes such as Piers Morgan Uncensored, BBC Sunday Morning Live, and Channel 4 News. He has debated philosophy, religion, free speech, and more with leading thinkers Slavoj Žižek, Richard Dawkins, Neil deGrasse Tyson, and more.
Synopsis & Topics: Alex O'Connor critiques materialism and emergence theory, arguing that physical processes alone cannot explain consciousness. Discover the case for seeing consciousness as a fundamental property of the universe.

Title: The power and politics of shame
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kenneth Roth is an attorney, activist and author best known as the Executive Director of Human Rights Watch for nearly thirty years. He is currently a fellow of the Harvard Kennedy School and a lecturer at Princeton's School of Public and International Affairs.
Synopsis & Topics: Kenneth Roth, former director of Human Rights Watch, illustrates moral pressure and strategic shaming can compel even repressive regimes to change.

Title: The green technology paradox
Guests & Speakers: Erik Swyngedouw, Paul Stein, Sheila Jasanoff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Erik Swyngedouw is a leading critical geographer at the University of Manchester. He combines political ecology and economics with analyses of contemporary capitalism, showing how urbanisation, water, and governance are entwined with power and democracy. Harvard scholar Sheila Jasanoff is one of the most influential voices in Science and Technology Studies, dismantling the myth that science and technology operate above human choices, cultural assumptions, and political power. Paul Stein is one of the most influential engineers of his generation, shaping aerospace and energy as former CTO of Rolls-Royce and co-founder of Floral Energy. His work links technological innovation to climate action and national strategy.
Synopsis & Topics: Sheila Jasanoff, Paul Stein and Erik Swyngedouw discuss whether technological development is fundamentally unsustainable, or whether green tech is an achievable ideal.

Title: The universe existed before the Big Bang, with Phil Halper
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Phil Halper is a prominent science communicator whose work probes the limits of cosmology and challenges the dominance of the standard Big Bang narrative.
Synopsis & Topics: Astrophysicist Phil Halper explores alternatives to the Big Bang, including cyclic universes and multiverses, which challenge whether the universe had a singular beginning, or whether is part of a deeper, eternal reality.

Title: Russia, Ukraine, and the failures of the West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Owen Matthews is a British author, historian and journalist. He is author of several books including Stalin's Children , which was shortlisted for the 2008 Guardian First Book Award and the Orwell Prize for political writing. He is one of Britain's leading authorities on Russian history and politics.
Synopsis & Topics: Trump's Ukraine-Russia peace push: bold or reckless? Expert Owen Matthews explores why Western Russia policy has failed, what drives Trump's approach, and the global fallout for Europe, China, and world order.

Title: The grandest of grand narratives
Guests & Speakers: Steve Fuller, Jessica Frazier, Barry C. Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the founder of the research program of social epistemology and the author of dozens of books, including Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. Barry C. Smith is a professor of philosophy and director of the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London. He is an expert on the senses and consciousness and leads groundbreaking interdisciplinary work on flavour, smell, and perception. Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. She is an expert on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. Phil Collins hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Science, history, philosophy, and religion each claim the role of humanity's grand narrative. But which, if any, is the best? Barry C. Smith, Jessica Frazier, and Steve Fuller discuss.

Title: The trouble with meritocracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar, best known for his work on law and behavioural economics, contract law, distributive justice, and market regulation. His best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap: How America's Foundational Myth Feeds Inequality, Dismantles the Middle Class, and Devours the Elite, has sparked a significant discussion about the problems inherent in meritocratic societies.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor Daniel Markovits argues that meritocratic societies are fundamentally flawed, succumbing to economic stagnation and societal decay.

Title: How to hack the reality simulation, with Roman Yampolskiy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roman Yampolskiy is a professor and computer scientist at the University of Louisville who specialises in artificial intelligence, AI safety, digital forensics and behavioural biometrics. He is the author of Considerations on the AI Endgame.
Synopsis & Topics: Roman Yampolisky explores the idea that reality might be a simulation - and, if so, whether there is any way of hacking our way out.

Title: Mental health in an age of over-diagnosis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alastair Santhouse is a consultant psychiatrist with over 20 years of experience at Guy's Hospital and the Maudsley Hospital in London. From 2013 to 2017, he served as Vice Chair of the Royal College of Psychiatrists' Faculty of Liaison Psychiatry. Santhouse also served as the President of the Psychiatry Section of the Royal Society of Medicine. His clinical work focuses on the often overlooked intersection of physical and mental health.
Synopsis & Topics: Is mental illness being over-diagnosed? Psychiatrist Alastair Santhouse explores how culture and science have expanded mental health labels, blurring the line between normal and unhealthy.

Title: Overcoming evolution
Guests & Speakers: Simon Baron-Cohen, Subrena Smith, Keith Frankish
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Critic of evolutionary psychology Subrena E. Smith, philosopher of mind Keith Frankish, and clinical psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen debate the significance of evolutionary psychology. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Subrena Smith, Keith Frankish, and Simon Baron-Cohen as they debate whether we can overcome our evolutionary psychology or whether our behaviour is genetically fixed.

Title: Catherine Liu on taking down the cultural elite
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Liu is an American cultural theorist, critic, and professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine. A sharp public intellectual, Liu is best known for her incisive critiques of elite liberalism, academic hypocrisy, and the commodification of virtue. She brings together Marxist cultural analysis with polemic flair, offering a compelling—and at times confrontational—challenge to the moral self-image of the contemporary professional class.
Synopsis & Topics: Catherine Liu argues that the professional managerial class has hijacked progressive politics, swapping material redistribution for virtue signalling and cultural status.

Title: The Left's identity crisis
Guests & Speakers: Maurice Glasman, Bhaskar Sunkara, Pam Cox
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Maurice Glasman is a political theorist, Labour life peer, and founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Pam Cox is the Labour MP for Colchester who was recently elected to Parliament in 2024. Prior to this she was a professor of social history and criminology at the University of Essex and a fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. Bhaskar Sunkara is currently the president of The Nation, the oldest continuously published weekly magazine in the United States. He is a former vice-chair of the Democratic Socialists of America and the author of The Socialist Manifesto. Roger Hearing hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the Left shifting from compassionate welfarism to a more hard-nosed politics focused on productivity? Maurice Glasman, Bhaskar Sunkara and Pam Cox discuss.

Title: The life and philosophy of Jeremy Corbyn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour Party's leader from 2015 to 2020. Representing the constituency of Islington North since 1983, he was a vocal backbencher with a reputation of voting against his party until he was elected leader with the largest party membership for a generation. He contested the 2017 general election and won 40% of the vote, the largest Labour share since 2001. Since he has been expelled from the Labour Party, Jeremy has gone on to win his Islington seat as an independent and has recently been elected the parliamentary leader of Your Party, a party he founded with fellow MP Zarah Sultana. His views place him firmly on the progressive left where he is staunchly anti-war, anti-austerity, pro-nationalisation and pro-Palestine. In the current Parliament, Jeremy is a key opponent to Keir Starmer, holding the government to account from the left.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Jeremy Corbyn to explore the experiences that shaped, tested, and reaffirmed his philosophy — making him one of the most influential political figures of our time.

Title: The end of ideology
Guests & Speakers: Glenn Greenwald, Seyla Benhabib, Sam Kiley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Glenn Greenwald is a Pulitzer-prize winning journalist, known for publishing the Snowden files and uncovering the largest corruption scandal in Brazil's history. One of the most influential political philosophers of her generation, Seyla Benhabib is Senior Research Scholar at Columbia Law School and has shaped global debates on democracy, migration, and human rights. Sam Kiley is a multi-award winning journalist currently working as World Affairs Editor of The Independent and has covered conflict for more than 30 years, reporting from the front lines in Afghanistan, Iraq and Somalia, among other war zones.
Synopsis & Topics: Sam Kiley, Glenn Greenwald and Seyla Benhabib discuss whether geopolitics is witnessing the end of ideology and the return of raw geography.

Title: Forgiving the unforgivable
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lucy Allais is Professor of Philosophy at Johns Hopkins University and the University of the Witwatersrand, renowned for her work on Immanuel Kant, forgiveness, punishment, and bioethics. She is the author of Manifest Reality: Kant's Idealism and His Realism.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor Lucy Allais argues true forgiveness is radical: forgiving even “unforgivable” acts without excuses or amends. It means refusing to define people by their worst actions and seeing them as capable of moral growth.

Title: All the world's a stage
Guests & Speakers: Paul Bloom, Michelle Terry, Claire Blencowe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claire Blencowe is an associate professor of Sociology and co-chair of the Just Eco-Geo-Political Futures research group at Warwick University. She is a leading scholar of Foucault. Paul Bloom is a psychologist and the author of several bestselling works, including Against Empathy . He is Emeritus Professor of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto. Michelle Terry is an Olivier Award-winning actor and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare's Globe, where she has gained critical acclaim for her modern interpretations of Shakespeare's plays. Matthew Taylor is a British former political strategist and current Chief Executive of the Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce.
Synopsis & Topics: Claire Blencowe, Michelle Terry, and Paul Bloom discuss whether it is possible to stop performing our own identity - and whether there is even a "true self" at all.

Title: Glenn Greenwald: Trump's Iran attacks are business as usual for the US
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: After founding a law firm concentrating on First Amendment litigation (protecting free speech and a free press), Glenn Greenwald turned to journalism. He became a vocal critic of the Iraq War and American foreign policy, a position he has maintained. He started contributing to Salon in 2007 and to The Guardian in 2012, and in the latter published a series of reports detailing covert American and British global surveillance programmes based on classified documents provided by Edward Snowden. For this work, his team won a Pulitzer Prize. Glenn Greenwald has written multiple best-selling books, including How Would a Patriot Act and No Place to Hide: Edward Snowden, the NSA, and the U.S. Surveillance State . He now hosts System Update , where he has interviewed academics, political figures, and commentators including Jeffrey Sachs, John Mearsheimer, Edward Snowden, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and many others.
Synopsis & Topics: Pulizter Prize-winning journalist Glenn Greenwald argues that Trump's war with Iran is in line with the US's existing foreign policy strategy, rather than a deviation from it.

Title: The structure of consciousness
Guests & Speakers: Karl Friston, Jan Westerhoff, Susan Schneider
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Karl Friston is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and Principal Research Fellow for the Wellcome Trust. Jan Westerhoff is Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford University. He researches the philosophical aspects of the religious traditions of ancient India, and contemporary analytic metaphysics. Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Do modern theories in neuroscience support the idea that perception is neutral data about the world, or do they suggest that our brains actively construct the reality we experience—and what does that mean for the existence of the self? Jan Westerhoff, Karl Friston and Susan Schneider discuss.

Title: How the Right won the culture war
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Inaya Folarin Iman is a British political commentator, writer, and the founder of the Equiano Project, an initiative promoting free speech, open dialogue, and a more inclusive approach to discussions about race and identity. Recently, she has focused on challenging the dominance of identity politics in public discourse and advocating for policies rooted in shared humanity rather than divisive rhetoric. Her work at the Equiano Project emphasizes the need for critical reflection on how society addresses complex issues like racial inequality and multiculturalism. She argues for open debate on topics often constrained by political correctness, such as integration and cultural identity. She was a regular presenter on GB news and is also a regular writer for Spiked Online , the Telegraph , and the Daily Mail .
Synopsis & Topics: Inaya Folarin Iman argues that there is a growing multiracial political base which rejects the identity politics of the Leftand embraces the cultural populism of the Right.

Title: Atomic dreams and nuclear nightmares
Guests & Speakers: M. V. Ramana, Sheila Jasanoff, Tim Gregory
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: M. V. Ramana, physicist and Simons Chair at the University of British Columbia, is a leading critic of nuclear power. Tim Gregory is a senior nuclear chemist at the UK’s National Nuclear Laboratory and author of Going Nuclear , where he makes a passionate case for atomic power as the backbone of a sustainable future. Harvard scholar, Sheila Jasanoff, is one of the most influential voices in Science and Technology Studies, dismantling the myth that science and technology operate above politics.
Synopsis & Topics: Tim Gregory, Sheila Jasanoff, and M.V. Ramana debate the risks and promise of nuclear power: is it our best hope of delivering clean, reliable energy, or an expensive and dangerous distraction?

Title: Unelected elites and the limits of democracy
Guests & Speakers: Kenneth Roth, Hélène Landemore, James Bacchus
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ken Roth is an attorney, activist and author best known as the Executive Director of Human Rights Watch for nearly thirty years. Political Philosopher and Professor at Yale University, Hélène Landemore is also a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI. James Bacchus is a lobal trade judge and legal scholar renowned for shaping WTO law and championing sustainable international governance. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Democracy is meant to prevent tyranny, yet power still concentrates in corporations, media, bureaucracies, and elites. Is it possible to sustain unelected elites in a democratic system? Hélène Landemore, Ken Roth, James Bacchus discuss.

Title: The age of mania and conformity, with Lionel Shriver
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lionel Shriver is an American author and journalist best known for her 2003 novel We Need to Talk About Kevin , which won the Orange Prize for Fiction. Her work often explores controversial social and political themes with dark wit and psychological insight. A dual US-UK citizen, Shriver is also a frequent commentator on cultural issues in publications like The Spectator and The Guardian.
Synopsis & Topics: Author and journalist Lionel Shriver argues that social and political manias on topics such as gender, COVID, and climate change, are harmful forces that feed conformity.

Title: The medicalisation of mental illness, with Joanna Moncrieff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joanna Moncrieff is a British psychiatrist and academic. She is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London and a leading figure in the Critical Psychiatry Network.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor Joanna Moncrieff argues that the medicalization of mental illness has been unduly influenced by pharmeceutical marketing, and can both increase social stigma and hinder patient recovery.

Title: Environmental science needs new politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mike Berners-Lee is a fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University and director and principal consultant of Small World Consulting.
Synopsis & Topics: Climate scientist Mike Berners-Lee explores the political and bureaucratic barriers to climate action, and what we can do about them.

Title: The brain filters consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Àlex Gómez-Marín is a theoretical physicist and neuroscientist. He is Associate Professor at the Institute of Neuroscience, Alicante, and Director of the Pari Center in Italy.
Synopsis & Topics: Àlex Gómez-Marín argues that the brain may not produce consciousness, but instead filter or permit it. Science, he claims, needs to take inner experiences seriously in order to investigate this possibility.

Title: Anxiety and the soul's itch, with Sarah Wilson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sarah Wilson is multi - New York Times bestselling author, social philosopher and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan Australia at 29 and founded the global I Quit Sugar movement.
Synopsis & Topics: Social philosopher Sarah Wilson argues that anxiety is a social as well as a psychological phenomenon, caused by technological acceleration, neoliberal atomisation and an increasing separation between humans and the natural world.

Title: Rethinking the fundamentals of quantum physics, with Jacob Barandes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jacob Barandes is a theoretical physicist and philosopher of physics known for his work on the foundations of quantum mechanics and his proposal of “Indivisible Quantum Theory."
Synopsis & Topics: Harvard physicist Jacob Barandes challenges the fundamental assumptions of quantum physics, arguing that  individual quantum events cannot be isolated and explained separately from the complex temporal correlations between these events.

Title: Beyond truth and reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. Hilary Lawson is a post-post modern philosopher and the author of Closure . Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: In a world of radically incompatible and competing perspectives, it seems that the search for a single true version of the reality may be futile. Hilary Lawson and Slavoj Žižek debate our possible alternatives.

Title: Us and them
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Scott-Brown, Thangam Debbonaire, Harvey Whitehouse
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords and former MP for Bristol West. Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford. Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian with research interests in modern European political thought, Anarchism and the history of education. She is a lecturer in Philosophy at the University of East Anglia and former director at the Europaeum Institute at the University of Oxford. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Social groups create a sense of belonging but also divide “us” from “them,” often fueling fear of outsiders. Harvey Whitehouse, Thangham Debonnaire and Sophie Scott-Brown discuss the challenge of building strong bonds without creating exclusion or conflict.

Title: The one and the many
Guests & Speakers: James Ladyman, Sabine Hossenfelder, Ivette Fuentes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and acclaimed science communicator, known for her sharp critiques of the scientific mainstream. She is also a best-selling author and YouTuber. Ivette Fuentes is a theoretical quantum physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. James Ladyman is a philosopher of science at the University of Bristol. He is best known for his book Every Thing Must Go, calling for a metaphysics grounded in physics and complexity science. Hosted by Jack Symes.
Synopsis & Topics: Is reality best understood as a unified whole or as a collection of separate parts, and can science or philosophy ever coherently explain how the two fit together? Physicists Sabine Hossenfelder, Ivette Fuentes and James Ladyman discuss.

Title: The future of artificial minds
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. Former NASA Chair in Astrobiology, Exploration, and Scientific Innovation, Susan Schneider, is a philosopher and cognitive scientist, specialising in consciousness and AI.
Synopsis & Topics: AI is becoming more powerful and intelligent, but whether consciousness will arise with it remains unclear. Susan Schneider and Anders Sandberg weigh up our options.

Title: Stories of unreality
Guests & Speakers: Martha Fiennes, Josh Cohen, Joanna Kavenna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning filmmaker and pioneering AI artist, known for Onegin, Chromophobia, and her AI-driven work Yugen, which has been showcased from Venice to the Serpentine Gallery. Josh Cohen established himself as an academic in American literature and critical theory, before deciding to train as a psychoanalyst. Novelist and travel writer Joanna Kavenna won the Orange Award for New Writers for her novel Inglorious . She's held the Alistair Horne Fellowship at St Antony’s College Oxford and the Harper-Wood Award at St John’s College Cambridge. Johnny Thomson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Martha Fiennes, Josh Cohen and Joanna Kavenna discuss whether, in the aftermath of modernism and postmodernism, literature should attempt to represent portray realistic events.

Title: The chains of freedom
Guests & Speakers: Elizabeth Anderson, Daniel Markovits, Yaron Brook
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Markovits is Professor of Law at Yale Law School and the Founding Director of the Center for the Study of Private Law. He is the author of the bestselling book The Meritocracy Trap Elizabeth Anderson is Professor of Public Philosophy, Politics and Economics at the University of Michigan. She specialises in moral, social and political philosophy, as well as feminist theory and the philosophy of economics and the social sciences. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur, writer, activist, and political scientist. He is currently chairman of the board of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of the Yaron Brook Show. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Although freedom is seen as a fundamental political goal, critics have warned that it burdens us with responsibility and anxiety. Daniel Markovits, Yaron Brook, and Elizabeth Anderson debate whether freedom really is a universal good.

Title: Europe's last chance
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Prominent political commentator Timothy Garton Ash is a leading Oxford Professor of European Studies and a Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institute.
Synopsis & Topics: From the war in Ukraine to Trump’s tariff threats, crises are shaking Europe. Timothy Garton Ash argues they offer a chance to renew, unite, and defend liberal democracy.

Title: How to build real relationships, with Jordan Stephens
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jordan Stephens is a British musician, writer, performer, and mental health advocate best known as one half of the hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, who rose to fame in the early 2010s with hits like “Down with the Trumpets” and “Mama Do the Hump.” Since then, Stephens has emerged as a multi-talented creative voice, using his platform to explore issues of identity, masculinity, race, fame, and mental health through music, television, and activism.
Synopsis & Topics: Jordan Stephens argues that the crises affecting boys today reflects an important cultural transition. Drawing from his own experiences of fame, addiction and ADHD, he argues in favour of vulnerability and emotional honesty as the foundations of modern masculinity.

Title: Sex, society, and erotic capital
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specializing in women’s employment and gender issues, with over 100 papers and numerous books published.
Synopsis & Topics: Catherine Hakim argues that beauty, sex appeal, and social skills form “erotic capital,” a powerful asset society often ignores, yet one that strongly shapes gender, power, and equality debates.

Title: The future of the Right: populism vs conservatism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jesse Norman is a British politician, author, and academic. Serving as the Member of Parliament for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010, he has held various ministerial roles and currently serves as Shadow Leader of the House of Commons. Sir Vernon Bogdanor is a British political scientist and constitutional expert. He is a research professor of Contemporary British History at King's College London.
Synopsis & Topics: As new right-wing movements reshape politics across the US and Europe, and populism challenges free markets and institutions, Jesse Norman and Vernon Bogdanor debate the divided future of conservatism.

Title: The battle of the Big Bang
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Phil Halper is a fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society and science popularizer. He is the creator of the popular YouTube series Before the Big Bang.
Synopsis & Topics: Phil Halper shows how cosmology has become a battlefield of rival theories, from inflation and multiverses to quantum gravity, revealing why the universe’s origins remain profoundly uncertain.

Title: Neighbours before strangers
Guests & Speakers: Tommy J. Curry, Seyla Benhabib, Alain de Botton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alain de Botton is the best-selling philosopher and founder of The School of Life, an organisation dedicated to developing emotional intelligence through philosophy, psychotherapy, and culture. Seyla Benhabib is one of the most influential political philosophers of her generation and is the author of At the Margins of the Modern State . Tommy Curry is the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh, renowned for his critical scholarship on the intersection of race, gender, and power. Alex O'Connor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Alain de Botton, Seyla Benhabib, and Tommy Curry discuss whether universalism wrongly ignores natural partiality to those close to us, or whether it remains essential to Western values.

Title: The return of Sparta
Guests & Speakers: Sarah Wilson, Anders Sandberg, David Pearce
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, international keynote speaker, minimalist, and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan magazine Australia at 29, founded the global ‘I Quit Sugar’ movement and hosted MasterChef Australia – the most-watched TV series in the nation’s history. Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. He served as a senior research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute and the Oxford Martin School at the University of Oxford. His research encompasses societal and ethical implications of emerging technologies, cognitive enhancement, and existential risks. David Pearce is a British philosopher best known for his advocacy of the abolitionist project, the ethical vision of using advanced science and technology to eliminate suffering in all sentient life. A co-founder of the World Transhumanist Association (now Humanity+), he authored The Hedonistic Imperative, a manifesto that argues for the use of genetic engineering, nanotechnology, and neuroscience to replace the biological substrates of pain with gradients of intelligent bliss.
Synopsis & Topics: Sparta prized the body, Athens the mind, and the West chose Athens. But today, declining reasoning, AI-outsourced thinking, and body fixation raise doubts about an intellect-led age.

Title: How brains construct reality, with Karl Friston
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Karl Friston is a neuroscientist and theoretical neurobiologist best known for developing the Free Energy Principle, a unifying framework for understanding brain function, perception, and action. He is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and a leading figure in computational psychiatry, cognitive neuroscience, and the philosophy of mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Friston argues the brain predicts rather than mirrors reality. Under the Free Energy Principle, it minimizes surprise by updating beliefs or acting, so perception and action construct the world.

Title: Living without limits
Guests & Speakers: Anna Lembke, Barry Schwartz, Federico Campagna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert at Stanford. She is author of Drug Dealer MD and most recently Dopamine Nation which argues that too much pleasure in the short time leads to pain in the long-term. Federico Campagna is a leading philosopher, metaphysician and expert on Nihilism. His book Technic and Magic: The Reconstruction of Reality argues for a completely different conception of the structure of reality. Barry Schwartz is an American psychologist and the Dorwin Cartwright Emeritus Professor of Social Theory and Social Action at Swarthmore College. He is author of several famous books including Why We Work and The Paradox of Choice. He argues for a moderated and balanced approach to life. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Anna Lembke, Federico Campagna and Barry Schwartz debate whether moderation enriches life or suppresses authenticity. They explore addiction, excess and meaning in a world engineered for stimulation.

Title: Cracking the code for thought
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski, Max Tegmark
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and black holes, and for his public appearances popularising physics and philosophy. Max Tegmark is a Swedish‑American MIT physicist and cosmologist, and president and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute. He is known for championing the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis and pioneering the notion of consciousness as a state of matter. Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a theoretical physicist at the Perimeter Institute whose work on space, time, and gravity has been cited by Stephen Hawking. She now leads efforts to encode the universe as a hologram, a bold step toward uniting quantum theory with general relativity.
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscience has long treated the brain like a computer, despite it being biological, adaptive, and conscious. Max Tegmark, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski, and Roger Penrose debate whether it is a mistake to see the mind as a complex machine.

Title: The strange search for knowledge in the age of post-truth, with Steve Fuller
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve Fuller is Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick, and a founding figure in the field of social epistemology. He has authored dozens of books, including Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game .
Synopsis & Topics: Rather than a linear march toward truth led by experts, Fuller portrays knowledge as contingent and communal. Post-truth, he argues, exposes how media, education and AI actively shape what we know.

Title: Psychoanalysis reveals the unconscious effects of capitalism, with Alenka Zupancic
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alenka Zupančič is a Slovenian philosopher whose work focuses on psychoanalysis and continental philosophy. A prominent member of the Ljubljana School of Psychoanalysis, Zupančič is best known for her rigorous and often provocative readings of Freud and Lacan, filtered through the lens of German Idealism and Nietzsche.
Synopsis & Topics: Zupančič argues that despite being well aware of unpleasant truths about the world, our mass psychology is increasingly indifferent towards political action, leaving us vulnerable to new crises.

Title: Jeremy Corbyn: "Arrogance in office comes back to bite you in the end"
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020.
Synopsis & Topics: Jeremy Corbyn argues that deindustrialisation from Thatcher-Reagan economics and decades of underinvestment have fuelled social breakdown and the rise of the far right.

Title: Making Europe great again
Guests & Speakers: Johnny Mercer, Timothy Garton Ash, Nathalie Tocci, Yascha Mounk
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Timothy Garton Ash is a leading British historian, political writer, and one of Europe’s most compelling chroniclers of modern transformation. He is Professor of European Studies at the University of Oxford and a Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution, Stanford University. Nathalie Tocci is one of Europe’s most influential and thoughtful strategists on international affairs, known for her pivotal role in shaping European foreign policy and advancing a nuanced approach to diplomacy, security, and global cooperation. She currently serves as the director of the Instituto Affari Internazionali. Johnny Mercer is a former Veterans Minister, Conservative MP and British Army Captain who served three tours of duty in Afghanistan. He used his time in Parliament to aid veterans in their access to healthcare, mental health support and housing, as well as fighting the criminal prosecution of soldiers in Iraq and Northern Ireland. Yascha Mounk is a political scientist and public intellectual known for his analysis of the threats to liberal democracy. A Professor at Johns Hopkins and founder of the online magazine Persuasion, he argues that identity-based ideologies can undermine democratic norms and social cohesion. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
Synopsis & Topics: Trump’s America First policies may fracture the West, but will they spur Europe to reclaim global leadership?

Title: How our modern work ethic destroys work
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Elizabeth Anderson is Arthur F. Thurnau Professor and John Dewey Distinguished University Professor of Philosophy and Women’s Studies at the University of Michigan and author of Hijacked .
Synopsis & Topics: The moral language of rigour and self-discipline has been reworked to legitimize inequality, rather than empower workers, argues Elizabeth Anderson.

Title: Beyond the limits of science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton. Her work ranges across epistemology and the philosophy of religion, with a distinctive focus on the ethical and existential dimensions of thought in Ludwig Wittgenstein and Søren Kierkegaard.
Synopsis & Topics: Faith and science are often seen as rivals. Drawing on Wittgenstein, Genia Schönbaumsfeld argues religion isn’t bad science or emotion, but a truth-oriented practice alongside science.

Title: Nicola Sturgeon has a lot to be frank about
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nicola Sturgeon, is the former First Minister of Scotland and former leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) and remains a prominent political figure, despite stepping down from her leadership roles in 2023. She has been at the forefront of Scottish politics since 2004 when she first ran to be leader of the SNP.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nicola Sturgeon, in conversation with Mary Ann Sieghart, discusses the philosophical outlook which has driven behind her remarkable career in politics.

Title: Nuclear is not the solution
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: M.V. Ramana is the Simons Chair in Disarmament, Global and Human Security and Professor at the School of Public Policy and Global Affairs, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, Canada.
Synopsis & Topics: Nuclear energy is not a rapid, safe, or cost-effective route to clean energy, argues policy expert M. V. Ramana.

Title: Freedom and fate
Guests & Speakers: Paul Bloom, Lucy Allais, Robert Sapolsky
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. He is Professor Emeritus at Yale and a professor at the University of Toronto. Bloom’s work explores human nature, morality, and pleasure. Joining us from California is Robert Sapolsky. Sapolsky is a distinguished neuroscientist, primatologist, and author, best known for his research on stress and its impact on behaviour and health. He is also a professor at Stanford University. Lucy Allais is a philosopher at Johns Hopkins University and the University of the Witwatersrand, renowned for her work on Immanuel Kant. Her writing spans ethics, metaphysics, and political philosophy. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: If our actions are determined by neurological processes, can we still hold common-sense beliefs about freedom and responsibility? Robert Sapolsky, Lucy Allais and Paul Bloom weigh up our options.

Title: The life and philosophy of Neil Kinnock
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Neil Kinnock is a Welsh politician who was Leader of the Opposition and Leader of the Labour Party from 1983 to 1992. He undertook the monumental task of modernising the party after its crushing electoral defeat, battling internal factionalism, confronting Militant entryism, and laying the groundwork for the eventual rise of New Labour.
Synopsis & Topics: Alasdair Campbell speaks to Neil Kinnock about the latter's political philosophy and career in the British government, as well as the state of modern politics.

Title: We don't know what genes are, with Philip Ball
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Ball is a renowned British science writer and former editor of Nature, celebrated for uncovering the poetic wonder within hard science. In over thirty books, including Critical Mass (Royal Society Winton Prize), Beyond Weird (Physics World Book of the Year), and How Life Works, he explores how science is deeply entwined with culture, politics, and imagination.
Synopsis & Topics: Philip Ball challenges the idea that genomes are blueprints and genes are instructions, and argues that we should view life as a self-organizing, multilevel system.

Title: The great innovation race
Guests & Speakers: Anu Bradford, Daniel A. Bell, Jason Furman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel A. Bell is a prominent political theorist known for his work on Chinese political thought and comparative political philosophy. He currently serves as Chair of Political Theory at the University of Hong Kong's faculty of Law. Previously, he served as Dean of the School of Political Science and Public Administration at Shandong University and as a professor at Tsinghua University Anu Bradford is a leading scholar on the EU’s regulatory power and a sought-after commentator on the European Union, global economy, and digital regulation. She is the Henry L. Moses Professor of Law and International Organisation at Columbia University and was previously at Chicago Law School. Jason Furman is a prominent American economist known for his extensive contributions to public policy, academia, and economic analysis. He currently serves as the Aetna Professor of the Practice of Economic Policy at Harvard University. He served as the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) under President Barack Obama from August 2013 to January 2017. In this role, he acted as a principal economic advisor to the President. Roger Hearing hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Our expert panel discusses whether innovation thrives better under liberal democracy, or whether China's state-led authoritarian capitalism provides a better model.

Title: The end of materialism, with Àlex Gómez-Marín
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Àlex Gómez-Marín is a Theoretical physicist and neuroscientist, Associate Professor at the Instituto de Neurociencias of Alicante in Spain, and director of the Pari Center in Italy.
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscientist Àlex Gómez-Marín argues that near death experiences challenge the materialist account of consciousness.

Title: Lies, damned lies, and misinformation
Guests & Speakers: Philip Collins, Myriam François, Aaron Maté, Inaya Folarin Iman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations and U.S. foreign policy. Writer-in-chief at The Draft, Phil Collins has held positions at almost every major newspaper in the country. Inaya Folarin Iman is a British political commentator, writer, and the founder of the Equiano Project. Myriam François is a trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. She is also the founder of MPWR productions. Hosted by Sophie Scott-Brown.
Synopsis & Topics: In an era of mistrust, distinguishing political facts from lies is harder than ever, with both sides claiming the other's truth is misinformation. Should we accept biased rhetoric or demand objective truth?

Title: The search for higher states of consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies. During her academic career, she has explored key philosophical themes across various cultures cultures, ranging from Indian concepts of Being to 20th century phenomenology. In addition, Frazier is the founding editor of the 'Journal of Hindu Studies' and a frequent contributor to BBC radio.
Synopsis & Topics: Jessica Frazier examines historical accounts of higher states of consciousness, including their revival in the twentieth century, and explores their scientific and spiritual connotations.

Title: We must exploit tribalism as a force for good
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Cognitive scientist Harvey Whitehouse argues that tribalism can be be beneficial for humans, underpinning peaceful coexistence and sustainability.

Title: Erotic power and the new sexual revolution
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Hakim, Minna Salami, Farha Khalidi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specialising in women’s employment and gender issues, with over 100 papers and numerous books published. Minna Salami is a writer and thinker who blends feminism, philosophy, and politics, and is the author of Can Feminism Be African? Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker and OnlyFans model with 1.7 million followers on TikTok.
Synopsis & Topics: Farha Khalidi, Catherine Hakim, and Minna Salami debate the impact of sex work and sites like OnlyFans on women and the feminist movement

Title: The self and the world
Guests & Speakers: Slavoj Žižek, Carlo Rovelli, Alenka Zupančič
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is one of the most famous philosophers in the world and is the author of more than 50 books, including most recently at the time of the debate Zero Point . Alenka Zupančič is a leading Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica. Joining from America, Carlo Rovelli is a leading theoretical physicist, the author of several best-selling books, and a founding figure in the field of quantum gravity. His recent book, Reality Is Not What It Seem s, has ethical implications for the nature of the self and personal identity. Jack Symes hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In this panel debate, Carlo Rovelli, Alenka Zupančič and Slavoj Žižek discuss whether  human minds are separate from material world.

Title: Skeletons in the academy's closet
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy J. Curry is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Edinburgh, holding a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies. He is the author of several influential works, including The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood, which won an American Book Award in 2018, and Another White Man’s Burden: Josiah Royce’s Quest for a Philosophy of Racial Empire.
Synopsis & Topics: Tommy J. Curry argues that liberal political theory’s claims of neutrality weaken frameworks like intersectionality and mask real-world harm

Title: Reimagining the Right
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Tice is a British businessman and politician, best known for his leadership of Reform UK, formerly the Brexit Party prior to Nigel Farage. A prominent advocate for Brexit, Tice played a key role in the campaign for the UK's departure from the European Union and was elected to Parliament in 2024. Since founding the Brexit party in 2018, Tice has been at the heart of a political movement that has upended politics and reached out to many dissatisfied voters.
Synopsis & Topics: Reform UK's Richard Tice argues rising right-wing populism and “common-sense” ideas are reshaping global politics for the century ahead.

Title: Humanity's next step with Zoltan Istvan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Zoltan Istvan is a transhumanist, futurist, entrepreneur, and former US Presidential candidate. With his bestselling book The Transhumanist Wager, and speeches at institutions like the World Bank, World Economic Forum, and the UK Parliament, Zoltan Istvan has spearheaded the effort to transform transhumanism into a thriving worldwide phenomenon.
Synopsis & Topics: Istvan argues that transhumanism will enable humans to achieve immortality, despite the concerns of some critics.

Title: Transhumanism: the future or the world's most dangerous idea?
Guests & Speakers: Susan Schneider, Àlex Gómez-Marín, Zoltan Istvan, Adam Goldstein
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Zoltan Istvan is a transhumanist, futurist, entrepreneur, and former US Presidential candidate. He has spearheaded the effort to transform transhumanism into a thriving worldwide phenomenon. Àlex Gómez-Marín is a theoretical physicist, neuroscientist, and director of the Pari Center in Italy. He explores the nature of consciousness, human experience, and the limitations of mainstream science. Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind. She is the founding director of the Center for the Future Mind at Florida Atlantic University. Adam Goldstein is the Co-Founder, Chairman, and Head of Research at Softmax, a company that seeks to engineer AI that scales through coordinated diversity rather than imposed control. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
Synopsis & Topics: Àlex Gómez-Marín, Zoltan Istvan, Susan Schneider, and Adam Goldstein debate the promises and dangers of transhumanism and conquering biology.

Title: Gravity reveals the quantum world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Raphael Bousso is a theoretical physicist at the University of California, Berkeley, who studies how gravity, space, and quantum physics fit together. He is known for discovering powerful limits on how much information the universe can store, using ideas from black holes and cosmology to reveal how reality works at its most fundamental level.
Synopsis & Topics: Physicist Raphael Bousso suggests general relativity may guide quantum mechanics, showing gravity can unexpectedly reveal deep quantum properties.

Title: Aaron Maté on the contradictions of liberalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics.
Synopsis & Topics: In this hard-hitting interview, journalist Aaron Maté breaks down why he believes liberalism has strayed from its professed values and how that shapes today’s political landscape.

Title: The good, the bad, the transgressive
Guests & Speakers: Rowan Williams, Catherine Liu, Josh Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. Josh Cohen established himself as an academic in American literature and critical theory, before deciding to train as a psychoanalyst. Catherine Liu is a professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine, renowned for her incisive critiques of contemporary cultural and political dynamics. Hosted by Barry C. Smith.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we accept that transgression is vital to a healthy culture central and necessary for humans to flourish? Or should we seek to remove transgressive behaviour from all public and private life? Join theologist Rowan Williams, psychoanalyst Josh Cohen and cultural theorist Catherine Liu as the discuss morality. Barry C. Smith hosts.

Title: The rise of technofeudalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yanis Varoufakis is a leading critic of the economic establishment. He was the former Finance Minister of Greece, and is a professor, bestselling author, and current chair of the Democracy in Europe Movement 2025.
Synopsis & Topics: Yanis Varoufakis exposes the rise of technofeudalism, arguing that Big Tech’s new overlords threaten democracy and global power. Discover why he believes we must challenge this emerging system before it’s too late.

Title: The substance of the world
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Sabine Hossenfelder, Tim Maudlin, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University. Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and acclaimed science communicator, known for her sharp critiques of the scientific mainstream. She is also a best-selling author and YouTuber. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a theoretical physicist at the Perimeter Institute whose work on space, time, and gravity has been cited by Stephen Hawking. She now leads research on uniting quantum theory with general relativity through celestial holography. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Sabine Hossenfelder, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski, Hilary Lawson, and Tim Maudlin discuss whether particles truly exist and what relationship they have to fields.

Title: Perversity and the limits of the rational, with Paul Bloom
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Bloom is Professor Emeritus of Psychology and Cognitive Science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto. His research explores the psychology of morality, identity, and pleasure.
Synopsis & Topics: Some of the most puzzling and “perverse” things humans do—those acts that seem pointless, mischievous, even self-undermining—may hold surprising benefits. In this interview, Bloom challenges the simple dichotomy of rationality as good and irrationality as bad, urging us to think more carefully about the messy middle.

Title: The philosophy of performance
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michelle Terry is an Olivier-Award-winning actor and writer, and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe. Renowned for her innovative interpretations of Shakespeare, she is a leading figure in contemporary British theatre. Dr Myriam François is a journalist, filmmaker and writer. She also founded MPWR productions, an independent documentary production company which seeks to platform minority voices.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Olivier-winning actor Michelle Terry, Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe, in a deep dive on performance. Is acting always an act? And where is the line between our true, authentic selves and the multitude of characters we all play each and every day?

Title: The life and philosophy of Nicola Sturgeon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nicola Sturgeon, is the former First Minister of Scotland and former leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) and remains a prominent political figure, despite stepping down from her leadership roles in 2023. She has been at the forefront of Scottish politics since 2004 when she first ran to be leader of the SNP. Hosted by journalist and author of The Authority Gap Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Mary Ann Sieghart in conversation with Nicola Sturgeon as they explore the life, philosophy, and political journey of Scotland’s former First Minister. Discover the beliefs, experiences, and challenges that shaped her leadership, from nuclear disarmament and independence to her 2023 resignation.

Title: The blueprint for life
Guests & Speakers: Denis Noble, Joanna Moncrieff, Stuart Kauffman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Stuart Kauffman is a theoretical biologist whose work on self-organisation and complexity reshapes our understanding of life’s origins. He is Emeritus professor at the University of Pennsylvania and a MacArthur Fellow.Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at UCL and a consultant psychiatrist with the NHS. She is a leading critic of the “chemical imbalance” theory of depression.Denis Noble is a world-renowned biologist and pioneer of Systems Biology, Professor Emeritus, and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford. Hosted by Philip Ball.
Synopsis & Topics: Denis Noble, Joanna Moncrieff, and Stuart Kauffman discuss the successes and failures of the Human Genome Project and the current state of genetic medicinal technology.

Title: Foreign policy isn't guided by morality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sir Simon Jenkins is a British Author, newspaper columnist and editor. He was an editor of the Evening Standard from 1976 to 1978 and of the Times from 1990 to 1992.
Synopsis & Topics: Simon Jenkins discusses rejecting left–right politics, promoting localism, and urging pragmatic peace and non-intervention in foreign policy.

Title: Journalism in the age of post-truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cathy Newman is the first female main presenter of Channel 4 News. She spent over a decade in Fleet Street, latterly with the Financial Times. Since joining Channel 4 News in 2006 she has broadcast a string of scoops, including allegations of violent abuse against the British barrister John Smyth, sexual harassment allegations against the Liberal Democrat Peer Lord Rennard, and an investigation into a British sex offender, Simon Harris, which saw him jailed for 17 years. She was also the only broadcast journalist to travel with Angelina Jolie and the foreign secretary William Hague to the Congo as part of a campaign against sexual violence.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Cathy Newman and Elizabeth Oldfield in a thought-provoking discussion on journalism's role in a post-truth democracy. Explore media trust and narrative shaping.

Title: Human perception isn't a hallucination, it's imagination, with Nadine Dijkstra
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the innovative work of Nadine Dijkstra as she investigates the neural processes behind mental imagery and its implications for mental health.

Title: The future of European thought
Guests & Speakers: Babette Babich, Genia Schönbaumsfeld, Christoph Schuringa
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Associate Professor of Philosophy at Northeastern University London, Christoph Schuringa is known for his works on German philosophy and is Editor of the Hegel Bulletin.Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton and the author of several books – most recently, Wittgenstein on Religious Belief. Babette Babich is Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University and the editor of the journal New Nietzsche Studies. Hosted by Danielle Sands.
Synopsis & Topics: Christoph Schuringa, Genia Schönbaumsfeld, and Babette Babich discuss the current state of philosophy, the divide between the analytic and continental schools, and the place of philosophy in the modern world.

Title: The life and philosophy of John Gray
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Gray is one of Britain’s leading philosophers and public intellectuals, renowned for his penetrating critiques of liberalism, humanism, and the Enlightenment faith in progress. A former professor at the London School of Economics, Gray is the author of numerous acclaimed works including Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals, and The New Leviathans . His writing challenges our most cherished assumptions about morality, politics, and what it means to be human. Andy Owen is a writer and former British Army officer whose work explores morality, leadership, and the human experience in conflict.
Synopsis & Topics: Discover the life and philosophy of John Gray, one of Britain's most provocative thinkers. Explore how his experiences shaped his critiques of progress and morality.

Title: The end of free trade and the new world economy
Guests & Speakers: Greg Hands, Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven, Ben Chu, Mark Littlewood
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven is a Senior Lecturer in International Development at King’s College London and critic of economic orthodoxy. Mark Littlewood is an economist, politician and former director of the Institute of Economic Affairs. He is a regular fixture of UK political media defending free market and laissez-faire approaches to managing the economy. Policy and Analysis correspondent at BBC Verify, Ben Chu was formerly the Economics Editor of Newsnight and is a non-fiction economics author. Greg Hands is a former Conservative Minister who most recently was the Minister of State for Trade Policy under Rishi Sunak. Isabel Woodford hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the the debate on tariffs versus free trade, examining their impact on economies and industries. Will Trump's tariffs reshape the future of global trade?

Title: Lost in thought
Guests & Speakers: Steven Pinker, Barbara Tversky, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steven Pinker is a cognitive psychologist, linguist, and bestselling author known for his work on language and human nature. A Professor of Psychology at Harvard University, his books, including Enlightenment Now and The Better Angels of Our Nature , have made him one of the world’s most influential public thinkers. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and leading critic of realism. His major work, Closure: A Story of Everything , sets out a radical non-realist metaphysics that challenges traditional views of truth and the world. Barbara Tversky is Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. A pioneer of embodied cognition, she has written extensively on memory, spatial thinking, and creativity, exploring how our minds shape the world we perceive. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the intricate relationship between language and thought. Discover how philosophers and scientists debate whether language shapes our ideas or merely expresses them.

Title: Copying consciousness: the future of mind uploading
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anders Sandberg is a senior fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford University and is best known for his work on human enhancement and emerging technologies.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we upload the human mind? Anders Sandberg explores brain emulation, digital consciousness, and the science behind future mind uploading.

Title: The West versus the Islamic World, with Ali Allawi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ali Abdul-Amir Allawi was Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. An Iraqi politician and scholar, from May 2020 to August 2022, he ran as Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. He resigned from the post of finance minister on August 16, 2022 due to the deteriorating political situation in Iraq. Interviewed by Alasdair Craig
Synopsis & Topics: Former Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Ali Allawi explores how Western perceptions of the Middle East distort its realities. He argues that progress must come from within—through stability, equality, and reform on the region’s own terms.

Title: How words warp reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research.
Synopsis & Topics: Language shapes how we think, remember, and reason. But does it help us to uncover the fundamental nature of reality? Join the author of Language vs. Reality and linguistic anthropologist, Nick Enfield, as he explores why language excels at persuasion but falters at faithfully representing reality.

Title: The age of the universe
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Claudia de Rham, Karen Crowther
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist at Imperial College London, working at the interface between gravity, cosmology and particle physics, and in 2020 won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for her ground-breaking work. Karen Crowther is a Professor at the University of Oslo, specialising in the philosophy of science and physics. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Roger Penrose, Claudia de Rham, and Karen Crowther as they debate the origins of the universe, the finality of the Big Bang, and the possibility of an infinite cosmos.

Title: The future of the Right
Guests & Speakers: Mark Littlewood, Rachel Maclean, Sohrab Ahmari, Gawain Towler
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sohrab Ahmari is a celebrated journalist and cultural critic and co-founder of Compact magazine and author of Tyranny, Inc. Gawain Towler is a British political strategist, journalist, and long-standing figure in the Eurosceptic movement. Best known for his work in party communications and media strategy, he currently serves on the governing board of Reform UK. Rachel Maclean is a former UK minister, Conservative peer, and is Director of Strategy to the Leader of the Opposition. Mark Littlewood is a libertarian economist and media commentator known for his provocative advocacy on free markets, regulation, and public policy. He’s currently director of the think tank Popular Conservatism. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
