Synopsis & Topics: Join journalist Sohrab Ahmari, political strategist Gawain Towler, former minster Rachel Maclean, and economist Mark Littlewood as they debate the future of right wing politics.

Title: The metaphysics of quantum mechanics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alyssa Ney is Professor and Chair of Metaphysics in the Faculty of Philosophy, Philosophy of Science, and Religious Studies at LMU Munich.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Alyssa Ney in this video as she describes some fascinating recent proposals ranging from the picture of the quantum world as a wave function in higher dimensions to the many worlds theory.

Title: Girl power
Guests & Speakers: Clare Chambers, Susie Orbach, Aaron Bastani
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Clare Chambers is Professor of Political Philosophy at Jesus College Cambridge, and the author of Intact and Against Marriage: An Egalitarian Defence of the Marriage-Free State. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian. Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic, who came to prominence with the book Fat Is a Feminist Issue, and was therapist to Diana, Princess of Wales. Barry Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Clare Chambers, Aaron Bastani, and Susie Orbach as they debate the future of feminism.

Title: Lessons for the left
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Diane Abbott is a British politician and a Member of Parliament for Hackney North and Stoke Newington since first being elected in 1987. She served in the Shadow Cabinet of Jeremy Corbyn as Shadow Home Secretary from 2016 to 2020 and is an advisor to the Privy Council. She was the first black woman elected to parliament and is the longest-serving black MP.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Britain’s longest-serving female MP, Diane Abbott, as she explores why traditional appeals from the progressive left no longer resonate and what must change.

Title: Norman Ohler on Hitler and the Nazis' little-known drug habit
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Norman Ohler is an author, novelist and screenwriter, best known for his popular history book 'Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich'. His most recent book, 'Tripped: Nazi Germany, The CIA and the Dawn of the Psychedelic Age', explores the US government's research into LSD as a mind control drug following their discovery of Nazi experimentation during the Holocaust.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Norman Ohler expands on his book 'Blitzed', arguing that the Nazis wouldn't have been such an effective fighting force without Methamphetamine, but that it was also part of what led to their ultimate failure.

Title: In search of nothing
Guests & Speakers: David Deutsch, Lee Smolin, Amanda Gefter
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Deutsch is a pioneering theoretical physicist best known as the founding father of quantum computation and as a key figure and advocate for the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics. Amanda Gefter is a celebrated science writer specialising in fundamental physics, cosmology, cognitive science and philosophy. Lee Smolin is a renowned theoretical physicist known for his work on loop quantum gravity, cosmological natural selection, and, more broadly, in the philosophy of physics. Hosted by Matt O’Dowd.
Synopsis & Topics: Join David Deutsch, Lee Smolin, Amanda Gefter, and Matt O'Dowd as they explore the concept of 'nothingness' in cosmology.

Title: Hilary Lawson on God, the world, and what exists
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher, renowned critic of philosophical realism, and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, 'Closure: A Story of Everything', has been described as "the first non-realist metaphysics". Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. You can find out more about Closer to Truth HERE .
Synopsis & Topics: Post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson explains his theory of closure and demonstrates how we can have useful and effective ways of intervening in the world even though we don't have truth.

Title: The holy grail of economics
Guests & Speakers: Cahal Moran, Matthew Lynn, Daniela Gabor
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniela Gabor is a Professor of Economics at SOAS. She has been published in The Guardian, Financial Times and Jacobin. Matthew Lynn is a financial columnist and author. He writes for The Daily Telegraph, The Spectator, and MoneyWeek, and he has worked as a columnist for The Sunday Times and Bloomberg. Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist and Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and Political Science and the creator of the YouTube channel Unlearning Economics. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: Should economic growth be the aim of society? Join Daniela Gabor, Matthew Lynn, and Cahal Moran as they debate the holy grail of modern economics.

Title: The biology of conflict
Guests & Speakers: Massimo Pigliucci, John Dupré, Maria Balaet
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Massimo Pigliucci is an Italian-American philosopher and biologist specialising in evolutionary biology and the philosophy of science. His recent work focuses on Stoicism. John Dupre is Professor of Philosophy and Director of Egenis, The Centre for the Study of Life Sciences, at the University of Exeter. He has wide-ranging interests in the philosophy of biology and naturalistic, empirically grounded metaphysics. Maria Balaet is a leading psychedelics researcher and neuroscientist in the Department of Neuroimaging at King’s College London.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Robert Lawrence Kuhn, creator and host of Closer to Truth, alongside philosophers Massimo Pigliucci and John Dupré, and neuroscientist Maria Balaet to explore the biology of conflict  .

Title: Why we worship without knowing it with Alain de Botton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alain de Botton is a philosopher, author, and founder of The School of Life. Known for works such as The Consolations of Philosophy, Religion for Atheists, and The Course of Love, his writing explores how ancient wisdom can guide us through the complexities of modern existence. Alex O’Connor, known online as The Cosmic Skeptic, is a philosopher, podcaster, and broadcaster whose work investigates the boundaries between reason, faith, and moral life.
Synopsis & Topics: Alain de Botton joins Alex O’Connor (Cosmic Skeptic) to ask how we can rediscover meaning, ritual, and reverence in a secular age.

Title: Why imaginary numbers are central to quantum physics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the world's foremost philosophers of physics, Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. He is a member of the "Foundational Questions Institute" of the Académie Internationale de Philosophie des Sciences and is the recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship. Maudlin is the author of 'The Metaphysics Within Physics', 'Truth and Paradox: Solving the Riddles' and 'Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity'.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher of science Tim Maudlin as he argues that the appearance of complex numbers in Schrödinger’s equation is not arbitrary, but motivated by the need for a particular kind of wave-like structure in fundamental dynamics.

Title: A world without morality
Guests & Speakers: John Mearsheimer, Christina Lamb, Kenneth Roth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Famed international relations professor John Mearsheimer, former Executive Director of Human Rights Watch Kenneth Roth, and Chief Foreign Correspondent of The Sunday Times, Christina Lamb, debate a world without morality. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: Join professor of international relations, John Mearsheimer, human rights lawyer Kenneth Roth, and Times Foreign Correspondent Christina Lamb as they debate the state of geopolitics in a world without morality.

Title: The delusions of the digital age
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lionel Shriver is an award winning author and provocative voice in contemporary literature, unafraid to tackle contentious subjects with unflinching honesty. Her acclaimed novel, We Need to Talk About Kevin, delves into the complexities of motherhood and moral responsibility, which earned her the Orange Prize for Fiction in 2005.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Lionel Shriver as she unmasks the fraud and deception behind these social manias and suggests a path forward to escape the grip of these delusions, which threaten not just free speech, but our way of life.

Title: The philosopher behind JD Vance: Curtis Yarvin vs Alastair Campbell
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Yarvin has profoundly influenced American politics, counting among his readers Steve Bannon, Peter Thiel, and Vice-President J.D. Vance. Alastair Campbell is one of the most important voices in modern British politics. Best known for his role as chief spokesman and strategist under Tony Blair, Campbell now works predominantly as a writer and broadcaster, remaining a leading thinker on the centre-left. He is also the co-host of multi award winning podcast, The Rest is Politics.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Curtis Yarvin as he is interviewed on his radical political philosophy. Interviewed by host of The Rest is Politics and Tony Blair's Head of Communications Alastair Campbell.

Title: Dimensions of the unknown
Guests & Speakers: Raphael Bousso, Dean Rickles, Karen Crowther
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Karen Crowther is a Professor at the University of Oslo, specialising in the philosophy of science and physics. Raphael Bousso is Professor and The Chancellor's Chair in Physics at UC Berkeley, where he studies quantum information, gravity, black holes, and cosmology. Dean Rickles is Professor of History and Philosophy of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, Australia, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. Hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Karen Crowther, Raphael Bousso, and Dean Rickles as they ask how many dimensions our universe has and debate if we can ever know.

Title: Technology and freedom
Guests & Speakers: Timothy Nguyen, Janne Teller, Yanis Varoufakis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yanis Varoufakis is a world-renowned economist, academic, and politician. His latest book is Technofedualism: What Killed Capitalism. Timothy Nguyen is a leading AI researcher at Google DeepMind and the host of the podcast The Cartesian Café . Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller’s work includes existential themes on a grand scale, which often spark controversial debate. Hosted by Shini Somara.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Yanis Varoufakis, Timothy Nguyen, and Janne Teller as they debate whether it's possible for us to have freedom and autonomy with our current usage of technology.

Title: Massive gravity and the dark energy enigma
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claudia de Rham is a leading Professor of Theoretical Physics at Imperial College, London. Claudia is recognised for her revitilisation of and research into massive gravity theory, for which she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Claudia de Rham as she reveals how great minds, from Newton and Einstein to Stephen Hawking and Roger Penrose, led her to radically rethink gravity. The result is a new theory called "massive gravity," that eliminates the need for dark energy altogether.

Title: Hilary Lawson on reality and the illusion of truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher, renowned critic of philosophical realism, and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, 'Closure: A Story of Everything', has been described as "the first non-realist metaphysics". Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. You can find out more about Closer to Truth HERE .
Synopsis & Topics: Post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson explains his theory of closure and demonstrates how we can have useful and effective ways of intervening in the world even though we don't have truth.

Title: The art of crossing borders
Guests & Speakers: Rowan Williams, Subha Mukherji, Issam Kourbaj, Natalya Din-Kariuki
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rowan Williams former Archbishop of Canterbury is a theologian, poet, and author known for his wide-ranging work on Christian theology, ethics, and the relationship between faith and society. Natalya Din-Kariuki is an Associate Professor at the Department of English and Comparative Literary Studies at the University of Warwick. She is also affiliated with the Centre for the Study of the Renaissance and the Global History and Culture. Issam Kourbaj was born in Syria and trained at the Institute of Fine Arts in Damascus. His work has been widely exhibited and collected. His Dark Water, Burning World is in the permanent collection of the Pergamon Museum and the British Museum. Subha Mukherji is Professor of Early Modern Literature and Culture. Since her influential book on Renaissance law and drama she has been working on a project titled Crossroads of Knowledge in Early Modern England.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former Archbishop of Canterbury, Rowan Williams, early modernists Natalya Din-Kariuki Subha Mukherji, and artist Issam Kourbaj as they discuss the role of migration in art, the processes of meaning-making they embody, and how they represent and negotiate with dispossession in a way that can also recreate exchange, agency, and even homecoming.

Title: Why you're probably getting poorer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist, host of the YouTube channel "Unlearning Economics", and author of the books, "The Econocracy" and "Why We’re Getting Poorer". Cahal is also a Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and Political Science.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Cahal Moran, also known as Unlearning Economics, as he argues the economy is set up to fail and we need to free economics from its self-imposed straightjacket. Only then can we make the economy work for all.

Title: The story of the universe
Guests & Speakers: Ivette Fuentes, John Dupré, Alex Rosenberg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Dupré is a celebrated Professor of Philosophy and Director of Egenis, The Centre for the Study of Life Sciences, at the University of Exeter. He has made important contributions to the philosophy of biology, as well as naturalistic, empirically-grounded metaphysics. Alex Rosenberg is a novelist and philosopher, renowned for his work in the philosophy of biology and the philosophy of economics. He is one of the most prominent defenders of physical reductionism, and his radical stances have earned him the moniker, "The Mad Dog Naturalist." Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. Her work considers fundamental quantum mechanics and she is a close collaborator with Roger Penrose.
Synopsis & Topics: Join John Dupré, Alex Rosenberg, and Ivette Fuentes as they debate the truth and reality of modern physics at providing a description of the universe.

Title: The importance of giving up
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Adam Phillips is a psychoanalytic psychotherapist and essayist. He has been the general editor of the Penguin Modern Classics translations of Sigmund Freud. Hosted by Claudia Canavan the Head of New Features at the New Scientist. She writes on mind, drugs, hormones, and emotions, with a focus on emerging health trends.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychoanalyst Adam Phillips argues that refusing to give up has dark and hidden consequences and instead we should be constantly open to revising ourselves and opposing the tyranny of completion.

Title: Slavoj Žižek on the madness of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. Foreign Policy named Žižek a Top 100 Global Thinker "for giving voice to an era of absurdity”. Interviewed by Charlie Barnett.
Synopsis & Topics: Join this expressive and content-packed exclusive interview with globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic, Slavoj Žižek, to find out.

Title: The language of the unconscious
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alenka Zupančič is a Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading Lacanian philosopher and collaborator of Slavoj Žižek, Alenka Zupančič, as she argues that AI shows the unconscious is structured like a large language model.

Title: ChatGPT doesn't understand anything with Michael Wooldridge
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Wooldridge is the Ashall Professor of the Foundations of Artificial Intelligence in the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford, and a Senior Research Fellow at Hertford College.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Michael Wooldridge explores what it will take for machines to achieve higher-order reasoning, the challenges and ethical consequences that come with this pursuit, and what these developments mean for the future of AI and society at large.

Title: A world that cares
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Liu, David Goodhart, Tim Jackson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Liu is a professor of Film and Media Studies at UC Irvine. Her work critiques cultural politics, political economy, and the professional managerial class. Her books include Virtue Hoarders and The American Idyll. Tim Jackson is an ecological economist and writer. He has been at the forefront of international debates on sustainability and has worked closely with the UK Government, the UN, the European Commission, and numerous NGOs. David Goodhart is the former editor of Prospect and Director of the London based think tank Demos. Author of The British Dream: successes and failures of post-war immigration. Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study.
Synopsis & Topics: Join UC Irvine professor Catherine Liu, economist Tim Jackson, and journalist David Goodhart as they debate how to build hope in a world that doesn't care.

Title: The collapse of the wave function
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Jacob Barandes, Alyssa Ney
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jacob Barandes is a Harvard University theoretical physicist and philosopher of science. His research explores the foundations of quantum theory, spacetime, and the nature of scientific explanation. Alyssa Ney is a philosopher at LMU Munich whose work reshapes how we think about reality through the lens of quantum mechanics. Specializing in the metaphysics of physics, she challenges deeply held assumptions about the nature of the universe and our place within it. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics.
Synopsis & Topics: Might 'the collapse of the wave function' be an Emperor's New Clothes phrase that describes precisely nothing? Does the failure to explain the mystery mean quantum mechanics isn’t our best fundamental theory after all? Or should we accept the weirdness and see it as an unbridgeable limit on our understanding? Watch Roger Penrose, Alyssa Ney and Jacob Barandes debate the topic.

Title: Democracy, gender, and the future of politics
Guests & Speakers: David Goodhart, Catherine Mayer, John Burn-Murdoch, Nicola Sturgeon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist, and the co-founder and president of the Women's Equality Party. Nicola Sturgeon is the former First Minister of Scotland and leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP), the first woman to hold both titles. John Burn-Murdoch is a columnist and the chief data reporter for the Financial Times, where he writes the weekly 'Data Points' column. David Goodhart is a journalist, author, and policy analyst. He founded Prospect magazine and later directed the think tank Demos. His books, including 'The Road to Somewhere', examine social divisions, work, and identity.
Synopsis & Topics: Join writer and activist, Catherine Mayer, former leader of the Scottish National Party, Nicola Sturgeon, chief data reporter for the Financial Times, John Burn-Murdoch, and founder of Prospect magazine, David Goodhart, as they debate recent trends in male/female voting patterns and the rise of populist politics.

Title: Beliefism: how to stop hating the people we disagree with
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is a British behavioural scientist and the Professor of Behavioural Science at the London School of Economics. His research and writing focus on how pleasure and purpose weave together in everyday life, arguing that happiness lies in what we do and attend to, not the grand narratives we tell ourselves. Dolan is the author of three widely acclaimed books: 'Happiness by Design', 'Happy Ever After', and 'Beliefism'. He combines rigorous academic analysis with accessible advice grounded in behavioural science.
Synopsis & Topics: Behavioural scientist Paul Dolan explains how, while we might like to think that we're tolerant, many of us struggle to engage with people whose opinions differ strongly from our own, even if they might have something useful to contribute to the debate.

Title: Reform UK's Richard Tice under fire: The philosophy of populist nationalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Tice is a businessman and politician. Since 2024, he has served as member of parliament for Boston and Skegness, as well as deputy leader of Reform UK, having previously been the chairman of the party from 2019 to 2021 and again briefly in 2024. Interviewed by Hilary Lawson. Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview with the IAI's editorial director, Hilary Lawson, deputy chairman of Reform Richard Tice argues his party's success comes from borrowing ideas from across the political spectrum to forge a new path.

Title: The rise and fall of identity politics
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Thangam Debbonaire, James Schneider
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Schneider is a journalist and political organiser currently serving as Communications Director for Progressive International. He previously served as Spokesperson and Head of Strategic Communications for Jeremy Corbyn. Myriam François is a trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. She is a former columnist at the New Statesman and a familiar face on the BBC, Channel 4, and Al Jazeera. Thangam Debbonaire was Labour MP for Bristol West and a senior member of Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. She now advises on culture, tech, and global policy, focusing on issues like migration, identity, and democracy. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: Is identity politics still a useful tool for the left? Or should the left return to a more traditional focus on economic and class issues?  Join political organiser James Schneider, journalist Myriam François, and political adviser Thangam Debbonaire as they debate the future of the left.

Title: Out of our minds
Guests & Speakers: Norman Ohler, Maria Balaet, Joanna Moncrieff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Maria Balaet is a leading psychedelics researcher and neuroscientist in the Department of Neuroimaging at King’s College London. Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, and a consultant psychiatrist for the NHS. Norman Ohler is an award-winning novelist and investigative journalist, best known for Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich, an explosive account of the Nazi regime’s covert use of psychedelics and stimulants.
Synopsis & Topics: Delve into the historical significance of psychoactive intoxicants across cultures. Discover their potential roles in spirituality, pleasure, and societal evolution.

Title: Organisms are processes, not things, with Wahida Khandker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Wahida Khandker is a senior lecturer in philosophy at Manchester Metropolitan University. Her research focuses on intersections between process and thought, particularly the work of Henri Bergson, and the philosophy of biology. Khandker currently also serves as co-chair of the Society for European Philosophy. Khandker is the author of two monographs, Philosophy, Animality, and the Life Sciences (2014) and Process Metaphysics and Mutative Life (2020).
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Wahida Khandker as she makes the case that we should abandon our traditional views about reality and view the world in terms of processes rather than objects.

Title: Draining the swamp
Guests & Speakers: David Goodhart, Richard Tice, Sherelle Jacobs
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Tice is a British businessman and politician, currently serving as the Deputy Leader of Reform UK and MP for Boston and Skegness. Sherelle Jacobs is Assistant Comment Editor at The Daily Telegraph, known for her bold columns on politics, culture, and identity. A former foreign correspondent, she brings a global lens to Britain’s evolving conservatism. David Goodhart is a British journalist and author, best known as the founder and former editor of Prospect magazine. His book The British Dream argues that high immigration can undermine national solidarity and social cohesion.
Synopsis & Topics: Does the Right need a powerful state to deliver its goals?  Or should the eradication of the state be its primary aim? Find out in this engaging debate.

Title: The struggle for the good life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Massimo Pigliucci is a renowned philosopher and professor at the City College of New York. He is the author of several books, including, 'How to be a Stoic' and 'Beyond Stoicism'. A former co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast and a self-proclaimed sceptic, Pigliucci is a champion of Enlightenment notions of reason and rationality.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Massimo Pigliucci in exploring the foundations of a fulfilling life. Learn how pleasure, character, and purpose lead to genuine contentment.

Title: Why politics, not the internet, should be the focus of feminism with Catherine Mayer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist and the co-founder and President of the Women's Equality Party. She started her career in journalism at The Economist. She then went on to be FOCUS's London-based correspondent. She later joined TIME as a senior editor, becoming the London Bureau Chief, the Europe Editor and, finally, Editor at Large. She was the founding Executive Director of the think tank Datum Future and has also co-founded the Primadonna Festival, which debuted in 2019. She is the author of Attack of the 50ft Women, Amortality: The Pleasures and Perils of Living Agelessly and Charles: The Heart of A King, a political biography of the King Charles that made headlines across the world in 2015. Her upcoming works include TIME/LIFE, her first novel, and Send Them Victorious: Royal Women, Their Battles and Why We Should Care.
Synopsis & Topics: Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist and the co-founder and President of the Women's Equality Party. She started her career in journalism at The Economist, and later joined TIME where she worked her way up to become the Editor at Large. In this interview she discusses feminism and the ways in which online culture can polarise people.

Title: The future of entanglement
Guests & Speakers: Tim Maudlin, Ivette Fuentes, Jacob Barandes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jacob Barandes is a Harvard University theoretical physicist and philosopher of science. His research explores the foundations of quantum theory, spacetime, and the nature of scientific explanation. Ivette Fuentes is a physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. Her work and previous collaborations with Roger Penrose considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher of science, Tim Maudlin, theoretical physicists Jacob A. Barandes and Ivette Fuentes as they debate the future of quantum mechanics and explore the evidence for reality being non-local.

Title: Einstein's biggest blunder with Claudia de Rham
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist based at Imperial College London, who works on cutting-edge research at the interface of gravity, cosmology and particle physics. In 2020 she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for revitalizing the theory of massive gravity.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, physicist Claudia de Rham explores the cosmological constant, Einstein’s “greatest blunder.” Probing why quantum vacuum fluctuations don’t overwhelm cosmic expansion, she asks whether relativity breaks on vast scales, if gravitons have mass, and how gravity shapes our evolving understanding of the universe.

Title: After postmodernism
Guests & Speakers: Robin Van den Akker, Abby Innes, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Robin van den Akker is Senior Lecturer in the Philosophy of Culture. He is a leading scholar of Metamodernism and founding editor of Notes on Metamodernism. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism.
Synopsis & Topics:
"Hugely influential in the latter decades of the 20th century, postmodernism transformed many academic disciplines and culture at large. Associated with an attack on objective truth and the uniqueness of meaning, it called into question the whole edifice of knowledge which Western culture had previously glorified. But it left many lost, and in the wake of a polarising post-truth world, there is a widespread recognition that we need to move on. Feminist and post-colonial critics though claim there is a danger that instead we risk retreating to the questionable certainties of the past. Alongside defenders of objective truth like Richard Dawkins and Noam Chomsky, figures like Jordan Peterson argue for a return to moral certainties and belief in the existence of God.  

Are there viable alternatives to postmodernism that are not simply a return to belief in universal truth? Are metamodernism or model-theoretic realism possible ways forward? Or is the chaos initiated by postmodernism so profound that the only credible approach is to return to the Enlightenment notion that we can arrive at the objective truth?"

Title: The new world order and the fight for democracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Malcolm Rifkind is the former UK Foreign Secretary. He was one of only five ministers to serve throughout the whole Prime Ministerships of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major. In 1997, he was knighted in recognition of his public service. Rifkind also served as Chairman of the Standards & Privileges Committee from 2009 to 2010, and as the UK’s representative to the Eminent Persons Group from 2010 to 2011. He also served as chairman of the Intelligence and Security Committee from 2010 to 2015. Roger Hearing hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former UK Foreign Secretary, Malcolm Rifkind, as he analyses the state of modern geopolitics, tackling issues like the war in Ukraine, autocracy in China, and the early months of the new Trump administration.

Title: Trouble with temptation
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the LSE. His main research interests are human behaviour and happiness, and the relationships between them, particularly as they apply to policy. Jordan Stephens is a musician and author. He is one-half of the chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, and recently released his first novel, 'Avoidance, Drugs, Heartbreak and Dogs'.
Synopsis & Topics: We are all tempted by short-term pleasures. But, as Ancient Greek philosopher Epicurus counselled, pleasure can be so much more than simply giving into temptation. Join Jordan Stephens, one-half of the chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, for an intimate interview on how giving into short-term desires is not only destructive to our health but also to our creativity.

Title: The unconscious mind
Guests & Speakers: Barbara Tversky, Edward Harcourt, Josh Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Josh Cohen is a distinguished academic in American literature and critical theory, as well as a trained psychoanalyst. Barbara Tversky is an active Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. Edward Harcourt is a philosopher at the University of Oxford, where he researches ethics, the philosophy of mind, and Wittgenstein.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychoanalyst Josh Cohen, philosopher Edward Harcourt, and psychologist Barbara Tversky discuss whether or not the unconscious is real, and its importance as a concept.

Title: Stranger than fiction
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary Ann Sieghart is a distinguished journalist and the author of The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men, and What We Can Do About It. Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist and the co-founder and was the President of the Women's Equality Party. She started her career in journalism, writing for The Economist, FOCUS and TIME.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Catherine Mayer and Mary Ann Sieghart as they debate how science fiction can shed light on our present political reality.

Title: The untold power of small states with former Armenian President
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Armen Vardani Sarkissian is an Armenian politician, physicist, investor, businessman, and computer scientist who served as the 4th president of Armenia from 2018 to 2022. He also served as Prime Minister of Armenia from 1996 to 1997. He was the first president of post-Soviet Armenia born in former Armenian SSR.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview with the former President of Armenia, Armen Sarkissian argues that small states have tremendous advantages to carve out niches. As a former quantum physicist, Armen outlines his theory of quantum geopolitics and argues small, smart states have the power to dominate the 21st century.

Title: The politics of populism
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Maté, Jesse Norman, Lionel Shriver
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lionel Shriver is a bestselling author and outspoken commentator known for tackling incendiary themes in both fiction and public debate. Her novel We Need to Talk About Kevin won the Orange Prize for Fiction in 2005. Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his incisive analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics. Jesse Norman is a distinguished British politician, author, and academic. Serving as the MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010, he currently is Shadow Leader of the House of Commons. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Lionel Shriver, Aaron Maté, Jesse Norman in this video as they debate the politics of populism.

Title: Hacking our way out of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roman Vladimirovich Yampolskiy is a Latvian computer scientist at the University of Louisville, known for his work on behavioral biometrics, security of cyberworlds, and artificial intelligence safety. He holds a PhD from the University at Buffalo (2008). He is currently the director of Cyber Security Laboratory in the department of Computer Engineering and Computer Science at the Speed School of Engineering. Yampolskiy is an author of some 100 publications, including numerous books.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading computer scientist Roman Yampolskiy as he argues that if we are living in a simulation, we can also hack our way out of it.

Title: Reason, replication and reality with John Ioannidis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ioannidis is a Greek-American physician, scientist and writer. He is a Professor of Medicine, Epidemiology and Population Health, and Biomedical Data Science at Stanford University. His research focuses on evidence-based medicine, clinical research and the study of scientific research itself. Not only has Ioannidis served on the editorial board of over twenty scientific journals, but his 2005 essay "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False" was the most-viewed article in the history of the Public Library of Science, with over 3 million views.
Synopsis & Topics:
In 2005, John Ioannidis published an essay titled "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False," now the most accessed article in the history of the Public Library of Science.
Join Ioannidis for a wide-ranging interview covering his work and whether he believes there is a crisis in the sciences.

Title: The diagnosis delusion
Guests & Speakers: Gina Rippon, Alastair Santhouse, Karsten Juhl Jørgensen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Karsten Juhl Jørgensen is a leading medical researcher and professor at the University of Southern Denmark, known for challenging the idea that more tests mean better care. He’s a bold voice exposing the hidden harms of overdiagnosis and overscreening. Gina Rippon, Emeritus Professor of Cognitive Neuroimaging, is a trailblazing neuroscientist debunking brain-gender myths. Author of The Gendered Brain and The Lost Girls of Autism, she uses cutting-edge science to expose long-ignored truths. Alastair Santhouse is a leading consultant psychiatrist and former President of the Psychiatry Section at the Royal Society. Author of No More Normal, he is a sharp critic of the over-diagnosis trend in mental health today. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
Synopsis & Topics: How do we solve the overdiagnosis crisis? Join Karsten Juhl Jørgensen, Gina Rippon, Alastair Santhouse as they debate the philosophy of medicine.

Title: The seduction of advertising
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. Founding director of the Centre for the Study of Senses, Barry C Smith has created a platform for collaborative research between philosophers, psychologists and neuroscientists.
Synopsis & Topics: Join the founding director of the Centre for the Study of the Senses, Barry C. Smith, to explore the philosophy of advertising and how our senses are used against us.

Title: Kith, kin, and the birthrate crisis
Guests & Speakers: Harvey Whitehouse, Sophie Scott-Brown, David Goodhart
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Harvey Whitehouse is a Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford. He is the author of 'Inheritance: The Evolutionary Origins of the Modern World'. David Goodhart is a journalist, author, and policy analyst. He founded Prospect magazine and later directed the think tank Demos. Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian with research interests in Anarchism and modern European political thought. She is a Research Fellow at the University of St Andrews. Matthew Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Harvey Whitehouse, David Goodhart, Sophie Scott-Brown as they debate the future of childhood and parenting.

Title: Yanis Varoufakis on the end of capitalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yanis Varoufakis is a leading critic of the economic establishment. He was the former Finance Minister of Greece, a professor, bestselling author, and current chair of the Democracy in Europe Movement 2025. Interviewed by the host of The Why Curve podcast and BBC presenter Roger Hearing?
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Yanis covers the method behind Donald Trump, how Trump's understanding of global power makes some sense, whether a trade war with China can be won, and the massive opportunity Europe is about to miss.

Title: A landscape of consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. Kuhn has published over 30 books and is also a commentator on the BBC, CNN, CCTV, and Bloomberg as a trusted expert on China. Most recently, and what we’re discussing today, Robert released a paper, 'A landscape of consciousness', in which he chronicled over 200 theories of consciousness.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Closer to Truth's Robert Lawrence Kuhn as he surveys the possible answers, material and non-material, to the perennial question of consciousness.

Title: The Taiwan tripwire
Guests & Speakers: Malcolm Rifkind, Isabel Hilton, Bill Hayton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major, most famously in the roles of Foreign and Defense Secretary. Isabel Hilton is a renowned international relations expert, journalist and broadcaster. She is the founder of China Dialogue. Bill Hayton is a distinguished former BBC journalist and Chatham House associate fellow. He is the author of four books on Asia. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Malcolm Rifkind, Isabel Hilton, and Bill Hayton as they debate the future of US-China relations and the fate of Taiwan.

Title: The limits of nothingness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join philosopher Peter van Inwagen as he explores the metaphysics of 'nothing' in modern physics.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Peter van Inwagen as he explores the metaphysics of 'nothing' in modern physics.

Title: Indian philosophy and the search for unity with Jessica Frazier
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies. During her academic career, she has explored key philosophical themes across various cultures, ranging from Indian concepts of Being to 20th century phenomenology. In addition, Frazier is the founding editor of the 'Journal of Hindu Studies' and a frequent contributor to BBC radio.
Synopsis & Topics: In our everyday lives we act as though we are all separate individuals, but is this really the case? Jessica Frazier argues reality is ultimately unified. She argues this philosophy can change the way we view the world.

Title: Žižek: "Trump did what The Left couldn't"
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. Foreign Policy named Žižek a Top 100 Global Thinker "for giving voice to an era of absurdity”.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Slavoj Žižek, the man who has been called "the most dangerous philosopher in the West," who argues that the only progress we can hope for, will be found when we hit rock bottom, and only then will a path forward be possible.

Title: The worst prediction in the history of science
Guests & Speakers: Claudia de Rham, Bjørn Ekeberg, Raphael Bousso
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist based at Imperial College London, who works on cutting-edge research at the interface of gravity, cosmology, and particle physics. In 2020, she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for revitalizing the theory of massive gravity. Raphael Bousso is Professor and The Chancellor's Chair in Physics at UC Berkeley, where he researches theoretical cosmology and quantum gravity. He was elected Fellow of the American Physical Society "for fundamental discoveries in the field of quantum cosmology." Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose work focuses on the limits of scientific knowledge, challenging the standard model of cosmology by probing some of the biggest inconsistencies and mysteries in science today. Jacob Barandes hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Claudia de Rham, Raphael Bousso, Bjørn Ekeberg as they debates the cosmological constant problem and the future of dark energy?

Title: How neoliberalism broke economics with Abby Innes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Abby Innes is Associate Professor of Political Economy at the European Institute, London School of Economics. Her research focuses on state theory, post-communist transitions, and the political economy of the UK. She is the author of Late Soviet Britain: Why Materialist Utopias Fail. Interviewed by Harry Carlisle.
Synopsis & Topics: In this IAI Studio interview, political economist and LSE associate professor Abby Innes  explores how the UK’s embrace of managerialism and economic determinism has produced a system that promises technical neutrality but delivers ideological rigidity.

Title: Psychedelics, Nazi Germany, and the CIA
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Norman Ohler is an award-winning novelist and investigative journalist, best known for 'Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich', an explosive account of the Nazi regime’s covert use of psychedelics and stimulants.
Synopsis & Topics: Join New York Times bestselling author, Norman Ohler as he makes the controversial case for hidden connections between the Nazis, the CIA’s LSD brainwashing experimentation programme, MKUltra, and today's so-called psychedelic renaissance.

Title: Unmasking the mind
Guests & Speakers: John Ioannidis, David Yeager, Nick Brown
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nick Brown, a Cambridge-trained engineer, began studying psychology in his 50s and is known for debunking the "positivity ratio." His critiques have appeared in The Guardian, Science, and more. John Ioannidis, a Stanford professor, is known for his work on evidence-based medicine and research integrity. His 2005 essay Why Most Published Research Findings Are False has over 3 million views. David Yeager, a UT Austin psychology professor, studies brief interventions that shape adolescent behavior. Featured in major media, he authored 10 to 25 and teaches the MasterClass The Power of Mindset. Hosted by the editor of the New Humanist, Niki Seth-Smith
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nick Brown, John Ioannidis, David Yeager as they debate whether science can truly understand the workings of the mind, and solve the hard problem of consciousness.

Title: After the West
Guests & Speakers: Yanis Varoufakis, Zoe Strimpel, S. Y. Quraishi, Cenk Uygur
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Finance Minister of Greece and bestselling author Yanis Varoufakis, political commentator and host of The Young Turks, Cenk Uygur, former Chief Election Commissioner of India S.Y. Quraishi, historian, columnist, and author Zoe Strimpel, and others clash over the future of global power. Hosted by philosopher Hilary Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Yanis Varoufakis, Cenk Uygur, S.Y. Quraishi, Zoe Strimpel as they debate the end of the West's geopolitical dominance.

Title: Evolutionary psychology is a failure, with Subrena Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Subrena Smith is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of New Hampshire. She works at the intersection of biology and psychology, where she focuses on topics about human behaviour. Interviewed by Nour Khairi.
Synopsis & Topics: evolutionary psychology, philosophy, biology, evolution, race

Title: Crisis in the academy
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Liu, Yaron Brook, Eric Kaufmann
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yaron Brook is a political scientist, and chairman of the Ayn Rand Institute. He’s a bestselling author and the host of The Yaron Brook Show. Catherine Liu is a Professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine. She’s the author of Virtue Hoarders: The Case against the Professional Managerial Class Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham. He’s the author of Taboo and Whiteshift: Immigration, Populism and the Future of White Majorities. Jay Shapiro hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Catherine Liu, Yaron Brook, and Eric Kaufmann in this exciting video, where they debate the crisis in academia.

Title: Physics without numbers
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Tim Maudlin as he explores that question through the lens of quantum dynamics, arguing that the appearance of complex numbers in Schrödinger’s equation is not arbitrary, but motivated by the need for a particular kind of wave-like structure in fundamental dynamics.

Title: Human nature and the possibility of utopia
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author and celebrated speaker. He is the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor Emeritus of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading psychologist and author of Against Empathy, Paul Bloom, as he argues that human nature makes true utopia impossible.

Title: Consciousness in the clouds
Guests & Speakers: Massimo Pigliucci, Anders Sandberg, Nadine Dijkstra, Roman Yampolskiy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nadine Dijkstra is a Senior Research Fellow at the Wellcome Centre for Human Neuroimaging at UCL and leads the Imagine Reality Lab. Her research focuses on computational and neural mechanisms of mental imagery. Roman Yampolskiy is a professor and computer scientist at the University of Louisville who specialises in artificial intelligence, AI safety, digital forensics and behavioural biometrics. Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. Massimo Pigliucci is an Italian-American philosopher and biologist specialising in evolutionary biology and the philosophy of science. His recent work focuses on Stoicism. Hosted by mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer and author, Shini Somara.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nadine Dijkstra, Roman Yampolskiy, Anders Sandberg, and Massimo Pigliucci as they debate the reality of uploading consciousness.

Title: The Russia hoax
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics. He has contributed to various outlets, including The Nation, RealClearPolitics, and Grayzone News, where he serves as a senior writer.
Synopsis & Topics: Join left-wing journalist Aaron Maté as he argues that Russiagate was a falsehood perpetrated by the leadership of both political parties that directly led to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Title: The case for radical feminism with Finn Mackay
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, leading feminist activity Finn Mackay, explores the core ideas of radical feminism and challenges gender norms in a reactive patriarchal society.

Title: The US dollar and the future of the world
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, David McWilliams, Rana Mitter
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David McWilliams is a prominent Irish economist, author, broadcaster, and public intellectual. He has worked for the Irish Central Bank and famously predicted the 2008 financial crisis. He is also a columnist, author, festival organiser and podcaster. Janne Teller was formerly a UN macroeconomist specialising in developing economies. She has since become a bestselling author of novels, essays, and short stories. Hosted by Harvard's Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Join economist David McWilliams, writer Janne Teller, and historian Rana Mitter as they debate the past, present, and future role of the US Dollar.

Title: The mind-body problem and animal consciousness, with Peter Godfrey-Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Godfrey-Smith is a philosopher of science and a leading thinker on the evolution of consciousness and animal minds. He is a professor at the University of Sydney and the author of several acclaimed books, including Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness and Metazoa: Animal Life and the Birth of the Mind . His work combines philosophy, biology, and firsthand experience with marine animals to explore how subjective experience arises in the natural world. Through his research and writing, Godfrey-Smith offers a compelling naturalistic account of the mind that bridges science and philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: In this IAI Studio interview, philosopher and science writer Peter Godfrey-Smith explores the evolution of consciousness and the enduring mystery of the mind–body problem

Title: White holes are a mathematical fantasy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Sudarsky is a Professor of Theoretical Physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) and a Professor at the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics.
Synopsis & Topics: In this illuminating talk, theoretical physicist Daniel Sudarsky explores the intriguing idea of white holes, spacetime objects predicted by Einstein’s equations yet absent from our observations.

Title: The normal and the abnormal
Guests & Speakers: Bessel van der Kolk, Rose Cartwright, Frank Tallis, Dinesh Bhugra
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rose Cartwright is a writer for the Netflix hit show 3 Body Problem, she is a mental health advocate and author of a book on mental health, The Maps We Carry. Frank Tallis is a multi-award winning clinical psychologist and author, his latest book is The Act of Living: What the Great Psychologists Can Teach Us About Surviving Discontent in an Age of Anxiety. Dinesh Bhugra is the former President of the World Psychiatric Association and Professor of Mental Health and Cultural Diversity at King's College London. Bessel van der Kolk is a psychiatrist and expert in the field of trauma therapy. He is the author of the bestselling book The Body Keeps The Score. Hosted by Barry Smith.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Rose Cartwright, Frank Tallis, Dinesh Bhugra, and Bessel van der Kolk as they explore the philosophy of mental health in this engaging video debate.

Title: The theory of everything is a mirage
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jo Dunkley is a distinguished astrophysicist and Professor of Physics at Princeton University, working on major international projects including the Atacama Cosmology Telescope and Simons Observatory, which focus on measuring the earliest observable light in the universe. Her contributions have been recognised with numerous accolades, such as the Maxwell Medal and the Rosalind Franklin Award and she has recently been elected a fellow of the Royal Society. Dunkley works on uncovering evidence of "inflation" in our early universe and furthering our understanding of the big "tensions" in cosmology and dark matter.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Princeton cosmologist, Jo Dunkley, as she argues we will never fully comprehend the mystery of what is out there.

Title: The new surveillance culture
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Judith Donath is a writer, designer and artist whose work focuses on the co-evolution of technology and society. She has published numerous articles about social media, AI, ethics and anonymity, and is the author of The Social Machine: Designs for Living Online (MIT Press). As the former director of the MIT Media Lab's Sociable Media Group, she and her students designed innovative interfaces for on-line communities; their art projects examining the future of identity, privacy and mediated life have been exhibited in museums and galleries worldwide. Currently, she is a faculty fellow at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center and is writing a book about technology, trust and deception.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Harvard computer scientist and author, Judith Donath, as she argues that while many technologies promote themselves on the basis of trust, like Airbnb and Uber, they in fact replace it, with surveillance and control.

Title: The rules of war
Guests & Speakers: Malcolm Rifkind, Bronwen Maddox, Yanis Varoufakis, Jeremy Corbyn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020. Bronwen Maddox is the Director and Chief Executive of Chatham House.Yanis Varoufakis is a world-renowned economist, academic, and politician who rose to international prominence in 2015 as Greece's Minister of Finance. Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major, most famously in the roles of Foreign and Defence Secretary. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: "In times of war, the law falls silent" declared Cicero. Join Jeremy Corbyn, Bronwen Maddox, Yanis Varoufakis, and Malcolm Rifkind as they debate the rules of war.

Title: The fantasies of Descartes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Antonio Damasio is an award-winning neuroscientist known for his pioneering work on emotions, intuitions and the biological origins of consciousness. He is the author of several books including Descartes' Error and The Strange Order of Things. His most recent book Feeling & Knowing: Making Minds Conscious explores the origin and evolution of consciousness.
Synopsis & Topics: We tend to believe consciousness is purely mental. And since Descartes' "I think therefore I am", we've privileged the mind as the centrepiece of thought and consciousness. But such a view is mistaken argues award-winning neuroscientist Antonio Damasio.

Title: The politics of beauty
Guests & Speakers: Simon May, Jessica DeFino, Janne Teller
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica DeFino is an award-winning reporter and beauty culture critic. Her work sheds light on the negative impacts of the beauty industry. Simon May is a Visiting Professor of Philosophy at King's College London. May's most recent book, Love: A New Understanding of an Ancient Emotion, proposes a wholly new theory on the nature of love. Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller’s work explores existential themes and ethical questions of life and civilization. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Jessica DeFino, Simoy May, Janne Teller as they debate the politics of beauty.

Title: David Deutsch on the foundations of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Deutsch is a theoretical physicist best known as the founding father of quantum computation and as a key figure and advocate for the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics. Deutsch is a Visiting Professor of physics at the Centre for Quantum Computation and the Clarendon Laboratory, Oxford University. Interviewed by Charlie Barnett, Senior Producer at the IAI.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview, leading physicist David Deutsch explains the philosophy behind the many-worlds interpretation and argues that not only is it the best interpretation of quantum mechanics – it is the only interpretation.

Title: The equality dream
Guests & Speakers: Vicky Pryce, Tommy J. Curry, John Bercow
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Bercow is one of the most recognisable and iconoclastic figures in British politics. As Speaker of the House of Commons from 2009 to 2019, his distinctive bellow for order spanned the tenure of four Prime Ministers and a decade of political turmoil. Tommy J. Curry holds a Personal Chair in Africana philosophy and Black Male studies at the University of Edinburgh. Vicky Pryce is a British economist and a former Joint Head of the United Kingdom's Government Economic Service. Isabel Hilton hosts
Synopsis & Topics: Join John Bercow, Tommy J. Curry, and Vicky Pryce as they debate one of the toughest problems in modern politics: the pursuit of equality.

Title: The two party system is over with Carla Denyer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carla Denyer is co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales, selected along with Adrian Ramsay in October 2021. Carla is the MP for Bristol Central.
Synopsis & Topics: Co-leader of the Green Party, Carla Denyer, joins us to explore the realities of parliamentary success, the limitations of current political models, and the importance of holding on to both climate and social justice.

Title: Imagining the unimaginable
Guests & Speakers: Simon Baron-Cohen, Martha Fiennes, Joanna Kavenna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Film-maker and Director Martha Fiennes, professor of developmental psychopathology Simon Baron-Cohen, and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna, debate whether the imagination is limited. Hosted by Myriam François.
Synopsis & Topics: Join film-maker and director Martha Fiennes, professor of developmental psychopathology Simon Baron-Cohen, and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna, debate whether the imagination is limited. Hosted by Myriam François.

Title: Competition destroys collective intelligence
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Liv Boeree is an educator and researcher specializing in the intersection of game theory, technology and risk. She is also one of the UK's most successful poker players, winning multiple championship titles during her professional career. In 2014 she co-founded the charity movement Raising for Effective Giving, and today continues her work in the area as an ambassador for Longview Philanthropy. Liv also hosts the Win-Win Podcast.
Synopsis & Topics: In this wide-ranging interview, science communicator and poker champion Liv Boeree talks about the effect AI will have not only on our societies but our ability to think.

Title: Truth, science, and reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ioannidis is a physician, scientist and writer as well as a professor at Stanford University. He is the author of Why Most Published Research Findings Are False. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and long-standing critic of realism, best known for his theory of closure. Hosted by Imperial College London Material Physicist Jess Wade.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Stanford professor John Ioannidis and post-realist philosopher, Hilary Lawson to explore the problematic relationship between science, truth and reality, and what it means for our understanding of the world.

Title: The quantum unknown
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sabine Hossenfelder is a ground-breaking physicist, the creator of the YouTube channel "Science without the gobbledygook", and a New York Times best-selling author. Matt O'Dowd is an astrophysicist and the host of PBS Space Time. He is also Professor of Physics and Astronomy at City University of New York.
Synopsis & Topics: Join science communicators and physicists Sabine Hossenfelder and Matt O'Dowd in conversation, on how we might go about finding answers to the quantum puzzle, and what this means for the future of quantum theory.

Title: The journey in search of a destination
Guests & Speakers: Sandra Laugier, Frank Tallis, Babette Babich, Jonathan Webber
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Parisian philosopher Sandra Laugier, Nietzschian philosopher Babette Babich, clinical psychologist Frank Tallis, and author of Rethinking Existentialism Jonathan Webber debate the purpose of life. Hosted by Jack Symes.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Sandra Laugier, Babette Babich, Frank Tallis, and Jonathan Webber as they debate whether we should have goals in life.

Title: The making and unmaking of humanity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Harvey Whitehouse as he discusses how we got here and what can do to harness these evolved biases for good.

Title: What is wrong with history and how to change it
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philippa Gregory CBE is a renowned writer and author of historical fiction. She is best known for The Other Boleyn Girl (2001), which was adapted into two films and in 2002 won the Romantic Novel of the Year Award from the Romantic Novelists' Association.
Synopsis & Topics: Join one of the world’s leading historical novelists, Philippa Gregory, as she reveals the importance of ordinary people in determining the course of history.

Title: The future of money, with Gary Stevenson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Gary Stevenson is a British economist, former financial trader, and YouTuber known for his economic analysis and activism against economic inequality. Interviewed by Abby Innes, an Associate Professor of Political Economy in the European Institute at the LSE. She is the author of Czechoslovakia: The Short Goodbye (Yale University Press, 2001) and Late Soviet Britain: Why Materialist Utopias Fail (Cambridge University Press, 2023).
Synopsis & Topics: Join former top trader Gary Stevenson for an in-depth conversation on why the powerful often gain increasingly more power, and how we can restructure our economy and society to prevent this.

Title: The good, the bad, and the beautiful
Guests & Speakers: Babette Babich, Sarah Wilson, Ankhi Mukherjee, Paul Ernest
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Babette Babich is a philosopher of technology and science. She is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City. Ankhi Mukherjee is a Professor of English and World Literatures at Oxford University. She is the author of several books and is currently writing A Very Short Introduction to Postcolonial Literature, forthcoming with Oxford University Press. Paul Ernest is Emeritus professor of the philosophy of mathematics education at the University of Exeter. He is best known for his work on philosophical aspects of mathematics education and his contributions to developing a social constructivist philosophy of mathematics. Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan magazine Australia at 29 and founded the global I Quit Sugar movement. Hosted by British mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer, and author, Shini Somara
Synopsis & Topics: Join Babette Babich, Ankhi Mukherjee, Paul Ernest, and Sarah Wilson as they debate the philosophy of beauty.

Title: The forgotten crimes of war with Christina Lamb
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Christina Lamb is Chief Foreign Correspondent for The Times and Sunday Times. She is one of Britain’s leading foreign correspondents and a bestselling author.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview with Christina Lamb, Chief Foreign Correspondent for The Times and Sunday Times, she uncovers the hidden brutality of sexual violence in war, how this violence can make them outcasts in their own communities, and her experiences in conflicts around the globe.

Title: Capitalism and the end of innovation
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ali Abdul-Amir Allawi was Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. An Iraqi politician and scholar, he served in those positions from May 2020 to August 2022. He resigned from the post of finance minister on August 16, 2022 due to the deteriorating political situation in Iraq.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former Finance Minister of Iraq, Ali Allawi, as he argues our global economic framework has begun to prevent development.

Title: The essential philosophy of fun
Guests & Speakers: Freya India, James Tartaglia, Myriam François
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist and filmmaker Myriam François, author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life James Tartaglia, and the mind behind the Substack GIRLS , Freya India, debate the philosophy of fun. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Journalist and filmmaker Myriam François, author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life James Tartaglia, and the mind behind the Substack Girls Freya India, as they debate the philosophy of fun. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.

Title: Medicine, magic, and misunderstanding
Guests & Speakers: Bessel van der Kolk, John Ioannidis, Gina Rippon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of the highly influential paper, 'Why Most Published Research Findings are False', John Ioannidis, award-winning neuroscientist and feminist, Gina Rippon, and psychiatrist and groundbreaking author of 'The Body Keeps The Score', Bessel van der Kolk, debate whether we truly know what health and illness are. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
Synopsis & Topics: Join author of 'Why Most Published Research Findings are False' John Ioannidis, award-winning neuroscientist Gina Rippon, and psychiatrist and groundbreaking author of 'The Body Keeps The Score' Bessel van der Kolk as they debate whether we truly know what health and illness are. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.

Title: The mindful body with Ellen Langer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ellen Langer is Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and the author of The Mindful Body. Among other honours, she is the recipient of three distinguished scientist awards, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and the Liberty Science Genius Award. She is widely known as the mother of mindfulness.
Synopsis & Topics: Join renowned Harvard psychologist and mindfulness expert Ellen Langer, she explores the transformative power of mindfulness in our daily lives.

Title: We misunderstand mental health
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rose Cartwright is a trailblazing screenwriter, author, and mental health advocate. She is the writer of the Netflix hit show 3 Body Problem, and is also widely known for her 2016 memoir Pure, which detailed her experiences living with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Beyond her writing, Cartwright is an outspoken voice raising awareness about OCD and challenging the stigma surrounding it. She is also the co-founder of the mental health non-profit Made of Millions.
Synopsis & Topics: Join screenwriter, author and mental health advocate Rose Cartwright as she explores the common misunderstandings we have around mental health.

Title: Francis Fukuyama on why he was surprised by Trump's foreign policy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Francis Fukuyama is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar. He is most famous for his work The End of History and the Last Man which argues that liberal democracy and free-market capitalism are the final stages of humanity's political evolution.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Francis Fukuyama for this exclusive interview as he reveals whether he still stands by his famous argument in The End of History in light of recent events.

Title: Rupert Sheldrake in conversation with Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is an English scientist whose research into parapsychology and evolution led to the theory of morphic resonance, expounded in the book A New Science of Life. The theory posits that "memory is inherent in nature" which makes it possible for "telepathy-type interconnections between organisms." Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is Editorial Director of the IAI.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Rupert Sheldrake and Hilary Lawson for this fiery conversation where they explore the world of parapsychology, the limits of science, and wonders of consciousness.

Title: Nadhim Zahawi: The boy from Baghdad
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nadhim Zahawi is a British politician who served in various ministerial positions under Prime Ministers Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, and Rishi Sunak from 2018 to 2023. He most recently served as Chairman of the Conservative Party and Minister without Portfolio from 25 October 2022 until January 2023. As a member of the Conservative Party, he was Member of Parliament for Stratford-on-Avon from 2010 to 2024.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nadhim Zahawi in this engaging talk as he charts his journey from a young boy fleeing Iraq to his work in the beating heart of British politics.

Title: White Holes: Fact or Fantasy?
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Carlo Rovelli, Laura Mersini-Houghton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carlo Rovelli is a leading theoretical physicist and the author of 'White Holes'. Laura Mersini-Houghton is a pre-eminent physicist at the University of North Carolina and the author of 'Before The Big Bang: The origin of the universe and what lies beyond'. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematical physicist and philosopher of science. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 2020 for his work on black holes. Robert Lawrence Kuhn hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are white holes a mathematical fantasy? Or like black holes might we come to see them as an essential element of the universe? Join Carlo Rovelli, Roger Penrose and Laura Mersini-Haughton as they debate the most exotic objects in the cosmos.

Title: Why more is less
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Barry Schwartz is an American psychologist and the Dorwin Cartwright Emeritus Professor of Social Theory and Social Action at Swarthmore College. He is author of several famous books including Why We Work and The Paradox of Choice. Schwartz is famous for his insight that too much choice paradoxically limits freedom.
Synopsis & Topics: Join author of The Paradox of Choice, Barry Schwartz, as he argues that having more and more freedom can lead us to be psychologically overloaded and unsatisfied,

Title: Having it all
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Claire Provost, Vicky Pryce
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media. He is the author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism and an upcoming book on the aging crisis. Claire Provost is an investigative journalist and co-founder and co-director of the non-profit Institute for Journalism and Social Change. Vicky Pryce is an economist and the Chief Economic Advisor and Board Member at the Centre for Economics and Business Research. She is the former Joint Head of the UK's Government Economic Service. Roger Hearing presents the BBC World Service's Business Matters and World Business Report. He formerly presented Bloomberg Radio and BBC Radio 4's The World Tonight.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Aaron Bastani, Claire Provost, and Vicky Pryce as they debate the reality of womens lives today.

Title: The psychology behind the culture wars
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Andrew Gold is a YouTuber and former BBC Presenter who writes about the culture wars and cultish ideologies. He is the author of The Psychology of Secrets and creator of the Heretics YouTube Channel.
Synopsis & Topics: Join documentary filmmaker and former BBC Presenter Andrew Gold as he argues that same the psychology of belief exploited by cult leaders also affects mainstream organisations on both sides of the political divide.

Title: Therapy, psychedelics, and why the body keeps the score, with Bessel van der Kolk
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bessel van der Kolk is one of the world’s leading experts on trauma. A pioneering psychiatrist and author of the groundbreaking bestseller The Body Keeps the Score, he has spent over 50 years researching how trauma reshapes both body and brain. His work has revolutionized our understanding of psychological suffering, showing that trauma is not limited to soldiers or those in extreme situations, but is a far more common and deeply human experience.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Bessel van der Kolk explores how trauma is imprinted on the body as well as  the crucial role of language, not only as a tool for making sense of the world but as a foundation for human connection and healing.

Title: A world without values
Guests & Speakers: Dale Turner, Janne Teller, Robin Van den Akker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dale Turner, Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and Centre for Indigenous Studies at the University of Toronto, Janne Teller, critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays and short stories, and Robin van den Akker, Senior Lecturer in the Philosophy of Culture at Erasmus University College Rotterdam, debate the values that govern our lives, and whether they are universal.
Synopsis & Topics: Join political scientist Dale Turner, novelist Janne Teller, and philosopher Robin van der Akker as they debate the meaning of values.

Title: Darwin vs consciousness
Guests & Speakers: Stuart Hameroff, Denis Noble, Antonella Tramacere
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Stuart Hameroff is an American anesthesiologist and professor at the University of Arizona. He is known for his controversial and creative theories on the quantum origin of consciousness. Antonella Tramacere is an expert in the philosophy of cognition and neuroscience. She is an assistant professor at the Department of Philosophy, Communication and Performance at Roma Tre in Rome. Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford University. He is known for his ground-breaking work in biology and physiology. Hosted by Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Stuart Hameroff, Antonella Tramacere, and Denis Noble as they debate the relationship between consciousness and evolution. Güneş Taylor hosts.

Title: The return of empire
Guests & Speakers: Gideon Rachman, Juliet Samuel, Robert Kaplan, Francis Fukuyama
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Leading journalist and foreign policy analyst, Robert Kaplan, author of The End of History? Francis Fukuyama, chief foreign affairs commentator of the Financial Times, Gideon Rachman, and Times and Telegraph columnist Juliet Samuel lock horns over the future of Europe and the West.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading journalist and foreign policy analyst, Robert Kaplan, author of The End of History? Francis Fukuyama, chief foreign affairs commentator of the Financial Times, Gideon Rachman, and Times and Telegraph columnist Juliet Samuel lock horns over the future of Europe and the West.

Title: Nietzsche, the birth of tragedy, and the technology trap with Babette Babich
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Babette Babich is a leading philosopher of technology and science. Renowned for her exploration of the philosophy, history, and sociology of science as well as studies of ecology and animal philosophy, Babich is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City. Her work crosses the analytic-continental divide, drawing heavily on Nietzsche, Heidegger, Adorno, and Illich. She is the director of The Nietzsche Society. Her latest book, Günther Anders’ Philosophy of Technology, explores the philosophy of isolation.
Synopsis & Topics: World renowned Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University in New York Babette Babich discusses Nietzsche, the importance of tragedy, and the danger of technology interfering with our judgement.

Title: AI and the story of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Marika Taylor is Professor of Theoretical Physics and Pro-Vice Chancellor and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences, University of Birmingham. She completed her doctorate at Cambridge University under the supervision of Stephen Hawking and her research ranges from exploring the frontiers of fundamental physics to using physics led approaches to develop artificial intelligence.
