Synopsis & Topics: Join former student of Stephen Hawking and black role researcher, Marika Taylor, as she argues AI can help us do better science.

Title: Lost in Stories
Guests & Speakers: Matthew Beaumont, Ruth Padel, Theodore Dalrymple
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matthew Beaumont, Professor of English literature at University College London and acclaimed author, joins Ruth Padel, award-winning poet, and Theodore Dalrymple, a well-loved English cultural critic, prolific writer and psychiatrist, to discuss the power of the narratives we tell ourselves. Myriam François hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore how narratives shape our understanding of the world, from personal stories to societal myths. Can we escape the delusions they create?

Title: Faster than light
Guests & Speakers: João Magueijo, Claudia de Rham, Tim Maudlin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: João Magueijo is a Portugese cosmologist and Professor of theoretical physics at Imperial College, and a pioneer of varying speed of light theory. Claudia de Rham is a prize winning theoretical cosmologist, known for her theory of massive gravity which is seen as an explanation for the acceleration of the universe and an alternative to dark energy. Tim Maudlin is a leading professor of the philosophy of science at New York University who proposes that we should determine our metaphysics from physics. Hosted by post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: Ever since Einstein's special theory of relativity in 1905, it has been known that the speed of light is an absolute fixed limit. But critics argue this is a mistaken assumption. Join João Magueijo, Claudia de Rham, and Tim Maudlin as they debate the speed of light.

Title: AI and the future of film with Martha Fiennes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer, producer and digital artist, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. Her directorial debut was lavished with praise, including winning the London Film Critic's Choice Newcomer of the Year and the Tokyo International Film Festival award for Best Director.
Synopsis & Topics: Martha Fiennes has had a long career as a film director, writer, and producer. In this in-depth interview, she looks to the future of film and moving image and questions how we can embrace AI and all its creative opportunities whilst warning that human expression, above all else, must be protected

Title: Peril and progress
Guests & Speakers: Camila Vergara, Nadhim Zahawi, Guy Standing, John Bercow
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Camila Vergara is a critical legal theorist, historian, and journalist writing on the relation between inequality and the law. Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions including as Chancellor, Secretary of State for Education and Chairman of the Conservative Party. Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions including as Chancellor, Secretary of State for Education, and Chairman of the Conservative Party. John Bercow is the former Speaker for the House of Commons, former chancellor of the University of Essex and current professor at Royal Holloway. Guy Standing is a labour economist known for his support for Universal Basic Income. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nadhim Zahawi, Guy Standing, Camila Vergara, and John Bercow as they discuss how we can recover the meaning and direction of progress.

Title: Why we are out of our minds
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ruby Wax OBE is a seminal British-American talent, excelling as an actress, writer, TV personality, and mental health advocate. Her impressive career includes captivating performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company and a memorable role in the ITV sitcom Girls on Top.
Synopsis & Topics: Join celebrated comedian and author of the bestselling book I'm Not As Well As I Thought, Ruby Wax in conversation to discuss how to celebrate life's highs, deal with life's lows, and focus on being true to ourselves rather than the façade we put up. Dinesh Bhugra hosts.

Title: The dawn of machine consciousness with Joscha Bach
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joscha Bach is a cognitive scientist, AI researcher, and philosopher whose research aims to bridge cognitive science and AI by studying how human intelligence and consciousness can be modeled computationally.
Synopsis & Topics: Join cognitive scientist and AI researcher Joscha Bach in this exclusive interview on the limits, risks, and future of AI. From the potential of Artificial General Intelligence to the alignment problem and the fundamental ways AI learns differently from humans, Bach explores whether AI might one day grasp reality on a deeper level than we can.

Title: Something for nothing
Guests & Speakers: Nancy Sherman, Paul Bloom, Dan Ariely
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. Bloom has written widely on human nature, and he won the Klaus J. Jacobs Research Prize for his investigations into how children develop a sense of morality. Dan Ariely is a Professor of Psychology and Behavioural Economics at Duke University and best-selling author. Ariely is a scholar of irrationality and decision-making, explaining how we repeatedly and predictably make the wrong decisions in many aspects of our lives. Nancy Sherman is a Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University who has conducted research in general ethics, moral psychology, and the history of philosophy with focus on the Stoic tradition. A New York Times Notable Author and sought-after speaker, her views on military ethics have been influential. Hosted by Myriam François, trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. Myriam’s writing and work has appeared in the Guardian, TIME, Foreign Policy, the Telegraph, CNN online, Middle East Eye, the BBC, Channel 4, and Al Jazeera.
Synopsis & Topics: Studies show rewards can damage wellbeing, fostering dependence and undermining our own sense of control. Join Paul Bloom, Nancy Sherman, Dan Ariely as they debate the philosophy of value.

Title: Data, deception, and truth
Guests & Speakers: Kenneth Cukier, Abby Innes, John Burn-Murdoch
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Burn-Murdoch is a columnist and the chief data reporter for the Financial Times where he writes the weekly Data Points column. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE focusing on the UK state and empiricism. She is the teaching chair of the European Institute. Kenneth Cukier is deputy executive editor at the Economist and the host of the hugely popular weekly podcast, Babbage. Hosted by The Head of New Formats for the Financial Times, Juliet Riddell.
Synopsis & Topics: In an ever more complex world, we think data is crucial to helping us make sense of things. But critics claim there is a danger our trust in data is misplaced. Join John Burn-Murdoch, Abby Innes, Kenneth Cukier as they debate the reality of data today.

Title: Adventures in space
Guests & Speakers: Matt O'Dowd, Avi Loeb, Carol Cleland
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matt O'Dowd is a renowned professor of astrophysics and host and writer of the biggest physics and space show on YouTube, PBS Space Time. Avi Loeb is a leading theoretical astrophysicist and the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Carol Cleland is Director of the Center for the Study of Origins and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder.
Synopsis & Topics: Should humans conquer the great vastness of space or instead focus on the problems here on Earth? Join Matt O'Dowd, Avi Loeb, and Carol Cleland as they debate the future of space exploration.

Title: The ugly truth behind beauty
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica DeFino is an award-winning beauty reporter and critic, having written for the New York Times, Sunday Times, and Vice. She currently writes the Guardian’s beauty advice column Ask Ugly. DeFino also writes a weekly newsletter, The Review of Beauty, which “basically gives the middle finger to the entire beauty industry” (HuffPost). She is working on her first book.
Synopsis & Topics: Discover the hidden costs of the $260 billion beauty industry with journalist Jessica DeFino. Explore exploitation and the call to abandon beauty products.

Title: Anne Applebaum and Penny Mordaunt in conversation
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anne Applebaum is a Pulitzer Prize winning author and a Staff Writer at The Atlantic. Her condemnation of Russian aggression has seen her personally sanctioned by Putin's government. Her most recent book is Autocracy Inc. She is interviewed by Penny Mordaunt, former Foreign Secretary and Conservative MP.
Synopsis & Topics: Around the world democracies seem to be on the retreat and dictators are on the rise. But why is this? And how do autocracies help each other when they don't have formal alliances? Join Anne Applebaum, Pulitzer Award-winning journalist at the Atlantic, as she uncovers Autocracy Inc, a backchannel support and finance network that keeps autocrats and their cronies afloat.

Title: Language wars
Guests & Speakers: Babette Babich, Graham Priest, Sandra Laugier
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Babette Babich is a pioneering philosopher known for her deep exploration of science, technology, and ecological thought. She is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, NYC, and the director of The Nietzsche Society. Graham Priest is the Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the Graduate Center, City University of New York, renowned for his work in logic, especially non-classical logic. Sandra Laugier is an acclaimed Professor of Philosophy at Université Paris 1 Panthéon Sorbonne, known for her influential work on ordinary language philosophy and the intersection of philosophy and popular culture.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosophers, Babette Babich, Graham Priest, and Sandra Laugier as they debate the true meaning of language.

Title: The price of everything, the value of nothing
Guests & Speakers: Abby Innes, Will Hutton, Richard Kibble, Daniel Susskind
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Will Hutton is a leading political economist, author and journalist. Throughout his career, he has gone from being an investment banker in the City, to holding the Economics editorship of the Guardian and BBC2 Newsnight and the Principal of Hertford College Oxford. Daniel Susskind is an associate member of the Economics Department at Oxford University specialising in growth and the impact of AI. His most recent book is Growth: A Reckoning . Richard Kibble is a Deloitte Partner and former banking executive. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE focusing on how the UK’s economy mirrors the Soviet Union. Her work blends the philosophy of science, economics, and history. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing
Synopsis & Topics: Oscar Wilde once remarked, "a fool is someone who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing". Join Will Hutton, Abby Innes, Daniel Susskind, Richard Kibble as they debate the economics of value.

Title: Mental health is not a medical condition
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Wessely is a visionary psychiatrist and epidemiologist at the forefront of research in medicine, psychiatry, clinical epidemiology and military health. He currently holds the position of Regius Professor of Psychiatry at King's College London.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading psychologist Simon Wessely as he argues that physicians and psychiatrists are severely inflating the diagnosis of mental health conditions and why this poses a grave risk to society.

Title: John Ioannidis on why science is broken
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ioannidis is one of the world’s leading experts on scientific integrity and evidence-based medicine. A professor at Stanford University, his groundbreaking work has exposed systemic flaws in research methodology, publication bias, and the reproducibility crisis. Best known for his landmark paper Why Most Published Research Findings Are False, he continues to challenge the scientific establishment and advocate for more rigorous, transparent, and reliable research practices.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Stanford professor John Ioannidis as he explores why bad science persists, how we can fix it, and why our trust in research is more precarious than ever.

Title: The meaning of sex
Synopsis & Topics: Join futurist Anders Sandberg, sociologist Finn Mackay, and author Janne Telle in this debate as they tackle the philosophy of sex in the modern day.

Title: The rise of the new right
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Times columnist David Aaronovitch has won the Orwell prize for journalism, and the What the Papers Say columnist of the year award in 2003. He is the author of Paddling to Jerusalem and Voodoo Histories.
Synopsis & Topics: The right-wing has new faces and new ideas. Immigration is now being combined with political religiosity, with some right-wing figures converting to Catholicism. But why this mix of philosophies, and why has this movement gained such ground on the right? Join leading journalist David Aaronovitch as he examines the rise and future of the New Right.

Title: Quantum and the unknowable universe
Guests & Speakers: Slavoj Žižek, Roger Penrose, Sabine Hossenfelder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. He is also the author of The Road to Reality , Cycles of Time and Shadows of the Mind . Fearlessly critical of the scientific mainstream, Sabine Hossenfelder is a groundbreaking theoretical physicist who specialises in the foundations of science. She is a leading science communicator, best-selling author and researcher. Her recent books include Lost in Math , and the bestselling Existential Physics . Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities at the University of London, visiting professor at New York University and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. He is the author of several books, including The Sublime Object of Ideology , The Parallax View , and Heaven in Disorder. Hosted by Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we accept that the quantum mechanics has made the universe unknowable? Join Roger Penrose, Slavoj Žižek, and Sabine Hossenfelder as they debate the madness of quantum mechanics.

Title: Masculinity, femininity, and the unmodified body with Clare Chambers
Synopsis & Topics: For so long, the female body has been limited by the patriarchal notion of femininity, an ideal which is impossible for women to meet. Clare Chambers calls for a radical new framework that can help us keep our bodies intact, unmodified, and as canvasas for joyful expression rather than as vehicles of control.

Title: The life and philosophy of Peter Singer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Singer is the most prominent figure in contemporary ethics. He has made groundbreaking contributions to animal welfare, bioethics, effective altruism and practical ethics more broadly. He is a founder of both Animals Australia and The Life You Can Save, and has been a key figure in the Effective Altruism movement - an initiative that uses evidence and careful analysis to find the very best way for individuals to do good. Singer has received multiple accolades for his work, including a nomination as one of Australia's ten most influential public intellectuals and the $1 million Berggruen Prize in 2021.
Synopsis & Topics: Peter Singer is one of the world's leading philosophers. From animal ethics to effective altruism, Singer has shaped the philosophical landscape. In this interview we uncover the key events in his life that led to his ideas.

Title: The world at sea
Guests & Speakers: Isabel Hilton, Simon Jenkins, Duncan Potts
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Jenkins is an author, newspaper columnist and editor. He is currently a columnist for the Guardian and was formerly editor of the Times and Evening Standard. Duncan Potts is a retired Vice Admiral of the Royal Navy where he was the Director of the Joint Force Development. Before this, he was commander of the EU's counter-piracy operations in the Indian Ocean at the height of Somali Piracy. Isabel Hilton is a renowned international relations expert, journalist and broadcaster. She is the founder of China Dialogue, an organisation dedicated to fostering understanding of China. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: Simon Jenkins, Duncan Potts, and Isabel Hilton discuss naval power and if it is the ultimate determinant of global influence, or if the relative decline of US and Western naval forces is a sign of the end of Western dominance.

Title: Stories and poems from the front lines
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lindsey Hilsum is the International Editor of Channel 4 News and a regular contributor to The Sunday Times, The Times Literary Supplement, and The Guardian among others. She is also a bestselling author. Sarah Howe, award-winning poet, hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: International Editor at Channel 4 News Lindsey Hilsum reveals how poetry and language can create hope in times of conflict, and bring us closer together. Join her for an intimate conversation with poet Sarah Howe as she explores why the false promises of war and the humanity of its victims are best expressed in poetry.

Title: The philosophy of dehumanisation with David Livingstone Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Livingstone Smith is a philosopher and author, most recently of Making Monsters: The Uncanny Power of Dehumanization. His research interests include self-deception, dehumanization, human nature, ideology, race and moral psychology. His book Less Than Human: Why We Demean, Enslave, and Exterminate Others, won the Anisfield-Wolf Book Award.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview, philosopher David Livingstone Smith explores the history, nature, and evolution of dehumanisation. As what is 'acceptable' in society changes, so do the tactics of undercover dehumanisation. How can we identify these, and how might we progress?

Title: The phantom of the present
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Rupert Sheldrake, Timothy Morton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Winner of the Orange First Novel prize, Joanna Kavenna’s works include A Field Guide to Reality, The Ice Museum and Inglorious. Her journalism has appeared in the London Review of Books, The Guardian, and the New York Times. Timothy Morton is the Rita Shea Guffey Chair in English at Rice University. A member of the object-oriented philosophy movement, Morton's work explores the intersection of object-oriented thought and ecological studies. Morton has published numerous books including 'Dark Ecology: For a Logic of Future Coexistence', 'The Ecological Thought' and 'Hyposubjects: On Becoming Humane'. Rupert Sheldrake is a scientist, author, and parapsychology researcher. At Cambridge University, he worked in developmental biology as a Fellow of Clare College. He was Principal Plant Physiologist at the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics in Hyderabad, India. Hosted by Curt Jaimungal, renowned filmmaker and presenter. He is founder and host of the legendary Theories of Everything YouTube podcast that explores cutting-edge topics in physics, consciousness, free will and AI with some of the leading experts in the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Joanna Kavenna, Rupert Sheldrake, Timothy Morton as they debate the role of the present not only in our understanding of time but of experience and being itself.

Title: Profit, planet, and pretence
Guests & Speakers: Carla Denyer, Guy Shrubsole, Socrates Mokkas
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carla Denyer is co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales. Carla is the MP for Bristol Central and was instrumental in getting Bristol Council to declare a climate emergency, the first in Europe. Guy Shrubsole is a researcher, writer and campaigner. He wrote The Lost Rainforests of Britain (The Sunday Times Science book of the Year 2023) and, most recently, The Lie of the Land. Socrates Mokkas is a leading economist operating at the intersection of macroeconomic policy and sustainability. He has close to 20 years of experience across academia, government and industry. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
Synopsis & Topics: Can capitalism solve the climate crisis? Carla Denyer, Guy Shrubsole and Socrates Mokkas debate it out.

Title: Reality vs Theory
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Priya Natarajan is a Professor of theoretical astrophysics at Yale University. Natarajan was included on the TIME100 list of most influential people in the world in 2024 and is the 2025 recipient of the Dannie Heineman Prize in Astrophysics awarded by the American Astronomical Society and the American Institute of Physics. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is Editorial Director of the IAI.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading theoretical astrophysicist and TIME100 most influential people of 2024, Priya Natarajan, and Post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson for a conversation that lifts the lid on dark matter and dark energy and the future of modern physics.

Title: The danger and promise of the algorithm
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian. Craig Gent is a director at Novara Media, where he has worked for over ten years. He is the author of Cyberboss: The Rise of Algorithmic Management and the New Struggle for Control at Work (2024, Verso Books).
Synopsis & Topics: Join Novara Media's Craig Gent and Aaron Bastanias they discuss how algorithms are not only running what we see on our phones but are beginning to run our society as a whole.

Title: Make China great again: Steve Tsang on Xi Jinping
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve is the Director of the SOAS China Institute. Before taking on his current position in 2016, he was the Head of the School of Contemporary Chinese Studies at the University of Nottingham, and before that a Professorial Fellow at St Antony’s College, Oxford. He is a frequent commentator for the BBC, including for programmes like Newsnight, BBC News and the World at One.
Synopsis & Topics: Steve Tsang argues that, before Xi Jinping, China did not want a leadership role in global affairs. All this changed in 2017 when Xi consolidated his power. As a result, if we are to understand China, we need to understand Xi.

Title: Controlling the Tech Titans
Guests & Speakers: Joscha Bach, Shannon Vallor, Kenneth Cukier, Alexander Evans
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alexander Evans is a former diplomat and visiting Senior Fellow at LSE. His research includes the relationship between geopolitical insecurity, modern technology and online child safety. Kenneth Cukier is deputy executive editor of The Economist, following two decades as a foreign correspondent, technology writer, data editor and commentary editor. He is the coauthor of the NYT bestselling book “Big Data”. Shannon Vallor is the Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the Edinburgh Futures Institute. Her research explores how new technologies especially AI reshape our lives. Joscha Bach is a AI researcher, cognitive scientist and consciousness researcher. He currently works at Liquid AI in Silicon Valley. Roger Hearing hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we seek to regain control by breaking up the Big tech giants? Or is the value of innovation sufficient to overcome fears of the growing political and cultural power of the technology behemoths? Alexander Evans, Kenneth Cukier, Shannon Vallor and Joscha Bach debate.

Title: Creating life in a lab
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Katarzyna (Kate) Adamala is a pioneering synthetic biologist and genetics professor at the University of Minnesota. Her groundbreaking work spans the realms of astrobiology, synthetic cell engineering, and biocomputing.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch leading biologist Kate Adamala explore how synthetic biology helps us understand the origins of life on this planet and beyond.

Title: Consciousness is quantum mechanical, with Stuart Hameroff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Stuart Hameroff is a Professor of Psychology and Anesthesiology, and Director of the Center for Consciousness Studies at The University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona.
Synopsis & Topics: For decades, physicists have explored the idea that consciousness causes the collapse of the wavefunction— the moment quantum particles cease being in strange superpositions of states. Esteemed anesthesiologist Stuart Hameroff, following his collaboration with Roger Penrose, proposes a different story: consciousness is the collapse itself.

Title: The rise of the rest
Guests & Speakers: Malcolm Rifkind, Penny Mordaunt, Elizabeth Knup, Inna Sovsun
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join us as former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, Yale Jackson School Senior Fellow Elizabeth Knup, former Defence Secretary Penny Mordaunt, and current Ukrainian MP Inna Sovsun debate the rise of a new global world order.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, Yale Jackson School Senior Fellow Elizabeth Knup, former Defence Secretary Penny Mordaunt, and current Ukrainian MP Inna Sovsun debate the rise of a new global world order and the West's place in it.

Title: A world of order and chaos
Guests & Speakers: Marika Taylor, Nick Lane, Marcus Du Sautoy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Marcus du Sautoy is a leading British mathematician, and Simonyi Professor for the Public Understanding of Science at the University of Oxford. Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics, Pro-Vice Chancellor, and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences at the University of Birmingham.She previously studied under Stephen Hawking at Cambridge. Nick Lane is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author of five critically-acclaimed books on evolutionary biochemistry. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
Synopsis & Topics: Order and disorder are central to our understanding of the world. Biologists define life as the expending of energy to create order.  In neuroscience, a 2023 MIT study concluded the mind operates in the play between order and chaos when seeking to make sense of the world. While physics goes further embedding the notion in a fundamental law of the universe, the Second Law of Thermodynamics, which requires that disorder, defined as 'entropy', always increases. But critics argue order and disorder are human concepts and depend on our perspective. How are we then to make sense of the idea they are objective states of the universe?

Title: The dark side of ‘mental health’ with Susie Orbach
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic. She is a best-selling author, a columnist for The Guardian, and a visiting scholar at the New School for Social Research, in New York, whilst continuing to run her well-known practice, in London.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Susie Orbach in a thought-provoking discussion on psychotherapy's role in health, the dominance of the body over the mind, and the concept of self.

Title: A politics for the future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Will Hutton is a British writer, weekly columnist at the Guardian and the Observer, and currently Principal of Hertford College, Oxford and Chair of the Big Innovation Centre.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading economist and former editor of the Observer, Will Hutton, as he offers his vision of a path forward for the new government; a new kind of politics that doesn't rely on the wishful thinking that capitalism without guardrails works.

Title: The world as one
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies.
Synopsis & Topics: The world can be divided into its constitutive parts and the connections between, or so we thought. Join Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier as she explores the long traditions from around the world of philosophical monism, makes the case that distinction and separation are but an illusion, and explores its startling implications.

Title: Lies, damned lies, and economics
Guests & Speakers: Gary Stevenson, Abby Innes, Nadhim Zahawi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions under Prime Ministers Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, and Rishi Sunak. Gary Stevenson is a former financial trader who became an activist against inequality and a prominent YouTuber. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at LSE focusing on how the UK’s economy mirrors the Soviet Union. Hosted by Hilary Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: Governments, bankers and economists spend a great deal of time, money and effort trying to predict the economy. So why are their forecasts always wrong? Join Gary Stevenson, Abby Innes and Nadhim Zahawi as they debate the reality of economics.

Title: Physics' next paradigm shift with Matt O'Dowd
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matt O'Dowd is a renowned astrophysicist and science communicator. He researches extragalactic astrophysics (black holes, quasars, gravitational lensing, and more) and is a Professor of Physics and Astronomy at City University of New York, Lehman College. O'Dowd is also the host and writer of the weekly YouTube show PBS Space Time, currently the biggest physics and space show on YouTube with over 3 million subscribers. He is also a regular guest at StarTalk radio, the popular science show with Neil Degrasse Tyson.
Synopsis & Topics: Join astrophysicist and science communicator Matt O'Dowd for an in-depth interview on physics, in which he discusses cutting-edge black hole research, the possibility of extraterrestrial life, the importance of science education, and the next big paradigm shift in physics.

Title: Untangling Language
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sandra Laugier is an award-winning Professor of Philosophy at Université Paris 1 Panthéon Sorbonne. She is the author of the celebrated book, 'Why We Need Ordinary Language Philosophy'. A key liaison between American and European philosophical thought, her work spans moral philosophy, political philosophy, philosophy of language, gender studies, and popular culture.
Synopsis & Topics: Join French philosopher Sandra Laugier as she makes the case that there is no core of meaning shared among languages and explores the radical consequences this has for our understanding of the world.

Title: Why artists shouldn't fear A.I.
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jaron Lanier is a computer scientist, visual artist, composer, futurist, and writer. His 2014 book Who Owns the Future? received critical acclaim, winning Harvard’s Goldsmith Book Prize and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade. He has performed and recorded with a wide range of musicians, including Philip Glass, Yoko Ono, and Ornette Coleman, and his paintings and drawings have been displayed in museums and galleries across the globe. TIME magazine has named him one of the world’s 100 most influential people. Join Lanier as he discusses his recent artistic projects and the role of originality in art.
Synopsis & Topics: Jaron Lanier, a visionary computer scientist, artist, composer, futurist, and writer, discusses his latest artistic ventures and the importance of originality in art.

Title: Video games and the meaning of life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Tartaglia is Professor of Metaphysical Philosophy at Keele University. HIs latest book is Inner Space Philosophy: Why the Next Stage of Human Development Should Be Philosophical, Explained Radically (Suitable for Wolves).
Synopsis & Topics: Video games are changing how we think. Many are so realistic that some argue they are becoming reality. In this talk by philosopher James Tartaglia, he uncovers the relationship between games and reality.

Title: The lie of meritocracy with Daniel Markovits
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar, best known for his work on law and behavioural economics, contract law, distributive justice, and market regulation. His best-selling book, "The Meritocracy Trap: How America's Foundational Myth Feeds Inequality, Dismantles the Middle Class, and Devours the Elite", has sparked a significant discussion about the problems inherent in meritocratic societies.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Daniel Markovits in this exclusive interview where he argues that we should abandon our traditional ideas of meritocracy if we truly want a fairer society.

Title: The values of AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ruth Chang is the Professor and Chair of Jurisprudence at the University of Oxford, a Professorial Fellow of University College, Oxford, and a professor of philosophy. She is known for her pioneering research on the incommensurability of values and making hard choices.
Synopsis & Topics: A prophecy-maker or aid? How should we view the future of AI in making decisions for us? Join Ruth Chang as she discusses where our training of AI to make decisions is going wrong, how to fix it, and where we should draw the line.

Title: Consciousness, AI, and the pattern of reality, with Joscha Bach
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joscha Bach is an exceptional cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. As an AI researcher for MIT Media Lab and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics, he is constantly exploring new frontiers in cognitive architectures, mental representation, emotion, social modelling, and multi-agent systems. Bach's groundbreaking MicroPsi project is creating virtual agents that are revolutionizing our understanding of how emotion, motivation, and cognition interact in situated agents.
Synopsis & Topics: Join cognitive scientist and AI researcher Joscha Bach for an in-depth interview on the nature of consciousness, in which he argues that the brain is hardware, consciousness its software and that, in order to understand our reality, we must unlock the algorithms of consciousness.

Title: The divided self
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Sam Harris, Sophie Scott
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joining us live from the US via Zoom, neuroscientist and philosopher Sam Harris, Nobel Prize winner Roger Penrose and director of the Institute of Cognitive Neuroscience Sophie Scott discuss whether the self is divided.
Synopsis & Topics: Join psychologist Sam Harris, physicist Roger Penrose, and neuroscientist Sophie Scott as they debate the reality of the divided self.

Title: What is meaningful work?
Guests & Speakers: Guy Standing, Nilufar Ahmed, Caleb Althorpe, Isabel Berwick
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Isabel Berwick is the host of the Financial Times' Working It podcast, editorial lead for the FT's Women in Business forum, and author. Caleb Althorpe is a Research Fellow in the Department of Philosophy at Trinity College Dublin. He researches contemporary political theory and political philosophy. Dr Nilufar Ahmed is an award-winning professional psychologist with over 20 years of experience working in academia, the third sector, and as a freelance researcher and evaluator. Guy Standing is professor of Development Studies at SOAS and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Avery Anapol from The Conversation, FT podcaster Isabel Berwick, political philosopher Caleb Althorpe, psychologist and psychotherapist Nilufar Ahmed, and economist Guy Standing, as they try to discover what meaningful work is, and debate whether it's worth pursuing.

Title: Turtles all the way down
Guests & Speakers: Priyamvada Natarajan, Hilary Lawson, Donald Hoffman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Donald Hoffman is a renowned anti-reality theorist and Professor of Cognitive Sciences at the University of California, Irvine. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. Hosted by Jack Symes.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Jack Symes, Donald Hoffman, Priya Natarajan, and Hilary Lawson as they debate whether science can access the fundamental level of reality.

Title: The lasting legacy of stolen land
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dale Turner is an Associate Professor of Political Science at the University of Toronto. He works on Indigenous politics, contemporary Indigenous intellectual culture, contemporary political theory, and the philosophy of Ludwig Wittgenstein. He is currently working on a new book which draws from his community’s experiences over the past few hundred years in dialogue with the venerated Western European philosophical tradition.
Synopsis & Topics: Join academic Dale Turner as he argues that we must bridge the gap between Western and indigenous world-views to bring about a new legal and political conversation on stolen land.

Title: The communication crisis
Guests & Speakers: Nolen Gertz, Katie Farrell, Julia Hobsbawm
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of applied philosophy at the University of Twente. He is the author of the books Nihilism, and Nihilism and Technology. Julia Hobsbawm OBE is an award-winning writer and broadcaster who captures the zeitgeist about work, life, and technology. Her books include "Fully Connected" and The Nowhere Office which is now a popular podcast. Katie Farrell is the lead of the brand practice at Deloitte Digital, she works with executive teams to develop and build influential ideas for organisations. Shini Somara hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Nolen Gertz, writer Julia Hobsbawm and, leading digital strategist Katie Farrell as they debate the nature of communication in this technical age.

Title: How liberals get education wrong
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Enter Katharine Birbalsingh, known as "the world's strictest headmistress" and the leader of one of the U.K.'s most successful schools. Birbalsingh passionately argues that this crisis of meaning begins in childhood. She believes that unless we embrace discipline, endure boredom, and return to more traditional methods of teaching and parenting, we will fail to reverse this troubling trend.
Synopsis & Topics: Join leading educator and "Britain's Strictest Headmistress" Katherine Birbalsingh in this exclusive interview unpacking her philosophy of education.

Title: Nothing and everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Graham Priest is a philosopher and logician at CUNY. A key defender of dialetheism, the view that there are true contradictions.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Graham Priest as he controversially sides with Hegel and maintains nothingness is a paradoxical object that lies at the foundation of reality, with radical consequences for our understanding of everything...and nothing.

Title: Stories of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sunetra Gupta is a novelist and professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, with an interest in infectious disease agents that are responsible for malaria, HIV, influenza and bacterial meningitis. Her fictional works include So Good in Black and A Sin of Colour.
Synopsis & Topics: Join outspoken scientist, Sunetra Gupta, as she explores how storytelling is foundational to both our understanding of science and reality.

Title: The freedom fable
Guests & Speakers: Uriel Abulof, Lisa Cameron, Faiza Shaheen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Faiza Shaheen is a UK politician, former professor of economics, think-tank director, and expert in Inequality. Uriel Abulof is a professor of political science and expert in the politics of nationalism, social movements, and conflict. He is the author of several books, including The Morality and Mortality of Nations. Lisa Cameron is a Scottish Conservative politician who has served as a Member of Parliament. Lisa is also a former clinical psychologist who worked for the NHS. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
Synopsis & Topics: If we are unable to determine what it is to be free, should we stop appealing to it as a political goal? Or should we accept it as a rhetorical device to encourage others to adopt our outlook?

Title: Lisa Randall on theory, fantasy and discovery
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the most daring theoretical physicists alive today, Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Due to Randall's advances in understanding and testing the Standard Model of particle physics, supersymmetry, and cosmology of extra dimensions, Newsweek called her "one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation."
Synopsis & Topics: In this insightful interview, renowned physicist and author Lisa Randall delves into the fine balance between theory and speculation in modern science.

Title: The global population crisis
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Janne Teller, Peter Godfrey-Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and author, Presenter of BBC Radio 4's Briefing Room, and former long-standing columnist for The Times. Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. She was educated as a macro-economist and has previously worked for the United Nations on humanitarian assistance and conflict resolution. Peter Godfrey-Smith is a philosopher of science. He is the author of Other Minds: The Octopus, The Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness as well as Metazoa: Animal Life and the Birth of the Mind. Hosted by Harvard's Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Will population decline lead to economic and social collapse argue? Watch this debate, recorded at HowTheLightGetsIn London 2024, featuring David Aaronovitch, Janne Teller and Peter Godfrey-Smith, hosted by Rana Mitter.

Title: The values and prejudices of science
Guests & Speakers: Tim Palmer, Shini Somara, Ben Ware
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Palmer is a world renowned expert on climate physics at the Royal Society Institute in Oxford. He was appointed as CBE in the 2015 New Year’s Honours list for services to science. Shini Somara is a highly accomplished British mechanical engineer. With a mission to bring science to everyone, she has participated as an engineering expert on Sky, Discovery, and more. Ben Ware is a leading philosopher and an expert on Wittgenstein. He is the co-director of the Centre for Philosophy and the Visual Arts at King’s College London and the author of On Extinction: Beginning Again at The End. Hosted by post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: From the origins of the universe to the functioning of the brain, we see science as a quest for the underlying truth of things. But has this always been the case?

Title: The theory of quantum politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Armen Vardani Sarkissian is an Armenian politician, physicist, investor, businessman, and computer scientist who served as the 4th president of Armenia from 2018 to 2022. He also served as Prime Minister of Armenia from 1996 to 1997. He was the first president of post-Soviet Armenia born in former Armenian SSR.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Armen Sarkissian, former President of Armenia, as he argues for his new theory of quantum politics, in which individuals are necessarily connected across space and our world is dominated by randomness, uncertainty, and possibility.

Title: Creating the meaning of life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Babette Babich is a trailblazing philosopher of technology and science. Renowned for her exploration of the philosophy, history, and sociology of science, Babich also works on the philosophy of digital media, poetry and art. Babich is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City.
Synopsis & Topics: Discover the insights of Babette Babich, a leading philosopher of technology and science, exploring the intersections of philosophy, digital media, and art.

Title: The real risks of AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Natalie Cargill is a renowned philanthropic advisor and researcher of AI risk. Cargill is also the founder and President of LongView Philantropy.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Natalie Cargill as she delves into the key problems that could shape the trajectory of human development and our treatment of AI.

Title: Martha Nussbaum: A new theory of ethics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martha Nussbaum is Distinguished Professor of Law and Ethics at the University of Chicago. She has made ground-breaking contributions to topics ranging from sex and gender, ethics and politics, to justice. Her latest book is Justice for Animals .
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher and renowned ethicist Martha Nussbaum, as she argues for a brand new theory of animal ethics, demonstrating why we need and how we have a moral and philosophical reawakening.

Title: The riddle of the beginning
Guests & Speakers: Scott Aaronson, Joscha Bach, Priyamvada Natarajan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Scott Aaronson is a world renowned quantum complexity theorist and Associate Professor at MIT. He currently works at OpenAI, where he researches the theoretical foundations of AI safety. Joscha Bach is a computer scientist and AI researcher for MIT and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics. With a mission to build a model of the mind, Bach is at the forefront of the creation of Strong AI. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been just named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Hosted by British mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer, and author, Shini Somara.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Scott Aaronson, Joscha Bach and Priya Natarajan as they debate the mystery of how the universe began and why there is something rather than nothing.

Title: Morality and prejudice
Guests & Speakers: Tommy J. Curry, Michael Huemer, Melis Erdur
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy J. Curry is a Professor of Philosophy and holds the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh. He is the author of The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood, which won the 2018 American Book Award. Michael Huemer is a professor of philosophy at the University of Colorado. He is the author of more than eighty academic articles in epistemology, ethics, metaethics, metaphysics, and political philosophy, and he has written several books including Ethical Intuitionism. Huemer is also known for his detailed defence of philosophical anarchism. Melis Erdur received her Ph.D. in philosophy from the New York University in 2013. In her philosophical work, she examines central meta-ethical questions concerning moral truth and objectivity and argues that common ways of posing and answering these questions are based on serious moral mistakes.
Synopsis & Topics: Most have a clear sense of what is right and wrong, and we imagine that our assessment is reasoned and sensible.  But critics argue this is an illusion and morality is commonly little more than concealed prejudice.  Join Tommy J. Curry, Michael Huemer, and Melis Erdur as they debate the implicit bias of morality.

Title: The crisis of the new
Guests & Speakers: Stanley Fish, Martin Puchner, Claire Hynes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The author Joanna Kavenna hosts this debate between Martin Puchner, the Byron and Anita Wien Professor of Drama and English and Comparative Literature at Harvard University, Claire Hynes, an Associate Professor in Literature & Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia, and Stanley Fish, a literary critic, legal scholar, and public intellectual who is currently a Distinguished Visiting Professor of Law at Yeshiva University's Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law in New York City.
Synopsis & Topics: From fashion to fantasy, entertainment to enterprise, we seek the 'new' as the means to originality, change, and creativity but is our obsession with the new misguided? We found out in this engaging debate.

Title: The future of multiculturalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Katharine Birbalsingh is a British teacher and education reform advocate who is the founder and head teacher of Michaela Community School, a free school established in 2014 in Wembley Park, London. Katharine read Philosophy & Modern Languages at The University of Oxford and has always taught in inner London. She has made numerous appearances on television, radio, podcasts and has written for several publications. Katharine has also written two books and edited another two about Michaela; Battle Hymn Of The Tiger Teachers and The Power of Culture. Katharine was appointed Honorary Fellow of New College, Oxford in 2021 and Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2020. Follow Katharine on Twitter: @Miss_Snuffy
Synopsis & Topics: Multiculturalism is seen by many as a success of modern society. However, might it sometimes be best for us to leave our cultural and religious differences at the door, for the benefit of individual progress? According to Katharine Birbalsingh, this is what is required to create the best environment for optimal learning in schools.

Title: Objects from other worlds
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avi Loeb is a theoretical astrophysicist and the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University.
Synopsis & Topics: Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb has made the controversial claim that an object of alien origin has been found on Earth. Join Professor Loeb as he defends this controversial claim and explores the radical implications this would have if true.

Title: Recovering meaning in the information age
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer, producer and digital artist, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. Her directorial debut was lavished with praise, including winning the London Film Critic's Choice Newcomer of the Year and the Tokyo International Film Festival award for Best Director. Richard Davey is a Senior Research Fellow at Nottingham Trent University.
Synopsis & Topics: Join film director and digital artist Martha Fiennes, for a conversation with Richard Davey, as she argues technology has all too often closed, not opened, our minds. Technology has built new mental prisons around education, media, healthcare, and everywhere else.

Title: Humanity and the gods of nature
Guests & Speakers: Slavoj Žižek, Peter Singer, Nancy Sherman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek, renowned ethicist Peter Singer, and Georgetown professor of philosophy Nancy Sherman, question human centred morality. Hosted by public philosopher Jack Symes.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Slavoj Žižek, renowned ethicist Peter Singer, and Georgetown professor of philosophy Nancy Sherman, question whether it is right to centre morality around humans.

Title: The politics of time
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Guy Standing is professor of Development Studies at SOAS and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network. He is best known as a long-standing and prominent advocate of Universal Basic Income, but he is also responsible for redefining and revitalizing the term ‘precariat’ which describes a new emerging social class suffering from job insecurity as well as identity insecurity and lack of time control.
Synopsis & Topics: Time is political. Throughout history, how we use our time has been controlled by the rich and powerful, and today is no exception. Even outside of work, we're almost always 'on the clock'. Join pioneering economist, Guy Standing, as he shows us how to reclaim our most valuable asset: time.

Title: Consciousness beyond the brain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is a preeminent biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His books include Science and Spiritual Practices, Ways to Go Beyond And Why They Work and The Science Delusion. Furthermore, he was ranked in the top 100 thought leaders for 2013 by the Duttweiler Institute, Switzerland's leading think tank, and has been recognised as one of the 'most spiritually influential living people' by Watkins' Mind Body Spirit Magazine.
Synopsis & Topics: Join distinguished Cambridge scientist Rupert Sheldrake as he argues that the mind extends beyond the brain and explores the radical implications of this account

Title: Roger Penrose on the blatant contradiction of quantum mechanics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. Interviewed by renowned filmmaker and presenter, Curt Jaimungal.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview, Roger Penrose discusses the shortcomings and blatant contradictions of quantum mechanics which led his career down a different path to most. Whilst others are on the quest to quantise gravity Penrose discusses his alternative approach to "gravitise" quantum mechanics.

Title: Sartre vs Baldwin: The unknown other
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Jonathan Webber, Marie-Elsa Bragg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jonathan Webber is a professor at Cardiff University specializing in moral philosophy and the philosophy of psychology. Marie-Elsa Roche Bragg is an author, teacher, and priest. Her first novel, Towards Mellbreak is about four generations of a quiet hill farming family on the North Western fells of Cumbria. Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. She was born in the UK but as a seasoned traveller, she was led to her first book, The Ice Museum, which details her experience travelling in the remote North. Hosted by presenter, writer and professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford, Rana Mitter
Synopsis & Topics: Can we ever know what is it like to be someone else? The philosophers James Baldwin and Jean-Paul Sartre took radically different approaches as discussed in this engaging debate.

Title: Gary Stevenson on hidden dangers of inequality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Gary Stevenson (born 1986 in Ilford) is a British economist, former financial trader, and YouTuber known for his economic analysis and activism against economic inequality. Interviewed by Alyssa Erspamer.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview at the HowTheLightGetsIn festival, Gary argues that we urgently need to tackle inequality if we hope to have a middle class left to save.

Title: What religion and stoicism both misunderstand
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. In addition to his ten-year post as Archbishop, Lord Williams has also enjoyed an esteemed academic career, having been a lecturer at the University of Cambridge as well as having held the Lady Margaret Chair of Divinity at the University of Oxford. Angie Hobbs is the chair for the Public Understanding of Philosophy at Sheffield, and a frequent contributor to the BBC’s In Our Time, Night Waves and The Forum. She is the author of Plato and the Hero and her forthcoming book is Why Plato Matters.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former Archbishop of Canterbury Rowan Williams and chair of public understanding at the University of Sheffield Angie Hobbes as they discuss how ancient philosophy and thought can help us living today.

Title: Science alone won't solve climate change
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Palmer is an internationally renowned meteorologist and Professor at the University of Oxford. He works on the tough, crucial problems of uncertainty in our weather and climate, drawing on his background in fundamental physics to do so.
Synopsis & Topics: Join internationally renowned meteorologist at the Universe of Oxford Tim Palmer, as he explores the uncertain future of our planets climate.

Title: Why most published research findings are false
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ioannidis is a physician-scientist, writer and Stanford University professor who has made contributions to evidence-based medicine, epidemiology and clinical research. Ioannidis studies scientific research itself, meta-research primarily in clinical medicine and the social sciences.
Synopsis & Topics: Twenty years ago, Stanford professor John Ioannidis shocked the scientific world by publishing evidence demonstrating that the majority of published scientific claims are false. It was hugely influential and led to the widespread recognition of a 'replicability crisis' in science. Join John Ioannidis to hear first-hand how he thinks things have moved on from his initial research and what he thinks needs to be done to rescue science from its falsehoods.

Title: Konstantin Kisin on wokeness, free speech, and tribalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Konstantin Kisin is a Sunday Times best-selling author, comedian, satirist, social commentator and host of the YouTube show, TRIGGERnometry. Born in the late Soviet Union and raised in Britain, Kisin has appeared on flagship TV shows like BBC Question Time and Real Time with Bill Maher, as well as the Joe Rogan Experience and other popular podcasts.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview, Konstantin Kisin discusses the pathologies of the "woke left" and "woke right." He covers immigration, climate change, free speech, and other hot-button issues dominating modern political discourse.

Title: The consciousness test
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Nick Lane, Yoshua Bengio, Sabine Hossenfelder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joining us live from Montreal, Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio, science YouTuber and theoretical physicist Sabine Hossenfelder, evolutionary biochemist Nick Lane, and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson lock horns over whether AI is, or can ever be, conscious.
Synopsis & Topics: Are thought and consciousness ultimately unobservable? Join Yoshua Bengio, Sabine Hossenfelder, Nick Lane, Hilary Lawson as they debate the validity of the Turing Test for Artificial Intelligence.

Title: The life and philosophy of Sadiq Khan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sadiq Khan is the current Mayor of London, former MP and human rights lawyer. He has had an extensive political career, most recently winning an unprecedented third term as Mayor. Prior to the mayoralty, Sadiq was an MP and member of the Shadow Cabinet under Ed Miliband where he held the posts of Shadow Secretary of State for Justice, Lord Chancellor, and Minister for London. In conversation with Will Hutton a leading political economist, author and journalist. His long and storied career has taken him from the City as an investment banker, the Economics editorship of the Guardian and BBC2 Newsnight , the editorship of the Observer, the chief executive of the Work Foundation and Principal of Hertford College Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Sadiq Khan is one of the most recognisable figures in British politics, best known for his transformation of the city's transport links and his fervent mission to tackle the capital's air pollution problem. Join Sadiq Khan to hear what he thinks he has learnt from his extraordinary life and how his philosophy has contributed to a remarkable set of achievements.

Title: A precarious peace
Guests & Speakers: Bill Browder, Camila Vergara, Malcolm Rifkind, Tariq Ali
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tariq Ali is a writer, political activist and filmmaker, and is considered to be a leading figure of the international left. Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major. Camila Vergara is a critical legal theorist, historian, and journalist writing on the relation between inequality and the law, and the possible institutional solutions to systemic corruption. William Browder is the CEO and co-founder of Hermitage Capital Management, firebrand financier and anti-Putin activist. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: With wars raging all around the world, an effective foreign policy looks increasingly elusive. Join Tariq Ali, Malcolm Rifkind, Camila Vergara and Bill Browder as they debate how to find peace in geopolitical chaos.

Title: The dangerous misunderstanding of disease
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sunetra Gupta is an award-winning epidemiologist and novelist. She is currently a Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford. Bahar Gholipour is a leading New York-based journalist and neuroscientist writing about cutting-edge issues in technology and science.
Synopsis & Topics: We typically think of illness as separate from ourselves, a foreign pathogen or external entity. But this framing may not capture its real character. Join Bahar Gholipour for an in-depth conversation with epidemiologist Sunetra Gupta as they explore the future of health and illness.

Title: Motherhood vs. the Machine
Synopsis & Topics: The invention of the artificial womb could have dramatic implications for the role of women in society. Join Theos Director Chine McDonald, alongside writers Charlotte Faircloth and Mary Harrington as they explore how and if, in changing how we think about birth and motherhood, we might change the very fabric of our society.

Title: The philosophy of longtermism with Hilary Greaves
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Greaves is a professor of philosophy at the University of Oxford and was the founding director of its Global Priorities Institute.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview with the founding director of Oxford's Global Priorities Institute, philosopher Hilary Greaves is challenged on the longtermist philosophy underpinning the effective altruist movement.

Title: The rise and fall of the grand narrative
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Konstantin Kisin, Jessica Frazier
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Konstantin Kisin is a Sunday Times best-selling author, comedian, satirist, social commentator and host of the leading YouTube show, TRIGGERnometry. David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist, presenter of BBC Radio 4's Briefing Room, and former long-standing columnist for The Times. Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. She is an expert on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. Hosted by Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: History never repeats but it does always rhyme however we like to think we exist outside of these grand narratives. Join David Aaronovitch, Konstantin Kisin, and Jessica Frazier as they debate the end of history.

Title: Books and the future of civilisation
Guests & Speakers: Juliet Mabey, David Shariatmadari, Johanna Thomas-Corr
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In a live recording of the podcast in partnership with Theos, Reading our Times, Senior Fellow at Theos Nick Spencer discusses the future of books and reading with Times literary critic Johanna Thomas-Corr, Guardian literary editor David Shariatmadari and editorial director of Oneworld Publications Juliet Mabey.
Synopsis & Topics: Delve into the complexities of reading in the digital era with insights from literary critics and publishers in this engaging podcast discussion on the future of literature.

Title: Denis Noble on the symmetry of order and disorder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the founders of the field of systems biology, Denis Noble is an Emeritus professor of cardiovascular physiology at the University of Oxford. He was the first to develop computer models of the heart in 1960.
Synopsis & Topics: In this exclusive interview, Denis Noble explores the intricate dance between order and disorder in biology, conciousness, language, A.I and more.

Title: John Bercow: How to change sides in politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The longest-serving Speaker of the House of Commons since the Second World War (2009-2019), John Bercow was once seen as on the right of the Tory party, later becoming a member of the Tory shadow cabinet. He moved to the left throughout his political career subsequently becoming a thorn in the side of the Conservative Johnson government and leaving the party.
Synopsis & Topics: Join John Bercow in this exclusive talk as he reveals his views on the recent UK election result and the upcoming US election, as well as his journey from a Conservative MP to his defection to the Labour Party.

Title: The democracy show
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Scott-Brown, Amy Chua, S. Y. Quraishi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: S.Y. Quraishi is an Indian civil servant who rose to be the 17th Chief Election Commissioner of India, the largest democracy in the world. He has served as a UN election observer in South Africa, Kenya, Russia, and Myanmar to name a few. Amy Chua is an author, professor of law at Yale Law School and populariser of the term ‘Tiger Mom’. She is a renowned commentator on everything from American politics, to populism and parenting. Sophie Scott-Brown is the former Director of Gresham College and an Honorary Research Fellow in the History faculty at the University of St. Andrews. Her work specialises in the history of anarchism. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: This exploration questions the actual impact of elections on policy, suggesting they may be more symbolic than substantial, as a study reveals little connection between citizens' views and real outcomes. It examines whether reforms are needed to enhance the effectiveness of democratic processes and the belief in their importance.

Title: AI is a mirror on humanity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Shannon Vallor is the Baillie Gifford Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the Edinburgh Futures Institute, the Director of the Centre for Technomoral Futures, and a former AI ethicist at Google. Her research explores how new technologies -- especially AI, robotics, and data science -- reshape human moral character, habits, and practices. Her work includes advising policymakers and industry on the ethical design and use of AI.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher of technology, Shannon Vallor, as she argues AI holds a mirror up to humanity and proposes how to address its flaws.

Title: Challenging Peter Singer's ethics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Singer is a prominent philosopher, author and academic. He a professor of Bioethics at Princeton University, and specialises in practical ethics. His is best known for his work on global poverty and animal ethics. His book Animal Liberation was a key to the early environmental movement. Interviewed by Senior Producer at the IAI Charlie Barnett.
Synopsis & Topics: Whether or not moral ideas can be objectively true has divided philosophers for centuries. In this challenging interview, Peter Singer defends his turn to objectivity and argues morality doesn't need religion, that we should resist our intuitions and that the future of the Effective Altruism movement isn't as bleak as it may appear.

Title: Caught in time
Guests & Speakers: Timothy Morton, Marijam Didžgalvytė, Freya India
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher Timothy Morton, author of Everything to Play For Marijam Didzgalvyte, and Guardian and UnHerd writer Freya India debate our obsession with recording every experience.
Synopsis & Topics: Today we take millions of photographs, the majority of which will never be viewed. Join Philosopher Timothy Morton, Author Marijam Didzgalvyte and Journalist Freya India to debate our obsession with recording every experience, as well as its potential benefits and pitfalls.

Title: Troubling echoes of the big bang
Guests & Speakers: Matt O'Dowd, Marika Taylor, Martín López Corredoira
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martín López Corredoira is an astrophysicist and philosopher at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias in Tenerife, Spain. Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics, Pro-Vice Chancellor, and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences at the University of Birmingham. She previously studied under Stephen Hawking at Cambridge. Matt O'Dowd is a renowned professor of astrophysics and host and writer of the biggest physics and space show on YouTube, PBS Space Time. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Martín López Corredoira, Marika Taylor, and Matt O'Dowd as they debate the CMB and the Big Bang, asking if radical theories can survive in cosmology.

Title: Lifting the lid on the economic elite
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Matt Kennard, co-founder and head of investigations at Declassified UK and a former fellow and then director at the Centre for Investigative Journalism (CIJ) in London, for an in-depth conversation with Tariq Ali. Ali is a writer, political activist and filmmaker, and is considered to be a leading figure of the international left. He has written numerous books on world history and politics as well as novels and scripts for the stage and screen.
Synopsis & Topics: Join investigative journalist Matt Kennard and activist Tariq Ali as they reveal the stark realities of wealth inequality and the flaws in our global economic system.

Title: Metaphysics vs consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Goff is a philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview. Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, philosopher Philip Goff elucidates his version of panpsychism - a theory that argues for consciousness as a ubiquitous feature of our world.

Title: Respect and loathing in the US
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeff Spinner-Halev is the Keenan Eminent Professor of Political Ethics at the University of North Carolina. He specialises in tensions within political identity and the ways people perceive their political opponents and social situation. Elizabeth Theiss-Morse is a professor of Political Science at the University of Nebraska-Lincon specialising in political psychology and identity. Their most recent book Respect and Loathing in American Democracy seeks to bridge the gaps between divided political tribes.
Synopsis & Topics: As we look towards the US Election, join political theorist Jeff Spinner-Halev and political scientist Elizabeth Theiss-Morse as they argue that despite respect being in short supply in American democracy, it is integral to overcoming the challenges we face.

Title: The age of emergency
Guests & Speakers: Daron Acemoglu, Steve Koonin, Genevieve Guenther
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daron Acemoglu is the 2024 Nobel Prize winner in economics, an Institute Professor at MIT, and is a regular writer on political economy and the state of liberal society. He was named the most cited economist in 2015 and he was awarded with Prospects 2024 thinker of the year. Genevieve Gunther is a climate activist and author of the book The Language of Climate Politics. She is a founding director of the organisation End Climate Silence. Steve Koonin is a theoretical physicist and the former director of the Centr for Urban Science and Progress at NYU. He served as President Obama's Undersecretary of Science in the Department of Energy and has since researched the science behind political claims about climate change. Hosted by Sophie Scott Brown, a political philosopher at NYU.
Synopsis & Topics: From the cost of living crisis to the climate crisis, the crisis in healthcare to the crisis of migration, we live in a world of seemingly relentless crises. Join the 2024 Nobel Prize winner in economics and an Institute Professor at MIT, Daron Acemoglu, climate activist Genevieve Gunther and theorhetical physicist Steve Koonin, as they debate The Age of Emergency.

Title: Politics, culture, and mass deception
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter York is a management consultant, author, and broadcaster, who has written columns for GQ and The Independent on Sunday.
Synopsis & Topics: Join distinguished journalist Peter York as he lifts the lid on the big money and big media that has torn apart the very fabric of our society by manufacturing  culture wars.

Title: What Einstein got wrong about time
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avshalom Elitzur is Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University. He is best known for his groundbreaking work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
Synopsis & Topics: According to Einstein, we live in a 'block universe', where the future is set, the past continues to exist, and there is no passage of time. Join controversial physicist Avshalom Elitzur as he argues that Einstein was wrong and offers a radical new theory of time.

Title: The myth of universal values
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focuses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies, and Public Health.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Tommy J. Curry as he makes the case that universal values are a fantasy, a myth created by those with power.

Title: Thinking set free
Guests & Speakers: Subrena Smith, Stuart Hameroff, Paul Bloom
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Quantum consciousness theorist Stuart Hameroff, evolutionary psychology critic Subrena E. Smith, and best-selling author and psychologist Paul Bloom, explore the nature of thought, philosopher Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Quantum consciousness theorist Stuart Hameroff, evolutionary psychology critic Subrena E. Smith, and best-selling author and psychologist Paul Bloom, explore the nature of thought, in this engaging video debate.

Title: The economics of a viable Palestinian state
Guests & Speakers: Uriel Abulof, Guy Standing, Nadia Naser-Najjab, Camila Vergara
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nadia Naser-Najjab is a Senior Lecturer in Palestine Studies at the European Centre for Palestine Studies, University of Exeter. Camila Vergara is a critical theorist, historian, and journalist. She is also a Senior Lecturer at the University of Essex. Guy Standing is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London. Uriel Abulof is an Associate Professor at Tel-Aviv University’s School of Political Science, Government and International Affairs. Hosted by Rana Mitter, ST Lee Chair in US-Asia Relations at the Harvard Kennedy School.
Synopsis & Topics: Since October 7th, the world has watched as Israel's war has reduced Gaza to rubble with 85% of the Palestinian population displaced. For a long-term solution to the crisis many look to a two-state solution which has widespread international support.  But realistically, how can this be achieved?

Title: Russia, China, and the future of world power
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Clarke is former Director of the Centre for Defence Studies and the International Policy Institute. He is now head of the School of Social Science and Public Policy at King's College London.
Synopsis & Topics: In this in-depth interview, Michael Clarke, former Director of the Royal United Services Institute, argues that the fundamental axis of world politics is changing. From NATO, to Western sanctions on Russia, and China's increasing presence to the threat of nuclear weapons, Clarke explains how the basis of geo-politics is fundamentally shifting.

Title: Screens aren't causing a mental health crisis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Christopher Ferguson is a psychologist and professor at Stetson University Florida. In 2013 he was awarded a Distinguished Early Career Professional Award from the American Psychological Association. Ferguson strongly disputes the link between video games and violent behaviour as well as social media and mental health problems.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning psychologist Christopher Ferguson argues that screens aren't the root cause of the mental health epidemic.

Title: Dark energy and the universe
Guests & Speakers: Priyamvada Natarajan, Claudia de Rham, Chris Lintott
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist working at the interface of gravity, cosmology, and particle physics. She is well known for her ground-breaking research into the theory of massive gravity. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Chris Lintott is Professor of Astrophysics in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford. He is also the Gresham Professor of Astronomy at Gresham College, and has worked as a presenter on several popular science projects including with the BBC. Hosted by Jonjoe McFadden.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Claudia de Rham, Priya Natarajan, and Chris Lintott as they debate dark energy. The mysterious force Einstein predicted that causes the universe to expand. Hosted by Johnjoe McFadden

Title: Marx deserves better critics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ben Burgis is a Jacobin columnist, an adjunct philosophy professor at Rutgers University and the host of the YouTube show and podcast Give Them An Argument. He’s the author of several books, most recently Christopher Hitchens: What He Got Right, How He Went Wrong, and Why He Still Matters.
Synopsis & Topics: Marxism is often blamed for everything from the horrors of communism to the cruelty of modern dictators, most in the mainstream have attempted to escape its grip. Join philosopher Ben Burgis as he argues that Marx deserves better critics than the ones we have today.

Title: Freedom of speech is necessary to democracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and a long-time champion of freedom of expression. He was the President of PEN International from 2009 to 2015, and has written a number of best-selling books on culture, politics and philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: In this in-depth interview, former President of PEN International John Ralston Saul discusses the importance of free speech, how it has recently come under threat, and why it is an integral to a democratic societies.

Title: The case for conscious AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joscha Bach is an exceptional cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. As an AI researcher, he is constantly exploring new frontiers in cognitive architectures, mental representation, emotion, social modelling, and multi-agent systems.
Synopsis & Topics: Most are sceptical that artificial intelligence will one day become conscious. But might this scepticism be misguided? Join leading AI researcher, Joscha Bach, as he argues that we can create artificial consciousness if we open ourselves up to the possibility of cyber-animism, the idea that consciousness and spirit is akin to a software agent that naturally emerges in a biological organism.
