His latest book Technofeudalism charts the end of Capitalism and the rise of new cloud feudal lords. Eshe Nelson is a reporter for the New York Times based in London. Her work focuses on central bank policy and the British macroeconomy.
Synopsis & Topics: Join this exclusive interview in which Yanis Varoufakis is interviewed by the NYT's Eshe Nelson on how our current inflation crisis ties in with 2008, quantitative easing and the end of capitalism.

Title: Epiphanies, ethics, and experience
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie-Grace Chappell is a Professor of Philosophy who writes about ethics, politics, feminism and epistemology. She argues that we should allow our epiphanies to guide us.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch philosopher Sophie-Grace Chappell in this thought-provoking talk where she argues that we should embrace ephiphanies and allow them to guide our actions.

Title: How medicine ignores our bodies
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Healy is a renowned professor of psychiatry at Bangor University. He is a psychiatrist, psychopharmacologist, scientist and author known for criticising a lack of neutrality regarding psychotropic drugs.
Synopsis & Topics: No it's not all in your head. Join outspoken psychopharmacologist David Healy as he argues the body, not the brain, is our behavioural and emotional centre.

Title: The perception bias
Guests & Speakers: Daniel Kahneman, Ellen Langer, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Scott-Brown is joined by Daniel Kahneman, a Nobel prize-winning economist, Ellen Langer, a Harvard psychologist known as the mother of mindfulness, and Hilary Lawson, a post-postmodernist philosopher and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas, to debate whether perceptual biases influence or alter the way we see the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Sophie Scott-Brown is joined by Daniel Kahneman, Ellen Langer, and Hilary Lawson to debate whether perceptual biases influence or alter the way we see the world.

Title: Roger Penrose | Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sir Roger Penrose is a world-renowned physicist, best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for their work on black holes.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nobel laureate Sir Roger Penrose as he outlines his views on quantum mechanics, Gödel's incompleteness theorem and consciousness. He also provides a glimpse into his visual thought process and scientific idol Galileo Galilei.

Title: The truth of fiction
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative Party politician, Jesse Norman, explores the use of fiction to uncover the truth in contemporary issues.
Synopsis & Topics: Join MP and author of the widely-acclaimed historical fiction The Winding Stair, Jesse Norman, to explore the power of story, and how the past provides us with a fresh perspective on contemporary issues.

Title: Utopian living
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kristen Ghodsee is an anthropologist and Professor of Russian and East European Studies at the University of Pennsylvania. Her latest work is Everyday Utopia, which explores pioneering experiments in communal living.
Synopsis & Topics: Kristen Ghodsee explores previous forms of communal living and the potential to radically reshape our society in a utopian vision.

Title: Beauty and the meaning of life
Guests & Speakers: George Ellis, Suchitra Sebastian, Denis Noble
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Dominic Walliman as he hosts a panel discussion on the nature of beauty. Debating the topic are Denis Noble, Emeritus Rrofessor of Cardiovascular Physiology at the University of Oxford, Suchitra Sebastian, condensed matter physicist and recent winner of the New Horizons in Physics Prize, and George Ellis, mathematician at the University of Cape Town and Stephen Hawking collaborator.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we conclude that beauty is not a subjective but instead an objective and vital quality of the universe? Join Dominic Walliman as he hosts, Denis Noble, Suchitra Sebastian, and George ellis in this thought-provoking debate.

Title: Perception as a fantasy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Donald Hoffman is an American cognitive psychologist working at the University of California, Irvine. Hoffman's Interface Theory of Perception suggests that, instead of presenting reality as it "really is", our perception is like a desktop interface that has evolved to ensure survival. To advance his theory of consciousness, Hoffman explores cutting edge physics that suggests spacetime is non-fundamental. For Hoffman we must explain consciousness in fundamental terms, beyond spacetime.
Synopsis & Topics: Join us as world-leading cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman discusses his cutting-edge research about consciousness and perception, as well as its astonishing implications for the ultimate nature of reality.

Title: Confronting lies in modern politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is a British Labour Party politician, serving as the Shadow Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport since 2023 and the Labour MP for Bristol West since 2015.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Thangam Debbonaire in this exclusive studio interview as she explains what is wrong with British politics, the plight of refugees arriving in the UK, and potential solutions to these problems that would benefit the entire country.

Title: Capitalism, Big Tech and the nation state
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Kenneth Cukier, Anu Bradford
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Stephanie Hare as she hosts a panel on the future of Big Tech, and its political and economic influence. Taking part in this debate are Aaron Bastani, the visionary co-founder of Novara Media, Kenneth Cukier, the host of the hugely popular podcast Babbage as well as the co-author of the best-selling book Big Data, and lastly Anu Bradford, a Professor of Law and International Organization at Columbia University.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Stephanie Hare as she hosts this debate on on the future of Big Tech, and its political and economic influence featuring Aaron Bastani, Kenneth Cukier, and Anu Bradford.

Title: The origin of life
Guests & Speakers: Addy Pross, Kate Adamala, Chrisantha Fernando
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join molecular biologist Güneş Taylor as she hosts a discussion on biology’s most central question: how did life begin? Joining her on the panel are cell biologist at the University of Minnesota Kate Adamala, Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at Ben Guiron University Addy Pross, and research scientist at Google DeepMind Chrisantha Fernando.
Synopsis & Topics: Is there something about the origin of life that means it will never be uncovered? Join Kate Adamala, Addy Pross, and Chrisantha Fernando in this thought-provoking video debate hosted by Güneş Taylor.

Title: China and India: The future of the next century
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bhavna Dave is a senior lecturer in Central Asian Politics at the Department of Politics and International Studies at the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. She specializes in issues of ethnic relations, identity politics and political transition in Central Asia.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Cindy Yu and Bhavna Dave in this intimate conversation on how China and India will shape the future of the global geopolitical order.

Title: The morality of sex work
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Maya Oppenheim is Women’s Correspondent - the only such job title at a UK news outlet - at The Independent. She also writes a popular weekly free newsletter titled Independent Women. Her most recent work is The Pocket Guide to the Patriarchy (2023).
Synopsis & Topics: Join journalist, Maya Oppenheim, as she offers a new direction for the philosophy, morality and politics of sex work, and explores the fine line between liberation and exploitation.

Title: Discovering the world beyond science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is an English scientist whose research into parapsychology and evolution led to the theory of morphic resonance. Other topics he has written and spoken on include precognition, the relationships between spirituality and science and the psychic staring effect. Sheldrake's most recent book is Science and Spiritual Practices (2017).
Synopsis & Topics: Join radical scientist and spiritualist, Rupert Sheldrake, to explore a reality that lies beyond the scientific view of reality.

Title: Redrawing the global order
Guests & Speakers: Bill Browder, Yuan Yang, Sergei Guriev
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Will the BRICS be the new superpower? Join Bill Browder, the famed thorn in Putin's side and CEO of Hermitage Capital, Yuan Yang the Financial Times' Europe China Correspondent, and Sergei Guriev, the provost and professor of economics and Science Po and former chief economist for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Hosted by Sasha Polakow-Suransky and this event was sponsored by Foreign Policy.
Synopsis & Topics: Will the BRICS be the next global superpower? Join Bill Browder, Yuan Yang, and Sergei Guriev, in this video debate hosted by Sasha Polakow-Suransky

Title: The happiness crisis and the futility of suffering
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rob Boddice is a writer and historian who unravels the complexities of the human condition; he is the author/editor of 14 books, most recently Knowing Pain: A History of Sensation, Emotion, and Experience (Polity Press). His 2018 and 2019 books, The History of Emotions and A History of Feelings, are defining works in the field. He is currently Senior Research Fellow at the Academy of Finland Centre of Excellence in the History of Experiences at Tampere University, Finland, and a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society.
Synopsis & Topics: In this intriguing talk, Rob Boddice challenges the tenets of happiness indices that flatten the subjective states of citizens, asking pointedly if it is still possible for suffering to be a virtue.

Title: The quantum age
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Famed futurist and co-founder of String Field Theory, Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature. His latest book is Quantum Supremacy: How the Quantum Computer Revolution Will Change Everything.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Michio Kaku and Curt Jaimungal in this exclusive interview as we enter the Quantum Era and unlock the mysteries of the universe.

Title: A rule to live by
Guests & Speakers: Daniel Markovits, Carol Gilligan, Peter Singer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Myriam François as she hosts this panel of distinguished guests as they discuss the idea of universal moral principles. Taking part in this debate are Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar and Professor of Law at the Yale Law School; Carol Gilligan, a celebrated feminist, ethicist and psychologist; and finally, Peter Singer, one of the world's foremost public philosophers and a prominent figure in contemporary ethics.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Myriam François as she hosts Daniel Markovits, Carol Gilligan, and Peter Singer, as they debate the Golden Rule of treating others how you wish to be treated.

Title: The psychedelic revolution
Guests & Speakers: Matthew Johnson, Kevin Sabet, Shayla Love
Synopsis & Topics: Join Dr Matthew Johnson, Shayla Love, and Kevin Sabet as they discuss the new role of psychedelics in treating mental illness in this thought-provoking video debate.

Title: Dreaming beyond time
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Gary Lachman is the former Blondie bassist turned philosopher. He is the author of many books on consciousness, precognition, psychology and the occult.
Synopsis & Topics: Uncover the captivating history of precognition, dreams, and the enigmatic notion of time's unidirectional nature as Gary Lachman, a philosopher and former Blondie bassist, delves into these fascinating subjects.

Title: The secrets of irrationality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dan Ariely is James B. Duke Professor of psychology and behavioural economics at Duke University. He explores the secrets of irrationality, explains why rational people believe irrational things and what we can do about it. His latest book is Misbelief: What Makes Rational People Believe Irrational Things.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the intricate problem of misinformation and its profound effects on our daily lives, as Dan Ariely's innovative approach offers a new perspective to combat misbeliefs and conspiracy theories, surpassing the limitations of policing social media alone.

Title: How spies think
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Omand is a former British spy who served as Director of GCHQ. He was responsible to the Prime Minister for the professional health of the intelligence community, national counter-terrorism strategy and “homeland security”.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former head of GCHQ and permanent secretary of the home office, Professor Sir David Omand, in this thought-provoking talk and find out how to think like a spy.

Title: The quantum hoax
Guests & Speakers: Joscha Bach, Dominic Walliman, Ruth Oulton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Quantum photonic expert Ruth Oulton, leading AI researcher Joscha Bach and science writer and YouTube sensation Dominic Walliman debate the potential of quantum computing. Neil Turok hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the truth behind the hype surrounding quantum computing and its potential to revolutionize the world with insights from renowned speakers in this informative debate.

Title: Solving the meaning crisis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Vervaeke is an award winning professor at the University of Toronto in the departments of psychology, cognitive science, and Buddhist psychology. He is the creator of the widely viewed, 50-part lecture series on Youtube, Awakening from the Meaning Crisis.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore a philosophical approach to finding meaning and purpose in the midst of the mental health crisis with John Vervaeke.

Title: Embracing solidarity in a secular age
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. In addition to his ten-year post as Archbishop, Lord Williams has also enjoyed an esteemed academic career, having been a lecturer at the University of Cambridge as well as having held the Lady Margaret Chair of Divinity at the University of Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Rowan Williams for an in-depth interview where he discusses everything from ritual, climate change, and moral responsibility.

Title: The spectre of the enlightenment
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aviva Chomsky is a leading historian and activist and the Coordinator of Latin American, Latino and Caribbean Studies at Salem State University in Massachussets. She is the author of 10 books, including most recently Is Science Enough?: Forty Critical Questions About Climate Justice.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the profound impact of Enlightenment values on contemporary issues such as the climate crisis and systemic racism through the insightful perspective of historian and activist Aviva Chomsky.

Title: The mystery of emergence
Guests & Speakers: Suchitra Sebastian, Hilary Lawson, Philip Goff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Suchitra Sebastian is a renowned scientist and a condensed matter physicist. She is based at the Cavendish Laboratory at the University of Cambridge where she is a Professor of Physics. Philip Goff is a leading philosopher of Consciousness in his field and a defender of panpsychism, the controversial proposal that everything contains consciousness, as the solution to the hard problem of consciousness. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and long-standing critic of realism, best known for his theory of closure. Jack Symes hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Join physicist Suchitra Sebastian, panpsychist pioneer Philip Goff, and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson as they debate the role of complexity and emergence when explaining nature's most puzzling phenomena.

Title: The Life and Philosophy of Billy Bragg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Billy Bragg is an English singer-songwriter and activist known for his blend of folk, punk rock, and protest music. Bragg's outspoken views and commitment to activism have cemented his place as one of the UK's most influential musical figures.
Synopsis & Topics: Join interviewer Myriam François to discover the life and philosophy of pioneering singer-songwriter Billy Bragg.

Title: Mearsheimer and the death of ideology
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Mearsheimer is the R. Wendell Harrison Distinguished Service Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago and is considered to be one of the most influential international relations theorists of his generation.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the complexities of global power dynamics with John Mearsheimer as he delves into the invasion of Ukraine and the influence of ideology and realism on geopolitics, providing a unique perspective on understanding world politics.

Title: Truth, beauty and other scientific misconceptions
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the most daring theoretical physicists alive today, Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Randall's books Warped Passages and Knocking on Heaven's Door have both been on the New York Times 100 notable books lists.
Synopsis & Topics: Join pioneering physicist Lisa Randall in this though-provoking talk to discuss the allure and dangers of equating beautiful advances with scientific achievement.

Title: The politics of desire
Guests & Speakers: Zoe Strimpel, Maya Oppenheim, Kimberly McIntosh
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Zoe Strimpel is an outspoken commentator, historian, and columnist at The Sunday Telegraph who specialises in all things gender and relationships. Maya Oppenheim is a writer and tireless advocate for women’s rights. Her role as Women’s Correspondent at The Independent is the only one of its kind in the UK. Kimberly McIntosh is a writer, Labour councillor and former love and dating columnist for ‘gal-dem’; her first book, black girl, no magic, is a searing collection of personal essays reflecting on living whilst black. Barry Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the societal implications of sexual desire and its connection to prejudice and discrimination in this thought-provoking debate featuring Zoe Strimpel, Maya Oppenheim and Kimberly McIntosh.

Title: The dark side of feminism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focuses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies, and Public Health.
Synopsis & Topics: Join pioneering philosopher of race, Tommy Curry, as he argues that feminism has been tarnished by racist ideology and explains how we can create a more inclusive world for all.

Title: The transgender mind-body problem
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Grace Chappell is a Professor of Philosophy at the Open University where she specialises in ethics, politics, feminism and epistemology. Her recent books include Ethics Beyond the Limits and Knowing What to Do.
Synopsis & Topics: In this eye-opening interview with Sophie Grace Chappell she explores whether gender has an essentialist element, the potential virtues of living without gender, and how this all intersects with gender, feminism, and consciousness.

Title: Gravity and the universe
Guests & Speakers: Sabine Hossenfelder, Erik Verlinde, Priyamvada Natarajan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join celebrated theoretical physicist, Erik Verlinde, leading astrophysicist, Priya Natarajan, and famous physicist-YouTuber, Sabine Hossenfelder, as they take on the problems surrounding our conceptions of gravity today. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
Synopsis & Topics: Gain insight into the enigma of gravity by exploring the limitations of current theories and questioning the fault lies with Einstein's general relativity or our understanding of quantum mechanics.

Title: Economic fact and economic fantasy
Guests & Speakers: Yanis Varoufakis, John Redwood, Vicky Pryce
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Yanis Varoufakis, former finance minister of Greece, John Redwood Conservative MP, and Vicky Pryce, chief economics adviser to the Centre of Economics and Business Research. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Yanis Varoufakis, John Redwood, and Vicky Pryce as they debate the role of central banks and the reality of economic predictions. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.

Title: The dream and danger of AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Liv Boeree is one of the most successful female poker players of all time. A self-confessed nerd with a first-class degree in astrophysics, Liv combined her science background and passion for games to become one of the most recognizable faces in professional poker. Dominic Walliman is a science writer, physicist, and YouTube sensation. His popular YouTube channel, Domain of Science, and award-winning Professor Astro Cat science books for children have captivated audiences worldwide.
Synopsis & Topics: Join renowned commentator and prize winning poker player, Liv Boeree, in conversation with Dominic Walliman, to explore how we can best utilise and regulate AI to change the world for the better.

Title: The TikTok uprising
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cindy Yu is a China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator. She has written extensively about Chinese society – from marriage to education – and politics for the Spectator. She is a frequent commentator on China issues for RTE and BBC World Service and World TV.
Synopsis & Topics: Join China expert and host of the Chinese whispers podcast, Cindy Yu, to chart how TikTok stole our attention, and how it could be a major player for China on the global political stage.

Title: Dostoevsky vs Nietzsche
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Oliver Ready, Kathleen Higgins
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kathleen Higgins is a leading continental philosopher at the University of Texas, Austin. Her research interests are broad and include the philosophy of aesthetics, emotions and music. Oliver Ready is a celebrated translator and literary scholar. His translation of Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment has received critical acclaim. Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed writer whose novels include Odin's Island, and Come, an existential novel about ethics in art and modern life. Niki Seth-Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the contrasting perspectives of Dostoevsky and Nietzsche on the existential threat of nihilism and the search for meaning in this thought-provoking debate.

Title: Putin and the cult of personality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Fiona Hill worked at the US National Intelligence Council as an intelligence analyst under Bush and Obama, and in 2017 was appointed by Donald Trump as Deputy Assistant to the President and Senior Director for European and Russian affairs on his National Security Council staff. She is now the Chancellor of Durham University.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore Fiona Hill's expert analysis on Russia, Putin, and the conflict in Ukraine in this thought-provoking interview.

Title: The impartiality illusion
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Scott-Brown, Philip Collins, Matthew Goodwin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Florence Read as she hosts a debate between Matthew Goodwin, Professor of Politics at the University of Kent and bestselling author, Philip Collins, writer-in-chief at The Draft and contributing editor at the New Statesman, and Sophie Scott-Brown, fellow at the European Institute at the University of Oxford, on whether or not media can ever claim to be impartial.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Florence Read as she hosts a debate between Matthew Goodwin, Philip Collins, and Sophie Scott-Brown on whether or not media can ever claim to be impartial.

Title: We need a scientific revolution
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eric Weinstein is a mathematical physicist and the host of the podcast The Portal. He is the former Managing Director of Thiel Capital in San Francisco and was formerly a Co-Founder and Principal of the Natron Group in Manhattan as well as a Visiting Research Fellow at Oxford University for the Mathematical Institute.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Eric Weinstein for an in-depth interview where he explains the need to go beyond good science to pursue great science.

Title: The god desire
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Baddiel is an acclaimed comedian, screenwriter and actor. He is best known for creating and starring in The Mary Whitehouse Experience, as well as for his numerous collaborations with Frank Skinner. His most recent book, The God Desire, provides a fresh, exciting spin on the most ancient of debates.
Synopsis & Topics: Join David Baddiel and Chine McDonald in an enlightening discussion on the existential topics of mortality, the self, and the supernatural, delving into the complexities of religious belief and its implications.

Title: Speaking for the future
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Greaves, Jonathan Sumption, Sophie Howe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Greaves is a professor of philosophy at the University of Oxford and a a founding director of the Global Priorities Institute. Lord Jonathan Sumption is an author, political commentator and one of the most decorated lawyers of his generation; he sat as a judge on the Supreme Court between 2012 and 2018, and appeared as a barrister for the Hutton Inquiry. Sophie Howe is a sustainable futures and wellbeing adviser who was the first to hold the role of Future Generations Commissioner in Wales. Philip Collins hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we improve our long-run future and reduce the risk of annihilation with altruistic decision making? Or is this dangerous rhetoric open to abuse by interested parties and the reality that we cannot know how to act on behalf of an unknown future populace?

Title: Challenging the caricature
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emmy-award winning actress and writer for screen and stage best known for her role as one third of the anarchic Smack the Pony ensemble.
Synopsis & Topics: Join award-winning actress, Doon Mackichan as she explores creativity, caricatures, and how to escape our current prejudices.

Title: Uncovering the secrets of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Priyamvada Natarajan is a Yale Professor of Astronomy and Physics and a science communicator. She was also the first woman in astrophysics to be elected as a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge. Her pionieering work includes Mapping the Heavens: The Radical Scientific Ideas that Reveal the Cosmos.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Yale Professor of Astronomy and Physics, Priyamvada Natarajan, as she explores the radical consequences the discovery of black holes has for our understanding of the universe.

Title: The Enlightenment and its alternatives
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Scott-Brown, Director at Gresham College, hosts a debate between two of the most influential thinkers of our time. Join John Mearsheimer, Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago, and Steven Pinker, Professor of Psychology at Harvard University, as they discuss the Enlightenment and its alternatives.
Synopsis & Topics: Explore the contemporary relevance of Enlightenment principles through a captivating debate between Stephen Pinker and John Mearsheimer.

Title: When myth becomes reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed and best-selling novelist, known for her works Odin's Island and Nothing. Her books deal with the existential and ethical questions around life and civilisation.
Synopsis & Topics: Join best-selling author, Janne Teller, to explore how we can break free of fictitious narratives and and return to reality.

Title: Power, politics, and mental health
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Simon Wessely, Praveetha Patalay
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of population health Praveetha Patalay, Regius Professor of Psychiatry Sir Simon Wessley and co-founder of Novara Media and bestselling author Aaron Bastani debate the connection between science, politics, and mental health. Hosted by Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: The popular debate around our mental health epidemic has thrown the effectiveness of psychiatry into question. Is mental illness is a medical problem that can be 'cured' or a symptom of a greater social disease?

Title: Why we should question everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Della Rocca is one of the world's leading authorities on Spinoza and the author of numerous field-defining articles and books, including most recently the Parmenidean Ascent. He is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University, which is awarded to a tenured faculty member considered one of the best in his or her field and is Yale University’s highest faculty honour.
Synopsis & Topics: Gain a unique perspective on philosophy as Michael Della Rocca sheds light on the dangers of blindly accepting common sense and advocates for a critical questioning of everything in this exclusive studio interview.

Title: The quest for the common good
Guests & Speakers: Julia Davies, Gerry Mitchell, Louise Ashley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mike Herd is Investigations editor of The Conversation UK. Julia Davies is an angel investor, lawyer, philanthropist and environmental campaigner. Gerry Mitchell is a social researcher and writer who is also experienced in political campaigning, community engagement and teaching. Louise Ashley is Senior Lecturer in the School of Business and Management at Queen Mary University of London.
Synopsis & Topics: Many feel their future is under threat. But is a solution to be found in embracing the common good or a more individualistic, privatised future the answer?

Title: The morality of sex
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Steven Bonnell, Maya Oppenheim, Isabel Millar
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Famed twitch streamer Steven Bonnell (aka Destiny), Acclaimed filmmaker, journalist and writer Myriam Francois, Philosopher and Psychoanalytic theorist Isabel Millar, and Womens Correspondent at the The Independent Maya Oppenheim debate whether monogamy is still morally justified in our modern world. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Streamer Steven Bonnell (aka Destiny), filmmaker Myriam Francois, Psychoanalytic theorist Isabel Millar, and journalist Maya Oppenheim debate whether monogamy is still morally justified in our modern world.

Title: Quantum computing and the future of science communication
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dominic Walliman is a science writer, physicist, and YouTube sensation. His popular YouTube channel, Domain of Science, and award-winning Professor Astro Cat science books for kids have captivated audiences around the world
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Dominic Walliman discusses the future of quantum computing, its applications and possible future breakthrough; as well as his own work communicating science.

Title: The life and philosophy of Slavoj Žižek
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a Slovenian-born political philosopher currently serving as International Director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities. He has become world-renowned for his fearless overturning of the liberal left’s founding assumptions.
Synopsis & Topics: Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. Join him in conversation with author Joanna Kavenna, as they discuss intersection of his ideas and his personal life.

Title: The economics of almost everything
Guests & Speakers: Daniel Markovits, Martin Wolf, Madeleine Pennington
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chief Economics Commentator for the FT Martin Wolf, Yale Law professor Daniel Markovits and Head of Research at Theos, Madeleine Pennington debate whether the 21st century will prove to be unique.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Martin Wolf, Daniel Markovits and Madeleine Pennington as they debate whether modern society's obsession with productivity is helpful in the pursuit for economic growth.

Title: Science fiction for a dystopian present
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cory Doctorow (craphound.com) is a prolific science fiction author, activist and journalist. He is the author of many books, most recently The Lost Cause, a solarpunk science fiction novel of hope amidst the climate emergency. His most recent nonfiction book is The Internet Con: How to Seize The Means of Computation, a Big Tech disassembly manual. Other recent books include Red Team Blues, a science fiction crime thriller. Interviewed by Darcy Bounsall.
Synopsis & Topics:
In this exclusive interview Cory Doctorow pulls apart cryptocurrency and our relationship with tech overlords while giving insight into our ever-increasing entanglement with technology. 

Interviewed by Darcy Bounsall.

Title: The secrets of quantum emergence
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Recent winner of the New Horizons in Physics Prize and the Schmidt Science Polymaths Award, Suchitra Sebastian is an up and coming condensed matter physicist. She is based at the Cavendish Laboratory at the University of Cambridge where she is a Professor of Physics. Professor Sebastian is known for her discoveries of exotic quantum phenomena that emerge in complex materials. She was named as one of thirty Exceptional Young Scientists by the World Economic Forum in 2013, one of The Next Big Names in Physics by the Financial Times in 2013.
Synopsis & Topics: Suchitra Sebastian explores the science of quantum mechanics and demonstrates why we may be on the verge of discovering a completely new type of matter.

Title: The shadow of spirituality
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Grace Chappell, Michael Shermer, John Vervaeke
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning professor at the University of Toronto John Vervaeke, Professor at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell and founder of the Skeptics Society Michael Shermer join their host, Professor Barry C. Smith to discuss new-age spirituality.
Synopsis & Topics: In this debate John Vervaeke, Sophie-Grace Chappell and Michael Shermer join their host, Professor Barry C. Smith to discuss the dangers of new-age spirituality.

Title: Confronting the Enlightenment's mistakes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kehinde Andrews is the first black studies professor in the UK, currently working at Birmingham City University. He is the director of the Centre for Critical Social Research, founder of the Harambee Organisation of Black Unity, and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, leading Black studies thinker Kehinde Andrews examines the Enlightenment and its connections to colonialism and white supremacy.

Title: Dangerous media for dangerous times
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alan Rusbridger is a world-renowned journalist, former principal of Lady Margaret Hall and former editor-in-chief of The Guardian. Matt Kelly is a career journalist and the owner of The New European, a paper that has taken the UK by storm since its humble beginnings in the wake of the Brexit vote.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Alan Rusbridger in discussion with New European editor Matt Kelly, to explore how we reclaim journalistic integrity in times of faltering trust.

Title: The trouble with time
Guests & Speakers: Michio Kaku, Avshalom Elitzur, Jimena Canales, Tim Maudlin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Quantum theorist Avshalom Elitzur, theoretical physicist Michio Kaku, philosopher of physics Tim Maudlin, and historian of science Jimena Canales delve into the fascinating conundrum of time. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In this debate, Avshalom Elitzur, Michio Kaku, Tim Maudlin, and Jimena Canales delve into the fascinating conundrum of time.

Title: The psychology of AI
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr Isabel Millar is a groundbreaking philosopher and psychoanalytic theorist, currently working at Newcastle University and the Global Centre for Advanced Study.
Synopsis & Topics: In this fascinating interview, Dr Isabel Millar discusses her work deploying the tools of psychoanalysis to the study of AI.

Title: Marxism vs Capitalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, one of the most influential independent, radical left-wing media organizations in the UK. He is also author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism, a manifesto for his vision of 21st century communism. Matthew Lesh is the Director of Public Policy and Communications at the Institute of Economic Affairs. He is also a Fellow of the Adam Smith Institute and Institute of Public Affairs, and writes regularly for The Times, The Telegraph and The Spectator.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Novara Media's Aaron Bastani as he goes head-to-head with Institute of Economic Affairs’ Matthew Lesh on Marxism vs Capitalism.

Title: Imagining the universe
Guests & Speakers: Iain McGilchrist, Roger Penrose, Esther Freud
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-renowned mathematician and Nobel Laureate in Physics Roger Penrose, award-winning writer Esther Freud and ground-breaking polymath and former Oxford scholar Iain McGilchrist join Eliane Glaser to debate creativity, imagination and whether or not they can help us reframe our understanding of reality.
Synopsis & Topics: Roger Penrose, Esther Freud and Iain McGilchrist join Eliane Glaser to debate creativity, imagination and whether or not they can help us reframe our understanding of reality

Title: Science is broken
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr Helen Czerski is a a physicist, oceanographer, presenter and author, currently working as an Associate Professor at University College London in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
Synopsis & Topics: In this fascinating interview, physicist and oceanographer Dr Helen Czerski explores the ways in which we can harness the powers of science for good.

Title: Narcissism and self-love
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Think and Truth: A guide for the perplexed, Simon Blackburn has worked to bring philosophy to a wider audience. He was Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge and Vice President of the British Humanist Association.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Philosopher and Author Simon Blackburn as he asks if our modern fascination with self-love may end up creating a generation of narcissists.

Title: In pursuit of peace
Guests & Speakers: David Omand, Richard Wolff, Svitlana Morenets
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Renowned economist, Richard D. Wolff, award-winning journalist, Svitlana Morenets, and former intelligence chief, Sir David Omand, join Hilary Lawson to discuss escalating conflict worldwide and the possibility of peace.
Synopsis & Topics: Has the nuclear deterrent has enabled complacency and imagined that peace will be maintained when in practice it is being dangerously undermined? Join economist, Richard D. Wolff, journalist, Svitlana Morenets, and former intelligence chief, Sir David Omand as they discuss escalating conflict worldwide and the possibility of peace. Hosted by Hilary Lawson.

Title: Destiny and the new world of internet politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steven Bonnell (also known as Destiny) is an internet personality, live streamer and political commentator. He started out as a gaming livestreamer but became more politically engaged in the run up to Trump’s election in 2016. He is now known for debating far-right, white supremacist and antifeminist internet commentators in YouTube videos.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Destiny in this exclusive interview in which he gives his unique perspective into the world of online political discourse.

Title: The life and philosophy of Denis Noble
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Denis Noble is one of the pioneers of modern biology. He is a British physiologist and biologist who has worked at the University of Oxford. He developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart, and is the author of several best-selling books.
Synopsis & Topics: Join world-renowed systems biologist Denis Noble in this intimate interview reflecting on his life working at the forefront of biological research.

Title: The end of good and evil
Guests & Speakers: Rowan Williams, Richard Wrangham, Maria Balaska, Slavoj Žižek
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anthropologist and Harvard University Professor Richard Wrangham, renowened philosopher and cultural critic Slavoj Žižek, University of Hertfordshire professor Maria Balaska and the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury Rowan Williams join Myriam François to discuss the nature of good and evil.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Richard Wrangham, Slavoj Žižek, Maria Balaska and Rowan Williams as they debate whether we should apply notions of good or evil to humans.

Title: The broken economics of the sea
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Guy Standing is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS, University of London, and a founder and co-president of the Basic Income Earth Network (BIEN). His most recent work is The Blue Commons (2022).
Synopsis & Topics: In this fascinating talk, economist Guy Standing explores how corporate collusion is destroying the oceans and presents transformative proposals for how to save them.

Title: The awakened brain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr. Lisa Miller is an American professor, researcher and clinical psychologist, best known as a research scholar on spirituality in psychology. Miller is Founder of the Spirituality Mind Body Institute at Columbia University. Miller's published work on spirituality in renewal from addiction and depression has been featured in the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal, as well as in television interviews and podcasts. Tom Hodgkinson and Mark Vernon from The Idler host. This event was produced in partnership with The Idler.
Synopsis & Topics: Can science understand the spiritual world? Join best selling author Lisa Miller as she takes an analytic, academic look at alternative belief systems.

Title: Down the wormhole
Guests & Speakers: Eric Weinstein, George Ellis, Matt O'Dowd
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished cosmologist, George Ellis, famous mathematician and polymath, Eric Weinstein, and celebrated astrophysicist, Matt O'Dowd, join Katie Robertson to discuss wormholes.
Synopsis & Topics: Distinguished cosmologist, George Ellis, famous mathematician and polymath, Eric Weinstein, and celebrated astrophysicist, Matt O'Dowd, join Katie Robertson to discuss wormholes.

Title: The ethics of industry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Baroness Lola Young is a former actor and lecturer, and currently sits as an independent member of the House of Lords. As a peer, her work has focussed on ethics in industry and trade, founding and chairing key cross-party parliamentary groups on sustainability and modern slavery.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Lola Young (OBE) to explore the ethical issues surrounding modern industry, and to discover what we can do about them.

Title: On the edges of knowledge
Synopsis & Topics: What is it possible to know? Is the physical universe all there is, or is the immaterial part of reality too? Join Rupert Sheldrake and Michael Shermer, as they clash on where the edges of knowledge lie.

Title: Based on a true story
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Leading academic and author, Remi Adekoya, director of the Institute of Philosophy at UCL, Barry Smith, and award-winning writer, Esther Freud, join Eliane Glaser to discuss the problem of subjectivity in historical narratives.
Synopsis & Topics: We are critical of historical errors and assume there could be a correct version.  But many argue that there can be no one true story, no correct history. Remi Adekoya, Barry Smith and Esther Freud debate.

Title: Justice in jeopardy
Guests & Speakers: Harriet Wistrich, Myriam François, David Livingstone Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of The Centre for Women's Justice Harriet Wistrich, leading philosopher of psychology and morality David Livingstone Smith and journalist and film-maker Myriam François debate justice, judgement and punishment. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we reform justice in society to not be reliant on judgment and punishment? In doing so could we create a more egalitarian culture? Find out in this debate.

Title: Explaining away truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Gordon Horwich is a British analytic philosopher at New York University, noted for his contributions to philosophy of science, philosophy of physics, the philosophy of language and the interpretation of Wittgenstein's later philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Paul Horwich explores the binary frameworks of modern philosophy while providing therapy for how to trust our own thoughts in a post-truth world.

Title: Necessity and lies
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Rebecca Roache, Simon Baron-Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at Royal Holloway, Rebecca Roache, Professor of Psychology and Psychiatry at Cambridge University, Simon Baron-Cohen, and non-realist philosopher, Hilary Lawson join Samira Shackle to scrutinize honesty and deception.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we recognise that lying can be valuable, and sometimes necessary, for ourselves and those in power? Join Rebecca Roache, Simon Baron-Cohen and Hilary Lawson as they debate the merits of honesty.

Title: Dopamine nation
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert. Alongside her important clinical practice, Lembke has featured on the hit Netflix documentary, The Social Dilemma, and testified before various committees in the United States House of Representatives and Senate.
Synopsis & Topics: Step into the world of modern brain chemistry with psychiatrist and author Dr. Anna Lembke. Who draws on decades of expertise and research to argue how, in a world consumed by instant gratification, the pursuit of too much pleasure is having disastrous consequences

Title: Waking from darkness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve Taylor is a senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University, and has authored over fourteen books on psychology and spirituality.
Synopsis & Topics: We feel the need to be spiritually awakened, but in what sense are we currently asleep? Join psychologist of spirituality Steve Taylor as he explores our endless quest for meaning.

Title: The pleasure paradox
Guests & Speakers: Yaron Brook, Patricia Churchland, Anna Lembke
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Neurophilosopher Patricia Churchland, Ayn Rand Institute chairman Yaron Brook, and Stanford addiction expert Anna Lembke join host Robert Lawrence Kuhn to question why living standards do not seem to correlate with happiness. Produced in partnership with Closer To Truth.
Synopsis & Topics: Research shows that richer countries have higher rates of anxiety than poorer ones. Patricia Churchland, Yaron Brook, and Anna Lembke join host Robert Lawrence Kuhn to debate if our lifestyles are the true cause of our sadness.

Title: Data needs theory
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Newsweek has called Randall "one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation." Randall's books Warped Passages and Knocking on Heaven's Door have both been on New York Times 100 notable books lists.
Synopsis & Topics: Join world-famous Harvard theoretical physicist Lisa Randall to discuss how she entered the field, the joy of puzzle-solving, and her views on how to approach the most challenging questions in contemporary physics.

Title: How to fix sexual assault law
Synopsis & Topics: Join Emma Bryson in unraveling the determined journey of justice reform advocates. Discover the grounds for optimism in a realm where resilience crafts real change.

Title: Reality, models, and mayhem
Guests & Speakers: Bjørn Ekeberg, Sunetra Gupta, Michael Shermer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pioneering philosopher of science Bjørn Ekeberg, pre-eminent sceptic Michael Shermer, and Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford Sunetra Gupta debate whether science can ever achieve an objective model of ultimate reality.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch as Bjørn Ekeberg, Michael Shermer, and Sunetra Gupta debate whether science can ever achieve an objective model of ultimate reality.

Title: Fantasy, faith, and physics
Guests & Speakers: Sabine Hossenfelder, Michio Kaku, Max Tegmark, Juan Maldacena
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. She is the author of Lost in Math: How Beauty Leads Physics Astray. Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature. His latest book is Quantum Supremacy. Juan Maldacena is the Carl P. Feinberg Professor in the School of Natural Sciences at the Institute for Advanced Study. Due to his field-defining contributions to the foundations of string theory and quantum gravity, Leonard Susskind has called him “the greatest theoretical physicist of his generation.” Max Tegmark is a pioneering physicist, cosmologist, computer scientist, philosopher, and public intellectual based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Tegmark is the author of Our Mathematical Universe, which argues that reality is fundamentally a mathematical structure. Hosted by Mary-Jane Rubenstein, Professor of Religion and Science in Society at Wesleyan University.
Synopsis & Topics: We think we pursue the sciences solely for knowledge and truth. But is this a mistake? Should we accept that some beliefs, especially in the foundations of physics, are akin to religious beliefs dressed in mathematical language to give our theories meaning?

Title: The life and philosophy of Fiona Hill
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Fiona Hill is one of the most highly distinguished foreign affairs specialists and authors in the world today. Senior advisor to Presidents George W Bush, Barack Obama and briefly Donald Trump, she is a former official at the U.S. National Security Council specializing in Russian and European affairs.
Synopsis & Topics: Interviewer Isabel Hilton uncovers Fiona Hill's fascinating insights on UK mobility, Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and the future of Ukraine and Global Politics.

Title: The goodness paradox
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Wrangham is Ruth B. Moore Research Professor of Biological Anthropology at Harvard University and one of the most influential anthropologists in the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Richard Wrangham explores how humans evolved to be both docile and murderous at the same time.

Title: Your true self
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Betty Sue Flowers, James Tartaglia
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning writer Joanna Kavena, Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas Betty Sue Flowers and philosopher and jazz-musician James Tartaglia debate the notion of the authentic self. Bahar Gholipour hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: We're told to find our authentic selves, but many neuroscientists and philosophers challenge the very existence of a single true self. Should we aim to escape from the self, as Buddhists and more collectivist cultures have proposed? Or is this a dangerous notion that perpetuates dominant authority and undermines individual and personal growth?

Title: The blame game
Guests & Speakers: Guy Standing, Claire Ogley, Lola Young, David Livingstone Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Is blame a useful concept in the modern world? Join Baroness Young, development economicst Guy Standing, moral philosopher David Livingstone Smith and Claire Ogley, head of campaigns, policy and research at the Vegan society. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
Synopsis & Topics: In this thought-provoking debate, experts discuss the effectiveness of blaming induviduals, businesses, or governments when it comes to addressing societal issues such as climate change.

Title: On the nature of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Iain McGilchrist is a former Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford. He is committed to the idea that the mind and brain can be understood only by seeing them in the broadest possible context, that of the whole of our physical and spiritual existence. Rowan Williams is the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, and is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Rowan Williams and Iain McGilchrist in this though-provoking conversation as they explore the nature of meaning, and why we should move beyond the assumptions of a materialist worldview.

Title: Overcoming opposition
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is a Professor in the Department of Social Policy at the London School of Economics and Political Science, where he holds a Chair in Behavioural Science.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch Paul Dolan examine the origins of division in society as he unpacks norms and held beliefs from both sides of the political divide.

Title: Beyond the boundary
Guests & Speakers: Lisa Miller, Nick Lane, Paul Bickley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Lisa Miller, New York Times Bestseller and professor of Clinical Psychology, Paul Bickley, head of research at Theos and Nick Lane, professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Is there life after death? This debate explores the concept of the afterlife and discusses religious, spiritual and biological perspectives on what happens after we die.

Title: Rhetoric and reality
Guests & Speakers: Betty Sue Flowers, Nolen Gertz, Joscha Bach
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of applied philosophy at the University of Twente. He is the author of a number of books including Nihilism and Technology. Betty Sue Flowers is Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas at Austin. She pioneered the modern, psychological appreciation of ancient myths alongside Joseph Campbell. Joscha Bach is an AI researcher for MIT Media Lab and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics, where he explores new frontiers in cognitive architectures and mental representation. Katie Robertson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Does language accurately describe reality or are we being lied to? If we acknowledge the power of language in forming perspectives how can we make sense of the world around us?

Title: The future of psychedelic research and therapy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Nutt is the director of the Neuropsychopharmacology Unit in the Division of Brain Sciences at Imperial College, London and the author of six books, including most recently Psychedelics: The revolutionary drugs that could change your life.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Professor David Nutt as he explores the current state of the field and how these substances could revolutionise the way we treat mental health.

Title: The Contraception Delusion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Güneş Taylor is an award-winning geneticist and pioneer of public engagement in her field. She is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute where her research predominantly focuses on the genetic formation of ovaries and testes.
Synopsis & Topics: For centuries, humans have sought ways to separate the act of love from its potential consequences. Dr. Güneş Taylor delves deep into the intriguing world of hormonal contraception, shedding light on its past, present, and future. Curious about where reproduction is headed in our ever-evolving society?

Title: Why Is There Anything At All?
Synopsis & Topics: Why is there a world, a cosmos, something, anything instead of absolutely nothing at all? If nothing existed, there would be, well, ‘nothing’ to explain. To have anything existing demands some kind of explanation. Of all the big questions, this is the biggest. Why anything? Why not nothing? What can we learn from the absence of nothing? This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth

Title: Hilary Lawson on Closure
Synopsis & Topics: English philosopher Hilary Lawson discusses his book, Closure: A Story of Everything, a text that develops a comprehensive system of non-realist metaphysics. This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth.

Title: Are There Other Dimensions?
Synopsis & Topics: Extra dimensions—beyond length, width, height—seem like the stuff of science fiction. What would extra dimensions be like? Is time the fourth dimension? Does string theory require ten or eleven dimensions? Could deep reality be so strange? And, anyway, why would we care?This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth.

Title: Is Mathematics Invented or Discovered?
Synopsis & Topics: Mathematics describes the real world of atoms and acorns, stars and stairs, with remarkable precision. So is mathematics invented by humans just like chisels and hammers and pieces of music? Or is mathematics discovered—always out there, somewhere, like mysterious islands waiting to be found? Whatever mathematics is will help define reality itself. This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth.

Title: Guesses, errors and economics
Guests & Speakers: Guy Standing, Gillian Tett, Richard Werner
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Gillian Tett, US editor of the Financial Times, Guy Standing, professor of development at SOAS and UBI advocate, and Richard Werner, economist renowned for coining 'quantitative easing'. Hosted by Linda Yueh.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we ever make economic accurate economic predictions? Or is our dominant theory fundamentally outmoded? Join Guy Standing, Richard Werner and Gillian Tett as they search for truth in a uncertain world.

Title: What are Breakthroughs in Science?
Synopsis & Topics: What are specific signs of breakthroughs in physics and biology? Breakthroughs as new ways of thinking, new systems of thought, new perspectives for seeing the world. What distinguishes breakthroughs from normal good science? What drives breakthroughs? How is science driven by breakthroughs? This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth.

Title: Stephon Alexander on the Fear of a Black Universe
Synopsis & Topics: Stephon Alexander, cosmologist and professor of theoretical physics at Brown University, discusses his most recent book, Fear of a Black Universe, an important guide to both science and society. This interview was hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn and produced by Closer To Truth.

Title: Manners maketh man
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Scott-Brown, Grafton Tanner, Billy Bragg
Synopsis & Topics: In an age of increasing hostility, is the decline of politeness eroding the fabric of our society? As debates rage on its relevance, should we revive civility as a cornerstone of culture or dismiss it as outdated control?

Title: Free will is not an illusion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Denis Noble is a renowned physiologist and one of the pioneers of Systems Biology. He is Emeritus Professor of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University. Noble is known in his field for developing the first viable mathematical model of the working heart in 1960.
Synopsis & Topics: While determining what kind of free will are worth having occupies the philosophical realm, join world-renowned physiologist Denis Noble as he outlines a way in which physiological processes can enable the only free will worth having.

Title: The quest for freedom
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: As the leader of the Rights Lab's Law and Policy Programme at the University of Nottingham, Dr. Katarina Schwarz is dedicated to advancing our understanding of the legal and policy frameworks that govern anti-slavery efforts worldwide.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Dr. Katarina Schwarz as she explores the implications of modern day slavery and how we can work towards ending it.

Title: After knowledge
Guests & Speakers: Tommy J. Curry, Rupert Sheldrake, Suchitra Sebastian
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher of race Tommy Curry, theoretical physicist Suchitra Sebastian and outspoken scientist Rupert Sheldrake debate the limits of what we can know. Hosted by Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: How can we reconcile the quest for objective knowledge in Western thought with the view that all knowledge is shaped by personal and cultural factors? Is objective knowledge attainable or should more emphasis be placed on understanding the implications of individual belief systems?

Title: Ancient traits in the modern world
Guests & Speakers: Sunetra Gupta, Anders Sandberg, Subrena Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford Sunetra Gupta, research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford Anders Sandberg and philosopher of biology Subrena Smith debate whether or not our neurobiology inadequate to deal with the challenges of the 21st century. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: We see the remarkable evolution of the human brain as one of the driving factors behind our success as a species.  Our neurobiology evolved though to solve challenges in a drastically different world than we find ourselves in today.   Might our evolved traits, once advantageous, now be our Achilles heel? Can we find ways to change our behaviour before it is too late?

Title: Matt Hancock Unveiled: Regrets and Reflections
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matt Hancock is a British politician who served as Secretary of State for Health and Social Care from 2018 to 2021, and as Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport in 2018 for six months. A member of the Conservative Party, he has been Member of Parliament for West Suffolk since 2010. He served as Health Secretary during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom and oversaw the subsequent rollout of the UK's vaccination programme.
Synopsis & Topics: Matt Hancock discusses his roots, regrets and reflections on everything from cryptocurrency to the pandemic, the Ukraine War to dyslexia awareness.

Title: Surplus happiness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: World-renowned philosopher and cultural critic, Slavoj Žižek, warns us about the implications of surplus happiness and argues why we should stay away from it.

Title: Me, my world, and I
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Hannah Critchlow, Gary Lachman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Renowned musician and author on mysticism and the occult Gary Lachman, internationally aclaimed neuroscientist Hannah Critchlow, philosophy professor and expert of the senses Barry Smith debate collective experience versus subjectivity. Matt O'Dowd hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is experience subjective? We've historically considered it so in western society. But is experience actually always shared and mediated through others? Or is collective experience and behaviour a dangerous idea that can be used by authority to impose subservience?

Title: Diplomacy, deception, and disaster
Guests & Speakers: Malcolm Rifkind, Janne Teller, Laurie Bristow, David Omand
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Foreign Secretary Malcom Rifkind, GCHQ director David Omand, Ambassador Laurie Bristow and Novellist Janne Teller debate the future of diplomacy and conflict. Hosted by Sasha Polakow-Suransky.
Synopsis & Topics: Is diplomacy the art of strategic ambiguity? This has been the West's approach with Tawian for the better half of the past century. But in light lf the Russian invasion of Ukraine, ambiguity in foreign affairs looks mistaken. Is the West making a fundemental error with Taiwan that risks catastrophe?

Title: In Conversation: Iain McGilchrist and Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Iain McGilchrist is an Oxford scholar and polymath whose 'clarity, lucidity and almost hypnotically compelling style' has seen him rise to prominence as a world-wide lecturer and public intellectual.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychiatrist, writer and former Oxford scholar Iain Mcgilchrist is joined by post-post modern philosopher Hilary Lawson to explore the nature of the mind, our ability to access truth, and the risks of delusional thinking from the left brain.

Title: Technology  is not neutral
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr Stephanie Hare is a researcher, broadcaster and speaker on technology, politics, and history.Stephanie has worked as a Principal Director at Accenture Research and a senior analyst for Western Europe at Oxford Analytica.
Synopsis & Topics: We can think of technology as a neutral tool. But doing so misses how technology reflects ethical dilemmas in society. Join Stephanie Hare as she explores the intersection of technology and ethics.

Title: The future is quantum AI
Synopsis & Topics: Join physicist Gerard Milburn as he explores the connection between quantum physics and AI. When computing is freed from traditional coding, a whole new array of possibilities arise.

Title: Philosophy at war
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Paul Horwich, Lisa Randall
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Theoretical physicist Lisa Randall, post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson and philosopher of science Paul Horwich debate the connection between science, philosophy and truth. Hosted by Maria Balaska.
Synopsis & Topics: Are science and philosophy destined to be opposites or are they complementary fields, with either in isolation being wholly inadequete to answer the questions of our times? Join Lisa Randall, Hilary Lawson and Paul Horwich as they tackle this pressing question. Hosted by Maria Balaska.

Title: The importance of bad art
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emma Sulkowicz is a sexual assault activist, artist and political commentator.
Synopsis & Topics: What role does the moral and political content play in the way we value art? What relationship can art play in the process of healing? Political activist and artist Emma Sulkowicz explores.

Title: Cities of the future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lucelia Rodrigues is one of the world’s foremost experts on sustainability. She is Chair of Sustainable and Resilient Cities in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Nottingham.
Synopsis & Topics: Can improving our cities be the solution to climate change? Join Nottingham University Professor Lucelia Rodriguez as she sets out her vision for the cities of the future.

Title: Beyond reasonable doubt
Guests & Speakers: Peter Tatchell, Harriet Wistrich, Emma Bryson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: LGBT rights activist Peter Tatchell, lawyer Harriet Wistricht and advocate for justice reform Emma Bryson explore the burden of proof. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: Beyond reasonable doubt' has been adopted onthe Blackstone principle that 'it is better that ten guilty persons escape than one innocent suffer'. But is it better that a hundred guilty persons escape? Can punishing the innocent ever be worth it?

Title: The game of life
Guests & Speakers: Slavoj Žižek, Steven Bonnell, Lisa Miller
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-leading philosopher Slavoj Žižek, radical internet personality Steven Bonnell, and bestselling author and psychologist Lisa Miller grapple with the gamification of life. Hosted by pioneering journalist Myriam François.
Synopsis & Topics: Workplaces, dating lives, education and even friendships are being packaged as games. But critics argue games distort life and empty it of meaning. Do we need to end the relentless gamification of life? Or have games always been with us, for the very good reason that they are a powerful motivator for action?

Title: The reality beyond spacetime
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Donald Hoffman is an American cognitive psychologist working at the University of California, Irvine. He is making waves with a new theory suggesting that, instead of presenting reality as it "really is", our perception is like a desktop interface enabling us to use reality effectively.
Synopsis & Topics: Donald Hoffman claims spacetime is not fundamental. So, what lies beneath spacetime, and can we know about it?

Title: The best and worst of all possible worlds
Guests & Speakers: Tasneem Zehra Husain, Ben Burgis, Paul Horwich
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher of physics Paul Horwich, philosopher and author Ben Burgis and theoretical physicist Tasneem Zehra Husain debate the continued attraction of many worlds theory. Hosted by Niki Seth-Smith.
Synopsis & Topics: We are attracted by the idea of multiple or alternate realities. Is the idea of possible worlds credible or fundamentally misguided? Can we learn from it?

Title: Capitalism and the climate
Guests & Speakers: Helen Czerski, Troy Vettese, Rebecca Henderson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Join Rebecca Henderson, Harvard MBA's socialist, Troy Vettese, economic historian and author and Helen Czerski, pioneering physicist of the natural world as they debate the connection between capitalism and the climate. Hosted by Linda Yueh, Oxford professor of economics.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the link between climate change and capitalism essential, and the claims of bankers and conservatives to be in favour of reducing emissions insincere and illusory? Join Harvard MBA's socialist Rebecca Henderson, economic historian Troy Vettese, and pioneering physicist Helen Czerski debate the connection between capitalism and the climate.

Title: Searching for justice
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jesse Norman is a Conservative Party politician who has served as MP since 2010. He served as Financial Secretary to the Treasury from 2019 to 2021. His book Compassionate Conservatism has been described as the "handbook to Cameronism".
Synopsis & Topics: The Covid pandemic compels us to ponder the concept of a fair society. Harvard philosopher John Rawls' theories, such as his "veil of ignorance" and "difference principle," provide crucial insights for understanding and implementing justice. However, as illustrated by Jesse Norman, MP and former Financial Secretary to the Treasury, Covid also provokes challenging queries about the practicality of Rawls' theories and our image of a truly just society.

Title: Why the rational believe the irrational
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society, the editor-in-chief of its magazine Skeptic, and a Presidential Fellow at Chapman University, where he teaches Skepticism 101.
Synopsis & Topics: World-famous sceptic, Michael Shermer, presents an overarching approach to conspiracy theories and reveals why rational people fall into irrational belief.

Title: The fantasy of fame
Guests & Speakers: Polly Vernon, Stefan Simanowitz, Will Storr
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Al Jazeera's royal correspondant Stefan Simanowitz, Grazia columnist Polly Vernon and award-winning author Will Storr take celebrity to trial. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: While fame used to be a secondary product of success in a given field, now it is a goal in its own right and the key to wider success. The current generation pursues individual fame, with 86% of young people aspiring to be influencers. Is our focus on celebrity and fame destroying culture? Should we reclaim the value of the work over the individual, the ads and the social media followings?

Title: Democracy in the dock
Guests & Speakers: Jesse Norman, Thangam Debbonaire, Ruth Kinna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political philosopher Ruth Kinna, leading Conservative Party politician Jesse Norman and leading Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire debate the dire state of liberal democracy. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Democracy is in trouble. Many argue the system has created a highly divisive and potentially violent culture, with wild claims, undeliverable promises and leaders of little or sometimes no experience trying to run highly complex economies. Is the current form of liberal democracy fundamentally flawed? Could it be reformed?  Or is it time to recognise western democracy as a marvel of Enlightenment principles that should be nurtured?

Title: Consciousness and ChatGPT
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Tartaglia is a trailblazing philosopher and the author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: GODS AND TITANS. His main interest is in understanding and enhancing our awareness of the nature of philosophical inquiry, which for him centres on the question of the meaning of life.
Synopsis & Topics: Can ChatGPT ever be conscious? Join philosopher James Tartaglia in exploring how we confuse scientific and philosophical accounts of consciousness.

Title: The danger and desire of the frontier
Guests & Speakers: Cory Doctorow, Nolen Gertz, Bahar Gholipour
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Assistant Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente Nolan Geertz, renowned science fiction author, activist, journalist and blogger Cory Doctorow and leading New York-based journalist and neuroscientist Bahar Gholipour discuss the real goal is a technological journey into the unknown. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the global space race a fundamental mistake?  Critics argue the human race is no safer on another planet that is barren, inhospitable and which will itself soon be a focus of competition and potential conflict. Should we conclude that the desire to travel to an extraordinarily hostile location is not driven by a higher motive but simply because we might in principle be able to do it? Is the pursuit of new frontiers a detrement to our current geoplotical environment?

Title: Virtue ethics and the mob
Guests & Speakers: Simon Blackburn, Peter Tatchell, Sophie Scott-Brown
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Prolific moral philosopher Simon Blackburn, intellectual historian Sophie Scott Brown and renowned human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell debate the value of appearing ethical in modern society. Hosted by Rana Mitter
Synopsis & Topics: Prolific moral philosopher Simon Blackburn, intellectual historian Sophie Scott Broan and renowned human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell debate the value of appearing ethical in modern society. Hosted by Rana Mitter.

Title: How to philosophize behind bars
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Andy West is senior specialist with the Philosophy Foundation and philosopher in residence at HMP Pentonville, London. He is the author of The Life Inside: A Memoir of Prison, Family and Philosophy (2022).
Synopsis & Topics: For the last few years the debate about prison abolition has been steadily entering the mainstream. But is it morally desirable or politically plausible to knock down prisons? And what would take their place? Guiding us through these questions of crime and punishment will be Andy West, author of The Life Inside: A Memoir of Prison, Family and Philosophy.

Title: Psychoanalysis and revolution
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ian Parker is a psychoanalyst and Emeritus Professor of Management in the School of Business at the University of Leicester.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Ian Parker as he explores how psychoanalysis, personal liberation and social transformation are intimately connected.

Title: An unprecedented experiment with money
Guests & Speakers: Peter Schiff, Carmen Reinhart, Brad DeLong
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Entrepreneur Peter Schiff, World Bank Economist Carmen Reinhart and Economic Historian Brad de Long debate how our response to the financial crisis has impacted our current economy. Hosted by Gillian Tett.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we conclude that QE was a decade long mistake and central bankers do not know what they are doing? Entrepreneur Peter Schiff, World Bank Economist Camilla Reinhart and Economic Historian Brad de Long debate. Hosted by Gillian Tett.

Title: The end of everything
Guests & Speakers: Brian Greene, Sabine Hossenfelder, Michael Shermer, Eric Weinstein
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-leading string theorist Brian Greene, famed historian of science Michael Shermer, groundbreaking particle physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and radical mathematical physicist and podcast host Eric Weinstein lock horns over whether it's possible to find a theory of everything. Astronomer Royal for Scotland, Catherine Heymans, hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Brian Greene, Sabine Hossenfelder, Michael Shermer, Eric Weinstein debate the possibility of a theory of eveything. Astronomer Royal Catherine Heymans hosts.

Title: Desiring and being desired
Guests & Speakers: Peter Tatchell, Katherine Angel, Catherine Hakim
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Hakim is a pioneering British social scientist and author. She is perhaps best known for her groundbreaking book ‘Erotic Capital’, and she is currently Professorial Research Fellow at Civitas, the London think tank. Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Katherine Angel is an academic and writer. She is the author of numerous works, most recently ‘Tomorrow Sex Will Be Good Again’, published in 2021, which received much critical acclaim and widespread international coverage.
Synopsis & Topics: Fifty years of feminism and increasing status and influence for women, it is nevertheless still seen as the norm for men to be the ones seeking sex and women to be those who consent. Is the assertion of sexual desire key to power relationships between the sexes? Or is it irrelevant?

Title: Politics is broken
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Describing herself as a "northern European socialist", Thangam supports "fettered capitalism".
Synopsis & Topics: Is representative democracy fading away? Shadow Leader of the House of Commons Thangam Debbonaire argues that politics is broken and offers a way to fix it.

Title: Taking leave of reason
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Rebecca Roache, Rory Sutherland
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning English novelist Joanna Kavenna, renowned public intellectual Rory Sutherland, philosopher and senior Lecturer Rebecca Roache debate whether we need reason as much as we think we do in an increasingly chaotic modern age. Bahar Gholipour hosts.
Synopsis & Topics:
Recent studies show that reason does not lead to more successful outcomes in business or personal relationships. Should we abandon the idea of behaving rationally altogether?
Or does reason have another role to play?

Title: Anarchy and democracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian based at the University of East Anglia with research interests in modern European political thought and the history of education. She is the author of The Histories of Raphael Samuel: A Portrait of a People’s Historian and Colin Ward and the Art of Everyday Anarchy.
Synopsis & Topics: Does democracy provide fertile ground for populism and could anarchy offer a better way forward? Sophie Scott-Brown explores

Title: The trouble with string theory
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Brian Greene, Eric Weinstein, Tasneem Zehra Husain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel prize-winning physicist Roger Penrose, renowned string theorist and best selling author Brian Greene, groundbreaking scientist Tasneem Zehra Husain, and polymath mathematician Eric Weinstein debate the cosmological theory.
