Hosted by philosopher of physics Katie Robertson.
Synopsis & Topics: String Theory has dominated physics for 30 years, but critics argues it's been delivered. Is it time to abandon the field once heralded as the coveted theory of everything.

Title: Demystifying psychedelics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matthew Johnson is one of the world’s most published scientists in the field of psychedelics with prior appearances on the Lex Friedman Podcast, 60 Minutes and National Geographic.
Synopsis & Topics: World-leading psychedelic researcher Matthew Johnson lifts the lid on the science behind psychedelic experience.

Title: Beyond the big bang
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bjørn Ekeberg is a celebrated philosopher of science whose interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He is the author of erudite, Metaphysical Experiments.
Synopsis & Topics: Has cosmology gone astray, and might the entire scientific paradigm be wrong? Bjørn Ekeberg makes a radical case for a new way of seeing the universe

Title: The weapon that failed
Guests & Speakers: Bronwen Maddox, Michael Clarke, Simon Jenkins
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Commentator, journalist and historian Simon Jenkins, director and CEO of think tank Chatham House, Bronwen Maddox and Chief security and defence analyst for Sky News Michael Clarke debate the geopolitical soundness of sanctions.
Synopsis & Topics: Sanctions imposed against Russia were supposed to hobble their economy and halt their war effort. Neither has come to pass.

Title: Anonymity: the dream and the nightmare
Guests & Speakers: Hugh Tomlinson, Victoria Baines, Stephen Kinsella
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Stephen Kinsella is founder of Clean Up the Internet. He is a competition lawyer with a longstanding interest in human rights, digital technology, and democracy. Victoria Baines is part of the organisation Demos. Her interests cover content moderation, digital labour, datafication and blockchain technologies. Hugh Tomlinson is a barrister, famed for his role in the UK MP’s parliamentary expenses scandal and in the News of The World phone-hacking case.
Synopsis & Topics: Anonymity was thought to be the internet's greatest gift, providing a voice to those oppressed by regimes or institutions. But with the rise of online bullying and a lack of accountability, has this dream turned into a nightmare?

Title: The dark matter myth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pavel Kroupa is professor of astrophysics at University of Bonn, in Germany, where he heads the Stellar Populations and Dynamics research group.
Synopsis & Topics: Dark matter has been a mainstream concept in astrophysics for a number of decades. In this interview, astrophysics professor Pavel Kroupa exposes the damning evidence against dark matter and proposes an alternative way of looking at the universe.

Title: The crisis of ageing
Synopsis & Topics: Our rapidly ageing population poses multiple threats to our society, from healthcare and inequality to housing and democracy itself. Join Aaron Bastani as he argues for an urgent overhaul of political policy to deal with the crisis of ageing.

Title: Revolutionising our idea of the brain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Baron-Cohen is a pioneering psychologist whose work on autism has revolutionised the field of developmental psychopathology. As part of his empathizing-systemizing theory, Simon famously claimed that autism is an extreme of the male brain.
Synopsis & Topics: Pioneering psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen puts forward the case that neurodiversity is the next frontier in our understanding of the brain.

Title: The rise and rise of populism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Howard is the former Leader of the Conservative Party. Prior to his leadership in the early 200s, he earned the trust of Conservative leaders Margaret Thatcher and John Major, holding prestigious cabinet positions in their governments including Secretary of State for Employment, Secretary of State for the Environment and Home Secretary.
Synopsis & Topics: What are the greatest challenges facing political leaders today? Can the governing elite address growing resentment and the rise of populism?

Title: How I changed my mind about truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Blackburn is a philosopher at Cambridge University known for his work on meta-ethics. He has published over a dozen books on various philosophical issues and has appeared on shows such as Radio 4's The Moral Maze and PBS's Closer to Truth.
Synopsis & Topics: In this eye-opening interview, Cambridge philosopher Simon Blackburn explores whether we can objective morality without metaphysics, how we should navigate moral discussions, and where Richard Rorty went wrong.

Title: The obscure, the banal, and the magical
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Bence Nanay, Hannah Sullivan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: T. S. Eliot prize-winning poet Hannah Sullivan, professor of philosophy and film critic Bence Nanay and novelist Janne Teller debate whether poetry has lost its way.
Synopsis & Topics: Has poetry lost its way? Once an art form that was elevated above others, poetry has arguably been cheapened in the 21st century by declining interest and social media. Should we reclaim poetry as a profound artistic tool? Or accept that it is more democratised and down-to-earth than it has ever been?

Title: The good, the bad, and the ignored
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Scott-Brown, Peter Singer, Julian Baggini
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary moral philosopher Peter Singer (joining us live from Australia), eminent philosopher Julian Baggini and provocative biographer Sophie Scott-Brown clash over morality. Hosted by author Robert Rowland Smith.
Synopsis & Topics: Do our conversations on morality focus too much on agency? What about the good and bad we cause through inaction? Should we adopt a new focus on the morality of inaction, or will this risk undermining morality completely?

Title: AI consciousness cannot exist
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Markus is an internationally acclaimed philosopher and holds the Chair in Epistemology, Modern and Contemporary Philosophy at the University of Bonn. He is the Director of the Center for Science and Thought as well as Chairman of the International Centre for Philosophy NRW.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Markus Gabriel as he explores the problem of consciousness and the implications it may have for the future of machine intelligence.

Title: Life and Death on the Front Line
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anna Kent is a humanitarian aid worker, NHS nurse and midwife. After receiving a Nursing Master's Degree from the University of Nottingham, she completed a Diploma in Tropical Nursing in London and joined Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) in 2007. She gained her First Degree in Midwifery in 2010 and has worked as a midwife across the world, including in South Sudan, Haiti, Bangladesh and the UK.
Synopsis & Topics: Join humanitarian worker and author Anna Kent as discusses delivering babies in war zones, personal trauma and her vision for the future of healthcare.

Title: The secrets of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge working on the LHCb experiment at CERN. He is the author of How To Make An Apple Pie From Scratch: In Search of the Recipe for Our Universe.
Synopsis & Topics: Physicists were intrigued last year by the possible discovery of an entirely new force from the Muon G-2 experiment. Jon CERN physicist Harry Cliff, as he explores the secrets of our universe.

Title: A world by any other name
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Arif Ahmed, Ruth Kempson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher Arif Ahmed, radical linguist Ruth Kempson, and philosopher and author of Closure, Hilary Lawson put language to the test. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Language is seen as central to our understanding of the world. But can language provide a definitive description of the world? Or is language an insoluble puzzle that will always fail to capture reality?

Title: How to find and make sense of happiness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the London School of Economics and Political Science. Professor Dolan's research focusses on the measurement of happiness, its causes and consequences, and the implications for public policy. He is the author of books: Happiness by Design and Happy Ever After.
Synopsis & Topics: What makes for a happy life? And what can we do individually and societally to get there? Join happiness expert and LSE Professor of Behavioural Science, Paul Dolan, as he explores how we can achieve happiness by design

Title: The psychology of bad habits
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susan Michie is Professor of Health Psychology at University College, London.
Synopsis & Topics: Do we really control our own behaviour and choices? Join SAGE adviser and UCL Professor Susan Michie as she uses data to show us how to challenge our most ingrained habits.

Title: A better tomorrow
Guests & Speakers: Thangam Debbonaire, Michael Bociurkiw, Shaun Bailey
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Isabel Hilton is the founder and and editor of chinadialogue.net, and is a former editor-in-chief of opendemocracy.net. As CEO, she oversees China Dialogue's efforts to stoke discussion about the environment between Chinese and non-Chinese sources Shaun Bailey AM is a distinguished politician and former journalist who famously led the 2021 Conservative campaign in London as the party's candidate for Mayor of London. Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Michael Bocirkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst whose been on the frontline teams at many international humanitarian organizations. He is the esteemed author of Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good.
Synopsis & Topics: The majority of Westerners believe the world is getting worse when asked. Yet in key metrics such as extreme poverty and life expectancy, things are improving globally. Is our pessimism an error? Or is progress driven by dissatisfaction with the status quo?

Title: Getting everything, losing everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Maria Balaska is currently a research fellow at the University of Hertfordshire and at Åbo Akademi University. Anders Sandberg is a researcher, popular science debater, trans-humanist and author of Superhuman: Exploring Human Enhancement from 600 BCE to 2050. Massimo Pigliucci is a philosophy professor at the City College of New York and former co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast. His research interests include the Philosophy of Science and the Philosophy of Biology. Mazviita Chirimuuta is a Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Edinburgh. She is a self-described techno-pessimist and anti-transhumanist.
Synopsis & Topics: Virtual reality was once the stuff of science fiction, but is now a widely available technology. Its proponents suggest living more in the digital world will allow more people to access experiences currently only available to a few. Is a digital society an inevitable part of our future? Or this a dystopian nightmare that threatens human connection and vitality?

Title: The demons of thermodynamics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Katie Robertson is a research fellow and cutting edge philosopher of physics at the University of Birmingham. Her research focuses on the role that entropy plays in black holes.
Synopsis & Topics: Thermodynamics and the problem of entropy has puzzled scientists for many years. Join philosopher of physics Katie Robertson as she explores how we might exorcise the demons of thermodynamics.

Title: Democracy is dead
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Calvin Robinson is a political commentator, journalist, policy advisor and campaigner who is a senior fellow at the research institute Policy Exchange. Robinson worked as a secondary school teacher and became a video games journalist. He is a regular contributor to The Daily Telegraph and the Daily Mail.
Synopsis & Topics: In the wake of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the West has signalled a renewed commitment to democracy and freedom. But will this be enough to halt the rise of global authoritarianism?

Title: The seduction of thought
Guests & Speakers: Andy West, Steve Taylor, Miranda Keeling
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bestselling author Miranda Keeling, psychologist Steve Taylor and prison philosopher Andy West decide: to think, or not to think? Janne Teller hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Ever since the Enlightenment, Western culture has valued reason and thought highly. We spent most of our time puzzling, planning or pondering. But is this is a mistake? Might culture be better off were it to, in Nietzsche's words, 'free itself from the seduction of words and thought'?

Title: The strangeness of the universe
Guests & Speakers: Bjørn Ekeberg, Rupert Sheldrake, Sabine Hossenfelder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Influential scientist Rupert Sheldrake, prominent physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and esteemed philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg get to grips with whether the universe is stranger than we can imagine. Johnjoe McFadden hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Niels Bohr suggested the universe is stranger than we could possibly imagine. Was he right? Will science and philosophy ever be able to accurately capture the fundamental laws of the universe? Or should we accept that the mysteries of the universe will always transcend human understanding?

Title: Logic for the left
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ben Burgis is a philosophy professor at Morehouse University Perimeter College, a columnist for Jacobin Magazine and Arc Digital Media, and the co-host of the Dead Pundits Society. He also used to have a regular segment on The Michael Brooks Show called "the Debunk." Burgis is the author of several books including' Give Them an Argument: Logic for the Left' and 'Christopher Hitchens: What He Got Right, How He Went Wrong, and Why He Still Matters'.
Synopsis & Topics: In an age where the left are regularly accused of priotising feelings over facts, can the left reclaim logic? Join philosopher and Marxist Ben Burgis as he debunks contemporary political myths.

Title: The evolution of war
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Known for his trailbrazing research on cooperation, aggression, altruism, and war, Bonaventura Majolo is Professor of Social Evolution at the University of Lincoln.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the urge to go to war part of humanity's evolutionary make-up? Join trailblazing researcher Bonaventura Majolo as he explores whether the propensity for war is in our DNA.

Title: Forbidden Fruit
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Louise Perry, Zoe Strimpel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist Zoe Strimpel, radical social theorist Myriam François and writer Louise Perry fight over forbidden fruit. Hosted by Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: We've never talked so openly about sex. But is this frankness devaluing the very things that make sex appealing? Are romance, intimacy and mystery undermined in a society that is so casual about sex?

Title: Fact-checking the fact-checkers
Guests & Speakers: Stephanie Hare, Paul Mason, Freddie Sayers
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Renowned journalist Paul Mason, author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare and UnHerd editor Freddie Sayers debate the facts behind the facts. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In a world where truth is always in doubt, how should we approach organisations that present themselves as fact-checkers? Should we recognise that nations and individuals always embed a biased perspective? Or is it possible to promote a public discourse rooted in fact?

Title: How philosophy got lost
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities at the University of London, visiting professor at New York University and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. He is the author of several books, including The Sublime Object of Ideology, The Parallax View, Living in the End Times and Heaven in Disorder.
Synopsis & Topics: Globally renowned philosopher Slavoj Žižek takes us on a whirlwind tour of continental philosophy, Hegel's insights into contemporary political crises, the Covid-19 pandemic and how philosophy is like falling in love.

Title: Material girls
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
Synopsis & Topics: The conversation surrounding transgender rights is often divisive and unproductive. Join philosopher Kathleen Stock as she sets out her position on gender and biology, and how trans activists and feminist can unite for a less polarised future.

Title: Beyond the Darkness
Guests & Speakers: Francesca Chadha-Day, Bjørn Ekeberg, Pavel Kroupa
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Trailblazing philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg, theoretical physicist Francesca Chadha-Day and influential astrophysicist Pavel Kroupa explore the many mysteries of dark matter. John-Joe McFadden hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Dark matter has been put forward by scientists as a way to understand previously unexplainable aspects of our cosmos. But after much searching, scientists have not been able to discover dark matter particles. Is it time to radically reassess the dark matter paradigm? Or is a breakthrough discovery just around the corner?

Title: Truth, delusion and psychedelic reality
Guests & Speakers: Julian Baggini, Eileen Hall, James Rucker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: KCL psychiatrist James Rucker, philosopher Julian Baggini, and creative director and artist Eileen Hall debate psychedelics and science. Hosted by leading psychiatrist Mark Salter.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychedelics are being put forward as a potentially radical treatment for mental illness. But is this short-sighted? Will psychedelics replace mental illness with a distorted view of reality? Or can they help those suffering break out of unhelpful psychological paradigms?

Title: There is no Planet B
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mike Berners-Lee is a pre-eminent expert in carbon footprinting and Professor and Fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University. He is also the director and principal consultant at Small World Consulting and the author of three books, including There Is No Planet B: A Handbook for the Make or Break Years.
Synopsis & Topics: Acclaimed writer and researcher Mike Berners-Lee tackles the most common misconceptions surrounding climate change and argues for how we might achieve structural change.

Title: The science of uncertainty with Tim Palmer
Synopsis & Topics: We have all grown accustomed to living with uncertainty in recent years. But what are the scientific and mathematic forces governing uncertainty? Join acclaimed professor Tim Palmer as he argues that understanding uncertainty is crucial to progress.

Title: Society 2.0
Guests & Speakers: Ben Burgis, Thangam Debbonaire, Nemone Metaxas
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Member of the Shadow Cabinet House Thangam Debbonaire, Radio 6 DJ and psychotherapist Nemone Metaxas and Marxist philosopher Ben Burgis explore the undervalued people in our society. Hosted by Mary-Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: The pandemic opened our eyes to the jobs society can't live without. In the wake of Covid-19, should we prioritise key workers and abandon the idea that professional and managerial jobs are the best paid? Or should we still reward university education and a white-collar career with the highest wages?

Title: Being ourselves and being with others
Guests & Speakers: Stefan Priebe, Janne Teller, Sophie Ward
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Critically-acclaimed writer Janne Teller, world leading psychologist and psychiatrist Stefan Priebe, and actress-writer and Booker Prize nominee Sophie Ward debate the lures of loneliness. Hosted by renowned journalist Elaine Glaser.
Synopsis & Topics: In recent decades we have emphasised the importance of individualism, self-expression and self-sufficiency. Yet studies suggest we aren't happier for it. Is it time to let go of our attachment to independence and embrace a more communal way of living? Or is this a naive view which ignores how unique we all are?

Title: Why Dawkins is wrong
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Oxford Professor and one of the pioneers of Systems Biology, Noble developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart in 1960.
Synopsis & Topics: The sequencing of genetic information was expected to usher in a breakthrough in medical cures for illnesses, yet this hasn't happened. Join esteemed biologist Denis Noble as he argues our approach to biology is the wrong way round.

Title: In conversation with Peter Tatchell and Bobbi Pickard
Synopsis & Topics: Legendary activist Peter Tatchell and trans rights campaigner Bobbi Pickard unpick the fiery debate over transgender rights, and offer a path for society to move forward.

Title: The ignorance of experts
Guests & Speakers: Ellen Clarke, Julian Baggini, Ben Burgis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of How The World Thinks Julian Baggini, philosopher of biology Ellen Clarke, and radical philosopher Ben Burgis tackle our diminishing trust in experts and what to do about it. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Science is the belief in the ignorance of experts, argued Richard Feynman. Was he right to suggest that science is not a learnt set of facts, but a constantly evolving method of discovering knowledge? Or, in a world under threat from health crises such as Covid-19, do we need to treat science as an authority in order to get the best outcomes?

Title: The accurate, the perfect and the dangerous
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Stephanie Hare, Michael Parker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Futurist Anders Sandberg, Oxford bioethicist Michael Parker and author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare fight for the future of tech, data and AI. Hosted by pioneering economist Linda Yueh.
Synopsis & Topics: We tend to think of data and technology as impartial tools that can deliver us results free from human prejudice. But from sexist chatbots to racist algorithms, it seems our data is always coloured by human fallibility. Do we need to give up on the idea that data is impartial? Or is our technology not yet sophisticated enough to transcend our human flaws?

Title: Are we facing a new world order?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nigel Inkster is the distinguished former director of intelligence for the British Intelligence Service, and now Director of Intelligence Analysis at Enodo Economics.
Synopsis & Topics: Nigel Inkster discusses China's rise as a cyberpower, and who is seizing the upperhand on the world stage

Title: How to see the world through Kafka's eyes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steven Berkoff is an actor, author, playwright, theatre practitioner and theatre director. He is noted for his roles in the James Bond film, ‘Octopussy’, A Clockwork Orange, and The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo. On the stage, he has performed the title roles in Shakespeare’s Hamlet, Richard II and Macbeth. He is recognised for his brand of “Berkovian theatre", which combines elements of physical theatre, total theatre and expressionism.
Synopsis & Topics: Over a century since it was published, how can Kafka's Metamorphosis help us gain insights into the pressures of modernity? Join acclaimed actor and director Steven Berkoff as he helps see the world through Kafka's eyes.

Title: The equality myth
Guests & Speakers: Laurie Penny, Thangam Debbonaire, Louise Perry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist and writer Laurie Penny, Shadow Leader of the Commons, Thangam Debbonaire and campaigner-author Louise Perry try to tip the scales. Hosted by Oxford historian Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Despite advances in women's rights over the last 50 years, many surveys show women's happiness has decreased in this time. Is it time to refocus feminism towards goals of personal fulfilment rather than political equality with men? Or is this reported dissatisfaction itself a sign that women are now empowered to speak out about their lives?

Title: The democracy illusion
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Calvin Robinson, Shabnam Nasimi
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Trailblazing journalist Calvin Robinson, social activist Shabnam Nasimi, and radical journalist Aaron Bastani debate the changing face of democracy in the 21st century. Hosted by Manveen Rana.
Synopsis & Topics: Do politicans matter? Many people across the world feel that change rarely materialises in their ordinary lives, no matter who they vote for. Are politicians the public face for an unnaccountable network of technical decision-makers? Or is this apathetic mindset precisely what the ruling class depend on to sustain their rule?

Title: Head to Head: Philosophy vs Science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics and the Head of School within Mathematical Sciences at University of Southampton. Taylor's research is focussed on string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Julian Baggini is a philosopher, journalist, author and the co-founder of The Philosopher's Magazine. He is the acclaimed author of over 20 works of popular philosophy. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Historically, philosophy and science have been united as complementary methods of investigating life's fundamental questions. But since the Enlightenment the two have drifted apart and even become antagonistic. Join prize-winning physicist Marika Taylor and philosopher Julian Baggini as they discuss the relationship between the two fields.

Title: Deconstructing the art of storytelling
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Danny Robins is an award-winning British writer, broadcaster and journalist. His most recent play, 2:22 A Ghost Story, has received much critical acclaim.
Synopsis & Topics: How do you create great stories that keep your audience hooked? Join three-time Olivier Award-nominated playwright Danny Robbins as he reveals the secrets of effective storytelling

Title: The theory to end all theories
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Peter Woit, Becky Parker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Theoretical physicist Peter Woit, physicist and educator Becky Parker and critic of realism Hilary Lawson test their theories of everything. Hosted by award-winning science documentary filmmaker David Malone.
Synopsis & Topics: Physics' theory of everything was supposed to be just around the corner. Now it looks less likely than ever. Can any scientific theory ever be more than a model?

Title: The key to consciousness
Guests & Speakers: Sam Coleman, Donald Hoffman, Hannah Critchlow
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Revolutionary cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman (joining us live from across the pond), neuroscientist Hannah Critchlow and philosopher Sam Coleman battle to unlock consciousness. Hosted by award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: Modern neuroscience has brought us no closer to solving the mystery of consciousness. Can this puzzle ever be detached from the dichotomy of subject and object?

Title: Rebellion and rebirth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emma Sulkowicz is a performance artist living and working in New York City, most famous for her year-long performance art project Mattress Performance: Carry That Weight where she dragged a mattress around Columbia University in protest at the school’s mishandling of her sexual assault complaint, and becoming one of the faces of the movement against rape culture on college campuses.
Synopsis & Topics: What does it take for a person to heal from sexual trauma, and for society to adequately deal with the issue? Join activist and performance artist Emma Sulkowicz as she discusses her personal journey of rebellion and rebirth.

Title: The future of cosmology with Roger Penrose
Synopsis & Topics: Join Nobel Prize-winning mathematician Roger Penrose and philosopher of science Katie Robertson as they discuss the forces that govern our cosmos and the equations which define our reality.

Title: After happily ever after
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Sophie Fiennes, David Hare
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Academy award nominee David Hare, critically acclaimed writer Janne Teller and director-producer Sophie Fiennes talk endings. Hosted by Barry Smith, Director of the Institute of Philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: We expect closure from our stories. Does this reflect a desire for our fictional worlds to have order when our real one doesn't? Or are non-narrative structures doomed to be alienating and unsuccessful?

Title: Gravitational waves: a new frontier?
Synopsis & Topics: Join world-renowned physicist Paul Davies as he uncovers the importance of gravitational waves and why they might be the answer to some of the most complex problems in physics

Title: Feminism and identity politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning, Ugandan-born author and columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown currently writes for The Independent and The Evening Standard, and is the founder of British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Celebrated journalist and author Yasmin Alibhai-Brow explores whether identity politics and feminism are compatible.

Title: The future of freedom
Guests & Speakers: Julian Baggini, Peter Godfrey-Smith, Sarah Garfinkel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Prolific British writer, philosopher and co-founder of The Philosophers’ Magazine, Julian Baggini, renowned Australian philosopher of science, Peter Godfrey-Smith, and leading British neuroscientist and UCL professor, Sarah Garfinkel, argue about empiricism and its role in determining the existence of free will. Alex O'Connor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: A famed experiment by Libet in the 1980s claimed to demonstrate that free will was an illusion. Despite frequent challenges, the legacy of this idea looms over philosophy. Are we really just pre-programmed biological machines or can we shape our own destinies?

Title: Science fact or science fiction?
Guests & Speakers: Tim Maudlin, Marika Taylor, Harry Cliff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge working on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. A prominent promoter for the public's understanding of physics, Harry is also the author of the popular science book, How To Make An Apple Pie From Scratch. Tim Maudlin is a world leading researcher in the foundations of physics, metaphysics, and logic. He is a Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. Marika Taylor is one of the foremost researchers of string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Having completed her doctoral dissertation under Stephen Hawking, Taylor went onto be Professor of Theoretical Physics and head of Mathematical Physics at the University of Southampton. Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. He is the founding director of the Centre for the Study of Sensess.
Synopsis & Topics: Since the Enlightenment, we have made sure our scientific theories can be tested and produce empirical evidence. But many of today's most popular scientific theories - from the multiverse to string theory - have no way of being empirically tested. Should we conclude that these theories are pure speculation and unscientific? Or is it enough for a theory to be internally coherent?

Title: The enduring trauma of the caste system
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ashwini Deshpande is an Indian economist best known for her papers concerning various topics such as poverty, inequality, regional disparities and gender discrimination. She is currently working as a professor at Ashoka University, and formerly taught at Delhi School of Economics.
Synopsis & Topics: What role does the caste system play in Hindu society? Join Indian economist Ashwini Deshpande as she uncovers the reality of a social system cloaked in mystery for most Westerners.

Title: A tale of truth with Simon Blackburn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Think and Truth: A Guide for the Perplexed , Simon Blackburn has worked to bring philosophy to a wider audience. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge University and Vice President of the British Humanist Association.
Synopsis & Topics: Is there anything as contested as 'the truth'? Join renowned philosopher Simon Blackburn as he explores the difficulty of discerning truth in the modern age, and why pragmatism may be the best approach.

Title: The happiness delusion
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Joanna Kavenna, Paul Dolan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, an independent, self-described radical left-wing alternative media organisation. He is also the author ‘Fully Automated Luxury Communism’. Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and author of the bestselling book ‘Happiness By Design: Finding Pleasure and Purpose in Everyday Life.’ Joanna Kavenna is a multi-award-winning writer. She was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists for her ground-breaking novels including A Field Guide to Reality and Zed. Regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times, History Today, and the London Review of Books, Rana Mitter is Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Should society's main goal be the happiness of its citizens? Should governments put happiness at the centre of their policy-making? Or is obsessing over happiness a counterproductive mistake?

Title: The weaker sex?
Guests & Speakers: Mary Ann Sieghart, Maya Oppenheim, Minna Salami
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist and radio presenter and a former assistant editor of The Times . Her latest book is The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men . Minna Salami is journalist, feminist and author. She has written on the experiences of Nigerian women, the African Diaspora and feminism through her award-winning blog, MsAfropolitan . Her latest book is Sensuous Knowledge . Maya Oppenheim is Women's Correspondent for the Independent and writes on issues of domestic violence, sexual assault, abortion and period poverty. Rana Mitter is a regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times , History Today , and the London Review of Books . He is also a Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at the University of Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: In a post-feminist age, it is normal for women to be considered equal to men is most fields. Yet during war it is still standard for men to fight and for women to stay at home. Is this an understandable reflection of biological differences? Or an outdated patriarchal notion that women need 'defending' by men?

Title: The making of reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics arguing that we close the openness of the world with our thought and language.
Synopsis & Topics: The grand metaphysical narratives we have inherited assume the world is divided into discrete entities, which can we study and define. But what if this approach is wrong? Join post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson as he takes us through his theory of Closure and argues that we 'close' the openness of the world with our thought and language.

Title: The mystery of prehistory
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Known best for her work as a presenter, Mary-Ann Ochota specialises in anthropology, archaeology and social history. She co-presented Channel 4’s cult archaeology show ‘Time Team’, and recently fronted the hugely successful ‘Feral Children’ series.
Synopsis & Topics: Take a journey back through time with TV anthropologist Mary-Anna Ochota as she explores the surprising secrets of Britain's prehistoric people

Title: The medicine myth
Guests & Speakers: Denis Noble, Guy Brown, Nessa Carey
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Denis Noble is a world renowned biologist, and Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at the University of Oxford. Famous for developing the first mathematical model of cardiac cells. Nessa Carey is a ground-breaking British biologist working in the field of molecular biology and biotechnology. She is International Director of the technology transfer organization PraxisUnico and a Visiting Professor at Imperial College London. Guy Brown heads a research group at the University of Cambridge working on cell death in the brain, the heart and in cancer. His previous book The Energy of Life won the Wellcome Trust Prize for popular science. David Malone is an independent filmmaker, Green Party politician, and author of The Debt Generation.
Synopsis & Topics: Many futurists have believed that death is merely a technical problem science will one day solve. But living in the shadow of the Covid-19 pandemic, do we still believe in the absolute power of medicine to fight disease? Or do we need to accept we cannot be super-human and embrace mortality?

Title: The passion of reason
Guests & Speakers: Julian Baggini, Tommy J. Curry, Güneş Taylor
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher and acclaimed author, Julian Baggini, leading molecular biologist, Güneş Taylor, and critical race theorist, Tommy Curry, put passion and reason to the test.
Synopsis & Topics: For centuries we have believed in the separation of reason and emotion. But are we mistaken in ignoring how connected the two are? Is it time to rethink the way we think?

Title: Fiction, social construction and gender
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
Synopsis & Topics: What's the difference between sex and gender? Should individuals' private expressions of non-conforming gender be protected by law? Outspoken gender critical feminist Kathleen Stock outlines her unique views on gender, sex, philosophy and fiction

Title: How Occam's Razor changed the world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Johnjoe McFadden is a Professor of Modular Genetics at the University of Surrey and the author of Quantum Revolution. His work focuses on how quantum mechanics influences our biology and the use of quantum theory to uncover alternative evolutionary frameworks.
Synopsis & Topics: Modern science and the scientific method owe a lot to a 14th-century monk named Occam. Join quantum biologist Johnjoe McFadden as he explores how Occam's Razor, with its preference for simplicity, cut through superstition and medieval religion to help us understand the world more clearly.

Title: Is it moral to trade with the devil?
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Andrew Adonis, John Kay
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Andrew Adonis is a Labour Politian, leading journalist and academic. John Kay is a bestselling author and one of the UK's most renowned economists. Janne Teller is a novelist and former conflict advisor for the UNO and EU. Hosting this debate is journalist and columnist at the Irish Times, Finn McRedmond.
Synopsis & Topics: Free trade has historically been seen as a force for good, both financially and diplomatically. But has Europe's dependence on Russian oil, and the unstoppable growth of China, shown this to be a fundamental mistake?

Title: Love and other drugs
Guests & Speakers: Rupert Sheldrake, Anders Sandberg, Ella Whelan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anders Sandberg is a research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford, where his research focusses on the societal and ethical issues surrounding human enhancement and new technologies. He is also research associate at the Oxford Uehiro Centre for Practical Ethics and the Oxford Centre for Neuroethics. A regular commentator and participant of public debates concerning human enhancement, Anders comes to the festival in support of an exciting transhuman future. On Twitter he describes himself as an academic jack of all trades, and we are sure he is a master of some. Ella Whelan is a political commentator and freelance journalist. After graduating in 2014, Whelan joined online politics magazine spiked, and quickly rose to assistant editor. She is a producer of the annual Battle of Ideas Festival in central London and writes for the Sunday Times, the Irish Times, the Sun and The Economist. Whelan regularly appears in the media; her support for Brexit and criticism of no-platforming and 21st century feminism has caused her to clash with mainstream journalists on the BBC, Sky, and Channel 4. Her first book, What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism, was described as "a leading voice of a rising generation of young warriors for free speech" by distinguished social critic Camille Paglia. Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist, author and parapsychology researcher, best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. He is a critic of New Atheism, and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging. From 2005 to 2010, Rupert was Director of the Perrott-Warrick project for research on unexplained human and animal abilities, funded by Trinity College, Cambridge. Rupert has sole authored 9 books, including A New Science of Life, The Science Delusion and his newest book Ways to Go Beyond and Why They Work. Rupert is also famous for the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. Myriam Francois is an author, broadcaster and academic on issues related to Islam, France and the Middle East. She is host of the increasingly popular We Need to Talk about Whiteness Podcast.
Synopsis & Topics: We tend to view love and romance as organic. But scientific and anecdotal evidence has shown that psychoactive substances can enhance our feelings of love for others. Is time we let go of organic love as an antiquated ideal and embrace drugs as a means of 'hacking' love?

Title: Cosmology needs philosophy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose main interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He is also author of Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe.
Synopsis & Topics: There used to be little difference between science and philosophy, but gradually specialisation has pit the two fields against each other. Join renowned cosmologist Bjørn Ekeberg as he shares his insights into the union of science and philosophy

Title: How to uncover the truth with Manveen Rana
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Manveen Rana is a senior broadcast journalist who has hosted the Times Radio podcast Stories of our times since March 2020. Formerly she worked for the BBC, as a reporter for the Today programme.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the pursuit of truth in journalism more difficult than ever? Join acclaimed Times columnist Manveen Rana as she explores misinformation, ideology, war and modern journalism.

Title: Consciousness in the machine
Guests & Speakers: Donald Hoffman, Bernardo Kastrup, Susan Schneider
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary anti-reality theorist Donald Hoffman, fearless computer scientist and philosopher Bernardo Kastrup and distinguished AI ethicist and philosopher Susan Schneider lock horns over the possibility of AI consciousness. Theories of Everything's Curt Jaimungal hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: A Google engineer was recently fired for claiming its chatbot was sentient. But is conscious AI in fact quickly becoming a reality? Or is recreating consciousness in machines a fantasy, given how little we know about our own brains?

Title: Beyond Mad or Bad
Guests & Speakers: Simon Wessely, Sara Evans-Lacko, Stefan Priebe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. He is currently the media expert for the Royal College of Psychiatrists and has worked as a broadcaster for the BBC and ITV. Sara Evans-Lacko is an Associate Professorial Research Fellow at the Care Policy and Evaluation Centre at the London School of Economics. She has a particular interest in the role of health services and social support in the prevention and treatment of mental illness. At the global level, she has advised on national and state mental health plans and her work has been cited in key government reports in Brazil, Colombia, the Czech Republic, Germany, Mexico and the UK and by international organizations such as the World Health Organization. Sir Simon Wessely is Professor of Psychological Medicine at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King’s College London. He is a Consultant Psychiatrist at King’s College Hospital and the Maudsley Hospital. Sir Simon is currently Chair of the government’s Independent Review of the Mental Health Act. Stefan Priebe is a leading psychologist and psychiatrist and Professor of Social and Community Psychiatry at Queen Mary, University of London, He is also Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Mental Health Service Development, Director of the NIHR Global Health Research Group for Developing Psycho-Social Interventions.
Synopsis & Topics: In the last 60 years, we have dramatically reduced the number of people living in mental hospitals. But at the same time, the amount of people incarcerated with mental illness has shot up. Was it a fundamental mistake to choose punishment over rehabilitation? And do we need to think beyond 'mad' and 'bad'?

Title: Rationality and the Left
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosophy professor at Morehouse University Perimeter College, Ben Burgis is a columnist for Jacobin Magazine and a prolific Youtube debater.
Synopsis & Topics: Has logic been left behind by the left? Join Marxist philosopher Ben Burgis as he urges the left to take the ideas of the right seriously, and put an end to the new era of tribalism

Title: How to be a sceptic
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Massimo Pigliucci is a philosophy professor at City College New York and one of the world's leading thinkers in the study of Ancient Stoicism. His most recent books include The Quest for Character and Think like a Stoic.
Synopsis & Topics: Most of us like to think we are rational people. But research indicates many of our firmly-held beliefs are false. Join renowned philosopher Massimo Pigliucci as he explores how to be truly sceptical in an age of unreason.

Title: World history and the population crisis
Guests & Speakers: Mike Berners Lee, Tim Palmer, Thangam Debbonaire, Aveek Bhattacharya
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour MP for Bristol West and shadow leader of the House of Commons. She describes herself as a supporter of 'fettered capitalism' and has argued for drug reform. Dr Aveek Bhattacharya is the Research Director of the Social Market Foundation and a former policy analyst for the Institute of Alcohol Studies. He also contributes regularly to The Guardian, The Critic and the Financial Times. Tim Palmer is an internationally renowned meteorologist and Professor at the University of Oxford. He works on the tough, crucial problems of uncertainty in our weather and climate, drawing on his background in fundamental physics to do so. He was appointed as CBE in the 2015 New Year’s Honours list for services to science and has won numerous other awards in recognition of his world-leading work. Mike Berners-Lee is an English researcher and writer on carbon foot-printing. He is a professor and fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University and director and principal consultant of Small World Consulting, where he advises organisations on how best to respond to the current climate and ecological issues
Synopsis & Topics: Many thought that the Covid-19 pandemic would lead to a baby boom. But the opposite seems to be happening. Should we welcome a decreased population as a lesser strain on the planet's resources, or do we urgently need to boost global population to avoid economic downturn?

Title: Sins of the past, visions of the future
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Kehinde Andrews, Calvin Robinson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Myriam Francois is an award-winning Franco-Irish journalist and research associate at the Centre of Islamic Studies at SOAS University. She has also hosted several documentaries for the BBC and Al Jazeera among others. Calvin Robinson is a British political commentator and broadcaster who is also a deacon of the Free Church of England. He is a regular contributor to the Daily Telegraph, Daily Mail and Spiked. Kehinde Andrews is a British Academic and author specialising in Black Studies. He is a professor at Birmingham City University, director of the Centre for Critical Social Research and the first Black Studies Professor in the UK.
Synopsis & Topics: In modern society, we enjoy the rewards of hard-fought civil rights battles, from greater gender equality to more representation for ethnic minorities. But are we still haunted by legacies of colonialism and racism, and should we be doing more to combat discrimination? Or is this a counterproductive approach that stops us living harmoniously and without prejudice?

Title: Finding transcendence in a secular world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is a preeminent biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His books include Science and Spiritual Practices, Ways to Go Beyond And Why They Work and The Science Delusion. Furthermore, he was ranked in the top 100 thought leaders for 2013 by the Duttweiler Institute, Switzerland's leading think tank, and has been recognised as one of the 'most spiritually influential living people' by Watkins' Mind Body Spirit Magazine.
Synopsis & Topics: Religion has never been less popular in the West, yet people are searching for transcendence everywhere, in meditation, yoga or psychedelics. Join radical biologist Rupert Sheldrake as he explores spritual meaning in a secular age.

Title: How to learn from history
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matthew Green is an historian and broadcaster with a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He writes for national newspapers, has appeared in many television documentaries, and is the author of London: A Travel Guide Through Time. His latest book is Shadowlands: A Journey Through Lost Britain, which explores the lost causes and dead ends of history in a deeply evocative and dazzlingly original account of Britain's past.
Synopsis & Topics: How do we make sense of history today? Join acclaimed author and journalist Matthew Green as he walks through the changing face of maps, and humanity's precariousness.

Title: The code to the cosmos
Guests & Speakers: Marika Taylor, Peter Woit, Arif Ahmed
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Arif Ahmed is a University of Cambridge philosopher and well-known advocate for the tolerance of diverse political views. Peter Woit is a renowned theoretical physicist, Columbia University professor and critic of string theory. Marika Taylor is a Southampton University theoretical physicist and award-winning string theorist. Our host is David Malone, is an independent filmmaker, Green Party politician, and author of The Debt Generation.
Synopsis & Topics: From Einstein to quantum mechanics, mathematics is often thought to uncover fundamental truths about reality. But many scientists argue there are many elements of the Universe that mathematics cannot describe. Should we see mathematics as the ultimate code to the cosmos, or a useful but flawed tool?

Title: The dream of progress
Guests & Speakers: Kenneth Cukier, Nolen Gertz, Caitjan Gainty
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kenneth Cukier is a renowned American journalist and coauthor of the NYT Bestselling book “Big Data”. Caitjan Gainty is an established historian of 20th century health and co-runs the Healthy Scepticism project, Nolan Gertz is a philosopher of applied ethics, and author of the cutting-edge book "Nihilism and Technology". Our host, Jess Wade, is a well-loved British physicist, researcher and advocate for women in STEM.
Synopsis & Topics: Technological progress is often seen as inevitable and an unquestionably good thing. But with climate change, a powerful arms industry, and mental ill health resulting from mobile devices, is it time to rethink the dream of progress?

Title: The future of sex
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Güneş Taylor is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre. Her research predominantly focuses on the genetic formation of ovaries and testes. In 2018, Güneş was awarded the Crick Public Engagement Prize for her efforts in the public communication of science.
Synopsis & Topics: With the arrival of powerful new CRISPR gene editing technologies, is the human body now a work in progress that can be edited? How will genetic intervention affect sex, reproduction and gender? Join Francis Crick Institute fellow Güneş Taylor as she outlines the future of sex.

Title: New politics and old threats
Guests & Speakers: Zoe Strimpel, Tommy J. Curry, Michael Bociurkiw
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Bociurkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst and two-time TEDx speaker. He is also the author of Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good. Tommy Curry is a trail-blazing philosophy professor at the University of Edinburgh, and author of ‘The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood’. Zoe Strimpel is a British journalist, academic historian, author, and commentator on gender and relationships. She is a columnist for The Sunday Telegraph where she writes a weekly column, commenting on gender, feminism, dating, relationships and identity politics. Barry Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Young people in the UK and US have consistently named climate change as the most important issue of our time. Is this a result of social media and doomscrolling? Are they in fact right to dismiss the economy as something they're not included in, or should economic matters return to the centre of political debate?

Title: The new 10 commandments
Guests & Speakers: Sophie Grace Chappell, Massimo Pigliucci, Simon Baron-Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Philosophy at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell, Professor of Philosophy at the City College of New York Massimo Pigliucci and Professor in the Departments of Psychology and Psychiatry at the University of Cambridge Simon Baron-Cohen discuss if life can be reduced to a rulebook. Myriam François hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In an age where the number of self-described religious people is decreasing, do we still need to follow rules and codes in order to lead good lives? Can social media and self-help fill this gap? Or should we always view attempts to promote rules for life with suspicion?

Title: Dawkins on the crisis of rationality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Freeman formerly presented Science in Action for the BBC World Service as well as The Bookshow for Sky TV. For many years he hosted a daily book programme in Oxford. He has also featured on Jazz FM for many years and is now the resident expert on blues music.
Synopsis & Topics: Join legendary evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins in conversation with prolific science journalist David Freeman as they discuss the return of rational thinking, public science education and Dawkins' fascinating and controversial career.

Title: How to write a speech that will change the world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: 'Writer-in-chief at The Draft, contributing editor at The New Statesman, columnist for the Evening Standard, and the former lead writer at The Times, Philip Collins has held positions at almost every major newspaper in the country. Having previously been a speech writer for Tony Blair, the Director of the Social Market Foundation think tank and an Equity Strategist at two investment banks, Philip's wealth of experience makes him a one of the most trusted voices in politics.
Synopsis & Topics: Join one of the country's most influential speechwriters Philip Collins as he gives an insider's perspective on how to write an iconic speech that could change the world

Title: The one true story
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Janne Teller, Silvia Jonas
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer, whose oeuvre consists mainly of novels, essays, and short stories, often focusing on grand-scale existential topics which spark controversial debate. Barry C Smith is a philosophy professor, and the director of the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. He also co-directs the Centre for the Study of the Senses, a research centre trying to understand how our senses contribute to our perception of the world. Sophie Allen is a renowned philosopher, her work focuses on philosophical methodology, metaphilosophy and metaphysics. She is a lecturer at the University of Keele where she writes on the very understanding of philosophy itself. Myriam Francois hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the goal of philosophy to uncover the 'truth' about the world? Or in a postmodern society where different groups and individuals have their own truths, is this is fantasy which we should abandon?

Title: Living forever
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Henry Marsh, Anna Kent
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anders Sandberg is a researcher at the Future of Humanity Institute which centres on management of low-probability high-impact risks, estimating the capabilities of future technologies, and very long-range futures. Henry Marsh is a world leading neurosurgeon, pioneer of neurological advances and bestselling author. His memoir, Do No Harm: Stories of Life, Death and Brain Surgery, received wide acclaim detailing his work in the UK, former Soviet Ukraine and Nepal. Anna Kent is a humanitarian, a NHS nurse and a midwife. In her profoundly moving book 'Frontline Midwife' (2022) she gives a no holds barred account of delivering babies in war zones, Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In a world ravaged by climate breakdown and inequality, is living forever something any of us would desire? Or would medical breakthroughs in health give us the time and space to solve some of life's most fundamental puzzles?

Title: The worrying rebirth of expertise
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: 'David Goodhart is a British journalist, commentator and author. Along with being a correspondent for the Financial Times for 12 years, he is the founder and a former editor of Prospect magazine. 'Goodhart offers the best and most complete explanation I've seen for why things seem to be coming apart in so many countries at the same time.' -- Jonathan Haidt
Synopsis & Topics: Join journalist and author David Goodhart as he discusses the problematic tendency for societies to rely on a small and highly educated elite for political guidance, and what we can do make democracy more representative

Title: Humans are not morally superior
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alex O’Connor, also known by his YouTube alias ‘CosmicSkeptic’, is a prolific philosopher, youtuber, public speaker and animal welfare activist. His YouTube channel has amassed over 450 000 subscribers and discusses issues relating to free speech, free will, animal rights and the philosophical arguments against religion.
Synopsis & Topics: Popular philosopher and YouTube Alex O'Connor deconstructs the moral realities behind our diets and makes a philosophically powerful case for veganism.

Title: The Wealth Paradox
Guests & Speakers: Guy Standing, Janne Teller, Kristian Niemietz
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Radical economist Guy Standing, Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs Kristian Niemietz and acclaimed writer and former macroeconomist Janne Teller lock horns. Phil Collins hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Guy Standing, Kristian Niemietz, and Janne Teller debate theh true impact of trickle down economics.

Title: Breaking through the consciousness stalemate
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Goff is a renowned philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His unique research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview.
Synopsis & Topics: Distinguished philosopher and pansychist Philip Goff argues why we need a new theory of consciousness.

Title: How to write your first novel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Ward is a captivating stage and screen actress, and a writer of non-fiction and fiction. Her feature film debut in Steven Spielberg's Young Sherlock Holmes. She has written for The Guardian, The Times, and The Spectator, won the 2018 Royal Academy Pin Drop Award for her short story "Sunbed", and had her first novel, Love and Other Thought Experiments was longlisted for both the Desmond Elliott Prize and the Booker Prize.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Sophie Ward as she discusses her journey from captivating actor of stage and screen to a Booker Prize-nominated author, and hear her first-hand advice for writing your debut novel.

Title: Cosmology and the big bust
Guests & Speakers: Julian Barbour, Eric J. Lerner, Claudia Maraston
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The Big Bang Never Happened author, Eric Lerner, distinguished astrophysicist Claudia Maraston, and renowned physicist and author of The End of Time Julian Barbour argue lock horns over the Big Bang. Jess Wade hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it time up for the Big Bang? The theory depends on 'cosmic inflation' for which there is little evidence. Do we need to look elsewhere for proof of the Big Bang, or is it time to give up on the theory altogether?

Title: The good and the evil
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Tommy J. Curry, Massimo Pigliucci
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Fearless thinker, Tommy Curry, esteemed philosopher, Massimo Pigliucci, and author of Zed, Joanna Kavenna, explore whether 'good' and 'evil' are just categories used for coercion. Hosted by Myriam Francois.
Synopsis & Topics: People’s actions have long been categorised morally in terms of good or evil. But the idea that the individual is simply good is hard to sustain. And this tendency for everyone to think of their own actions as good often intensifies dispute and conflict. Are we capable of making ultimate moral judgements?

Title: Seeing happy with Mandy Seligman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mandy Seligman is an award-winning black and white photographer who began her career as a developmental social psychologist. She has spent the last thirty years traveling around the world with Martin Seligman spreading Positive Psychology.
Synopsis & Topics: Join award-winning photographer and Positive Psychology advocate Mandy Seligman as she explores the joy of capturing life's greatest moments on film, and how focussing on what makes you happy can make life worth living

Title: Finding an ultimate theory of everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eric Weinstein is an American podcast host and managing director of Thiel Capital. He received his PhD in mathematical physics from Harvard University in 1992 and in 2013, he proposed a unified theory of physics called ‘Geometric Unity’. Additionally, Weinstein was the first to coin the phrase the ‘intellectual dark web’, to describe a collection of heterodox commentators who oppose identity politics, political correctness and cancel culture.
Synopsis & Topics: Join podcast host Eric Weinstein and executive director of the Skeptics Society Michael Shermer as they have a wide-ranging and fascinating conversation on the nature of the universe and reality itself.

Title: The West in danger
Guests & Speakers: Nigel Inkster, Tulip Siddiq, Theodore Dalrymple
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour MP and Shadow Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Tulip Siddiq, renowned cultural critic Theodore Dalrymple, and former director of operations and intelligence for the British Secret Intelligence Service, Nigel Inkster lock horns. Myriam François hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In an age of turbulent political and social change, is it fair to say we are living in a new historical era in which the post-war stability we have known is over? Does the West need to rethink its values and place in the world to avoid a century of conflict and danger?

Title: The good, the great and the ghosts of the past
Guests & Speakers: Grafton Tanner, Stuart Semple, Jenni Murray
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: British artist Stuart Semple, English journalist and broadcaster Jenni Murray and author of 'The Hours Have Lost Their Clock: The Politics of Nostalgia' Grafton Tanner debate whether we should see our attachment to the Beatles, Blackadder and Bach as a deep conservativism that should be overcome. Myriam François hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: From the Beatles to old box sets, we are seemingly addicted to culture made in our past. Is this is a sign that cultural progress has slowed and we no longer innovate? Or is engaging in a dialogue with our past a productive way of dealing with our present?

Title: From one universe to the next
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes.
Synopsis & Topics: What exactly is the universe? Join Nobel Prize-winning physicist Roger Penrose as he ponders  everything from tiny quantum states to the larger scales of cosmology to offer his unique perspective on both physics and philosophy

Title: Truth and lies in politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. She describes herself as a "northern European socialist".
Synopsis & Topics: Can parliamentary democracy be saved from the lies and deception that plague it? Shadow Leader of the House Thangam Debbonaire argues that our government is not fit for the 21st century, and outlines steps to revive our failing democracy.

Title: Moral facts and moral fantasy
Guests & Speakers: Simon Blackburn, Joanna Kavenna, Slavoj Žižek
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek, bestselling author of Zed Joanna Kavenna, and philosopher and author of Truth Simon Blackburn debate objective morality in a postmodern age. Hosted by Professor and Chair of Jurisprudence at the University of Oxford, Ruth Chang.
Synopsis & Topics: Moral relativism, a popular postmodern idea, suggested that there is no objective morality. But a new swathe of philosophers are claiming the existence of absolute moral truths. Should we welcome this as an antidote to postmodern confusion, or call it out as an authoritarian fantasy?

Title: Dawkins re-examined
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-famous scientist Richard Dawkins goes head-to-head with celebrated biologist Denis Noble as they lock horns over the role of genes over the eons. Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Richard Dawkins and Denis Noble go head-to-head over the role genes play in driving evolutionary development.

Title: Towards a just economy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Angela Eagle DBE was the Former Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Skills, and has been the Labour MP for Wallasey since 1992. Her engaging book The New Serfdom: The Triumph of Conservative Ideas and How to Defeat Them addresses how we can build a successful economy with greater equality for all.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Angela Eagle DBE debunks the assumptions that have pervaded the economy post-Thatcher and explores how we can work towards a successful economy with greater equality for all.

Title: Why you can't pay attention
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bence Nanay is a Professor of Philosophy, whose research focuses on philosophy of mind, philosophy of biology and aesthetics. He is co-director of the Centre for Philosophical Psychology at the University of Antwerp and also Senior Research Associate at Peterhouse, Cambridge University.
Synopsis & Topics: Find yourself not being able to pay attention? In this talk, philosopher of mind Bence Nanay discusses the modern-day attention economy, and explores the societal costs of our waning attention.

Title: The betrayal of beauty
Guests & Speakers: Julian Spalding, Sophie Fiennes, Barry C. Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award winning director Sophie Fiennes, philosopher of the senses Barry Smith and legendary critic Julian Spalding battle for beauty. Mark Salter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: We used to see beauty and art as inseparable. But much of 20th century art viewed beauty as a clichéd dead end. Have we been conned by a modern art market that turns the least valuable art into the priciest commodities? Is it time we reclaimed beauty for the modern age?

Title: The fantasies of the West
Guests & Speakers: Paul Mason, Peter Hitchens, Bhavna Dave
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Mason is a radical author, commentator, and political journalist. Previously the Newsnight Business Editor, Economics Editor at Channel 4 News, where he reported on Europe's troubled economic crises. He is now a freelance author and journalist. Bhavna Dave is a Senior Lecturer in Central Asian Politics at the Department of Politics and International Studies at SOAS, University of London. Peter Hitchens is an award-winning conservative author, broadcaster, journalist and political commentator. He has a weekly column in the Mail on Sunday and is a prolific contributor to a wide range of magazines. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are current political conflicts in Ukraine and Hong Kong a result of an arrogant Western confidence that other countries will adopt democratic freedoms? Should we recognise that our worldview is one amongst many, or should we defend 'Western values' at all costs?

Title: The world after reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics.
Synopsis & Topics: Is realism dead? Post-post-modernist philosopher Hilary Lawson discusses whether 'reality' - elusive, unattainable and everywhere - is a concept we need to abandon in favour of a new and more compelling alternative.

Title: Tomorrow sex will be good again
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Katherine Angel is the author of Tomorrow Sex Will Be Good Again, published in 2021 to critical acclaim and widespread international coverage. She is also the author of Daddy Issues, and Unmastered: A Book on Desire, Most Difficult to Tell.
Synopsis & Topics: In a post-#MeToo era of empowerment and consent, women and men are expected to proclaim their deisres clearly. Yet research suggests women's desire is often slower to emerge. Katherine Angel suggets we should rethink our ideas of sex, pleasure and autonomy in this fascinating talk.

Title: The edge of the universe
Guests & Speakers: David Deutsch, Sara Walker, George Ellis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Oxford maverick physicist David Deutsch, leading cosmology theorist George Ellis and theoretical physicist and origin of life expert Sara Walker debate whether the notion of infinity is a key insight into the character of the universe, a mathematical artefact, or simply nonsense. Hosted by the renowned public intellectual, writer and producer Robert Lawrence Kuhn.
Synopsis & Topics: Infinity is discussed within science and mathematics as though it is understood. But many have argued that it corrupts physics and produces nonsensical predictions and answers. Is infinity still a crucial insight into our universe or should we remove it from our accounts of the world altogether?

Title: Lost in language
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Barry C. Smith, Maria Balaska
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished philosopher of language and the senses Barry Smith, Wittgensteinian expert Maria Balaska and maverick post-post modern philosopher Hilary Lawson lock horns over whether philosophy's fixation on language has held us back. Rufus Duits hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Analytic philosophy has dominated Western thought for over a century. But is it still relevant in a world where science claims to be the most rational methodology and emotions dominate our discourse?

Title: The life inside with Andy West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Andy West has taught philosophy in prisons since 2015. His first book, 'The Life Inside' - which explores the conversations he has with people inside about their lives, discusses their ideas and feelings and listens as the men and women he works with explore new ways to think about their situation.
Synopsis & Topics: Join philosopher Andy West as he discusses the thoughts, feelings and ideas of incarcerated men and women that he has documented in his new book The Life Inside.

Title: Solving the dark matter mystery
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ellis is a Maxwell prize-winning theoretical physicist, and is considered one of the world's leading physicists. John is currently Clerk Maxwell Professor of Theoretical Physics at King's College London, and since 1978 has held an indefinite contract at CERN.
Synopsis & Topics: Join CERN physicist John Elllis as he explores the mysteries of the Universe that physics can't explain.

Title: Overcoming tribal division
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Paul Dolan, Ella Whelan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Myriam François host of the ‘We Need to Talk About Whiteness’ podcast, which aims to explore the meaning of 'whiteness' in conversations around race and racism, is a writer and broadcaster. Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and author of the bestselling book ‘Happiness By Design: Finding Pleasure and Purpose in Everyday Life.’ Ella Whelan is a freelance journalist, commentator and author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: We can all agree that there seems to be more disagreement in society than ever before. Political and cultural tribalism is deepening, but is it a necessary phase in working out our differences? Or do we need to calm our rhetoric and rediscover a shared civic identity?

Title: Infinity in the palm of your hand
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Paul Muldoon, Isy Suttie
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Critically acclaimed writer Janne Teller, musical comedian and writer Isy Suttie, British philosopher James Tartaglia and Pulitzer prize poet Paul Muldoon as they debate whether art can uncover the essence of the world. Hosted by acclaimed author, Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: Can art uncover the essence of the world? Pulitzer laureate poet Paul Muldoon debates with Peep Show's Isy Suttie, philosopher James Tartaglia and writer Janne Teller. Joanna Kavenna hosts.

Title: The AI hoax
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mazviita Chirimuuta is a Senior Lecturer in philosophy at Edinburgh University, with interests in neuroscience and philosophy of mind, especially in colour perception.
Synopsis & Topics: We are familiar with human-like AI from science fiction. But could this fiction become fact? Join philosopher of perception Mazviita Chirimuuta as she argues that human-like AI will remain a fantasy.

Title: The future of money
Synopsis & Topics: Join former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable as he discusses the future of the world economy with BBC economics presenter Linda Yueh.

Title: Catching sight of our self
Guests & Speakers: Iain McGilchrist, Bence Nanay, Anil Ananthaswamy, Betty Sue Flowers
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of 'The Master and his Emmisary', Iain McGilchrist, Professor of Philosophy at University of Antwerp, Bence Nanay, Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas, Betty Sue Flowers, and famed author and science journalist, Anil Ananthaswamy, lock horns over the notion of self knowledge. Hosted by philosopher, Mary-Jane Rubenstein.
Synopsis & Topics: In an age where the self-help industry is booming, we are promised that we can attain knowledge of the self. But is this mistaken? Is knowing ourselves a dangerous illusion or can we really understand and change ourselves?

Title: Beyond the self and non-self
Guests & Speakers: Johnjoe McFadden, Ane Ogbe, Petter Brodin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Quantum biologist JohnJoe McFadden, distinguished immunologist Ane Ogbe and Professor of Paediatric Immunology Petter Brodin debate the self and the non-self. Gunes Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In the wake of the Covid pandemic and the medical and scientific community's response, is it time we rethought the health of the individual? Does the old attack-defence paradigm of illness still stand or do we need to resituate personal sickness in a societal and global framework?

Title: How to use philosophy for a better life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rebecca Roache is Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at Royal Holloway, University of London. Her research interests range from ethics and metaphysics to philosophy of mind and philosophy of language. She is a pioneer in field of philosophy of swearing, and her work has been featured in The Times, The Guardian and the BBC.
Synopsis & Topics: What is philosophy and how can it help us lead more meaningful lives? Join radical philosopher Rebecca Roache as she discusses the tools that philosophy can equip us with to create better lives and more enlightened societies.

Title: The future of Ukraine and the world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Bociurkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst and two-time TEDx speaker. He is also the author of ‘Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good’. Having worked on the frontlines of humanitarian emergencies, he’s become a familiar voice on BBC World Television, CNN, CNN International, Al Jazeera, and Bloomberg Television.
Synopsis & Topics: The Russian invasion of Ukraine has shocked the world and redrawn the geopolitical landscape. Join acclaimed writer Michael Bociurkiw as he discusses how we should understand the war and our global future.

Title: The status of things
Guests & Speakers: Paul Dolan, Steve Taylor, Mary-Ann Ochota
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Behavioural scientist Paul Dolan, senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University Steve Taylor and British broadcaster and anthropologist Mary-Ann Ochota debate the status of things. Eliane Glaser hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Behavioural scientist Paul Dolan, senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University Steve Taylor and British broadcaster and anthropologist Mary-Ann Ochota debate the status of things. Eliane Glaser hosts.

Title: Reigning men
Guests & Speakers: Mary Ann Sieghart, Kate Kirkpatrick, Nina Power
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist and author of 'The Authority Gap', Mary Ann Sieghart, lecturer and author of 'Becoming Beauvoir', Kate Kirkpatrick, and cultural critic and author of 'What Men Want', Nina Power, ask whether the sun is setting on the reign of men. Hosted by BBC News presenter and journalist, Joanna Gosling
