Synopsis & Topics: In the wake of fourth wave feminism and the #MeToo movement, are there signs that the entrenched dominance of men in many fields of work is receding? If not, can this be overturned? Or are we mistaken to seek gender equality in every aspect of society?

Title: Where sceptics fail
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alex O’Connor, also known by his YouTube alias ‘CosmicSkeptic’, is a prolific philosopher, youtuber, public speaker and animal welfare activist. His youtube channel has amassed over 450 000 subscribers and discusses issues relating to free speech, free will, animal rights and the philosophical arguments against religion.
Synopsis & Topics: YouTuber Alex O'Connor, AKA CosmicSkeptic, grapples with the limits of reason and rationality in this wide-ranging interview on veganism, religion and David Hume.

Title: What the world is made of
Guests & Speakers: Rupert Sheldrake, Paul Davies, Katie Robertson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary physicist Paul Davies, trailblazing author of 'The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake and ground-breaking philosopher of physics Katie Robertson debate the fundamental nature of reality. Acclaimed science presenter Dallas Campbell hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is there fundamental matter that constitutes our physical reality? Or should we instead give up on the idea that the world is made of physical things?

Title: The new science of consciousness
Guests & Speakers: Patricia Churchland, Carlo Rovelli, Bernardo Kastrup
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli, ground breaking metaphysical idealist Bernardo Kastrup, godmother of neurophilosophy Patricia Churchland lock horns over the New Science of Consciousness. Robert Lawrence Kuhn Hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Recently, a 'new science' of consciousness has emerged, with the promise of getting closer to definitively solving the problem of the self. But is this 'new science' marketing hype? Or is science about crack the ancient problem of the self once and for all?

Title: Silenced for following the science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Nutt is a neuropsychopharmacologist and the former chairman of the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs in the UK, a position he was dismissed from in 2009. Now chair of the Independent Scientific Committee on Drugs, Nutt has been a fierce defender of science based policy around the legalisation and decrimilisation of canabis and psychedelics. "Any sensible person or scientist knows that the drug laws are not based on the science of drugs."
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Professor David Nutt discusses his groundbreaking research on the medical use of cannabis and other drugs on conditions such as anxiety and depression.

Title: The lessons of failure
Guests & Speakers: Shabnam Nasimi, Stefan Dercon, Shabbir Lakha, Ezgi Basaran
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ezgi Basaran is a journalist and author. She was formerly the youngest ever editor of Radikal, the biggest centre-left news outlet in Turkey. Shabbir Lakha is a political activist. He is an officer at Stop the War, a People's Assembly activist and a member of the socialist organisation Counterfire. Shabnam Nasimi is a British-Afghan social activist and political commentator. She is the Executive Director of Conservative Friends of Afghanistan. Stefan Dercon is Professor of Economic Policy at Oxford University, as was formerly Chief Economist of the UK's Department of International Development. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Was the West's failure in Afghanistan partly responsible for the war in Ukraine? Watch Ezgi Basaran, Shabbir Lakha, Stefan Dercon, and Shabnam Nasimi discuss the lessons of failure.

Title: Kafka vs Camus
Guests & Speakers: Emma Sulkowicz, Andrea Elliott, Paul Muldoon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emma Sulkowicz is a performance artist, well-known for her year-long performance art project Mattress Performance: Carry That Weight protesting having to go to school with her rapist. Andrea Elliott is a Pulitzer Prize winning journalist, who writes for the New York Times as an investigative reporter, and is author of ‘An Invisible Child’. Paul Muldoon is a Pulitzer Prize winning poet and has served as both Professor of Poetry at Oxford University and the poetry editor of The New Yorker. Janne Teller hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Camus and Kafka were both central to 20th century thought. Kafka believed the individual was limited by the bureaucracy of state institutions, while Camus suggested we are radically free to change society. Who got it right?

Title: Science and the prejudice of the West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chandrima Ganguly is Wolfson's Henslow Junior Research Fellow at the University of Cambridge. They are a cosmologist interested in testing early universe models, and using cosmology to constrain particle physics and theories of gravity.
Synopsis & Topics: Is science objective? What do we mean by scientific truth? Henslow Research Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, Chandrima Ganguly discusses how science has been shaped by socio-political forces.

Title: The civilisation trap
Guests & Speakers: Natalie Bennett, Peter Lilley, Mark Williams
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paleobiologist Mark Williams, Conservative former cabinet minister Peter Lilley and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett weigh in on civilisation as we know it. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Prominent anthropologists have labelled the agricultural revolution 'humanity's worst mistake'. Is there any way of keeping the benefits of modern technology while living nomadically like our ancestors?

Title: The mystery of the multiverse
Guests & Speakers: Michio Kaku, Sabine Hossenfelder, Roger Penrose
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michio Kaku is the co-founder of string field theory and the author of several books including several New York Times best sellers such as ‘The God Equation: The Quest for a Theory of Everything became.’ He is also professor of theoretical physics in the City College of New York and CUNY Graduate Center. Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist who specializes in the foundations of physics. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the group on Superfluid Dark Matter. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: The theory of the multiverse has never been more prominent in popular culture. But should we take it seriously from a scientific perspective? Or should multiverses remain on the pages of comic books? String field theorist Michio Kaku debates with physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and renowned mathematician Roger Penrose.

Title: Economics matters
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David D. Friedman is one of the most renowned anarcho-capitalist theorists in the world. Son of Nobel Prize winning economist and father of modern economics, Milton Friedman, David has set out his own unique economic theory. His book, The Machinery of Freedom, is the go-to text for those interested in anarcho-capitalism, and it makes up one of the most reputable defences of setting capitalism completely free.
Synopsis & Topics: The state of the global economy is never far from the headlines. In this talk, anarcho-capitalist economist David D. Friedman gives a spirited overview of economic theory and how it affects all aspects of our lives

Title: Virtue, hypocrisy and the natural world
Guests & Speakers: Ella Whelan, Natalie Bennett, Ashwini Deshpande
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former leader of the Green Party and member of the House of Lords Natalie Bennett, influential economist Ashwini Deshpande and controversial Spiked journalist Ella Whelan clash over the merits of environmental ideals. Hosted by acclaimed historian, Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Many people believe we should reduce our carbon footprint to help the environment, yet consumption has never been quicker or easier. Is it true to say people only support measures to tackle climate change if it doesn't have a personal impact on them?

Title: Should we care for ants?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Godfrey-Smith is professor in the School of History and Philosophy of Science at the University of Sydney. His main research interests are in the philosophy of biology and the philosophy of mind. He is the author of numerous highly-acclaimed, including 'Other Minds: The Octopus, The Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness.'
Synopsis & Topics: Where should we draw the lines when it comes to our consideration for other animals' wellbeing? Peter Godfrey-Smith investigates the limits of our moral approach to animals

Title: The trauma of everyday
Guests & Speakers: Sarah Garfinkel, Joanna Kavenna, Ian Parker
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Neuroscientist Sarah Garfinkel, bestselling author of Zed Joanna Kavenna and fearless psychoanalyst Ian Parker explore modern trauma and what we can do about it.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we ever be certain about anything at all? Simon Blackburn, maverick philosopher Hilary Lawson, and groundbreaking philosopher of value Ruth Chang question everything. Maria Balaska hosts.

Title: The search for certainty
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Simon Blackburn, Ruth Chang
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished philosophy professor Simon Blackburn, maverick post post-modern philosopher Hilary Lawson and ground-breaking philosopher of value Ruth Chang question whether we can be certain about anything. Maria Balaska hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we ever be certain about anything at all? Simon Blackburn, maverick philosopher Hilary Lawson, and ground-breaking philosopher of value Ruth Chang question everything. Maria Balaska hosts.

Title: Writing the self
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Meg Rosoff is an award-winning writer. She is perhaps best known for the novels 'How I Live Now' which won the Guardian Prize, and 'Just In Case, for which she was awarded the Carnegie medal. Her most recent novel, 'The Great Godden' is a coming-of-age novel which was nominated for the Costa Book Award in 2020.
Synopsis & Topics: How do we know if a story is worth telling? Can we actively seek out inspiration, or do we have to wait for it to strike? Award-winning author of 'How I Live Now', Meg Rosoff, provides an insight into her writing philosophy.

Title: Corporations vs The People
Guests & Speakers: Nick Gillespie, Daron Acemoglu, Beata Javorcik
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Elizabeth and James Killian Professor of Economics at MIT Daron Acemoglu, journalist and editor-at-large of libertarian publication Reason Nick Gillespie and Chief Economist at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development Beata Javorcik debate whether the state should take more control of key sectors including big tech. Linda Yueh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it time we reigned in the power and influence that corporations wield over us? Or do we need to accept that competition between corporations will generate the innovative solutions to the problems we face?

Title: Truth and prejudice
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Tommy J. Curry, Kathleen Stock
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focusses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies and Public Health. Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, an independent, self-described radical left-wing alternative media organization based in the United Kingdom, and author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism. In his book, Bastani argues that ‘Fully Automated Luxury Communism’ is the paradigm of the future – and the path to a world of luxury, liberty and happiness. Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published several articles and her most recent book 'Material Girls' which argues against the idea of gender as a social construct.
Synopsis & Topics: Do modern universities fulfil their original goal of pursuing truth? Or has institutional group think undermined the mission of universities to spread knowledge?

Title: Afghanistan and the Failures of the West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Shabnam Nasimi is a British-Afghan social activist and political commentator. She is the Executive Director of Conservative Friends of Afghanistan, a group that exists to promote understanding and support for Afghanistan in the United Kingdom.
Synopsis & Topics: What obligations does the West have to Afghanistan now it has left the country? Director of Conservative Friends of Afghanistan Shabnam Nasimi discusses where we go from here.

Title: The knowledge delusion
Guests & Speakers: Santiago Zabala, Corine Besson, Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Freedom in Age of Alternative Facts Santiago Zabala, pragmatic epistemologist Corine Besson and expert of Indian thought Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad clash over whether it is ever possible to be definitely right about anything.
Synopsis & Topics: Throughout history, politicians, scientists and philosophers have claimed to be right about certain issues. Is moral certainty essential to progress, or should we give up the idea of being definitely right and welcome a new era of compromise?

Title: In search of a cleaner world
Guests & Speakers: Chris Huhne, Mike Berners Lee, Lierre Keith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Expert in greenhouse gas footprinting and author of There is No Planet B , Mike Berners-Lee, radical environmentalist and author of Bright Green Lies, Lierre Keith, and former Secretary of State for Energy and Climate Change, Chris Huhne, debate renewable energy as the solution the climate crisis. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are 'clean' energy technologies like solar panels and electric car batteries the solution to the climate crisis we face? Or will these create problems in fighting climate change further down the line?

Title: The challenge of China
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Vince Cable is the former leader of the Liberal Democrats, an economist by trade, and now author of a number of bestselling non-fiction works including China: Engage! Money and Power and the The Chinese Conundrum.
Synopsis & Topics: What challenges does China's rise as an economic superpower present for the rest of the world? Former Liberal Democrat leader Vince Cable discusses the challenge of China.

Title: Big tech and lost promises
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Thangam Debbonaire, Polly Mackenzie, Damian Tambini
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Oxford fellow Anders Sandberg, chief executive of leading think-tank Demos, Polly Mackenzie, author of 'Media Freedom', Damian Tambini, and Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire lock horns over the nightmare and dreams coming true with Big Tech. Hosted by metahumanist philosopher, Luke Robert Mason.
Synopsis & Topics: Was the promise of democratic empowerment from big tech corporations always a marketing con? Or can we recover the lost dream of the internet? Luke Robert Mason hosts.

Title: The equality puzzle
Guests & Speakers: Minna Salami, Nicky Morgan, Ella Whelan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Minister for Women and Equalities Nicky Morgan, author and commentator Ella Whelan, and award-winning social critic and writer Minna Salami disucss the best way forward.
Synopsis & Topics: Should feminism focus on getting women into traditionally male roles? Or is this a wrongheaded approach that misunderstands the purpose of feminism?

Title: Science, religion and the quest for reason
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Alister McGrath is a theologian, intellectual historian, scientist, and public intellectual. He currently holds the Andreas Idreos Professorship in Science and Religion in the Faculty of Theology and Religion, at the University of Oxford, McGrath is noted for his work in historical theology, systematic theology and the relationship between science and religion.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Alister McGrath, the Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Religion at the University of Oxford, explores the relationship between science and certainty

Title: The web corporation
Guests & Speakers: Tulip Siddiq, Luke Johnson, Ben Tarnoff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour front bencher Tulip Siddiq, serial entrepreneur and philanthropist Luke Johnson and author of Internet for the People Ben Tarnoff debate the dismantling of Big Tech. Hosted by senior broadcast journalist at the Times, Manveen Rana.
Synopsis & Topics: Join entrepreneur Luke Johnson, writer and tech worker Ben Tarnoff and Labour politician Tulip Siddiq as they debate whether we need to reign in the corporate power of big tech giants. Journalist Manveen Rana hosts.

Title: Postmodernism in the dock
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Minna Salami, Julie Bindel, Julian Baggini
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Co-founder and editor of The Philosophers’ Magazine Julian Baggini, award-winning journalist Minna Salami, radical philosopher Hilary Lawson and boundary pushing feminist Julie Bindel line up as prosecution and defence with postmodernism in the dock. Hosted by journalist and author David Aaronovitch.
Synopsis & Topics: Are we right to embrace postmodernism or does objective truth still matter? Join philosopher Julian Baggini, award-winning journalist Minna Salami, feminist author Julie Bindel and radical philosopher Hilary Lawson as postmodernism is put in the dock. Hosted by David Aaronovitch.

Title: Reviving feminism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I, International Business Times, and New European. Describing herself as a "leftie liberal, anti-racist, feminist, Muslim", she is known for her interventions in UK immigration and multiculturalism policy. Born in Kampala, Uganda into a Shia Muslim family, Yasmin moved to the UK to complete her studies at Oxford. She worked as a teacher before moving into journalism in the 1980s, and has since published a slew of acclaimed books about her unique experience as an insider/outsider in British culture. Her most recent book Ladies Who Punch tells the story of courageous women who have changed history and remoulded our culture.
Synopsis & Topics: Celebrated journalist and author Yasmin Alibhai-Brown explores what feminism is, and how we can all become better feminists.

Title: Forests, hypocrisy and the West
Guests & Speakers: Vince Cable, Aviva Chomsky, Virgilio Viana
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, historian and author Avivia Chomsky and Director General of the Amazonas Sustainable Foundation Virgilio Viana take on the topic of Brazil’s Amazon. Hosted by economist and author, Linda Yueh.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the West hypocritical for demanding Brazil preserve its rainforests, when Europe felled its forests years ago to fuel its economy? American historian Aviva Chomsky and former Liberal Democrats leader Vince Cable debate. Economist Linda Yueh hosts.

Title: Crisis and desire
Guests & Speakers: Meg Rosoff, Elise Valmorbida, Nick Zangwill
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning authors Elise Valmorbida and Meg Rosoff and philosopher and an honorary professor at UCL Nick Zangwill discuss the call of the catastrophe and calamity. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is our focus on negative human experiences universal, a hangover from our evolutionary past and originally a survival technique? Award-winning authors Elise Valmorbida and Meg Rosoff, and philosopher Nick Zangwill discuss the call of the catastrophe and calamity. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.

Title: Extra-terrestrial life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Avi Loeb is Professor of Science at Harvard University, working primarily in astrophysics and cosmology. A New-York Times bestselling author, he consistently makes headlines for advocating that the search for intelligent extra-terrestrial life should be mainstream science. The only reason it isn't, he maintains, is unscientific prejudice.
Synopsis & Topics: Join Avi Loeb as he discusses the potential for alien life on other planets.

Title: Beyond innocence and guilt
Guests & Speakers: Galen Strawson, Massimo Pigliucci, Sarah Garfinkel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eminent philosopher and literary critic Galen Strawson, stoic philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, and neuroscientist Sarah Garfinkel debate the essence of innocence and guilt. Hosted by novelist Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: Eminent philosopher Galen Strawson, stoic philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, and neuroscientist Sarah Garfinkel debate the essence of innocence and guilt. Joanna Kavenna hosts.

Title: How we failed to predict inflation
Guests & Speakers: Rana Mitter, Vince Cable, Izabella Kaminska
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder and editor of the Blind Spot Izabella Kaminska, former Leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, and Professor of the history and politics of modern China at Oxford University Rana Mitter discuss how accurate economic forecasting can be. Stephanie Hegarty hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we really trust economic forecasting? Founder and editor of the Blind Spot Izabella Kaminska, former Leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, and Professor of the history and politics of modern China at Oxford University Rana Mitter discuss. Stephanie Hegarty hosts.

Title: How innovation works
Synopsis & Topics: Journalist and popular science writer Matt Ridley gets real about innovation, arguing that revolutions, be they in business, government, or the academy, have to start from the bottom up.

Title: A material world
Guests & Speakers: Deirdre McCloskey, Peter Tatchell, Bhaskar Sunkara
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founding editor and publisher of Jacobin and author of 'The Socialist Manifesto' Bhaskar Sunkara, Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics and History Deirdre McCloskey and human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell discuss consumer culture. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: What should we really think about consumer culture? Author of 'The Socialist Manifesto' Bhaskar Sunkara, Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics and History Deirdre McCloskey and human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell discuss. Rana Mitter hosts.

Title: This is my land
Guests & Speakers: Minna Salami, Rana Mitter, Eric Kaufmann
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Minna Salami is a Finnish Nigerian journalist, feminist and author. She has written on the experiences of Nigerian women, the African Diaspora and feminism through her award winning blog, MsAfropolitan. Additionally, she authored 'Sensuous Knowledge: A Black Feminist Approach for Everyone' and co-authored 'The Power Book: What is It, Who Has it and Why?'. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at Birkbeck College, University of London. He specialises in nationalism, political demography, and demography of the religious and irreligious. His most recent book is ‘Whiteshift: Populism, Immigration and the Future of White Majorities’ about the upsurge of right-wing populism in the West. Rana Mitter is Professor of the history and politics of modern China at Oxford University. Rana was educated at King's College. He has been elected for several prestigious positions including president of the Cambridge Union, Kennedy Scholar at Harvard University and Fellow of the British Academy. In 2019 he was appointed an OBE for his services to education. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can the West only atone for its colonial past by giving back all it took from indigenous communities?

Title: How to lose your head
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Lang is an 'enlightened mystic' and teacher of spirituality. He is also the author of "The Man with No Head: The Life and Ideas of Douglas Harding", where he gives us insight into who this great man was and what he discovered.
Synopsis & Topics: While hiking in the Himalayas, philosopher of mind Douglas Harding suddenly realised that he had no head. Now, enlightened mystic and author of "The Man with No Head: The Life and Ideas of Douglas Harding" Richard Lang gives us insight into  who this great man was and what he discovered.

Title: Life, death and money
Guests & Speakers: James Davies, Susan Michie, Linda Bauld
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chief Social Policy Advisor to the Scottish government Linda Bauld, author of Sedated James Davies and eminent psychologist Susan Michie debate the future of healthcare. Hosted by leading psychiatrist, Mark Salter.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we stop focussing on doctors and hospitals, money and medical intervention, and instead focus on lifestyle and well being? Chief Social Policy Advisor to the Scottish government Linda Bauld, author of Sedated James Davies and eminent psychologist Susan Michie debate the future of healthcare. Mark Salter hosts.

Title: The dawn of consciousness
Guests & Speakers: Donald Hoffman, Iain McGilchrist, Eva Jablonka, Michelle Montague
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Famed cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman, celebrated psychiatrist and former literary scholar Iain McGilchrist, trailblaizing evolutionary theorist and geneticist Eva Jablonka and pioneering philosopher of consciousness Michelle Montague lock horns over whether consciousness evolved. Robert Lawrence Kuhn hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is consciousness an accurate description of what's happening to us, a sort of internal dashboard of the current state of affairs? Or is it a construction made to achieve certain outcomes? Robert Lawrence Kuhn hosts a debate with cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman, psychiatrist and author Iain McGilchrist, theorist Eva Jablonka and philosopher Michelle Montague.

Title: The life and philosophy of Martin Rees
Synopsis & Topics: Astronomer Royal and best-selling science author, Martin Rees discusses the ideas and experiences which led to his illustrious career.

Title: Innovation and the future of capitalism
Guests & Speakers: Michael Howard, Pravin Krishna, Prem Shankar Jha
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pravin Krishna is the Chung Ju Yung Distinguished Professor of International Economics and Business at Johns Hopkins University. He has served as a consultant to the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and is also a regular host on the podcast Transforming India. Michael Howard was Leader of the Conservative Party in the early 2000s. Prior to his leadership, he was a senior cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher and John Major, holding prestigious positions including Secretary of State for Employment, Secretary of State for the Environment and Home Secretary. Prem Shankar Jha is an Indian economist, journalist and writer. He has served in the United Nations Development Programme, the World Bank and as the information advisor to the Prime Minister of India. Rajini Vaidyanathan hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: From Adam Smith to John Maynard Keynes economists have argued for free trade, and the innovative power of capitalism, to improve living standards and prosperity. But are free trade and innovation not the capitalist panacea, but rather the cause of increased inequality? Former conservative leader Michael Howard debates with Johns Hopkins professor of economics Pravin Krishna and eminent Indian economist Prem Shankar Jha. Rajini Vaidyanathan hosts.

Title: Language and power
Guests & Speakers: Kehinde Andrews, John McWhorter, L. A. Paul
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Black Studies at Birmingham City University Kehinde Andrews, linguist and Associate Professor of English and comparative literature at Columbia University John McWhorter, and Professor of philosophy and cognitive science at Yale University Laurie Ann Paul discuss whether or not language is capable of communicating lived experience. Mary-Jane Rubenstein hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Will language ever allow us to truly communicate? And if not, what are we to do? Birmingham City professor of black studies Kehinde Andrews debates with Columbia's John McWhorter and Yale cognitive scientist Laurie Ann Paul. Mary Jane Rubenstein hosts.

Title: Truss defends vision for the future of Britain
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Elizabeth Truss is a British politician who has been the Member of Parliament for South West Norfolk since 2010. She has served in numerous ministerial poisitions, and currently holds the position of Foreign Secretary.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Tory leadership hopeful Liz Truss outlines her vision for how the conservative party needs to adapt. The current foreign secretary has served in numerous ministerial posts since becoming the MP for Sout West Norfolk in 2010.

Title: Seeing how it is
Guests & Speakers: Angela Saini, Steve Fuller, Rupert Sheldrake, Peter Atkins
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steve Fuller is an academic studying science and technology. Fuller has published prolifically on such topics as intelligent design, the sociology of academia, and transhumanism. Fuller believes that academics reserve the special right to express their views without fear of retaliation. Angela Saini is an award-winning science journalist, author and broadcaster.She regularly presents science programmes for the BBC, and her writing has appeared in publications ranging from New Scientist, Wired and the Guardian. She wrote Inferior: How Science Got Women Wrong in 2017. Her book Superior: The Return of Race Science addresses the racial biases present in current scientific practices. Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist and bestselling author. Best known for his 2012 book 'The Science Delusion' and the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. He has taken issue with the New Atheists and has challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging. Peter Atkins is a chemist and Fellow of Lincoln College. He’s a Distinguished Supporter of Humanists UK, Atkins is outspoken in his opposition to religion. He argues that religion involves a lack of confidence in human powers of comprehension, encouraging us to be satisfied with ignorance instead of striving to understand the universe. Danielle Sands hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: From Newton to Einstein, science has been built on observation. But might it be time to rethink the value of the empirical? Academic Steve Fuller, journalist Angela Saini, scientist Ruper Sheldrake and chemist Peter Atkins debate. Danielle Sands hosts.

Title: China and the art of peace
Guests & Speakers: Cindy Yu, Nigel Inkster, Chris Parry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author and strategic forecaster Chris Parry, former director of operations and intelligence for MI6 Nigel Inkster, China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator Cindy Yu. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: The ancient Chinese philosopher Sun Tzu declared 'in peace prepare for war'. Should this be Western strategy? Author Chris Parry, former  MI6 director Nigel Inkster, and editor at the Spectator Cindy Yu debate. Hilary Lawson hosts

Title: Gods, worlds and monsters
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, USA. Her book Worlds Without End: The Many Lives of the Universe examines cosmological models throughout history, from the world-views of the Ancient Greeks through to the well-respected multiverse theory in modern science. She links contemporary models of the universe to their forerunners and explores the reason for their recent resurgence.
Synopsis & Topics: Pantheism is the belief that reality and gods are one and the same. Join Mary Jane Rubenstein, professor of religion at Wesleyan University, Connecticut, as she explores how this idea threatens more than just religion.

Title: Bad boys
Guests & Speakers: Rowan Pelling, Myriam François, Ella Whelan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political commentator and assistant editor at Spiked, Ella Whelan is the author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. Myriam François is a journalist and presenter, as well as a Research Associate at the SOAS Centre for Islamic Studies. Journalist and broadcaster, Rowan Pelling is former editor of The Erotic Review, founder of The Amorist and columnist at the Daily Telegraph. Sean Curran hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it time to address the idea that 'bad boys' are sexy, and redefine masculinity? Spiked journalist Ella Whelan debates with SOAS's Myriam François and broadcaster Rowan Pelling. Sean Curran hosts.

Title: A matter of facts
Guests & Speakers: Anandi Hattiangadi, Sophie Grace Chappell, Simon Blackburn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Philosophy at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell, Professor of Philosophy at Stockholm University Anandi Hattiangadi and Professor of Philosophy at the New College of the Humanities Simon Blackburn dicuss the changing value of truth in contemporary society. Julian Baggini hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Simon Blackburn, Sophie-Grace Chappell, Anandi Hattiangadi challenge the value of facts in contemporary society.

Title: Freeing Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tulip Siddiq is a British politician serving as the Member of Parliament for Hampstead and Kilburn since 2015. A member of the Labour Party, she previously was the Camden London Borough Councillor for Regent's Park from 2010 until 2014.
Synopsis & Topics: Left-wing politician Tulip Siddiq explores the background behind Ratcliffe's case and how it ultimately got resolved.

Title: The world that disappeared
Guests & Speakers: Peter Atkins, James Ladyman, Joanna Kavenna
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chemist and Fellow of Lincoln College Peter Atkins, Philosopher of Science at the University of Bristol James Ladyman and author of A Field Guide to Reality Joanna Kavenna debate whether the everyday objects that surround us are an illusion. Julian Baggini hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Chemist Peter Atkins, Philosopher of science James Ladyman and author of "A Field Guide to Reality" Joanna Kavenna take part in a discussion over what the world is made of.

Title: Profits, value and fantasy
Guests & Speakers: Mark Littlewood, Anatole Kaletsky, Nicole Aschoff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of 'The New Prophets of Capital', Nicole Aschoff, Director of the Institute of Economic Affairs, Mark Littlewood and economist Anatole Kaletsky explore the current asymmetries between profits and value. Hosted by researcher and author, Stephanie Hare.
Synopsis & Topics: Once companies needed to make profits to be successful. Now that seems so 20th century. But are we heading for bust, chaos and disruption? Author Nicole Aschoff, Institute of Economic Affairs Director Mark Littlewood and economist Anatole Kaletsky debate. Stephanie Hare hosts.

Title: Dilemmas of Black Manhood
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focusses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies and Public Health.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, philosopher Tommy Curry discusses how we distinguish racism as a structural, cultural and historical process from racism merely as an individual bias.

Title: Russia, Ukraine and the Future of Economics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Vince Cable is a former acting leader of the Liberal Democrats and was an MP for over twenty years. He is the author of Money and Power, and the Chinese Conundrum.
Synopsis & Topics: Join former Liberal Democrat leader Vince Cable to explore how those in power have controlled the global economy over history and how they are shaping it today

Title: Nature: friend or foe?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-famous intellectual Yuval Noah Harari and firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek debate whether nature is friend or foe. Hosted by scientist Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Is our attachment to nature undermining belief in ourselves? Should we have more faith in the human and less trust in nature? World-famous intellectual and Sapiens author Yuval Noah Harari debates with firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.

Title: What is Happiness?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the LSE. His main research interests are human behaviour and happiness, and the relationships between them, particularly as they apply to policy. He is author of the bestselling books Happiness by Design and Happy Ever After. He is also host of the Duck / Rabbit podcast about the polarisation problem in our society.
Synopsis & Topics: From ancient philosophers to modern scientists we have been perplexed by happiness. In this interview, Professor of Behavioural Science at the LSE, Paul Dolan, discusses what happiness is and whether it should affect public policy.

Title: From the matrix to the metaverse
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Chalmers is an Australian philosopher and cognitive scientist who specialises in the philosophy of mind, language and more recently, virtual reality. He is a Professor of Philosophy and Neural Science at New York University, as well as co-director of NYU's Center for Mind, Brain and Consciousness.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we really live meaningful lives inside a virtual world? From virtual reality to the metaverse, join world-renowned philosopher and cognitive scientist David Chalmers as he outlines his highly original take.

Title: The oldest gods
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Melanie Challenger, Peter Sjöstedt-H, Tim Palmer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes, internationally-renowned climate scientist Tim Palmer, and author-broadcaster-podcaster Melanie Challenger test each other's beliefs about nature and god. Hosted by philosopher Hilary Lawson
Synopsis & Topics: Psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes, internationally-renowned climate scientist Tim Palmer, and author-broadcaster-podcaster Melanie Challenger test each other's beliefs about nature and god. Hosted by philosopher Hilary Lawson

Title: The life and philosophy of Matt Hancock
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matt Hancock is a British politician who served as Secretary of State for Health and Social Care from 2018 to 2021. He is a member of the Conservative Party, and has been Member of Parliament for West Suffolk since 2010.
Synopsis & Topics: Senior Times journalist Manveen Rana hosts a tell-all interview with former UK Health Secretary Matt Hancock. Hancock explores his life as a politician, how he got where he is, and where he goes next.

Title: Dreams, delusions and data
Guests & Speakers: Kenneth Cukier, Joanna Bryson, Noortje Marres
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished journalist Kenneth Cukier, celebrated professor of ethics Joanna Bryson and esteemed academic Noortje Marres debate the opportunities and limits of Big Data. Luke Robert Mason hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Distinguished journalist Kenneth Cukier, celebrated professor of ethics Joanna Bryson and esteemed academic Noortje Marres debate the opportunities and limits of Big Data. Luke Robert Mason hosts.

Title: The end of affluence
Guests & Speakers: Vince Cable, Grace Blakeley, Stephen D. King
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary economist Stephen King, distinguished British politician Vince Cable and trailblazing political commentator Grace Blakeley debate the limits of government debt. Linda Yueh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: The West is facing what some are calling the greatest debt crisis of all time in the wake of the pandemic. But is it as bad as it sounds? Economist Stephen King debates with British politician Vince Cable and trailblazer Grace Blakeley. Linda Yueh hosts.

Title: The world is not made of things
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Iain McGilchrist is psychiatrist, writer, and former Oxford literary scholar. He is committed to the idea that the mind and brain can be understood only by seeing them in the broadest possible context, a notion which is fundamental to his two most famous works: The Master and his Emissary, and The Matter With Things
Synopsis & Topics: Psychiatrist, writer and former Oxford scholar Iain Mcgilchrist has a unique perspective on the world, the mind, and everything in between. Here he discusses his latest book, The Matter with Things: Our Brains, Our Delusions, and the Unmaking of the World.

Title: How to write a memoir
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Laura Coleman is the author of the widely praised memoir 'The Puma Years', which tells of her liberating journey in the Amazon jungle.
Synopsis & Topics: We all have a life story. But how best to tell it? Join Laura Coleman, author of the widely praised memoir The Puma Years, to learn the ins and outs of telling your story.

Title: Inheriting inequality
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Paul Mason, Polly Mackenzie
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning journalist and broadcaster David Aaronovitch, British commentator and former economics editor at the BBC Paul Mason and Chief Executive of Demos Polly Mackenzie discuss how to tackle inherited wealth. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is inherited wealth an issue - and if so, how do we tackle it? Commentators David Aaronovitch and Paul Mason debate with Demos' Polly Mackenzie. Hosted by Rana Mitter

Title: If it doesn't kill you
Guests & Speakers: Havi Carel, Anders Sandberg, Susie Orbach
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Britain’s most beloved psychotherapist and author of “Fat is a Feminist Issue” Susie Orbach, renowned transhumanist Anders Sandberg, and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Bristol Havi Carel explore the significance of suffering in modern society. Hosted by philosopher Julian Baggini.
Synopsis & Topics: Is suffering necessary for a meaningful life? Psychotherapist Susie Orbach, transhumanist Anders Sandberg, and philosopher Havi Carel debate. Hosted by Julian Baggini.

Title: Untangling space and time
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Maudlin is founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics and he is also Professor of Philosophy at New York University. He has done influential work on the metaphysical foundations of physics and logic.
Synopsis & Topics: Is our understanding of 'space-time' in need of a rethink? Influential philosopher of science and founder of the John Bell Institute, Tim Maudlin, argues for the separation of space and time.

Title: Rethinking reason
Guests & Speakers: Timothy Williamson, Nina Power, Sophie Archer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eminent philosopher of mind and psychology Sophie Archer, groundbreaking Oxford logician Timothy Williamson and trailblazing cultural critic Nina Power put reason and emotion to the test. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher of mind and psychology Sophie Archer, Oxford logician Timothy Williamson and  cultural critic Nina Power put reason and emotion to the test. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart

Title: The universe, fixity and flux
Guests & Speakers: Lee Smolin, Sabine Hossenfelder, Paul Davies
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Physics professor Lee Smolin, theoretical physicist and author Sabine Hossenfelder and cosmologist and author Paul Davies thrash out the big questions about the nature of the universe. Hosted by renowned science writer, Phillip Ball.
Synopsis & Topics: Physics legend Lee Smolin, theoretical physicist and author Sabine Hossenfelder and cosmologist Paul Davies thrash out the big questions about the nature of the universe. Phillip Ball hosts.

Title: The truth about the nuclear threat
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The author of Winning and Losing the Nuclear Peace: The Rise, Demise, and Revival of Arms Control Michael Krepon uncovers the truth about nuclear deterrence, and what it means for the future of conflict.
Synopsis & Topics: Have we been ignoring a central paradox in political theory? Nuclear risk expert Michael Krepon uncovers the truth about nuclear deterrence, and what it means for the future of conflict.

Title: How to do philosophy with Moby Dick
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dean Moyar is Professor of Philosophy and Director of Graduate Studies at Johns Hopkins University. He is the author of 'Hegel's Conscience' and 'Hegel's Value: Justice as the Living Good'. He is currently working on an edited volume on Moby-Dick for the Oxford Studies in Philosophy and Literature series.
Synopsis & Topics: Herman Melville’s philosophical aspirations in Moby-Dick have long been recognized. Yet it often seems like the quest for ultimate knowledge is part of the problem rather than an answer. Join John Hopkins Professor of Philosophy Dean Moyar as he expounds on the philosophy of the landmark text.

Title: The eclipse of the West
Guests & Speakers: Peter Tatchell, Philip Collins, Cindy Yu
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Writer-in-chief at The Draft Phil Collins, eminent LGBT activist and human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell and China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator Cindy Yu debate whether the strengths of liberal democracy win through and survive the economic eclipse of the West. Linda Yueh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the West on its way out? The Draft's Phil Collins, eminent activist Peter Tatchell, and The Spectator's China reporter Cindy Yu debate. Linda Yueh hosts.

Title: Human justice and machine intelligence
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Joanna Bryson is professor at Hertie School in Berlin. She works on Artificial Intelligence, ethics and collaborative cognition. She advises governments, corporations, and other agencies globally, particularly on AI policy.
Synopsis & Topics: Are the problems with AI just technological? Artificial Intelligence expert athe the Hertie School in Berlin Joanna Bryson discusses human intelligence, social conditions and the problem of anthropomorphism.

Title: Heaven is other people
Guests & Speakers: Mark Salter, Lucy Johnstone, Sarah Garfinkel
Synopsis & Topics: Is mental wellbeing a purely social issue? Clinical psychologist Lucy Johnstone, NHS psychiatrist Mark Salter and UCL Professor of Neuroscience Sarah Garfinkel debate. Hosted by author Joanna Kavenna.

Title: Fantasy and the void
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Scientist, author, and parapsychology researcher Rupert Sheldrake, Hegelian psychoanalyst Slavoj Zizek and Professor of History at University of Madison-Wisconsin Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen discuss whether the persistence of religion is an extended but ultimately temporary phenomenon. Wes Alwan hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Will science ever replace religion? Slavoj Zizek debates with Rupert Sheldrake and Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen. Wes Alwan Hosts.

Title: How to fight back
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter also identifies as a humanist, believing that reason, science and ethics are the best way to promote human rights and welfare.
Synopsis & Topics: Interview with legendary activist, co-founder of queer human rights group OutRage, and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, Peter Tatchell. Peter discusses his life in activism and the progress of the LGBT movement, free speech and social progress.

Title: From feminism to politics and back again
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Thangam has co-authored two books and published numerous papers on domestic violence.
Synopsis & Topics: Shadow Leader of the House Thangam Debbonaire expounds on the idea of a feminist politician, explaining her move from political feminism to feminist politics.

Title: Sex, relationships and the future
Guests & Speakers: Julie Bindel, John Milbank, Olivia Fane
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Writer and author of ‘Why Sex Doesn’t Matter' Olivia Fane, English Anglican theologian and Emeritus Professor at the University of Nottingham John Milbank and radical feminist writer, journalist and author Julie Bindel discuss the idea of separating sex and relationships. Barry Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we pursue love and sex separately? Author Olivia Fane, Theologian John Milbank, and radical feminist Julie Bindel debate sex and love. Barry C. Smith Hosts.

Title: The quest for a final theory
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Famed futurist and co-founder of String Field Theory Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature, penning numerous bestselling books along the way.
Synopsis & Topics: String Field Theory co-founder and famed YouTube futurist Michio Kaku carries on Einstein's quest to unify the four fundamental forces of nature.

Title: Atheism revisited
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Julian Baggini is a British philosopher, journalist and author of over 20 philosophical books. Since graduating with a PhD from University College London in 1997, he has co-founded The Philosopher's Magazine and been a regular contributor to both national and international newspapers.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher and author of Atheism: a Very Short Introduction, Julian Baggini, explores the new landscape of atheism in the 21st century.

Title: Dangerous desires
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, David Nutt, Anna Waldstein
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chair of the Independent Scientific Committee on Drugs, David Nutt, Medical Anthropology and Ethnobotany academic Anna Waldstein, and bestselling author Joanna Kavenna go head to head on desire and restraint. Hosted by Postdoctoral Training Fellow at the Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Drug expert David Nutt, Medical anthropologist Anna Waldstein and author Joanna Kavenna go head to head on desire and restraint. The Crick Institute's Güneş Taylor hosts.

Title: War and peace in Afghanistan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tariq Ali is a famed political activist, writer, journalist, historian, filmmaker, and public intellectual. His latest book 'The Forty-Year War in Afghanistan: A Chronicle Foretold' explores the history and present of the war in Afghanistan.
Synopsis & Topics: What does the future hold for a traumatised Afghan people? Legendary activist and author of 'The Forty Year War in Afghanistan' Tariq Ali explores the history and present of war in Afghanistan.

Title: The trouble with sex
Guests & Speakers: Yaron Brook, Liara Roux, Suzannah Weiss
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Current chairman of the board at the Ayn Rand Institute, Yaron Brook, sex worker and activist Liara Roux, and feminist writer Suzannah Weiss discuss how our attitudes to sex are affected by an increasingly technological world. Hosted by writer and broadcaster, Myriam François.
Synopsis & Topics: Why is our culture obsessed with sex? Ayn Rand institute chair Yaron Brook, sex worker Liara Roux, and writer Suzannah Weiss debate the impact of technology on sex. Myriam Francois hosts.

Title: Reality, fantasy and metaphor
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Rupert Sheldrake, Peter Atkins, Güneş Taylor
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Fellow at the Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor, scientist and author Rupert Sheldrake, chemist and author of popular works of science Peter Atkins and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson debate whether scientific metaphors can be considered real descriptions of an underlying universe. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Can science really describe reality through metaphor? Crick Institute Geneticist Güneş Taylor, parapsychologist Rupert Sheldrake, chemist Peter Atkins and philosopher Hilary Lawson debate. Joanna Kavenna hosts.

Title: Determinism is a superstition
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: James Tartaglia is a British philosopher, and Professor of Metaphysical Philosophy at Keele University. He is the author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: Gods and Titans. His main interest is in understanding and enhancing awareness of the nature of philosophical inquiry. James also leads a Jazz-Philosophy fusion band called 'Continuum of Selves'.
Synopsis & Topics: British philosopher and  author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: Gods and Titans, James Tartaglia, discusses his life and career in philosophy and jazz.

Title: The new ruling class
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Economist, politician and best-selling author Yanis Varoufakis argues that a radical reassessment of property rights over machines and data is the only way for us to confront this new ruling class.
Synopsis & Topics: Economist, politician and author Yanis Varoufakis argues that command capital is crushing democracy and giving rise to a technofeudal new ruling class.

Title: Popularity and prejudice
Guests & Speakers: Janne Teller, Meg Rosoff, Minna Salami, Stanley Fish
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Literary theorist Stanley Fish, author of How I Live Now, Meg Rosoff, journalist and editor of MsAfropolitan, Minna Salami and writer and essayist Janne Teller rethink what makes a great work of art. Hosted by BBC Parliamentary Correspondent, Sean Curran.
Synopsis & Topics: Do we need to rethink what makes a great work of art? Literary theorist Stanley Fish, author Meg Rosoff, MsAfropolitan editor Minna Salami and writer Janne Teller debate. Sean Curran hosts.

Title: In conversation with Rupert Sheldrake
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of The Science Delusion, Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist whose research led to the theory of morphic resonance and nature's memory. He has also written on altered states of consciousness in Ways To Go Beyond.
Synopsis & Topics: Influential scientist whose research led to the theory of morphic resonance, and author of Ways to Go Beyond, Rupert Sheldrake discusses the past, present and future of the mind with philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes.

Title: The new right
Guests & Speakers: Bim Afolami, Deirdre McCloskey, Paul Mason
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative MP for Hitchin and Harpenden, Bim Afolami, author and Professor of Economics at the University of Illinois, Deirdre McCloskey, and author and political commentator, Paul Mason discuss the past, present and future of conservatism. Hosted by distinguished historian, Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Does the right need to re-assess its core values? Conservative MP Bim Afolami, Professor of Economics Deirdre McCloskey, and author Paul Mason discuss the nature of conservatism. Rana Mitter hosts.

Title: Models, metaphors and minds
Guests & Speakers: Kenneth Cukier, Peter Sjöstedt-H, Joanna Bryson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Senior Economist Editor and author Kenneth Cukier, world-leading ethics, technology and AI expert Joanna Bryson, and psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes get to grips with the concept of a 'mind'.
Synopsis & Topics: Economist senior editor Kenneth Cukier, ethics and AI expert Joanna Bryson, and psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes get to grips with the concept of a 'mind'.

Title: How to create art: by a scientist
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Walter Gilbert is biochemist, physicist, businessman, Nobel laureate and artist. Since being awarded the 1980 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, he has launched a successful career in digital photography.
Synopsis & Topics: Nobel prize winning biochemist, physicist and artist Walter Gilbert discusses his work and explores the powerful connections between art and science

Title: Life, the universe, and everything else
Guests & Speakers: Julian Baggini, Peter Atkins, Philip Goff, Güneş Taylor
Synopsis & Topics: Can philosophy offset the limitations of the scientific model in the search for progress? Editor Julian Baggini, chemist Peter Atkins, researcher Güneş Taylor, and philosopher Philip Goff debate. Melanie Challenger hosts.

Title: Cracking the girl code
Guests & Speakers: Hannah Dawson, Nina Power, Maya Oppenheim
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Social theorist and philosopher Nina Power, journalist Maya Oppenheim and historian of political thought at Kings College London Hannah Dawson debate whether or not women should support other women independently of their qualities and their approach. Barry Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: With the gap between girl bosses and activists widening, where is the future of feminism heading? Journalist Maya Oppenheim, philosopher Nina Power and historian Hannah Dawson debate the infamous 'girl code'. Barry Smith hosts.

Title: Science needs philosophy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist who specialises in the foundations of physics. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the group on Superfluid Dark Matter. She is the author of Lost in Math: How Beauty Leads Physics Astray, and the forthcoming Existential Physics: A Scientist's Guide to Life's Biggest Questions. Hossenfelder also has a popular YouTube channel called "Science without the gobbledygook".
Synopsis & Topics: What is the relationship between physics and philosophy? Physicist and dark matter expert Sabine Hossenfelder explores how the two disciplines interact and intersect.

Title: Sex against the system
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Liara Roux is an American author, sex worker, indie porn director and human rights activist. Roux has written for Vice Media and HuffPost and has gathered a strong online following throughout her career. She is also an activist and community organizer who predominantly champions fighting structural discrimination against sex workers.
Synopsis & Topics: The politics of sex work have been contested for millennia - but what is the current state of affairs? American author, sex worker and activist Liara Roux lays bare her experiences.

Title: New gods and lost rituals
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Peter Atkins, Myriam François
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Research associate at the Centre for Islamic Studies at SOAS Myriam François, Oxford scientist and humanist Peter Atkins and philosopher and Closure theorist Hilary Lawson debate spirituality and secularism. Hosted by leading psychiatrist, Mark Salter.
Synopsis & Topics: Does religion have a place in today's world? Philosopher Hilary Lawson, humanist Peter Atkins, and Islamic Studies expert Myriam Francois debate. Psychiatrist Mark Salter hosts.

Title: The workforce revolution
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lord Peter Lilley is a British Conservative politician. He is a member of the House of Lords and was an MP from 1983 to 2017. He was a Cabinet minister in the governments of Margaret Thatcher and John Major, and was Chairman of the Globalisation and Global Poverty Policy Review Group under David Cameron.
Synopsis & Topics: Former cabinet minister Lord Peter Lilley offers his answer to the burgeoning workforce crisis facing the UK in the wake of Brexit and COVID-19 - setting out his vision for home-grown talent rising to the occasion.

Title: Dangerous data
Guests & Speakers: Donald Hoffman, Tim Maudlin, Lisa Randall
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pioneering American physicist Lisa Randall, renowned philosopher of science Tim Maudlin and legendary cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman argue over the fundamental nature of science. Biologist Güneş Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we abandon the idea that science provides absolute answers? Physicist Lisa Randall, philosopher Tim Maudlin and cognitive expert Donald Hoffman debate. Gunes Taylor hosts.

Title: The power of the present
Guests & Speakers: Meg Rosoff, Peter Doran, Alex Nunn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lecturer in Law and Government at Queen's University Belfast, Peter Doran, Head of Movement Building at Action For Happiness, Alex Nunn, and award-winning author, Meg Rosoff, debate the value of mindfulness. Hosted by distinguished historian, Rana Mitter.
Synopsis & Topics: Is mindfulness a vital antidote to the misery of humankind - or is it just a means to hide from the reality of life? Award-winning author Meg Rosoff debates with Action for Happiness' Alex Nunn and QUB Law expert Peter Doran. Rana Mitter hosts.

Title: How philosophy occupies the everyday
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Timothy Williamson is the Wykeham Professor of Logic at the University of Oxford and a fellow of New College, Oxford. His main research areas are philosophy of logic, philosophy of language, epistemology and metaphysics. He is the author of the widely translated Knowledge and Its Limits and The Philosophy of Philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Legendary philosopher of logic Timothy Williamson discusses philosophy's place in our lives, its similarities to natural sciences, and how language fails to help us understand reality.

Title: The hidden virtues of commercialism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jesse Norman is a leading British Conservative Party politician currently serving as the Financial Secretary to the Treasury and has been an MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010. He was a director at Barclays before leaving to research and teach at University College London. Norman has been recognised by the political editor of the Spectator as a potential future Leader of the Conservative Party.
Synopsis & Topics: UK Financial Secretary to the Treasury Jesse Norman explores how commercial societies can produce virtuous moral norms.

Title: Memes all the way down
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Massimo Pigliucci, Joanna Bryson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson, Professor of Ethics and Technology at Hertie School Joanna Bryson and Professor of Philosophy at City College of New York Massimo Pigliucci discuss whether or not it is useful to think about sharing mimetic information like genetic information. Gunes Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is Dawkins' concept useful? Philosophers Hilary Lawson and Massimo Pigliucci discuss with ethics and technology professor Joanna Bryson. Gunes Taylor hosts.

Title: The trouble with modern feminism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Julie Bindel is a radical feminist activist, author and columnist for The Guardian. She co-founded Justice for Women and has campaigned against male violence and sex-trafficking. Her most recent book is 'Feminism for Women'.
Synopsis & Topics: Feminist activist, author and Guardian columnist, Julie Bindel, discusses her early years as an activist and the trouble with modern day feminism.

Title: Asking ultimate questions
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the creator, writer, host and executive producer of Closer To Truth. He has written or edited over 30 books, including The Mystery of Existence: Why is there Anything At All? And Closer to Truth: Challenging Current Belief.
Synopsis & Topics: Closer to Truth host Robert Lawrence Kuhn uncovers the most common thread running through the most profound mysteries of existence and human sentience.

Title: The inflation crisis
Guests & Speakers: Izabella Kaminska, Polly Toynbee, Steve Hanke
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Reagan advisor Steve Hanke, award winning author and journalist Polly Toynbee and Lead Editor of FT Alphaville Izabella Kaminska clash over the causes of inflation and the future of our economy. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Former Reagan advisor Steve Hanke, award winning journalist Polly Toynbee and the FT's Izabella Kaminska clash over the future of our economy. Rana Mitter hosts.

Title: Wave goodbye to being human
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Futures theorist Luke Robert Mason is a researcher, filmmaker and digital media artist. He has been a frequent contributor to BBC Click Radio, The Guardian, Discovery Channel, VICE Motherboard, Wired Magazine and Futurism.com.
Synopsis & Topics: The transhumanist dream may soon be a reality. Join BBC Click, VICE and Wired contributor Luke Robert Mason as he examines the possibilities of an enhanced future.

Title: Trash, trends and the transcendent
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Rupert Sheldrake, Minna Salami, Olivia Fane
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Thought-provoking author Olivia Fane, journalist and social critic Minna Salami, radical biologist Rupert Sheldrake and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna interrogate our awe at what lies beyond, and how it does - and doesn't - manifest today. Mark Salter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: What really is the sublime and where can we find it? Author Olivia Fane, radical biologist Rupert Sheldrake and novelist Joanna Kavenna debate. Mark Salter hosts.

Title: The return of metaphysics
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Galen Strawson, Patricia Churchland
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary Neurophilosophy pioneer Patricia Churchland, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and analytic philosopher Galen Strawson lock horns over the future of metaphysics.
Synopsis & Topics: Neurophilosophy pioneer Patricia Churchland, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and analytic philosopher Galen Strawson lock horns over the future of metaphysics.

Title: Ukraine: The Deceit of the West
Guests & Speakers: Joseph Nye, Tariq Ali, Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Domitilla Sagramoso
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political activist and historian Tariq Ali, professor Emeritus at Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government Joseph Nye, writer and political commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown and senior lecturer in Security and Development Domitilla Sagramoso debate whether the West become a deceitful and untrustworthy ally. Economist Linda Yueh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Has the West become an untrustworthy ally? With author Tariq Ali, Harvard's Joseph Nye, Russia expert Domitilla Sagramoso and Yasmin Alibhai-Brown. Linda Yueh hosts.

Title: Our place in the cosmos
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Astrophysicist and Astronomer Royal for Scotland Catherine Heymans takes us on a virtual tour of the visible night sky from the Royal Observatory, Edinburgh.
Synopsis & Topics: Astronomer Royal for Scotland Catherine Heymans takes us on a tour of the cosmos, discussing Dark Matter, the possibility of life on other planets, and more.

Title: Evolutionary Masters of the Universe
Guests & Speakers: Steve Fuller, Angela Saini, Natalie Kofler
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Molecular biologist and founding director of Editing Nature at Yale University Natalie Kofler, author of Humanity 2.0 Professor Steve Fuller, and science journalist and author of Geek Nation Angela Saini explore the radical new possibilities of biotechnology. Hosted by filmmaker and politician David Malone.
Synopsis & Topics: Is CRISPR gene editing the key to improving health? Or is this a dangerous fantasy? With Natalie Kofler, Steve Fuller, and Angela Saini. David Malone hosts.

Title: Consciousness and fundamental physics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Goff is a philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview. His 2019 book Galileo's Error sets out his defence of panpsychism rooted in an analysis of the work of Arthur Eddington and Bertrand Russell.
Synopsis & Topics: Philip Goff responds to recent critiques of panpsychism by theoretical physicists Sean Carroll and Sabine Hossenfelder, and explores some implications for the science of consciousness.

Title: The African dream
Guests & Speakers: Eka Ikpe, Stefan Dercon, Vince Cable
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Watch former leader of the Liberal Democrats Sir Vince Cable, researcher Eka Ikpe and economist Stefan Dercon as they discuss whether foreign investment a necessary and valuable part of economic growth, or if it is simply ceding power and wealth to others. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is pan-Africanism the way forward? Sir Vince Cable debates with Africa expert Eka Ipke and economist Stefan Dercon. Isabel Hilton hosts.

Title: How to write and why we should
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Elise Valmorbida grew up Italian in Australia, and lives in London. Her 2018-19 award-winning novel The Madonna of the Mountains has been published internationally in several languages and editions. Other books she has authored include Matilde Waltzing, The TV President, The Winding Stick and The Book of Happy Endings. Elise is also an award-winning indie film producer and wrote SAXON: The Making of a Guerrilla Film.
Synopsis & Topics: Join author of The Madonna of the Mountains and creative writing tutor, Elise Valmorbida, to learn how fantasising can improve well-being and deepen your appreciation of life.

Title: Form and ritual, power and prejudice
Guests & Speakers: Hannah Dawson, Linda Woodhead, Noël Carroll
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Historian of ideas Hannah Dawson pulls no punches debating philosopher of religion Linda Woodhead and distinguished art critic Noel Carroll on the place of formality and ritual in the modern world. Writer and broadcaster Myriam Francois hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is formality outdated? Or is ritual the only way to lift ourselves from the mundane? Historian of ideas Hannah Dawson debates with philosopher Linda Woodhead and art critic Noel Carroll. Myriam Francois hosts.

Title: Tolerance and outrage
Guests & Speakers: Toby Young, Roger Bolton, Myriam François
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Television producer Roger Bolton, broadcaster and academic Myriam Fran ç ois and journalist Toby Young debate why it appears we have become an increasingly intolerant society. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Why does it appear that society is becoming less tolerant? Roger Bolton, Myriam Francois and Toby Young discuss tolerance and outrage.

Title: The science of consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anil Seth is a Professor of Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience at the University of Sussex and author of Being You: A New Science of Consciousness. He is also Co-Director of the Sackler Centre for Consciousness Science and Editor-in-Chief of Neuroscience of Consciousness. He is also a regular contributor to the New Scientist, The Guardian, and BBC, and writes the blog NeuroBanter.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor of Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience, and Author of Being You: A New Science of Consciousness, Anil Seth explores the ultimate mystery of our consciousness experience in this exclusive interview.

Title: Technological parenting
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Melanie Challenger is a researcher on the history of humanity and the natural world, and on environmental philosophy. Her latest book, How to Be Animal: A New History of What It Means to Be Human was published by Canongate in 2021.
Synopsis & Topics: Author Melanie Challenger asks the big questions about parenting and technology. From smartphones to gene-editing; what does it mean to be a parent in a technological age?

Title: Virtue and vice
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Matthew Taylor, Rebecca Roache
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chief Executive of The RSA and former head of the No. 10 Policy Unit Matthew Taylor, ethicist Rebecca Roache and philosopher and Closure theorist Hilary Lawson ask whether it's time to move beyond our fixation on morality is misguided. Author Danielle Sands hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is our belief in morality a dangerous fantasy?UK Policy Unit Head Matthew Taylor, philosopher Hilary Lawson, and ethicist Rebecca Roache debate virtue and vice.

Title: What really makes up China's DNA
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times, History Today, and the London Review of Books, Rana Mitter is Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor of History and Politics of Modern China at Oxfrod University, Rana Mitter, dissects the social, political and economic factors behind China's global rise.

Title: The making of us
Guests & Speakers: Angela Saini, Güneş Taylor, Robert Plomin, Simon Baron-Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Blueprint Robert Plomin, geneticist at The Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor, author of The Essential Difference Simon Baron Cohen and author of Superior Angela Saini lock horns. Hosted by philosopher Barry Smith.
Synopsis & Topics: Are humans shaped by their genetics or their environment? Robert Plomin, Güneş Taylor, Simon Baron Cohen and Angela Saini debate, hosted by Barry Smith.

Title: The search for meaning
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished scientist and author Rupert Sheldrake, philosopher of Wittgenstein Maria Balaska and Professor of Metaphysics James Tartaglia ask whether philosophy can really give meaning to our lives. Danielle Sands hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Do we need the transcendental to give our lives meaning? Rupert Sheldrake, Maria Balaska, James Targalia discuss.

Title: Free will is a necessary illusion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Galen John Strawson is an acclaimed British analytic philosopher and literary critic who works primarily on philosophy of mind and metaphysics. His work covers free will, panpsychism, the mind-body problem, and the self. He has been a consultant editor at The Times Literary Supplement for many years, and a regular book reviewer for The Observer, The Sunday Times, The Independent, the Financial Times and The Guardian. He is the son of philosopher P. F. Strawson.
Synopsis & Topics: Acclaimed analytic philosopher Galen Strawson discusses free will, ultimate moral responsibility, and the illusion of the self.

Title: The Arc of Life: Peter Mandelson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: After navigating himself through a sizeable series of appointments and dismissals during his time in government, Peter Mandelson sheds light on his wealth of political experiences.
Synopsis & Topics: Former spin doctor, architect of Blairism and cabinet minister Lord Peter Mandelson discusses his life in politics with David Aaranovitch.

Title: The next environmental crisis
Guests & Speakers: Martin Rees, Thomas Sterner, Judith Curry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cosmologist, astrophysicist, and Astronomer Royal Martin Rees, award winning economist and Professor of Environmental Economics Thomas Sterner, and controversial climatologist Judith Curry join us to ask if we're heading towards a new environmental crisis.
Synopsis & Topics: Are we unwittingly fostering a new kind of climate crisis? Martin Rees, Judith Curry, Thomas Sterner and Linda Yueh discuss.

Title: Making Sense Of Mental Health
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. He served as the media expert for the Royal College of Psychiatrists and has worked as a broadcaster for the BBC and ITV.
Synopsis & Topics: Consultant psychiatrist and RCP media expert Mark Salter makes sense of mental health issues.

Title: The unsayable
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Joanna Kavenna, Raymond Tallis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of the bestselling Zed Joanna Kavenna, philosopher and neuroscientist Ray Tallis, and post-realist philosopher and author of Closure, Hilary Lawson lock horns over how we understand the world. Hosted by author and research fellow at the University of Hertfordshire, Maria Balaska.
Synopsis & Topics: Joanna Kavenna, Ray Tallis and Hilary Lawson  tackle the limits of language with Maria Balaska.

Title: Deconstructing development
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eka Ikpe is an academic and a senior lecturer in Development Economics in Africa and the Director of the African Leadership Centre at King’s College London. Her research centres around a critical understanding of socio-economic transformation processes within an African context.
Synopsis & Topics: Developmental economist Eka Ikpe deconstructs modern questions of international relations.

Title: AI, emotions and the tech evolution
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Fotini G. Markopoulou-Kalamara is a Greek theoretical physicist interested in quantum gravity, foundational mathematics and quantum mechanics and a design engineer working on embodied cognition technologies. Markopoulou is co-founder and CEO of Empathic Technologies.
Synopsis & Topics: Complex systems pioneer Fotini Markopoulou explores how we co-evolve with our technologies.

Title: Knowledge v creativity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative MP and thinker Jesse Norman, psychologist and author of How Emotions Are Made Lisa Feldman Barrett, and director of the StoryLab Research Institute Shreepali Patel debate the value of creativity. Hosting this debate is economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondent, Linda Yueh.
Synopsis & Topics: Is knowledge worth more than creativity? Jesse Norman, Lisa Feldman Barrett, and Shreepali Patel discuss.

Title: Alien thinking
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Ball is a science writer and broadcaster. He is the former editor of the journal Nature and a prolific author of popular science books. Ball’s 2004 book Critical Mass won the Aventis Prize, and in the same year, he presented Small Worlds, a three-part series on nanotechnology for BBC Radio 4.
Synopsis & Topics: Acclaimed science writer and broadcaster Philip Ball explores how alien minds might think.

Title: Democracy: freedom or tyranny?
Guests & Speakers: Claire Fox, Kenneth Cukier, Rutger Bregman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dutch Historian Rutger Bregman, journalist and author Kenneth Cukier and journalist and politician Claire Fox debate whether we live under a tyranny of the majority. British historian Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Rutger Bregman, Kenneth Cukier and Claire Fox debate the nature and efficacy of modern democracy.

Title: The end of the universe
Guests & Speakers: Alexander Franklin, Chandrima Ganguly, Steffen Gielen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Big Bounce theorist Steffen Gielen, cosmologist Chandrima Ganguly, and philosopher of science Alexander Franklin debate the end of everything. Scientist and writer Jonjoe McFadden hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Steffen Gielen, Chandrima Ganguly, and Alexander Franklin debate the end of the universe.

Title: Cancel culture and the limits of free speech
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter also identifies as a humanist, believing that reason, science and ethics are the best way to promote human rights and welfare.
Synopsis & Topics: Legendary campaigner Peter Tatchell sets out his vision for reconciling free speech and cancel culture in today's world.

Title: Moral truths and moral tyrannies
Guests & Speakers: Timothy Williamson, David D. Friedman, Maria Baghramian
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Infamous anarcho-capitalist David Friedman, leading analytic philosopher Timothy Williamson and morality specialist Maria Baghramian dig into the true nature of morality. Robert Rowland Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Infamous anarcho-capitalist David Friedman, leading analytic philosopher Timothy Williamson and morality specialist Maria Baghramian dig into the true nature of morality. Robert Rowland Smith hosts.

Title: Democracy - a failed strategy?
Guests & Speakers: Alex Guerrero, Taisu Zhang, Tom Brake, Yasmin Alibhai-Brown
