Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award winning columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, groundbreaking 'lottocracy' theorist Alexander Guerrero, Unlock Democracy director Tom Brake and expert on Chinese law Taisu Zhang get to grips with the myriad failures of democracy, and try to chart a way forward. Best-selling economics author Linda Yueh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is democracy doomed to fail? Or with alternative models, like China, on the rise, is democracy even still worth fighting for? Award winning columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, groundbreaking 'lottocracy' theorist Alexander Guerrero, Unlock Democracy director Tom Brake and expert on Chinese law Taisu Zhang get to grips with the myriad failures of democracy, and try to chart a way forward. Best-selling economics author Linda Yueh hosts.

Title: Life in the quantum universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Johnjoe McFadden is a scientist, professor and writer at the University of Surrey. He has written many popular science books including Life on the Edge: The Coming of Age of Quantum Biology and Quantum Evolution.

Title: The pattern seekers
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Simon Baron-Cohen's lifelong work on autism has revolutionised the world of experimental psychology. As part of his empathizing-systemizing theory, Simon famously claimed that autism is an extreme of the male brain. His new book The Pattern Seekers: How autism drives human invention presents dramatic evidence that autistic people and hyper-systemizers – those who can effortlessly analyse the patterns in systems to invent – share some of the same genes.
Synopsis & Topics: The world-renowned psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen argues that the genes for pattern-seeking abilities overlap with the genes for autism.

Rutger made headlines when he appeared at the World Economic Forum in Davos, and use the opportunity to call out the super-rich audience for tax avoidance.
Synopsis & Topics: Neo-marxist economist Grace Blakeley and anti-establishment historian Rutger Bregman discuss the future of the left, and whether humanity is inherently good after all…

Title: Islands and the end of modernity

His most recent monograph is Ontopolitics in the Anthropocene: An Introduction to Mapping, Sensing and Hacking (2018). Chandler’s long-term research focus is on new forms of subjectivity, shaped by both a retreat from the human as subject and the world as object.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor at the Centre for the Study of Democracy, David Chandler explores the importance of islands in the Anthropocene.

Synopsis & Topics: Shashi Tharoor, Tania Branigan, and Kishore Mahbubani consider the future of trade with China.

Title: The stories that make us

She has written several books including Four Shields of Power; Presence: Exploring Profound Change in People, Organizations and Society; and Transformations of Myths Through Time. In addition, she edited and consulted on the 1988 documentary, The Power of Myth, a series of interviews between Joseph Campbell and Bill Moyers.
Synopsis & Topics: Betty Sue Flowers investigates narrative and how stories have the power to influence our lives

Title: How to be an animal

Melanie has been a Fellow at the AHRC Centre for the Evolution of Cultural Diversity at UCL, a visiting Fellow at Durham University's philosophy department, and is currently a member of the Nuffield Council on Bioethics.
Synopsis & Topics: Melanie Challenger, researcher and writer on natural and environmental history, explores how animal sentience ought to influence our ethical decision-making.

As a key public figure, she has spoken at over 200 universities, cultural events and conferences spanning over 5 continents.
Synopsis & Topics: Minna Salami discusses the importance of sensuous knowledge, its place within a euro-patriarchal framework, its relationship to beauty and power and its effects on our well-being.

In 2007, she presented F*** Off, I'm a Hairy Woman on BBC Three, a documentary about body image and contrasting stereotypes surrounding women's body hair.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning comedian Shazia Mirza explores the role that laughter and comedy has in our lives, and what it reveals about us as a species.

Wodehouse Comedy Literary Award. Best known for his 2012 book The Science Delusion and the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. He has taken issue with the New Atheism of many and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging.

Title: Electric brains
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anders Sandberg is a research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford, where his research concerns the societal and ethical issues surrounding human enhancement and new technologies. He is also research associate to the Oxford Uehiro Centre for Practical Ethics and the Oxford Centre for Neuroethics.
Synopsis & Topics: Oxford professor and transhumanist Anders Sandberg, explores the history and modern impact of the idea of wireheading.

Title: Nothing but the truth
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen, Michael Shermer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder of The Skeptics Society, Michael Shermer, author of Closure, Hilary Lawson, and Professor of History at the University of Wisconsin-Madison Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen lock horns over the existence of truth. Hosted by Mary-Jane Rubenstein.
Synopsis & Topics: Michael Shermer, Hilary Lawson and Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen lock horns over the existence of truth.

Title: How to view suffering
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Martin Seligman is a hugely influential American psychologist and author. His groundbreaking theories of positive psychology and well-being - especially of ‘learned helplessness’ - have made him one of the most referenced psychologists of the 20th century. Mandy Seligman is an award-winning black and white photographer who began her career as a developmental social psychologist. She has spent the last thirty years traveling around the world with Martin Seligman spreading Positive Psychology.
Synopsis & Topics: Martin Seligman and Mandy Seligman dissect what it really means to build well-being, and how art can help us.

Title: Leadership, hypocrisy and power
Guests & Speakers: Chris Hirst, Joseph J. Ellis, Natalie Bennett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pultizer prize winning historian Joseph J Ellis, Global CEO of Havas Creative and author of 'No Bullsh*t Leadership' Christ Hirst, and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate leadership, hypocrisy and power. Myriam Francois hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Joseph J Ellis, Christ Hurst and Natalie Bennett debate Leadership, hypocrisy and power.

Title: Status and wonder
Guests & Speakers: Minna Salami, Peter Atkins, Polly Toynbee
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Veteran columnist and former BBC Social Affairs Editor Polly Toynbee, award winning writer and cultural theorist Minna Salami, and Oxford chemist and prolific science writer Peter Atkins ask if we undervalue artistic education or overvalue its cultural worth. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Polly Toynbee, Minna Salami, and Peter Atkins ask if we undervalue artistic education or overvalue its cultural worth.

Title: The limits of Western thought
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sundar Sarukkai was, till 2019, a professor of philosophy at the National Institute of Advanced Studies. He was also the Founder-Director of the Manipal Centre for Philosophy and Humanities. His work is primarily in the philosophy of natural and social sciences.
Synopsis & Topics: Sundar Sarrukai, uses the Indian philosophical tradition to make the case for non-western philosophy's paramount place.

Title: The necessity and danger of belief
Guests & Speakers: George Ellis, Carlo Rovelli, Philip Goff, Shami Chakrabarti
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Director of Human Rights NGO Liberty, Shami Chakrabarti, groundbreaking physicist Carlo Rovelli, Consciousness expert Philip Goff, and world leader in relativity and cosmology George Ellis discuss the necessity and danger of belief. Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Shami Chakrabarti, Carlo Rovelli, Philip Goff and George Ellis discuss the necessity and danger of belief.

Title: The matrix or the miracle
Guests & Speakers: David Pearce, Güneş Taylor, Theodore Dalrymple
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher and co-founder of the World Transhumanist Association David Pearce, social commentator Theodore Dalrymple, and biomedical researcher Güneş Taylor imagine the future of the family. Stephanie Hare hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: David Pearce, Theodore Dalrymple, and Güneş Taylor imagine the future of the family.

Title: Arc of life: Ayaan Hirsi Ali
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ayaan Hirsi Ali is a Somali-born classical liberal, free speech advocate and an activist for the rights of women and girls. Ayaan rejected the her Muslim faith and became an atheist, and has since been a vocal critic of both Islam and the woke left.
Synopsis & Topics: Rana Mitter interviews Ayaan Hirsi Ali to discover, in her own words, how she became the distinguished person she is today.

Title: How to think about sex
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Writer and researcher, Victoria Brooks teaches Criminal Law, Philosophy of Law and Environmental Law at the University of Westminster. Her research interests include sex and its relationship to identity, femininity, law and philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Sexuality writer Victoria Brooks explores our carnal selves, and learn how we might apply philosophy to our sex lives.

Title: Humans and other animals
Guests & Speakers: Kay Peggs, Jamie Blackett, Raymond Tallis, Melanie Challenger
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher, cultural critic and author of Aping Mankind Ray Tallis, writer, poet and podcaster Melanie Challenger, farmer, author, politician Jamie Blackett and Professor of Sociology at Kingston University Kay Peggs debate the hypocrisy of the way we treat animals. Myriam Francois hosts. In association with Future Normal
Synopsis & Topics: Ray Tallis, Melanie Challenger, Jamie Blackett and Kay Peggs debate the hypocrisy of the way we treat animals.

Title: Understanding ourselves
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Patricia Churchland is a the distinguished founder of neurophilosophy. A pioneer of eliminative materialism, Patricia heralds a radically different way to understand the brain, arguing that ideas like pure morality and reason will eventually be abandoned in favour of a purely scientific view of the human mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Renowned philosopher of mind and founder of Neurophilosophy Patricia Churchland takes us on a journey into the brain and the nature and data of morality

Title: The return of eugenics?
Guests & Speakers: Kári Stefánsson, Jacob Appel, Rebecca Bennett, Simon Baron-Cohen
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder of deCODE Genetics Kári Stefánsson, bioethicist Rebecca Bennett, controversial polymath Jacob Appel and world-leading autism expert Simon Baron-Cohen debate designer babies. Science author, Emily Grossman, hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Kári Stefánsson, Rebecca Bennett, Jacob Appel and Simon Baron-Cohen debate designer babies

Title: Belief, hypocrisy and reason
Guests & Speakers: Anandi Hattiangadi, Graham Harman, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished philosophy professor Graham Harman, author of Oughts and Thoughts Anandi Hattiangadi and post-post-realist Hilary Lawson explore the difference between opinion and truth. Hannah Dawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Graham Harman, Anandi Hattiangadi and Hilary Lawson explore the difference between opinion and truth.

Title: How laughter can change the world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Helen Lederer is a comedian, writer and actress, best known for her role as Catriona in Absolutely Fabulous. She is also the author of the comedy novel Losing It.
Synopsis & Topics: Acclaimed comedian, actress and writer Helen Lederer explores the powerful influence that humour can have on society.

Title: The authority gap
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist and radio presenter. A former assistant editor of The Times, Mary Ann is chair of the Social Market Foundation - a think tank for fairer markets and open public services. Mary Ann has also written for The Independent, The Economist and the Financial Times and was the presenter of Start the Week, Beyond Westminster and many other one-off documentaries.
Synopsis & Topics: Mary Ann Sieghart delves into the unconscious biases at work and in our everyday lives and reveals the scale of the gulf that still exists between the genders.

Title: Technology in trouble
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Priyadarshini Karve, Silkie Carlo
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Outspoken Oxford transhumanist Anders Sandberg, inventor of groundbreaking green technology Priyadarshini Karve and Director of Big Brother Watch Silkie Carlo get to grips with the potential of technology. Hosted by Aman Sethi.
Synopsis & Topics: Anders Sandberg, Priyadarshini Karve and Silkie Carlo get to grips with the potential of technology.

Title: Ideas, identity and influence
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kwame Anthony Appiah is Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University and author of The Lies That Bind: Rethinking Identity and Cosmopolitanism: Ethics in a World of Strangers.
Synopsis & Topics: NYU Philosopher Kwame Anthony Appiah details his journey and life works on identity and expereince.

Title: Saving liberal democracy
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Son of a Nigerian immigrant, Bim Afolami is a Conservative MP. After studying at Eton and Oxford, Bim worked in the City for 10 years before going into politics. He is known for his centre-ground beliefs
Synopsis & Topics: We are all aware of the grave threats to liberal democracy. But can it be saved? Conservative Party MP Bim Afolami injects some much-needed hope for the future.

Title: Getting real about global power
Guests & Speakers: Malcolm Rifkind, Cindy Yu, Michael Pembroke, Melissa Chan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, China reporter and broadcast editor at The Spectator Cindy Yu, writer and historian Michael Pembroke, and Global Reporting Centre collaborator Melissa Chan get real about global power. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Malcolm Rifkind, Cindy Yu, Michael Pembroke, and Melissa Chan get real about global power and whether the west is irrelevant.

Title: Time and a new story of the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lee Smolin is a theoretical physicist who has been, since 2001, a founding and senior faculty member at Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. His main contributions have been to the quantum theory of gravity. He has been a co-inventor and major contributor to the field in two major directions: loop quantum gravity and deformed special relativity.
Synopsis & Topics: Theoretical physicist and co-founder of Loop Quantum Gravity Lee Smolin leads us towards a unified physics.

Title: Ways to go beyond
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist, author and parapsychology researcher, best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. He is a critic of New Atheism, and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging.
Synopsis & Topics: Author of Ways To Go Beyond Rupert Sheldrake asks why we are attracted to holy places.

Title: The survival paradox
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Distinguished Professor of Philosophy Graham Harman, Associate Professor of History and Philosophy of Science Mazviita Chirimuuta, and cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman debate the survival paradox. Hosted by documentary film-maker David Malone.
Synopsis & Topics: Graham Harman, Mazviita Chirimuuta, and  Donald Hoffman debate whethere we have evolved to see the truth about reality.

Title: The pursuit of happiness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Pearce is an eminent figure within the transhumanist movement, and co-founder of Humanity+, an international organisation which advocates for the technological enhancement of the human species. He envisions a future completely free of suffering for both humans and non-human animals, a pain-free paradise in which all thought, feeling, and experience is sublimated into what he calls "gradients of bliss". The abolition of suffering is for David an ethical necessity, elaborated in his manifesto, The Hedonistic Imperative.
Synopsis & Topics: David Pearce explores the practical possibilities of biomedically engineering a world of intelligent bliss.

Title: How to live forever
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr. Natasha Vita More is an author, strategic designer, and scientist, working in the fields of human enhancement technology and life extension. Natasha is the Executive Director of Humanity+, the world's largest transhumanist organisation, which advocates the ethical use of technology to expand human capacities.
Synopsis & Topics: Author of The Transhumanist Manifesto, Natasha Vita-More,  sets out her vision for a future where technology can lead to "radical life extension"

Title: The black hole paradox
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Sean Carroll, Amélie Saintonge
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel Prize-winning physicist and Hawking collaborator Sir Roger Penrose, theoretical physicist Sean Carroll, and UCL Professor of Astrophysics Amelie Saintonge tackle the paradox of black holes. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: World renowned mathematical physicist Sir Roger Penrose, theoretical physicist Sean Carroll and UCL Professor of Astrophysics Amelie Saintonge tackle the paradox of Black Holes.

Title: The Malthusian catastrophe
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Natalie Bennett, Paul Morland
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Transhumanist Anders Sandberg, author of Human Tide Paul Morland and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate the perils of population. This debate was filmed at our HowTheLightGetsIn London 2019 festival.
Synopsis & Topics: Transhumanist Anders Sandberg, author of the Human Tide Paul Morland and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate the perils of population.

Title: No bad women
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cari Mitchell is a spokeswoman for the English Collective of Prostitutes, a network of women working in different areas of the sex industry – both on the streets and indoors, which campaigns for decriminalisation of sex work and for sex workers' safety.
Synopsis & Topics: The English Collective of Prostitute's Niki Adams argues for the decriminalisation of sex work, and explores the powerful role that outdated laws play in fostering a culture of violence against sex workers.

Title: Dreams, delusions and class interests
Guests & Speakers: Dawn Butler, Jesse Norman, P. J. O'Rourke
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative Cabinet Minister Jesse Norman, world-renowned political satirist PJ O'Rourke and Jeremy Corbyn ally Dawn Butler wrestle with the relevance of class. Paul Waugh hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Conservative Cabinet Minister Jesse Norman, world-renowned political satirist PJ O'Rourke and Jeremy Corbyn ally Dawn Butler wrestle with the relevance of class

Title: Space, the new Wild West
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, USA. Her book Worlds Without End: The Many Lives of the Universe examines cosmological models throughout history, from the world-views of the Ancient Greeks through to the well-respected multiverse theory in modern science. She links contemporary models of the universe to their forerunners and explores the reason for their recent resurgence.
Synopsis & Topics: Mary-Jane Rubenstein explores the motivations and dangers of The New Age Space Race.

Title: The hunt for expertise
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anandi Hattiangadi is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Stockholm, with interests in the philosophy of mind and language, epistemology, and meta-ethics. She is a core part of the interdisciplinary program Knowledge Resistance: Causes, Consequences, and Cures.
Synopsis & Topics: Professor of Philosophy at Stockholm University Anandi Hattiangadi investigates the logical labyrinth of expertise.

Title: The truth about lies
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Åsa Wikforss, Santiago Zabala
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The Times journalist David Aaronovitch, author of Freedom In the Age of Alternative Facts Santiago Zabala, and philosophy of the mind specialist Åsa Wikforss lock horns over whether telling the truth still matters at all.
Synopsis & Topics: David Aaronovitch,  Santiago Zambala, and  Åsa Wikforss lock horns over whether telling the truth still matters at all.

Title: In Conversation with Armando Iannucci
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Armando Iannucci is a legendary satirist, writer and film-maker and Claire Armitstead is the Associate Culture Editor for the Guardian.
Synopsis & Topics: From creating Alan Partridge to writing The Thick of It, Armando discusses how he came to be called by The Daily Telegraph "the hardman of political satire".

Title: The oddity of life
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sara Walker is an astro-biologist and theoretical physicist interested in the origin of life and how to find life on other worlds.
Synopsis & Topics: Sara Walker explores how counterintuitive an explanation for life might be once we discover it.

Title: Beyond Us: Bonus Review
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
Synopsis & Topics: Series hosts Fred Matser and Bernardo Kastrup reflect on the series as a whole, discuss the views of their guests, and see if they have come to any new conclusions of their own.

Title: Mind over matter
Guests & Speakers: Natasha Vita-More, Rupert Sheldrake, Susan Schneider
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake, chairman of Humanity+ Natasha Vita-More and philosopher of mind and AI specialist Susan Schneider debate the potential of mind-computer interface technology.
Synopsis & Topics: Author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake, chairman of Humanity+ Natasha Vita-More and philosopher of mind and AI specialist Susan Schneider debate the potential of mind-computer interface technology.

Title: Why we need free speech
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society, the editor-in-chief of its magazine Skeptic, and a Presidential Fellow at Chapman University, where he teaches Skepticism 101.
Synopsis & Topics: Professional sceptic and bestselling author of Giving the Devil his Due Michael Shermer explores the dangerous possibility of a world without free speech.

Title: Land of the free
Guests & Speakers: Jason Brennan, Jon Sopel, Sarah Elliott
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The BBC's North America correspondent, Jon Sopel, chair of Republicans Oversees, Sarah Elliott and author of Against Democracy Jason Brennan clash over the future of the Land of the Free. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
Synopsis & Topics: The BBC's North America correspondent, Jon Sopel, chair of Republicans Oversees, Sarah Elliott and author of Against Democracy Jason Brennan clash over the future of the Land of the Free.

Title: The corruption of science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Atkins FRSC is an English chemist, outspoken atheist, and author of works of popular science such as Atkins' Molecules.
Synopsis & Topics: Chemist Peter Atkins explains why religion is science's great corrupter and its role in exposing the inner truths of the world

Title: How to die before you die
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Brian C. Muraresku is a classicist, lawyer and New York Times bestselling author. His debut book, The Immortality Key, combines Muraresku’s classical research interests to provide a groundbreaking dive into the role psychedelics have played in the origins of Western civilisation.
Synopsis & Topics: Brian Muraresku takes us on a trip back in time to uncover the importance of psychedelic experiences to Ancient Greek and early Christian culture.

Title: The rational animal
Guests & Speakers: Dan Ariely, Paul Bloom, Patty Kostkova
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Psychology and Behavioral Economics at Duke University Dan Ariely, Professor of Psychology and Cognitive Science at Yale Paul Bloom, and Patty Kostkova, Professor in Digital Health and the Director of UCL IRDR Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies debate if humans are truly rational animals. Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Dan Ariely, Paul Bloom and Patty Kostkova debate if humans are truly rational animals

Title: Evolution in politics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jesse Norman is a leading British Conservative Party politician, currently serving as the Financial Secretary to the Treasury and tipped by some to be a future leader of the party. He has been an MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010. Before becoming an MP he led an educational charity in Eastern Europe and was a director at Barclays bank.
Synopsis & Topics: Conservative MP Jesse Norman sets out his stall for genuinely conservative thought in Westminster.

Title: The Future Human
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Güneş Taylor is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre. Her research predominantly focuses on the the genetic formation of ovaries and testes.
Synopsis & Topics: Training Fellow at the Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor, discusses her research on the front line of new CRISPR technologies, and the genetics of gender.

Title: Beyond Us: Growth
Synopsis & Topics: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss what growth is for with former Chief Business Officer for Google X, entrepreneur and the author of the book Solve for Happy, Mo Gawdat.

Title: The anti-universe
Guests & Speakers: Lee Smolin, Sabine Hossenfelder, Tara Shears
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founding member at Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, Lee Smolin, professor of Physics at Liverpool University, Tara Shears and leader of the Superfluid Dark Matter group at the Frankfurt Institute, Sabine Hossenfelder battle over the very fabric of the universe. Hosted by Hilary Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: Lee Smolin, Tara Shears and Sabine Hossenfelder battle over antimatter and the very fabric of the universe

Title: Where is racial justice?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Now the Merton P. Stoltz Professor at Brown University, Glenn Loury became the first black tenured professor of economics in the history of Harvard University in 1982. Glenn's vehement criticism of affirmative action along with his argument that African-Americans' own behaviour is responsible for their plight, and not white racism, led to him becoming a hero of the Reagan intellectual Right. "A genuine maverick thinker and a shrewd political operator" The New York Times Magazine
Synopsis & Topics: Trailblazing thinker Glenn Loury dares to ask difficult questions about BLM and lays the real battleground of racial injustice.

Title: The limits of sexuality
Guests & Speakers: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Niki Adams, Olivia Fane, Mikki Kendall
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning author Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, writer and feminist Mikki Kendall, spokesperson for the English Collective of Prostitutes Nikki Adams, and novelist Oliva Fane debate the limits of sexuality. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning author Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, writer and feminist Mikki Kendall, spokesperson for the English Collective of Prostitutes Nikki Adams, and novelist Oliva Fane debate the limits of sexuality.

Title: Lessons from the universe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Head of Future Missions at Airbus, Ralph Cordey focuses on providing new engineering solutions for scientific missions. The space missions that Ralph works on can focus on anything from searching for life in our solar system and beyond, to gaining a greater understanding of our own planet's climate.
Synopsis & Topics: Airbus's Ralph Cordey considers the lessons learnt from space travel that can be applied back home, and the future of the industry as a whole.

Title: Arc of life: Daniel Dennett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daniel Dennett is a world-renowned philosopher and cognitive scientist. He is a major contributor to the understanding of the conceptual foundations of evolutionary biology. Alongside Sam Harris, Christopher Hitchens and Richard Dawkins, Daniel is well known for being one of the “four horse-men of new atheism” who dedicated themselves to actively countering religion in every form. He is currently the Austin B. Fletcher Professor of Philosophy, and Co-Director of the Center for Cognitive Studies at Tufts University “Perhaps America’s most widely read and debated living philosopher” New York Times
Synopsis & Topics: Award winning author Daniel Dennett is one of the best known living philosophers of today.  In this exclusive interview, find out how Daniel's life shaped his ideas.

Title: Chicken or egg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary American philosopher Daniel Dennett, astrobiologist and famed science communicator, Sara Walker, and evolutionary (and revolutionary) biochemist Professor Nick Lane tackle the most fundamental question of all. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
Synopsis & Topics: Legendary American philosopher Daniel Dennett, astrobiologist and famed science communicator, Sara Walker, and evolutionary  biochemist Professor Nick Lane debate Chicken or Egg.

Title: Deregulate to innovate
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Matt Ridley is a British journalist and businessman. Matt worked for the Economist for nine years as science editor, Washington correspondent and American editor, before turning to writing and business.
Synopsis & Topics: Innovation is unplanned, unpredicatable, and entirely crucial to human flourishing. Yet it is being stifled everywhere. Matt Ridley explains why we need to deregulate.

Title: The breakdown of cosmology
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science, author of Metaphysical Experiments Physics and the Invention of the Universe. "Ekeberg provides a unique synthesis that will be of interest to philosophers of science and contemplative scientists alike." Graham Harman
Synopsis & Topics: Author and metaphysician Bjørn Ekeberg dares to explore the big problems facing standard cosmology.

Title: Beyond us: language

Synopsis & Topics: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss the uses and limitations of language with renowned British philosopher of language, Jennifer Hornsby.

Title: Our saviour or our downfall
Guests & Speakers: Bret Weinstein, Luc Julia, Marc Edwards
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Biologist and evolutionary theorist Bret Weinstein, inventor of voice assistant SIRI Luc Julia, genetic researcher Güneş Taylor and Flint water crisis whistle-blower Marc Edwards debate our saviour or our downfall. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Biologist and evolutionary theorist Bret Weinstein, inventor of voice assistant SIRI Luc Julia, genetic researcher Güneş Taylor and Flint water crisis whistle-blower Marc Edwards debate Our Saviour or Our Downfall

Title: Arc of life: Paul Krugman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: "The most celebrated economist of his generation" The Economist
Synopsis & Topics: Paul Krugman is a Nobel-prize winning economist and a Distinguished Professor at City University of New York. Here he brings his expertise to the current state of economics.

Title: Race, identity and justice
Guests & Speakers: Dawn Butler, Glenn Loury, George The Poet
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award winning spoken-word artist George the Poet, economist and first black tenured professor of economics at Harvard Glenn Loury and First elected Black female government minister in the UK Dawn Butler debate the relevance of racial identity in the modern world.
Synopsis & Topics: George the Poet, Glenn Loury and Dawn Butler debate the relevance of racial identity in the modern world.

Title: Newton's Space
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emily Thomas is an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Durham University, whose research interests are in space and time, early modern metaphysics and the philosophy of travel.
Synopsis & Topics: Durham philosopher and historian of science Emily Thomas examines the enduring impact of Newton's ideas.

Title: East meets west
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chris Impey is a Distinguished Professor at Arizona University, where he leads one of the largest astronomy departments in the USA. "Chris Impey manages to rejuvenate that 'Space Is Our Future' feeling that pervaded human culture a half century ago." Neil deGrasse Tyson
Synopsis & Topics: Astronomist Chris Impey investigates what Buddhism and Western science can learn from one another

Title: Values of the West
Guests & Speakers: Kehinde Andrews, Myriam François, Raymond Tallis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cultural critic and philosopher Raymond Tallis, founder of the first Black Studies university course Kehinde Andrews, and writer, broadcaster and academic Myriam Franҫois question our faith in Western values.
Synopsis & Topics: Cultural critic and philosopher Raymond Tallis, founder of the first Black Studies university course Kehinde Andrews, and writer, broadcaster and academic Myriam Franҫois question our faith in Western values.

Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Linda Woodhead is a distinguished Professor of Religion and Society, director of the Religion and Society Programme and co-founder of the Westminster Faith Debates.
Synopsis & Topics: Linda Woodhead takes a look at what the Church is doing wrong, and what the spiritual gurus are getting right.

Title: In Conversation with Carlo Rovelli & Jim Al-Khalili
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carlo Rovelli is a theoretical physicist and founder of loop quantum gravity theory. Jim Al-Khalili is a theoretical physicist, author and broadcaster who regularly presents science programmes on BBC radio and television.
Synopsis & Topics: Theoretical Physicists Jim Al-Khalili and Carlo Rovelli delve into fundamental physics and the nature of reality.

Title: Beyond Us: Competition
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss this fascinating topic with American evolutionary psychologist, Donald Hoffman. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
Synopsis & Topics: Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss whether we evolved to compete or cooperate with American evolutionary psychologist, Donald Hoffman.

Title: Experimenting with the truth
Guests & Speakers: Claudia de Rham, Harry Collins, John Ioannidis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor at the Stanford University School of Medicine, and author of the most downloaded paper in history John Ioannidis, theoretical physicist and winner of the 2020 Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists Claudia de Rham and sociologist of science and author of Are We All Scientific Experts Now Harry Collins discuss the importance of replicability and objectivity in science.
Synopsis & Topics: John Ioannidis, Claudia de Rham and Harry Collins discuss the importance of replicability and objectivity in science.

Title: The economy of the future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Neoliberalism is failing us. Tech companies steal our data, banks control financial regulation, and inequality continues to skyrocket. As the global economy slowly recovers from Covid-19, policy makers need to take this chance to forge a new, progressive form of capitalism. Nobel prize winning economist and author Joseph Stiglitz proposes how we might rebuild the economy in a way that works for everyone.
Synopsis & Topics: Nobel prize winning economist and author Joseph Stiglitz proposes how we might rebuild the economy in a way that works for everyone.

Title: Are you an illusion?
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, Dan Zahavi, Lisa Bortolotti
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Self and Other Dan Zahavi, Philosophy Professor and philosophy of the cognitive sciences researcher Lisa Bortolotti and Research Fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute Anders Sandberg debate whether the self is an illusion.
Synopsis & Topics: Author of Self and Other Dan Zahavi, Philosophy Professor and philosophy of the cognitive sciences researcher Lisa Bortolotti and Research Fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute Anders Sandberg debate whether the self is an illusion.

Title: Trust in a relative world
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Maria Baghramian is the Professor of American Philosophy at University College Dublin and one of the world’s leading experts on moral and epistemological relativism."
Synopsis & Topics: World leading relativist Maria Baghramian discusses how we should decide which experts to trust in a world where they are evermore in the spotlight

Title: AI and the future of the mind
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susan Schneider is an American academic and public philosopher, the William F. Dietrich Professor of Philosophy at Florida Atlantic University, and a recipient of the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholar Award. She is the author of Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it possible that we'll ever be able to merge with the AI? Philosopher and cognitive scientist Susan Schneider explores this groundbreaking possibility.

Title: Power to the people
Guests & Speakers: Claire Fox, Julian Baggini, Matthew Taylor
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Brexit Party MEP Claire Fox, Academic Director of the Royal Institute of Philosophy Julian Baggini, and former political strategist Matthew Taylor clash over the future of democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Former Brexit Party MEP Claire Fox, Academic Director of the Royal Institute of Philosophy Julian Baggini, and former political strategist Matthew Taylor clash over the future of democracy.

Title: Preparing for Utopia

Synopsis & Topics: Transhumanist Anders Sandberg delves into how we're preparing for a transhumanist Utopia.

Title: The struggle for dignity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Goodhart is a British journalist and cultural commentator, and the founder and former editor of Prospect magazine. "David Goodhart is among the most insightful analysts of Anglo-American society" - Jonathan Haidt
Synopsis & Topics: Until recently care workers, supermarket shelf-stackers, delivery drivers and cleaners were thought of as lowly jobs. David Goodhart explores the struggle for dignity and status in the 21st century.

Title: Beyond Us: Knowledge

Synopsis & Topics: Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss what we may have lost in a culture that champions reason over intuition with champion of the enlightenment project Rebecca Goldstein.

Title: How we became who we are
Guests & Speakers: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Robert Plomin, Matt Ridley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Hugely influential geneticist Robert Plomin, libertarian journalist and author of The Evolution of Everything Matt Ridley, and award-winning journalist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown explore the relevance of politics in the nature/nurture debate. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Robert Plomin, Matt Ridley and Yasmin Alibhai-Brown explore the relevance of politics in the nature vs. nurture debate.

Title: The empathy trap
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dan Zahavi is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Oxford. "One of the most prolific and insightful phenomenologists of his generation" Distinguished Professor Alessandro Duranti, University of California
Synopsis & Topics: We have all been encouraged to imagine how it feels to be in someone else's shoes. But is empathy really a good base for our morality? Director of the Centre for Subjectivity Research, Dan Zahavi, probes the value of empathy.

Title: Consciousness and the world
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Bernardo Kastrup, Annaka Harris, Reza Negarestani
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Post-postmodern philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism Hilary Lawson, author of the NYT Bestseller '‘Conscious: A Brief Guide to the Fundamental Mystery of the Mind’ Annaka Harris, Iranian philosopher and the author of 'Intelligence and Spirit' Reza Negarestani, and computer scientist, researcher, and proponent of "metaphysical idealism" Bernardo Kastrup debate Consciousness and the World. Mary-Jane Rubenstein hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Hilary Lawson, Annaka Harris, Reza Negarestani, and Bernardo Kastrup debate Consciousness and the World.

Title: Cosmological mysteries
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chris Impey is a professor and deputy head of the department of astronomy at the University of Arizona. His astronomy research focuses on observational cosmology—using telescopes and other instruments to study the large-scale structure and evolution of the universe.
Synopsis & Topics: Chris Impey delves into the mysteries and puzzles of the cosmos, from the explanatory gaps of the Big Bang theory, to the problem of defining dark matter

Title: The future of feminism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ella Whelan is a freelance journalist, commentator and author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. She is the former assistant editor at spiked .
Synopsis & Topics: Journalist Ella Whelan questions whether we need feminism at all, and gives her take on where women's politics is going.

Title: Stories to believe in
Guests & Speakers: Grace Blakeley, Michael Sandel, Rory Stewart
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Conservative MP Rory Stewart, economist and voice of the left Grace Blakeley, and leading public intellectual Michael Sandel battle it out over the case for ideological politics.
Synopsis & Topics: Former Conservative MP Rory Stewart, economist Grace Blakeley, and leading public intellectual Michael Sandel battle it out over the case for ideological politics.

Title: Poetry Live
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Pulitzer Prize winner Paul Muldoon is one of the greatest poets alive today. Paul has served as both Professor of Poetry at Oxford University and the poetry editor of The New Yorker. He published his first book at the age of just 21, and is now the author of thirteen major collections of poetry, and has taught at Princeton University since 1987. "The most significant English-language poet born since the second World War". TLS
Synopsis & Topics: Pulitzer Prize-winning poet and former Oxford Professor of Poetry, Paul Muldoon's poetry is as difficult as it is renowned. Watch him perform a rare poetry reading.

Title: Uncovering black holes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Amélie Saintonge is a professor of Astrophysics at UCL whose research is currently funded by the Royal Society.
Synopsis & Topics: UCL astrophysicist Amélie Saintonge delves into how we can use gravitational waves to listen to black holes.

Title: A writer's voice
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Meg Rosoff is a writer best known for her award-winning novel How I Live Now. Her second novel, Just in Case, won the annual Carnegie Medal.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning author Meg Rosoff shines light on the conscious and sub-conscious parts of a writer's voice.

Title: The different places of the self
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, FBA is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions – Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism – and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
Synopsis & Topics: Eminent philosopher Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad explores different conceptions of the self around the world

Title: Our story of the universe
Guests & Speakers: Sabine Hossenfelder, Chris Impey, Bjørn Ekeberg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Astronomer, cosmologist and author Chris Impey, theoretical physicist and creator of the influential Backreaction blog Sabine Hossenfelder and philosopher of science Bjørn Ekeberg explore the beginning of everything. James Ladyman hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Chris Impey, Sabine Hossenfelder and  Bjørn Ekeberg explore the beginning of everything and whether we need to refine the Big Bang Theory.

Title: Human blueprints
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Robert J. Plomin, FBA is an American psychologist and geneticist best known for his work in twin studies and behavior genetics.
Synopsis & Topics: World leading behavioural geneticist Robert Plomin discusses his life works and the crucial importance of DNA and its influence on our personality, behaviour and who we really are.

Title: After the end of history
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Malcolm Rifkind is a politian who served in various roles as a Cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher and John Major, including Defence Secretary and Foreign Secretary. "Malcolm Rifkind was in the top rank of twentieth-century politicians. Few saw events at closer quarters." John Major
Synopsis & Topics: From the rise of China, to populist election victories, we are living through a period of seismic change. Former Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind explains how we remain on the right track.

Title: Promiscuity and power
Guests & Speakers: Myriam François, Shazia Mirza, Emma Sayle
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Multi-award winning comedian Shazia Mirza, founder of the sex-party company Killing Kittens Emma Sayle and writer, broadcaster and academic Myriam Fran ç ois clash over the role promiscuity plays in the fight for equality. Stephanie Hare hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Comedian Shazia Mirza, Emma Sayle and  Myriam François clash over the role promiscuity plays in the fight for equality.

Title: What's wrong with physics
Synopsis & Topics: Acclaimed physicist Sabine Hossenfelder lays out her plan to regain the once great reputation of physics.

Title: The known and the unknown
Guests & Speakers: Renata Salecl, Simon Blackburn, Philip Goff
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Renowned philosopher and ethicist Simon Blackburn, psychoanalyst and sociologist Renata Salecl, and author of Galileo's Error: Foundations for a New Science of Consciousness Philip Goff try to find their way through the fog of uncertainty. Joanna Kavenna.
Synopsis & Topics: Renowned philosopher and ethicist Simon Blackburn, psychoanalyst and sociologist Renata Salecl, and author of Galileo's Error: Foundations for a New Science of Consciousness Philip Goff try to find their way through the fog of uncertainty.

Title: Challenging the scientific dogma
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His book, The Science Delusion, was a bestseller.
Synopsis & Topics: Morphic resonance proposer Rupert Sheldrake challenges the scientific dogma we operate within today.

Title: How to right wrongs
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT+ social movements. Since 2011 he has been the Director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation.
Synopsis & Topics: Renowned activist Peter Tatchell charts the course to move forward without forgetting our past when it comes to righting the wrongs done to the LGBT+ community

Title: Eradicating gender
Guests & Speakers: Bianca Jagger, Eileen Myles, Nina Power
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Legendary poet Eileen Myles, Founder, President and Chief Executive of the Bianca Jagger Human Rights Foundation Bianca Jagger and social theorist and cultural critic Nina Power unravel the path to equality. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Legendary poet Eileen Myles, Founder, President and Chief Executive of the Bianca Jagger Human Rights Foundation Bianca Jagger and social theorist and cultural critic Nina Power unravel the path to equality.

Title: The continuity of the self
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, FBA is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions – Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism – and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
Synopsis & Topics: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad highlights the complexity and continuity of our discussions of the subjective.

Title: How to fathom timelessness via psychedelics
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Peter Sjöstedt-H is a philosopher of mind who specialises in the thought of Whitehead, Nietzsche, and Spinoza, and in fields pertaining to panpsychism and altered states of mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher of mind Peter Sjöstedt-H examines, through the lens of Spinozaism and psychedelic experience, our relationship to time.

Title: Uncovering the universe
Guests & Speakers: Sundar Sarukkai, Claudia de Rham, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Theoretical physicist Claudia de Rham, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and philosopher and author of Translating the World: Science and Language Sundar Sarukkai go head to head to investigate whether science can really uncover the secrets of the universe. Philosopher James Ladyman hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Theoretical physicist Claudia de Rham, Hilary Lawson and philosopher of science Sundar Sarukkai investigate whether science can really uncover the secrets of the universe.

Title: The path to the future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susan Schneider is an academic and public philosopher, who writes about the philosophy of mind and artificial intelligence. She believes that individuals, not companies, need to consider and decide the philosophical issues that will affect them as a result of artificial intelligence.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Susan Schneider considers the future of AI from Elon Musk's neurolink to the hard problem of consciousness.

Title: How to think about whiteness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Myrian Fran ç ois is an academic, documentary maker and currently a research associate at the School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London (SOAS).
Synopsis & Topics: Academic and documentary maker, Myriam Francois, guides us through how to consider what whiteness means to you and how you notice your whiteness day to day?

Title: Passion, action and hypocrisy
Guests & Speakers: Aaron Bastani, Emma Slade, John Zerzan, Vince Cable
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anarchist and primitivist ecophilosopher John Zerzan, financial analyst turned Buddhist nun Emma Slade, Novara Media co-founder Aaron Bastani, and former UK Liberal Democrat party leader Vince Cable debate passion, action and hypocrisy. Isabel Hilton hosts. This video is in association with Say Your Peace . Say Your Peace aims to spark global change through self-transformation and community dialogue. Find out more at sayyourpeace.org , and check them out on Instagram and Facebook.
Synopsis & Topics: Primitivist ecophilosopher John Zerzan, Buddhist nun Emma Slade, Novara Media co-founder Aaron Bastani, and LibDem Vince Cable debate passion, action and hypocrisy.

Title: How to transform your life with curiosity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Garrick Jones is a businessman, academic, musician and Founding Partner of The Ludic Group where his research into Cloud Based Transformation Consulting, Digital Learning Programmes and Engagement are put into practice. He is a Fellow at the LSE where his research is focused on organisational decision-making and Creative Economies. This video is in partnership with Ludic.
Synopsis & Topics: Co author of The Curious Advantage, Garrick Jones and discover how to use the '7 Cs of curiosity' to your own advantage.

Title: Loving animals, eating animals
Guests & Speakers: Peter Singer, Christopher Belshaw, Mary Ann Sieghart, Peter Egan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-renowned moral philosopher Peter Singer, Honorary Associate in Philosophy at the Open University Christopher Belshaw, former assistant editor of The Times Mary-Ann Sieghart and British actor and longtime vegan Peter Egan debate our love for animals. Myriam Francois hosts. In association with Future Normal .
Synopsis & Topics: Effective altruist Peter Singer, Christopher Belshaw, Mary-Ann Sieghart and Peter Egan debate veganism and the hypocrisy of eating meat.

Title: The Left and anti-Semitism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Aaronovitch is a journalist, television presenter and author. He is a regular columnist for The Times and the author of Paddling to Jerusalem: An Aquatic Tour of Our Small Country (2000).
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, David Aaronovitch discusses anti-Semitism and anti-Zionism in the UK Labour Party, especially during Corbyn’s leadership from 2015-2020.

Title: The happiness trap
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Described by Rowan Williams as "unquestionably among the most sophisticated voices in the whole world of modern theology", John Milbank is an Anglican theologian and Emeritus Professor in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies at Nottingham University, where he is the President of the Centre of Theology and Religion.
Synopsis & Topics: Theologian John Milbank believes it's time we outgrew this self-centred ideology for happiness. Hear him set out his vision for a post-liberal society.

Title: The crisis of particle physics
Guests & Speakers: John Ellis, Jim Baggott, Sabine Hossenfelder
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: CERN physicist John Ellis, theoretical physicist and Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies Sabine Hossenfelder, and award-winning science writer and quantum expert Jim Baggott debate the crisis in physics. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: CERN physicist John Ellis, theoretical physicist and Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies Sabine Hossenfelder, and award winning science writer and quantum expert Jim Baggott debate the crisis in physics.

Title: Confronting crisis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Santiago Zabala is a philosopher and ICREA Research Philosopher at the Pompeu Fabra University, where he currently teaches contemporary and political philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Santiago Zabala details why the greatest emergency is the absence of emergency itself and why we need to take warnings of emergencies far more seriously.

Title: The corona crash
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Described by Owen Jones as "one of the most inspiring, thought provoking and insightful voices on the left", Grace Blakeley is an economics and politics commentator and Marxist economist. She is a staff writer for Tribune and was previously the economics commentator of the New Statesman.
Synopsis & Topics: Marxist economist Grace Blakeley sets out the ways we need to radically restructure society  in order to live and work in the wake of Covid-19.

Title: Dicing with death
Guests & Speakers: Sunetra Gupta, David D. Friedman, Indira Jaising
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Epidemiologist Sunetra Gupta, anarcho-capitalist David D. Friedman and renowned human rights lawyer Indira Jaising debate whether human beings are capable of keeping themselves safe. Sean Curran hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Legal activist Indira Jaising, anarcho-capitalist David D. Friedman and epidemiologist Sunetra Gupta debate whether humans are capable of keeping themselves safe.

Title: Constructing consciousness
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Colm Tóibín is a novelist, short story writer, essayist, playwright and poet. Currently the Chancellor at the University of Liverpool, Tóibín's notable works include 'The Heather Blazing', 'Brooklyn' and 'The Master'.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, 'The Heather Blazing' and 'Brooklyn' author Colm Tóibín discusses his inspirations and motivations

Title: Arc of life: Peter Singer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Described by The New Yorker as "the world's most influential living philosopher" and known for his book Animal Liberation, Peter Singer specialises in applied ethics. He approaches ethical issues from a secular, utilitarian perspective, arguing in favour of veganism and of donating to help the global poor. Interviewer Jenny Kleeman is a documentary film-maker and journalist who is best known for her work on Channel 4's foreign affairs series Unreported World and BBC One's Panorama. Her book Sex Robots & Vegan Meat was published in 2020.
Synopsis & Topics: Influential moral philosopher, secular utilitarian and author of Animal Liberation Peter Singer discusses his life works.

Title: Artists' crusade
Guests & Speakers: Anish Kapoor, Eileen Myles, Frances Morris
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of the Tate Modern Frances Morris, conceptual artist and sculptor Anish Kapoor and legendary poet Eileen Myles consider the importance of politics in art. Mary-Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: From Swift and Dickens to Goya and Picasso, art has been interwoven with politics. Tate Modern Frances Morris, Anish Kapoor and Eilieen Myles debate its importance.

Title: Women vs feminism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Dr Joanna Williams is Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. She is an author, commentator and the associate editor of Spiked, writing on matters such as feminism, academic freedom and education.
Synopsis & Topics: Associate editor at Spiked Joanna Williams discusses why she believes feminism is no longer relevant today, from it's exclusive nature, to it's 'anti-men' rhetoric.

Title: Science, hypocrisy and lies
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: John Ioannidis is a physician-scientist, writer and Stanford University professor who has made contributions to evidence-based medicine, epidemiology, and clinical research. Ioannidid studies scientific research itself, meta-research primarily in clinical medicine and the social sciences.
Synopsis & Topics: During the Covid-19 pandemic, being lead by science became the mantra for governments the world over. John Ioannidis lays bare the hypocrisy that dog the discipline

Title: The freedom paradox
Guests & Speakers: Patrick Haggard, Daniel Dennett, Helen Steward
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Groundbreaking philosopher and cognitive scientist Daniel Dennett, Cognitive Neuroscience specialist Patrick Haggard and author of A Metaphysics for Freedom Helen Steward deliberate over the existence of free will. Mark Linsenmayer hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Groundbreaking philosopher and cognitive scientist Daniel Dennett, Cognitive Neuroscience specialist Patrick Haggard and author of A Metaphysics for Freedom Helen Steward deliberate over the existence of free will.

Title: Anarchy in capitalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David D. Friedman is an economist, physicist, legal scholar and anarcho-capitalist theorist. He is known for his popular book The Machinery of Freedom.David Friedman advocates a consequentialist version of anarcho-capitalism, arguing for anarchism on a cost-benefit analysis of state versus no state.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, economist David D. Friedman discusses anarcho-capitalism and the concrete steps we can take to move towards achieving it.

Title: In Conversation with Michael Sandel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Michael Sandel teaches political philosophy at Harvard University. His books What Money Can't Buy: The Moral Limits of Markets , and Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do? were international best sellers and have been translated into 27 languages. Sandel's legendary course 'Justice' was the first Harvard course to be made freely available online and on television and has been viewed by tens of millions of people. His BBC series 'The Global Philosopher' explores the philosophical ideas lying behind the headlines with participants from around the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Political philosopher Michael Sandel puts forward his alternative to meritocracy which is more attentive to an ethic of humility and solidarity.

Title: Not so equal
Guests & Speakers: Grace Blakeley, Lisa Nandy, Joseph Stiglitz
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel prize winning economist Joseph Stiglitz, rising economics commentator Grace Blakeley and Labour politician Lisa Nandy examine our commitments to global equality.
Synopsis & Topics: Nobel prize winning economist Joseph Stiglitz, economic commentator Grace Blakeley and Labour politician Lisa Nandy debate our commitments to global inequality.

Title: Life as we know it
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nick Lane is a biochemist, writer and professor in evolutionary biochemistry at University College London. He has published four books including The Vital Question: Why Is Life The Way It Is?
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, biochemist and UCL professor Nick Lane discusses life as we know it from human evolution to life elsewhere in the universe.

Title: The Arc of Life: Bianca Jagger
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bianca Jagger is Founder, President and Chief Executive of the Bianca Jagger Human Rights Foundation (BJHRF), which she established in 2005 to be a force for change and a voice for the most vulnerable. She is the recipient of numerous prestigious awards, including The Right Livelihood Award (2004) also known as the ‘alternative Nobel prize. In association with HuffPost.
Synopsis & Topics: Bianca Jagger has committed her life to defending human rights and civil liberties. Join HuffPost reporter Rachel Moss and Bianca Jagger as she discusses her life.

Title: For your own good
Guests & Speakers: Henry Marsh, Natasha Vita-More, Sarah Wootton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Transhumanist Natasha Vita-More, pioneering neuroscientist Henry Marsh and Chief Executive of Dignity in Dying Chief Sarah Wootton.
Synopsis & Topics: Should Doctors recognise that they are sacrificing wellbeing in the name of longevity? Natasha Vita-more, Henry Marsh and Sarah Wootton debate.

Title: Living in the now
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Rupert Sheldrake discusses the benefits of certain spiritual practices and encourages the adoption of panpsychism as a scientific theory

Title: The future of India
Synopsis & Topics: Former UN Under-Secretary General. Shashi Tharoor, discusses the future of Indian politics from sectarianism to secular liberalism

Title: The AI illusion
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Kate Devlin, Laura Mersini-Houghton, Martin Rees
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Astronomer Royal and author of On the Future Martin Rees, theoretical physicist Laura Mersini-Houghton, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and computer scientist Kate Devlin question the reality of artificial intelligence. Stephanie Hare hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we see the future in automation and machine learning and give up on AI. Astronomer Royal Martin Rees, Laura-Mersini-Houghton, Kate Devlin and Hilary Lawson debate.

Title: Women for liberation
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, Elif Sarican shines light on the role of women’s liberation in the Kurdish Independence movement

Title: Science and discovery
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Henry Gee is a paleontologist, evolutionary biologist and senior editor of the scientific journal Nature.
Synopsis & Topics: The more we discover, the more we have to learn. Editor of leading science journal Nature, Henry Gee, explores the limits of knowledge and dares us to look over the edge.

Title: Metaphysics, morality and mayhem
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Joanna Kavenna, Raymond Tallis, Simon Blackburn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cultural critic and polymath Raymond Tallis, award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna and renowned philosopher and ethicist Simon Blackburn investigate the relationship between metaphysics and morality. Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we put morality before metaphysics when it comes to our theories that shape the world? Raymond Tallis, Joanna Kavenna and Simon Blackburn debate.

Title: The future of war
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: The "dean of British strategic studies" Sir Lawrence Freedman is Emeritus Professor of War Studies at King's College London and was a member of the Iraq Inquiry published in 2016.
Synopsis & Topics: Sir Lawrence Freedman discusses his role in and the outcome of the Iraq Inquiry, the nuances of civil wars and international influence, and the future of war.

Title: The anxiety of choice
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Renata Salecl is a philosopher, sociologist and legal theorist currently working as a senior researcher at the Institute of Criminology at the University of Ljubljana.
Synopsis & Topics: In a consumer culture, we're presented with endless choices. Watch Renata Salecl dig deep into why the freedom to choose isn't making us as happy as we think.

Title: Getting high and being human
Guests & Speakers: David Nutt, Peter Sjöstedt-H, Annemarie Ward
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Imperial College psychiatrist and former government drugs adviser David Nutt, philosopher of mind Peter Sjöstedt-H, and addiction advocist Annemarie Ward get to the bottom of getting high. Psychiatrist Mark Salter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Recently countries have began legalising the use of drugs like cannabis. Does this show we need to reform all drug laws? David Nutt, Peter Sjöstedt-H and Annemarie Ward debate.

Title: Editing the future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Güneş Taylor is a postdoctoral Training Fellow at the Crick Institute where she currently researches the mechanisms of sex determination and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.
Synopsis & Topics: In this interview, postdoctoral Training Fellow at the Crick Institute Güneş Taylor sheds light on CRISPR-Cas9 and the ethics of gene editing

Title: The truth about free will
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor Raymond Tallis is a philosopher, poet, novelist and cultural critic and was until recently a physician and clinical scientist. In the Economist's Intelligent Life Magazine (2009) he was listed as one of the top living polymaths in the world.
Synopsis & Topics: Are we really free to decide, or is choice an illusion? Raymond Tallis unpicks the arguments against the existence of free will

Title: The key to progress
Synopsis & Topics: Is science making progress? Can it ever unravel objective truths? Nature editor Henry Gee,  Güneş Taylor and consciousness philosopher Philip Goff debate.

Title: Ideas to live and die by
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Terry Eagleton is a Marxist literary critic and public intellectual, widely recognised as a mainstay of British academia. He has published over forty books on topics ranging from Samuel Richardson to the banality of evil.
Synopsis & Topics: Leading Marxist literary critic Terry Eagleton discusses faith, Richard Dawkins, Sam Harris and the New Atheists.

Title: The return of the Colosseum
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Meg Rosoff, Soma Ghosh
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning author Meg Rosoff, cultural critic Soma Ghosh and Orange First Novel prize winning novelist Joanna Kavenna debate the return of the Colosseum. Roger Bolton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: We live in an internet culture filled with salacious desires. Where is this taking our morality? Are we seeing the return of the Colosseum and its ancient values?

Title: Leading from the left
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chantal Mouffe is a political theorist best known for her contribution to the development of the Essex School of discourse analysis, a post-Marxist political inquiry that redefines Leftist politics in terms of radical democracy.
Synopsis & Topics: Politics is having an identity crisis. Watch Chantal Mouffe make her case for left populism as the solution to current political problems

Title: Physics doesn't have to be pretty
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sabine Hossenfelder is an author and theoretical physicsist who researches quantum theory. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the Analog Systems for Gravity Duals group.
Synopsis & Topics: Watch theoretical physicist Sabine Hossenfelder dispose of the idea that physics and theories of physics have to be pretty.

Title: In search of the self
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: William Self is an author, journalist, political commentator and television personality. His fiction is known for being satirical, grotesque, and fantastical, and often explores mental illness, drug abuse and psychiatry.
Synopsis & Topics: Can psychogeography help with isolation loneliness? 'Umbrella' author Will Self explores.

Title: The rise and fall of globalisation
Guests & Speakers: Grace Blakeley, Mark Littlewood, Vince Cable
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director general of the Institute of Economic Affairs Mark Littlewood, Tribune staff writer Grace Blakeley, and former Leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable debate the rise and fall of globalisation. Editor of Chinadialogue Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is globalisation failing? Should we turn to localism? Mark Littlewood, Grace Blakeley and Vince Cable debate the rise and fall of globalisation.

Title: The half-life of Science
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Barry Barnes is a former Professor of Sociology at Exeter University, known for his naturalistic approach to science. He worked at the 'Science Studies Unit' at the University of Edinburgh with David Bloor, where they developed the strong programme in the Sociology of Scientific Knowledge.
Synopsis & Topics: Do scientific facts exist? In this interview, former Sociology Professor Barry Barnes discusses his work on scientific knowledge.

Title: The madness of quantum

Synopsis & Topics: Renowned quantum researcher Jim Baggott explains why he still doesn't understand the crazy but integral madness of quantum.

Title: Extinction and Renewal
Guests & Speakers: David Pearce, Henry Gee, Myriam François, Natalie Bennett

Synopsis & Topics: Is the sixth great extinction event already upon us? Or are new species emerging faster than others disappear? David Pearce, Natalie Bennett and Henry Gee debate extinction and renewal.

Title: Left, right and the future of politics

Synopsis & Topics: Has the Covid-19 pandemic confused our typically polarised political spectrum? Bim Afolami, Claire Fox and Paul Mason debate the crisis and calls for state intervention.

Title: The end of the whitewash

Synopsis & Topics: Does colourblind casting celebrate diversity, or simply sidestep the endemic racism in liberal society? Kehinde Andrews, Adjoa Andoh and Will Self debate the end of the whitewash.

Title: Church, State and Nietzsche

Synopsis & Topics: Can Nietzsche's anti-Christian thinking inspire conversions to Christianity? Rector Giles Fraser discusses the church, state, and Nietzsche

Title: The consciousness puzzle
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philip Goff is a philosopher and consciousness researcher at Durham University, who is a leading defender of panpsychism. ‘Suddenly the universe appears in a new and much more revealing perspective." Phillip Pullman
Synopsis & Topics: Is everything conscious? Philip Goff explains how panpsychism solves the problems of mateiralsm and dualism.

Title: The miracle of mind
Guests & Speakers: Tim Crane, Susan Blackmore, Bernardo Kastrup
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher of mind Tim Crane, metaphysical idealist Bernardo Kastrup and consciousness specialist Susan Blackmore debate the miracle of mind. Closure theorist Hilary Lawson hosts
Synopsis & Topics: Will science inevitably explain consciousness? Tim Crane, Bernardo Kastrup and Susan Blackmore debate the nature of consciousness and the prospect of AI with experiences

Title: Calculating reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Silvia Jonas is a philosopher at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy working in metaphysics, philosophy of mathematics, and epistemology. She is the author of 'Metaphysics: The Unspeakable in Art, Religion, and Philosophy'.
Synopsis & Topics: Can maths guide or philosophical investigations? Silvia Joan discusses the philosophies of ineffability and mathematics.

Title: Life without labels
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mark Salter is a consultant in adult general psychiatry. His special interests include risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. "It is not much to ask for mental health to be given the same degree of consideration as physical health." Mark Salter
Synopsis & Topics: Does catagorising psychological conditions help or hinder us? Mark Salter uncovers the challenges of an ever more complex world.

Title: China: ally or threat?
Guests & Speakers: Vince Cable, Malcolm Rifkind, Isabel Hilton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Foreign secretary under John Major, Malcolm Rifkind, founder of China Dialogue Isabel Hilton and former Lib Dem leader Vince Cable debate the West's future relationship with China. Director of Oxford University's China Centre Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we see China as a long term ally or threat? Malcolm Rifkind, Vince Cable and Isabel Hilton debate the future of international relations.

Title: Writing The Future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Claire Van Kampen is a highly respected director and composer, who has served as the Director of Theatre Music at the Shakespeare's Globe since 1997. She is now focusing her talents on playwriting. In this exclusive interview, Claire Van Kampen discusses how she made the transition from composer to playwright, the process of bringing life to the stage, the problems with theatre today and her hope for the future of the arts.
Synopsis & Topics: How can we bring theatre back to the people? Claire Van Kampen discusses the problems with the arts and how to fix them

Title: Drugs: the case for decriminalisation
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Nutt is a neuropsychopharmacologist and the former chairman of the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs in the UK, a position he was dismissed from in 2009. "Any sensible person or scientist knows that the drug laws are not based on the science of drugs." David Nutt
Synopsis & Topics: Is it time to decriminalise drugs? David Nutt explains the major flaws in the current criminal system

Title: Science to the Rescue
Guests & Speakers: Carlo Rovelli, Heather Douglas, Patricia Churchland
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder of loop quantum gravity theory Carlo Rovelli, philosopher of science at Michigan State University Heather Douglas, and esteemed analytic philosopher Patricia Churchland discuss how we should respond to disagreement in science during the Covid-19 pandemic. Award-winning science journalist Anil Ananthaswamy hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: How can science answer our biggest problems when scientist can't agree? Carlo Rovelli, Heather Douglas and Patricia Churchland ask how we should respond to disagreement in science

Title: Deceit and disinformation
Synopsis & Topics: In a world awash with information, and can we make informed decisions? Peter Pomerantsev digs into propaganda and misinformation

Title: Moments of Discovery
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sophie Grace Chappell is the author of numerous books and articles on ethics, ancient philosophy, epistemology and philosophy of religion. TLS described her as "an inspiring expression of an ethical vision"
Synopsis & Topics: How do we, and should we, pick a moral system? Philosopher Sophie Grace Chappell calls for a rejection of systems and an embracing of moments of discovery.

Title: Capitalism and Covid
Guests & Speakers: Paul Krugman, Deirdre McCloskey, Grace Blakeley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel Prize winning economist Paul Krugman, UIC Distinguished Professor Deirdre McCloskey and Tribune staff writer Grace Blakeley debate on Capitalism and Covid. Matthew Taylor hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are we ready for a radical economic overhaul in the wake of the pandemic? Paul Krugman, Grace Blakeley and Deirdre McCloskey debate capitalism and Covid.

Title: The Dark Energy Phenomenon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this interview, Oxford Professor of Physics Subir Sarkar outlines the problems with Dark Energy, cosmological homogeneity and questions our entire understanding of the universe.
Synopsis & Topics: Dark energy might explain the theory that the universe is rapidly expanding, but is the theory based on dubious analysis? Subir Sarkar explains.

Title: The smartphone society
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nicole Aschoff is the author of The Smartphone Society: Technology, Power, and Resistance in the New Gilded Age and The New Prophets of Capital and is on the editorial board of Jacobin. According to author Nicole Klein “Aschoff tackles slippery subjects with confidence and subtlety, providing readers with key intellectual tools to separate fact from fiction.”
Synopsis & Topics: Nichole Aschoff asks if, as smartphones become increasingly indispensable tools, we should worry about our digital privacy.

Title: Risk, Evidence and Lockdown
Guests & Speakers: David Spiegelhalter, Hugh Montgomery, Sunetra Gupta
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology Sunetra Gupta, director of the UCL Institute for Human Health and Performance Hugh Montgomery and ISI highly cited statistician David Spiegelhalter weigh up risk, evidence and lockdown. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the evidence of pandemic lockdown based on a false comparison? Is it doing more harm than good? Sunetra Gupta, David Spiegelhalter and Hugh Montgomery debate

Title: Evil acts, good people
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this interview, philosopher Stephen de Wijze outlines the messy issue of the Problem of Dirty Hands, what evil really is and why it may make sense to call acts, but not people, evil.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it a fact of life that we often have to do bad things for good outcomes? Philosophy Stephen de Wijze discusses evil acts, good people and dirty hands.

Title: How to talk about climate change
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Psychotherapist, Social Work Academic, and Climate Psychology Therapist and Researcher Caroline Hickman teaches us how to talk about climate change.
Synopsis & Topics: Climate change poses the greatest exitsential theat we're likely to face in the 21st century. Caroline Hickman explains how can can engage with this on an emotional level.

Title: Living dangerously
Guests & Speakers: Steven Pinker, Shami Chakrabarti, Daniel Kahneman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel Prize winning economist Daniel Kahneman, Harvard psychologist Steven Pinker and Labour MP, barrister and human rights activist Shami Chakrabarti explore risk, rationality and coronavirus. Anil Anathaswamy hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are humans capable ofrationally weighing up risk? Steven Pinker, Daniel Kahneman and Shami Chakrabarti debate life's inherent risks.

Title: How to decolonise your mind
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kehinde Andrews is a Professor of Black Studies, director of the Centre for Critical Social Research and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
Synopsis & Topics: The long term impact of colonial rule remains in force across the globe. Kehinde Andrews explains how decolonising your mind means recognising the need for radical change.

Title: Locking Down on Human Rights
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Shami Chakrabarti is a Labour Party politician, barrister and human rights activist who served as the director of the advocacy group Liberty.
Synopsis & Topics: What has lockdown taught us about human rights? Labour politician Shami Chakrabarti exmaines the unique ethical challenges we've had to face.

Title: Media, responsibility and a good story
Guests & Speakers: Jess Phillips, Nick Robinson, David Goodhart
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour MP Jess Phillips, journalist and presenter on the BBC's Today programme Nick Robinson, and founder and former editor of Prospect magazine David Goodhart debate the ethics of coronavirus coverage. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
