Synopsis & Topics: We rely on media to challenge authority, but in a crisis does negative press undermine efforts to implement effective strategy? Nick Robinson, David Goodhart and Jess Phillips debate.

Title: Illusions and Dreams
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this interview philosopher Jan Westerhoff outlines the philosophy of illusions and dreams, and his theory of an external world whose fundamental constituents are bits of mind, not bits of matter.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Jan Westerhoff examines what the phenomenon of illusions can teach us about the nature of reality.

Title: The Uncanny Valley
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, Sunetra Gupta addresses these tricky questions.
Synopsis & Topics: Do mathematical models help us understand reality of a pandemic? Or are abstractions all we need when planning for crises?

Title: The Morality of Pandemic
Guests & Speakers: Susan Neiman, Patricia Churchland, Peter Hitchens
Synopsis & Topics: In a pandemic, what is the right thing to do? Protect vulnerable people closest to us, or limit loss of life in the wder international community? Susan Neiman, Patricia Churchland and Peter Kitchens debate

Title: A physicist's approach to problem-solving
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chiara Marletto is a quantum phsycisist based at the University of Oxford who co-developed constructor theory, a proposal for a new mode of explanation in fundamental physics.
Synopsis & Topics: Quantum physicist Chiara Marletto argues that there's fun to be had in getting it wrong.

Title: Crime and punishment
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anthony Malcolm Daniels, also known by the pen name Theodore Dalrymple, is an English cultural critic, prison doctor and psychiatrist.
Synopsis & Topics: What can the criminal mind teach us about the human condition? Theodore Dalrymple shares insights gleaned from decades working in high security prisons.

Title: The Right Way to Think
Guests & Speakers: Alister McGrath, Mary-Jane Rubenstein, Paul Boghossian
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Oxford Intellectual Historian Alister McGrath, philosopher and author of Fear of Knowledge Paul Boghossian, and Professor of Religion and author of Strange Wonder Mary-Jane Rubenstein rethink our faith in rationality and reason.
Synopsis & Topics: Is reason society's guiding light or just rhetorical bluster? Alister McGrath, Paul Boghossian and Mary-Jane Rubernstein debate.

Title: Sex, brain and gender
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Daphna Joel is an Israeli neuroscientist. She is a senior member of the faculty of the School of Psychological Sciences and the School of Neuroscience at Tel Aviv University.
Synopsis & Topics: Why have neuroscientists found no consistent difference between make and female brains? Daphna Joel that the concept of gendered brains is obstructing scientific progress.

Title: A History of the Conscious World
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the panpsychist claim that everything is conscious much older than we might think? Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad delves into Indian philosophy to make sense of this theory

Title: The cause of death
Guests & Speakers: Toby Young, Michael Levitt, David Alexander, Anne Johnson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nobel-prize winning biophysicist Michael Levitt debates with Professor of Infectious Disease Epidemiology Anne Johnson and Professor of Risk and Disaster Reduction David Alexander, both at University College London, and associate editor of The Spectator Toby Young, who recently launched the website Lockdown Sceptics. Philosopher and author of Closure Hilary Lawson hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Are we certain how many deaths Covid-19 has caused? Do we know how many deaths lockdown will cause? Biophysicist Michael Levitt, epidemiologist Anne Johnson, professor of risk and disaster David Alexander and associate editor of The Spectator Toby Young debate.

Title: Brian Eno's philosophy of art
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Musical pioneer Brian Eno is co-founder of the art rock group Roxy Music and producer of recordings by the likes of David Byrne, U2, David Bowie, John Cale, and Robert Fripp.
Synopsis & Topics: Musical pioneer Brian Eno is co-founder of the art rock group Roxy Music and producer of recordings by the likes of David Byrne, U2, David Bowie, John Cale, and Robert Fripp.

Title: Where are we going?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: CERN physicist John Ellis is a pioneer in the emerging field of particle astrophysics, who has also made important contributions to particle physics, astrophysics, cosmology and quantum gravity.
Synopsis & Topics: What are we? Where did we come from and where are we going? Physicist John Ellis turns to particle physics and cosmology for answers to these complicated questions.

Title: The age of anxiety
Guests & Speakers: Mark Salter, David Nutt, Caroline Hickman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Psychotherapist and member of the Climate Psychology Alliance Caroline Hickman, neuropsychopharmacologist and author David Nutt, and consultant in adult psychiatry for the NHS Mark Salter debate the growing phenomenon of anxiety. Rana Mitter hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Anxiety is the most commonly diagnosed mental health illness. Is it a rational response to uncertain times that we're over medicalising? Caroline Hickman, David Nutt and Mark Salter debate the age of anxiety

Title: Cybersecurity and Huawei
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Security expert Nigel Inkster worked for 31 years in the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6), retiring as Assistant Chief and Director of Operations and Intelligence. After leaving MI6, he became Director of Transnational Threats and Political Risk at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, where he is now Senior Advisor, and has also been engaged in a variety of para-diplomatic activities on behalf of the UK government. His research portfolio has included transnational terrorism, insurgency, transnational organised crime, cyber security, intelligence and security, and the evolving character of conflict.
Synopsis & Topics: Former MI6 chief Nigel Inkster explains how China has become a digital superpower, why Huawei is more than an espionage issue, and how the field of international conflict is shifting.

Title: Against Psychiatry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Bentall is Professor of Clinical Psychology at the University of Sheffield, a Fellow of the British Academy and a leading researcher on schizophrenia, psychosis and public mental health. He is the author of Madness Explained and Doctoring the Mind.
Synopsis & Topics: Can we prevent mental health conditions, instead of simply treating them? Richard Bentall discusses the importance of asking what’s happened to someone, not just what's wrong with them

Title: Is capitalism broken?
Guests & Speakers: Guy Standing, Izabella Kaminska, Jamie Whyte, Stephen King
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Plunder of The Commons, Guy Standing, politician and libertarian economist Jamie Whyte, FT Alphaville editor, Izabella Kaminska and senior economic adviser at HSBC Holdings, Stephen King ask whether we can save Capitalism - and whether we should.
Synopsis & Topics: Is capitalism fundamentally broken? Guy Standing, Jamie Whyte, Izabella Kaminska and Stephen King ask if it can, and should, be saved

Title: Being Bad To Do Good
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political philosopher and author Stephen de Wijze looks beyond right and wrong.
Synopsis & Topics: We want politicians to do the right thing, but moral codes are inevitably broken amid the complexities of real life. Stephen de Wijze asks if there's a political alternative to a moral rule book.

Title: After the god particle
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cambridge physicist Ben Allanach, Maxwell prize-winning CERN theoretical physicist John Ellis and Edinburgh Astrophysicist Catherine Heymans look at what's missing from our picture of particle theory. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Will the Higgs Boson lead to a theory of everything? Why has it gone quiet at CERN? Catherine Heymans, John Ellis and Ben Allanach debate what's missing from our picture of particle physics.

Title: Metropolis untamed
Guests & Speakers: Shoshana Zuboff, Joanna Kavenna, Angela Eagle, Bim Afolami
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of The Age of Surveillance Capitalism Shoshana Zuboff, Conservative MP Bim Afolami, author of Zed Joanna Kavenna, and Labour MP Angela Eagle debate the power and peril of the tech giants.
Synopsis & Topics: Will tech giants decide our future, or can we escape these malevolent monopolies? Do we want to? Shoshana Zuboff, Angela Eagle, Bim Afolami and Joanna Kavenna debate.

Title: Learning to love uncertainty
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Åsa Wikforss is a professor of theoretical philosophy at Stockholm University. Wikforss is a member of Swedish Academy whose research focuses on the intersection of philosophy of mind, language and epistemology, ans in 2017 Wikfoss published Alternative facts. On knowledge and its enemies, a book that has had a great impact in Sweden.
Synopsis & Topics: Asa Wikforss asks if knowledge stands a chance in an age of alternative facts. In a world without certainty, how should we deal with the cacophony of information bombarding us?

Title: Science, Trust and Truth
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher of science and author of How The Laws of Physics Lie, Nancy Cartwright untangles the evidence and asks "science: why trust it?"
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Nancy Cartwright asks if science deserves the trust we place in it, and if criticism might spur scientific progress on more than blind faith

Title: Izabella Kaminska | In-depth interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Izabella Kaminska is editor of FT Alphaville. Before that she worked as a producer at CNBC, a natural gas reporter at Platts and an associate editor of BP's internal magazine.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the economy rigged against the working class, and is a new crash inevitable? Izabella Kaminska lifts the lid on the world of finance

Title: In search of freedom
Guests & Speakers: Julian Baggini, Hilary Lawson, Hannah Dawson, Paul Broks
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Historian of ideas and author of Life Lessons from Hobbes Hannah Dawson, post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson, neuropsychologist and science writer Paul Broks and author of Freedom Regained Julian Baggini ask who's really in control. David Aaronovitch hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is free will an illusion? Should we accept the deterministic nature of the universe in order to better understand human behaviour? Hannah Dawson, Paul Broks, Julian Baggini and Hilary Lawson go in search of freedom

Title: The tyranny of the new
Guests & Speakers: Brian Eno, Sophie Fiennes, Claire van Kampen, Ammar Kalia
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Composer and former musical director at Shakespeare's Globe Claire van Kampen, film director Sophie Fiennes, Observer music journalist Ammar Kalia and art rock icon Brian Eno debate the value of the new. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the new and novel necessarily more vital that all that's come before, or is true art timeless? Composer Claire van Kampen, director Sophie Fiennes, journalist Ammar Kalia and musician Brian Eno debate.

Title: Time is running out for supersymmetry and string theory
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Heymans, Ben Allanach, Subir Sarkar, David Tong, Tara Shears, John Horgan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Royal Observatory astrophysicist Catherine Heymans, theoretical physicist at the University of Cambridge Ben Allanach, head of the Particle Theory Group at Oxford University Subir Sarkar, Cambridge string theorist David Tong, experimental physicist Tara Shears, and author of The End of Science John Horgan discuss whether it is time to do away with beautiful theories.
Synopsis & Topics: Will supersymmetry or string theory ever deliver on their promise to solve major problems in modern physics?

Title: What's wrong with us?
Guests & Speakers: Anders Sandberg, David Healy, Natalie Bennett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Psychiatrist David Healy, Oxford University futurist Anders Sandberg, and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate the future of AI doctors. Emily Grossman hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is it time for AI to do more to help doctors and nurses?

Title: Digital Apes
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Nigel Shadbolt is the author of The Digital Ape and co-founder of the Open Data Institute with Tim Berners-Lee and was identified as 'one of the most fascinating and important scientists alive today' by Jim Al-Khalili.
Synopsis & Topics: Smart machines are shaping our future. Should we be worried? Nigel Shadbolt examines the impact of new technologies.

Title: Emily Thomas | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Emily Thomas is a historian of philosophy at Durham University. Her main research interests include space, time, and the relationship between philosophy and travel.
Synopsis & Topics: How has travel shaped philosophy? What can philosophy tell us about humanity's wanderlust? Emily Thomas explores everything from intellectual journeying to the origins of cultural relativism.

Title: Lies, damned lies, and post truth
Guests & Speakers: Sacha Golob, Åsa Wikforss, Steve Fuller, Peter Pomerantsev
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Post Truth Steve Fuller, theoretical philosopher Åsa Wikforss, continental philosopher Sacha Golob, and former Moscow journalist and author of This is Not Propaganda Peter Pomerantsev ask whether anybody has a monopoly on truth.
Synopsis & Topics: Did we give up on the idea of absolute truth too easily? Are we no longer able to call out blatant lies? Steve Fuller, Asa Wikforss and Sacha Golob ask if anyone has a monopoly on truth

Title: Ben Allanach | In-depth interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ben Allanach is a professor of theoretical physics at the University of Cambridge. His research focuses on collider searches for new physics with the Cambridge Pheno Working Group and at CERN's Large Hadron Collider.
Synopsis & Topics: Has CERN's failure to find evidence of supersymmetry thrown particle physics into crisis? Ben Allanach explains his shift to bottom-up science

Title: Bart Streumer | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Bart Streumer is professor of philosophy at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands. Streumer's main research interests are metaethics, ethics, and political philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Should ethical judgments be approached with a healthy scepticism?Do moral philosophies need real-world application to become meaningful? Bart Streumer unpacks the implications of error theory for metaethics.

Title: The Future of Thought
Guests & Speakers: Jamie Whyte, Julian Baggini, Vivienne Shue
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of How the World Thinks Julian Baggini, political philosopher Jamie Whyte, and Oxford Professor of China Studies Vivienne Shue consider China's influence on the future of ideas. Journalist and broadcaster Isabel Hilton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: daoism, confucianism, shinto, China, western philosophy, Eastern philosophy, Isabel Hilton, Julian Baggini

Title: The Value of Everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mariana Mazzucato is an economist, currently working at UCL. She is the author of The Value of Everything , which seeks to redefine how we measure value in our society. It was praised by the Financial Times 's Martin Wolf for 'forcing us to confront long-held beliefs about how economies work, and who benefits'.
Synopsis & Topics: Economic value is not the same as price, explains economist Mariana Mazzucato. It's time for new debates about what value is and how we nuture it.

Title: David Malone | In-depth interview
Synopsis & Topics: Documentary filmmaker David Malone discusses the prospect of a future defined by artificial intelligence, and the excitement of a resurgance in dualist metaphysical thinking.

Title: Work and play
Guests & Speakers: Susan Neiman, Janne Teller, Helen Lederer
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ab Fab star Helen Lederer, Director of the Einstein Forum and author of Why We Grow Up? Susan Neiman, and novelist Janne Teller join Julian Baggini to seek new answers to life’s biggest question.
Synopsis & Topics: We admire achievers but spend our lives waiting for weekends and holdays. Ab Fab's Helen Lederer, philosopher Susan neiman, The Business Romantic Society CEO Tim Leberecht debate work/play balance.

Title: Lucy Johnstone | In-depth interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lucy Johnstone is a consultant clinical psychologist, author of Users and abusers of psychiatry , and co-editor of Formulation in psychology and psychotherapy: making sense of people's problems and A straight-talking guide to psychiatric diagnosis . Former Programme Director of the Bristol Clinical Psychology Doctorate and lead author of 'Good practice guidelines on the use of psychological formulation'.
Synopsis & Topics: Lucy Johnstone discusses a new way to think about mental health, giving patients a greater role in understanding their conditions.

Title: Do we still need morality?
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Jason McKenzie Alexander, Justin Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Head of Philosophy at LSE Jason McKenzie Alexander, philosopher and author of Irrationality Justin Smith, and director of the Institute of Philosophy Barry C. Smith consider the foundations and future of morality. Myriam Francois hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is morality subjective? Or are there objective moral facts we can appeal to? Philosophers Jason Mckenzie Alexander, Justin Smith and Barry C. Smith debate morality’s role in the modern world.

Title: The Hidden Science of Spirituality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rupert Sheldrake is author of The Science Delusion and Ways to Go Beyond. New Scientist described him as 'an excellent scientist; the proper, imaginative kind that in an earlier age discovered continents'.
Synopsis & Topics: What’s the science of spirituality? Rupert Sheldrake exmaines the physiological impact of practices once thought to be wholly mystical.

Title: Kate Kirkpatrick | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Kate kirkpatrick is a lecturer in Religion, Philosophy and Culture at Kings College London, and author of Becoming Beauvoir: A Life.
Synopsis & Topics: Simone de Beauvoir expert Kate Kirkpatrick discusses the influence of de Beauvoir's work on the existentialist tradition, and its relevance today.

Title: Has greed got the better of us?
Guests & Speakers: Brian Eno, Guy Standing, Izabella Kaminska, Mark Littlewood
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of the most influential and innovative figures in pop music Brian Eno is joined by the editor of FT Alphaville Izabella Kaminska, Director General of the Institute of Economic Affairs Mark Littlewood, and author Guy Standing to diagnose the efficacy of our wants and needs.
Synopsis & Topics: Why do we remain unsatisfied in a world filled with possessions? Brian Eno, Mark Littlewood, Guy Standing and Izabella Kaminska ask if discontent drives success or if materialism is fuelling greed.

Title: How to talk about sex
Synopsis & Topics: Sex education can be a tricky subejct. Peter Tatchell argues we must break taboos if we're to educate future generations on sexuality across the spectrum.

Title: Julian Baggini | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher and author of How the World Thinks Julian Baggini discusses the applications of philosophy in everyday life, from the individual level to the societal.
Synopsis & Topics: Can philosophy save politics? Julian Baggini asks if philosophers have a responsibility to apply theories to public life.

Title: Why love is the most dangerous thing in the world
Guests & Speakers: Mark Salter, Helen-Ann Hartley, Phillip Blond
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Consultant Psychiatrist Mark Salter, Anglican Bishop Helen-Ann Hartley and political theorist Phillip Blond debate the darker sides of the emotion worth dying, and killing, for. Robert Rowland Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is acting in the name of love dangerous? Can love drive exclusion? Psychiatrist Mark Salter, Anglican Bishop Helen-Ann Hartley and political theoriest Phillip Blond debate

Title: How to Think About Free Speech
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Stanley Fish is a public intellectual and author of The First: How to Think About Hate Speech , Campus Speech , Religious Speech , Fake News , Post-Truth, and Donald Trump .
Synopsis & Topics: Free speech is a double-edged sword. It unshackles us but justifies the expression of harmful opinions. Stanley Fish interrogates the concept and asks how we can use it better.

Title: Cumrun Vafa | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: String theorist and professor of physics at Harvard University Cumrun Vafa explains what string theory is, how it fits within contemporary physics, and sets out his vision for its future.
Synopsis & Topics: What is string theory? Harvard professor Cumrun Vafa explains how string theory is the best candidate for combining Einstein's quantum mechanics in a consistent framework.

Title: The Illusion of Now
Guests & Speakers: Emily Thomas, Julian Barbour, Tim Maudlin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher of science Tim Maudlin joins author of The End of Time Julian Barbour and philosopher and historian of science Emily Thomas to go in search of lost time. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is time real, or just an illusion? Tim Maudlin, Emily Thomas and Julian Barbour query our experience of the present, and the radical theories of thinkers from Einstein to Derrida.

Title: Gene Editing in the Wild
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Yale biologist and founder of Editing Nature, Natalie Kofler unpicks the ethical problems posed by this new technology.
Synopsis & Topics: Editing Nature founder Natalie Kofler examines the vast possiblities of gene editing, and how it could go very wrong.

Title: Saul Kripke on Wittgenstein
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Saul Kripke has been described by many as the world's most influential living analytic philosopher, and in the top 10 of the last 200 years. Saul Kripke is a logician, emeritus professor at Princeton and a Corresponding Fellow at the British Academy. He is best known for reintroducing modal concepts, such as necessity and possibility.
Synopsis & Topics: Saul Kripke, considered the greatest living analytic philosopher, explains his own interpretation of the philosophy of Ludwig Wittgenstein, known as Kripkenstein.

Title: Victims and Warriors
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Minna Salami, Peter Tatchell
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Human rights and LGBT+ campaigner Peter Tatchell, journalist and founder of MsAfropolitan Minna Salami, and Times columnist David Aaronovitch debate the best route to empowerment.
Synopsis & Topics: Peter Tatchell, Minna Salami and David Aaronovitch ask whether it’s time to abandon our stiff upper lip mentality and call out injustice.

Title: Work Doesn't Pay
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour MP and author of The New Serfdom , Angela Eagle sets out her vision for a fairer future.
Synopsis & Topics: Angela Eagle investigates the growing phenomenon of working poverty, why jobs no longer guarantee stability, and sets out her vision for a fairer future.

Title: Zanna Clay | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Zanna Clay is a comparative and developmental psychologist with expertise in primatology, studying great apes and young children in order to investigate the evolutionary and developmental basis of hominid social cognition and behavior.
Synopsis & Topics: Psychologist and primatologist Zanna Clay discusses empathy in animals and asks what we can learn from other species, and where evolution will take us next.

Title: Tribal Truths and New Wisdoms
Guests & Speakers: Ella McPherson, Hilary Lawson, Paul Mason
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Post-Capitalism author Paul Mason, Cambridge sociologist Ella McPherson, philosopher and former editor of The World This Week Hilary Lawson question whether it is ever really possible to report the truth. Roger Bolton hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: In a post-truth world must we accept that facts are a thing of the past? Journalist Paul Mason, sociologist Ella McPherson and philosopher Hilary Lawson ask if truth will remain beyond our grasp.

Title: The War Against Reality
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of The War Against Reality Peter Pomerantsev sets the record straight on politics in the age of post-truth.
Synopsis & Topics: With political campaigns using our data to tap into our deepest fears, freedom and democracy are under attack: Peter Pomeranstev on politics after post-truth.

Title: Paul Mason | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Paul Mason is a British author, commentator, and political journalist, previously the Newsnight Business Editor, and Economics Editor at Channel 4 News.
Synopsis & Topics: Paul Mason explains why movements like Extinction Rebellion now have to contend with more than just state opposition, and why there’s still hope for solving the climate crisis.

Title: The Rise and Fall of Sex
Guests & Speakers: Barry Barnes, Daphna Joel, Stuart Ritchie
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Head of Psychobiology at Tel Aviv University Daphna Joel, genetic and developmental psychiatrist at KCL Stuart Ritchie, and sociologist of science Barry Barnes rethink sex, gender and the differences between men and women. Robert Rowland Smith hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Does the evidence for gendered brain theory stand up? Or could biological sex be an illusion? Experts in neuroscience, psychobiology and sociology debate.

Title: The Self Around the World
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher and author of How the World Thinks Julian Baggini examines philosophical traditions around the globe to highlight the nuance in differences between concepts of self.
Synopsis & Topics: Julian Baggini draws on philosophical traditions around the world to find answers to who we are, and alternatives to the West’s fixation with the self.

Title: Timothy Williamson | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher Timothy Williamson is a world-renowned philosopher of language and logic, who has written extensively on what philosophy is, and how it should be done.
Synopsis & Topics: Analytic philosopher Timothy Williamson outlines how philosophy can help us think more clearly, the value of logic, and the importance of debate for inclusivity.

Title: Thinking Straight
Guests & Speakers: Nigel Inkster, Thangam Debbonaire, Richard Bentall, Michael Lynksey
Synopsis & Topics: Should we ban alcohol as part of a global overhaul in drug policy to reduce crime and bring classification in line with the health risks?

Title: The adventure of space
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher Barry C. Smith unpacks the isolationist myths around space exploration, and brings to light the hidden heroes of Apollo 11.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Barry C. Smith unpacks the isolationist myths around space exploration, explaining why the moon landings were a global human achievement.

Title: How To Help Your Body Help Your Mind
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Fuller is a journalist, pro documentary maker and founder of media company Rebel Wisdom.
Synopsis & Topics: David Fuller outlines the psychology of conflict and teaches techniques from mindfulness and counselling, teaching us how have more productive conversations

Title: Paul Boghossian | In-depth Interview
Synopsis & Topics: Paul Boghossian explains why the argument that facts are constructed by human mental activity is misguided, and why he’s changed his mind about intuition.

Title: After Darwin
Guests & Speakers: Massimo Pigliucci, Tim Lewens, Zanna Clay
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosophers of science Massimo Pigliucci, author of Cultural Evolution Tim Lewens, and psychologist and primatologist Zanna Clay ask if there is more to evolution than we might think. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Is natural selection about to be replaced by a new science of cultural evolution? Massimo Pigliucci, Tim Lewens and Zanna Clay consider evolution after Darwin.

Title: How to See Life's Patterns
Synopsis & Topics: Anna Murray shares her perspective on how nature's patterns can inspire us to find more sustainable ways of living to bring about positive change in our lives.

Title: How to Change Your Habits of Thought
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jeremy Lent is an author whose writings investigate the patterns of thought that have led civilization to its current crisis of sustainability. He is the founder of the non-profit Liology Institute, which is dedicated to a worldview that could enable humanity to thrive sustainably.
Synopsis & Topics: Jeremy Lent on how the instinct to see patterns relates to humanity’s search for meaning, and why the patterns we’ve followed have led us to a climate crisis.

Title: Steven Pinker | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Steven Pinker is an experimental psychologist, cognitive scientist and linguist based at Harvard University. He is the author of Enlightenment Now, How the Mind Works and The Better Angels of our Nature.
Synopsis & Topics: Steven Pinker on why human nature does exist, why progress is widespread, and in spite of issues like rising populism, societies do follow enlightenment values.

Title: Nations, Borders and History
Guests & Speakers: David Blunkett, Elif Sarican, Ella Whelan, Eric Kaufmann
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Home Secretary David Blunkett, Birkbeck professor of politics and author of Whiteshift Eric Kaufmann, and Kurdish independence movement activist Elif Sarican debate what makes a nation. Ella Whelan hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Former home secretary David Blunkett, Kurdish independence activist Elif Sarican and professor of politics Eric Kaufmann ask if borders define a nation.

Title: A Paranoid World?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Richard Bentall, clinical psychologist and author of Madness Explained, interrogates the evidence.
Synopsis & Topics: Richard Bentall, clinical psychologist and author of 'Madness Explained', examines the roots of clinical paranoia.

Title: Rebecca Goldstein | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Rebecca Goldstein is a Visiting Professor of Philosophy at New York University and New College of the Humanities, and one of three philosophers who have been awarded the US National Humanities Medal.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Rebecca Goldstein traces the role of intuition and evidence in philosophy via Hume, Spinoza and Kant.

Title: How to Land on Another Planet
Guests & Speakers: Elizabeth Seward, Elie Allouis, Kerry Sanz, Stephen Kyle-Henney
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Robotics Systems Team Lead at Airbus, Elie Allouis joins MDA UK Operations Director Kerry Sanz and TISICS Limited Managing Director Stephen Kyle-Henney to discuss the challenges facing UK space organisations. Elizabeth Seward hosts. In partnership with Airbus.
Synopsis & Topics: How hard will it be to land on Mars? Scientists from Airbus and other space organisations discuss the challenges facing UK space exploration, and the strategies for overcoming them.

Title: The Case for Classical Liberalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of the Institute of Economic Affairs Mark Littlewood makes a case for why classical liberals are always right and wonders why do they always lose?
Synopsis & Topics: Institute of Economic Affairs director Mark Littlewood makes a case for why classic liberals are always right but always lose

Title: Julian Barbour | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Julian Barbour is a theoretical physicist and Emeritus visiting professor at the University of Oxford, who has been working on foundational issues in Physics for nearly fifty years, specialising in the study of time and motion.
Synopsis & Topics: Why do we think we experience time and why are we mistaken? Julian Barbour puts forward a radical new theory and considers its potential impacts on physics.

Title: A Crack In Everything
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Live from Ljubljana, philosopher and cultural critic Slavoj Žižek joins Oxford metaphysician Sophie Allen and post-realist philosopher and author of Reflexivity: the postmodern predicament Hilary Lawson to ask why paradox just won't go away. Shahidha Bari hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Slavoj Žižek, Sophie Allen and Hilary Lawson debate whether paradoxes prove our philosophical theories are wrong or simply that human understanding is limited.

Title: Dressed: A Philosophy of Fashion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher, broadcaster and author of Dressed: The Secret Life of Clothes , Shahidha Bari, unveils the hidden power of what we wear.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher, broadcaster and author Shahidha Bari considers the philosophy of fashion, and the place of clothes in our lives.

Title: Mary-Jane Rubenstein | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion, Feminist, Gender and Sexuality Studies at Wesleyan University. She is the author of Strange Wonder: The Closure of Metaphysics and the Opening of Awe, Worlds without End: The Many Lives of the Multiverse, and most recently, Pantheologies: Gods, Worlds, Monsters.
Synopsis & Topics: Multiverse research is providing new information about where we come from and the nature of the universe, which could radically impact faith as well as physics.

Title: The Universe That Wasn't There
Guests & Speakers: Roger Penrose, Catherine Heymans, Subir Sarkar
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: World-renowned physicist Roger Penrose, Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, and Professor of Astrophysics Catherine Heymans wonder why we can't find most of the universe. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Dark Matter and Dark Energy supposedly account for 95% of the universe, but we still can’t detect them. Roger Penrose, Subir Sarkar, and Catherine Heymans consider why.

Title: The True and the Trivial
Guests & Speakers: Joanna Kavenna, Barry C. Smith, Justin Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher and author of Irrationality Justin Smith, Director of the Institute of Philosophy Barry C. Smith, and author of Inglorious Joanna Kavenna unravel the relationship between humour and serious ideas. Philosopher Robert Rowland Smith hosts .
Synopsis & Topics: Nietzsche and Derrida argued rony and comedy are central to deep philosophical thought. Justin Smith, Barry C Smith and Joanna Kavena as if ideas need to be serious to have lasting impact, or can humour convey profound insight?

Title: Tim Maudlin | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Tim Maudlin, author of Philosophy of Physics, is an American philosopher of science responsible for influential works on metaphysical foundations of physics and logic.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher of science Tim Maudlin discusses interpretations of quantum mechanics, pilot wave theory and objective collapse theory.

Title: Massimo Pigliucci | In-depth Interview
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher Massimo Pigliucci makes the case for adopting stoicism as a philosophy to live by, and why scepticism is still relevant today.

Title: Susan Neiman | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Susan Neiman, author of Evil in Modern Thought and Moral Clarity: A Guide for Grown-Up Idealists , is a moral philosopher and director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam.
Synopsis & Topics: Moral philosopher Susan Neiman examines the nature of Evil and our fascination with it, from evil-doers in pop culture to what Hannah Arendt called banal evils.

Title: Donald Hoffman | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Donald Hoffman, author of The case Against Reality: How Evolution Hid the Truth from Our Eye, is a cognitive psychologist and professor in the Department of Cognitive Sciences at the University of California, with joint appointments in the Department of Philosophy, the Department of Logic and Philosophy of Science, and the School of Computer Science.
Synopsis & Topics: Donald Hoffman talks us through his work on evolutionary game theory, and the radical argument that our perceptions do not coincide with reality.

Title: Catherine Heymans | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Catherine Heymans is a British astrophysicist and Professor at the University of Edinburgh, based at the Royal Observatory.
Synopsis & Topics: Astrophysicist Catherine Heymans discusses dark energy, dark matter, and the keys to uncovering the mysteries of the dark universe.

Title: Roger Penrose | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Roger Penrose is a mathematical physicist best known for his work on general relativity. He shared the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for their work on black holes.
Synopsis & Topics: Roger Penrose on the origins of the universe, opposition to Big Bang theory, and the implications of quantum mechanics, touching on Hawking Points & Twistor Theory.

Title: John Ellis | In-depth interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: CERN physicist John Ellis is a pioneer in the emerging field of particle astrophysics, who has also made important contributions to particle physics, astrophysics, cosmology and quantum gravity.
Synopsis & Topics: CERN physicist John Ellis discusses supersymmetry, string theory and whether there could be a theory of everything that helps us understand the dark universe.

Title: David Blunkett | In-depth interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Blind since birth, and coming from one of Sheffield's most deprived districts, David Blunkett rose to become Education and Employment Secretary, Home Secretary, and Work and Pensions Secretary during Tony Blair's years in office.
Synopsis & Topics: Former Home Secretary and Labour party MP David Blunkett discusses Brexit, the Irish backstop, UK immigration policy, and Tony Blair's legacy from Iraq to privatisation.

Title: Anna Soubry | In-depth Interview
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Anna Soubry is MP for Broxtowe and a member of the Independent Group. Having threatened repeatedly to leave the Conservative Party on account of its leadership's Brexit stance, Soubry defected to the newly-formed group in February 2019.
Synopsis & Topics: Change UK leader Anna Soubry on populism, the rise of the right, and how to fix the UK’s broken politics.

Title: The age of surveillance capitalism
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Shoshana Zuboff is Charles Edward Wilson Professor Emeritus at Harvard Business School and a leading theorist of technology and privacy.
Synopsis & Topics: Shoshana Zuboff lifts the lid on surveillance capitalism, the new economic logic invented by Google and weaponised by Cambridge Analytica.

Title: Modern Crises and Ancient Gods
Guests & Speakers: David King, Natalie Bennett, Sister Jayanti
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Recent leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett, former chief science adviser David King, and European director of Brahma Kumari Sister Jayanti discuss what we must learn from the ancients to save our planet from its modern crises. David Malone hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Will science or spirituality provide solutions to the climate crisis? The Green Party’s Natalie Bennett debates with David King and Sister Jayanti.

Title: The Mystery of Life
Guests & Speakers: Monica Grady, Nick Lane, Ralph Cordey
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Biochemist and author of The Vital Question Nick Lane, Head of Future Missions at Airbus Ralph Cordey, and leading British space scientist Monica Grady grapple with the mysterious puzzles of life. In partnership with Airbus.
Synopsis & Topics: The search for extraterrestrial life goes on, but will we recognise what we find as life at all? Nick Lane, Monica Grady and Airbus' Ralph Cordey discuss the nature of life and Earth and beyond.

Title: On the Dogmatism Paradox
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Should one decide in advance never to consider evidence against what one knows? There is an argument that seems to show this. Saul Kripke explores the question of whether the dogmatic attitude is sometimes warranted.
Synopsis & Topics: Saul Kripke considers whether we are ever justified in dogmatically refusing to consider evidence that contradicts our beliefs.

Title: The end of Left and Right
Guests & Speakers: David Goodhart, Rory Stewart, Chantal Mouffe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of The Road to Somewhere David Goodhart, Conservative leadership candidate Rory Stewart and political theorist and author of For a Left Populism Chantal Mouffe debate new political divides.
Synopsis & Topics: Rory Stewart, David Goodhart, and Chantal Mouffe consider the future of Left and Right as events in UK politics blur the line between Conservative and Liberal

Title: The Arc of Life: Michael Morpurgo
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this biographical interview with critic and novelist Stephanie Merritt, Michael Morpurgo considers the role of children's fiction in cultivating empathy, and outlines how his latest book Boy Giant uses Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels as a springboard to discussing issues such as the refugee crisis, and Brexit.
Synopsis & Topics: Extended interview with Michael Morpurgo, author of War Horse, on how his biography and life experiences have shaped his ideas and works.

Title: A Mad World
Guests & Speakers: Richard Bentall, Lucy Johnstone, Ann John
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Madness Explained, Richard Bentall, clinical psychologist Lucy Johnstone, and consultant for Public Health Wales and Swansea Professor of Medicine Ann John examine the evidence.
Synopsis & Topics: Is this really a mad world? Is the rise in mental health problems down to modern living or are we medicalising normal huamn behaviour?

Title: Into the Unknown
Guests & Speakers: Elizabeth Seward, Martin Rees, Tony Milligan
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Astronomer Royal Martin Rees, philosopher and author of Nobody Owns the Moon Tony Milligan, and Senior Strategist for Airbus Elizabeth Seward reach out to the cosmos. In partnership with Airbus.
Synopsis & Topics: Is the future of space exploration commercial, robotic or manned, and will we go beyond our solar system? Martin Rees, Tony Milligan and Elizabeth Seward debate.

Title: How to be a Stoic
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Massimo Pigliucci is Professor of Philosophy at CUNY-City College, formerly co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast, and formerly the editor in chief for the online magazine Scientia Salon .
Synopsis & Topics: Hear philosopher of science and author of How to be a Stoic Massimo Pigliucci explain how stoicism can help us focus on what really matters, and confront the challenges of modern life.

Title: Reason, rage and revolution
Guests & Speakers: Vince Cable, Ella Whelan, Aaron Bastani
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder of Novara Media Aaron Bastani, former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, and political commentator and journalist Ella Whelan consider the conflict to come. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Will tolerance and pluralism give way to populism and revolution in the UK and beyond? Aaron Bastani debates with the Lib Dem’s Vince Cable and Ella Whelan.

Title: How to Rediscover Your Creativity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Lauren Baker is a British contemporary artist, who has created installations at the V&A, Tate Britain, and Tate Modern. Her Damien Hirst-inspired workshop was the Tate Modern's most popular to date.
Synopsis & Topics: Lauren Baker provides a workshop to enhance your creative skills and blue sky thinking with easy visualisation exercises, designed to unlock artistic potential.

Title: Britain in Uncharted Territory
Guests & Speakers: Claire Fox, Natalie Bennett, Owen Smith
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett, left-wing Leaver and Brexit party MEP Claire Fox, and Labour MP Owen Smith consider how we might navigate this uncertain future. BBC parliamentary correspondent Sean Curran hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Former Green party leader Natalie Bennett, Labour’s Owen Smith, MEP Claire Fox and the BBC’s Sean Curran debate Brexit and the changing landscape of UK politics.

Title: Rory Stewart in conversation with Emma Barnett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative party leadership candidate Rory Stewart was one of 21 anti no-deal rebels to be purged from the party on 3rd September 2019. The former Secretary of State for International Development under Theresa May is now an independent politician and champion of the fight against a No Deal Brexit. Rory Stewart is interviewed by the journalist Emma Barnett, who regularly presents BBC's Newsnight , Radio 5 Live , and Woman's Hour .
Synopsis & Topics: Former Conservative MP turned Independent candidate for the Mayor of London Rory Stewart talks to Emma Barnett on Boris Johnson's abuses of power.

Title: The Arc of Life: Roger Penrose
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sir Roger Penrose is one of the world's most prominent theoretical physicists, who collaborated with Stephen Hawking to produce the mathematics that showed how stars collapse to form black holes. Penrose invented twistor theory, spin networks, and many other quantum mechanical concepts, earning him the title of the founding father of quantum gravity.
Synopsis & Topics: Eminent theoretical physicist and Stephen Hawking collaborator Roger Penrose discusses logic, quantum and consciousness in this interview with David Malone.

Title: The Prejudice of Facts
Guests & Speakers: Barry Barnes, Joanna Kavenna, John Ellis
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Clerk Maxwell professor of theoretical physics John Ellis, post-Kuhnian sociologist of scientific knowledge S. Barry Barnes, and novelist Joanna Kavenna debate whether alternative facts are further proof that there is no objective truth. Phillip Dodd chairs.
Synopsis & Topics: Are alternative facts and fake news a recent invention or was objective truth always a myth? Perhaps Nietzsche was right to say ‘no facts, only interpretations’.

Title: Immigration and Identity
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire is shadow whip in Corbyn's front bench team. She describes herself as a democratic socialist and a supporter of "fettered capitalism".
Synopsis & Topics: Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire investigates why immigration has come to define UK politics and divide the nation, in this rethink of borders, identity and Europe.

Title: The New Mafia
Guests & Speakers: Anatole Kaletsky, Nicky Morgan, Phillip Blond
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Conservative MP and former Education Secretary Nicky Morgan joins economist and award-winning journalist Anatole Kaletsky and director of ResPublica think tank Phillip Blond to debate the threat of the digital giants. Stephanie Hare hosts.
Synopsis & Topics: Big Tech exploit their monopoly to manipulate users, eliminate competition, and evade tax. Should we regulate or tax tech giants or is it already too late?

Title: The Ladder of Success
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Labour MP Dawn Butler is the Shadow Women & Equalities Secretary, and former Shadow Minister for Diverse Communities.
Synopsis & Topics: Labour MP Dawn Butler argues for transparency in the career ladder so that improved gender representation at senior level confers benefits for all working women.

Title: The lure of Lucifer
Guests & Speakers: Terry Eagleton, Susan Neiman, Stephen de Wijze
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: One of Britain's most influential cultural critics Terry Eagleton, author of Evil in Modern Thought Susan Neiman, and philosopher Stephen de Wijze get to the bottom of evil's strange allure.
Synopsis & Topics: Terry Eagleton, Susan Neiman, and Stephen de Wijze consider the philosophy behind our fascination with evil and violence, from crime fiction to serial killers.

Title: Momentum and Young Socialists
Synopsis & Topics: Giles Fraser, Anglican priest, outspoken journalist and regular panelist on The Moral Maze, talks to Jon Lansman, the founder of Momentum - the pro-Corbyn, grassroots political movement that has polarised the Labour party since its inception. Hear Giles find out about Jon's life experiences and core values in an attempt to find out what "makes him tick".

Title: The Right to be Offended
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Joanna Williams
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. Joanna Williams is the author of Women vs Feminism , associate editor of the political magazine Spiked , and the Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I , International Business Times , and New European .
Synopsis & Topics:
Last year Ireland voted to get rid of its blasphemy laws, and most applauded the new right to offend the Catholic Church. We also expect our press and our comedians to be viciously critical of, even offensive to, our leaders. Yet to avoid giving offence, student campuses are introducing no-platforming and safe spaces. Should we seek to eradicate offence to create a more tolerant and equal society? Or is offence vital to freedom and a critical means of containing the powerful? Please be aware that, due to the nature of this debate, this video contains language that some viewers may find offensive.

David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. Joanna Williams is the author of Women vs Feminism, associate editor of the political magazine Spiked, and the Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I, International Business Times, and New European.

Title: Science and Religion
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of the Ian Ramsey Centre and Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Relgion at Oxford, Alister McGrath is a theologian, priest and intellectual historian.
Synopsis & Topics:
Are religion and science necessarily in conflict? What are the limits of a rational world view? Alister McGrath was once an atheist and is now an Anglican priest, physicist and intellectual historian whose books include Dawkins' God. Hear him delve into the debate around science, religion, and their changing relationship.

Director of the Ian Ramsey Centre and Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Relgion at Oxford, Alister McGrath is a theologian, priest and intellectual historian.

Title: The End of All Things
Guests & Speakers: John Dupré, Subir Sarkar, Nancy Cartwright
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, former mathematician turned philosopher of science Nancy Cartwright , and philosopher of science and author of The Disorder of Things John Dupré go in search of the stuff of the universe.
Synopsis & Topics:
We tend to think of physical, material things as the ultimate stuff of the universe. Yet contemporary physics has largely abandoned physical things in favour of energy and fields. And the late Mary Midgley argued that materialism was a profound mistake. Should we give up on our conviction that physical stuff is the bedrock of the world, or is such talk ivory tower nonsense?

Head of Particle Theory at Oxford Professor Subir Sarkar, former mathematician turned philosopher of science Nancy Cartwright, and philosopher of science and author of The Disorder of Things John Dupré go in search of the stuff of the universe.

Title: What's next for the Left?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Skills and author of The New Serfdom.
Synopsis & Topics: Many think British politics is more divided and more uncertain than ever before. What's next for the Left? Angela Eagle, Labour MP and author of The New Serfdom, puts forward her vision for the future.

Title: Where Women Rule
Guests & Speakers: Phillip Blond, Elif Sarican, Joanna Williams
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of the ResPublica think tank, Phillip Blond, author of Women vs. Feminism, Joanna Williams, and Kurdish women's activist Elif Sarican, consider the complexities and perils of power.
Synopsis & Topics:
The Patriarchy has become a powerful feminist watchword for the unequal division of power between men and women. In some fields, though, the tables have turned, with women a third more likely to go to university, three quarters of teachers being women, and the courts predominantly giving women custody of children. Should we be demanding equality for men in these areas? Or are there arenas where equality is a mistaken goal and women should have the upper hand?

Director of the ResPublica think tank, Phillip Blond, author of Women vs. Feminism, 
 Joanna Williams, and Kurdish women's activist Elif Sarican, consider the complexities and perils of power.

Title: How to Make the Right Decision
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Head of Philosophy at the London School of Economics, Jason McKenzie Alexander is an expert in evolutionary game theory and its application to the evolution of morality and social norms.
Synopsis & Topics:
Cognitive science has shown that all of us suffer from biases that distort our reality, impair our judgement and lead us to bad decisions. Hear author and head of philosophy at LSE, J. McKenzie Alexander guide a workshop session that talks through the findings of contemporary decision theory and what's really involved when we make a choice.

Head of Philosophy at the London School of Economics, Jason McKenzie Alexander is an expert in evolutionary game theory and its application to the evolution of morality and social norms.

Title: Mirror, Mirror
Guests & Speakers: Heather Peto, Julia Long, Miles Berry
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Plastic surgeon Miles Berry, radical feminist activist Julia Long and LGBT Labour Trans Officer Heather Peto consider apperance and identity.
Synopsis & Topics: We think being authentic is about remaining true to who we are, and many of us consider plastic surgery as a the preserve of tabloid celebritis rather than people like us. But from Caitlin Jenner to Chelsea Manning, plastic surgery is now seen as a means to ensure our bodies reflect authentic inner lives. Should we embrace cosmetic transformation as a way of becoming closer to who we really are, or who we might wish to become? Or should we be seeking to end society's obsession with appearance? Plastic Surgeon Miles Berry, radical feminist activist Julia Long and LGBT Labour Trans Officer Heather Peto consider apperance and identity.

Title: Liz Truss on Britain's Future
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Liz Truss is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the leader of the Conservative Party.
Synopsis & Topics: What will the United Kingdom look like in the future? Which issues should dominate British politics after Brexit? New UK Prime Minister Liz Truss makes predictions and puts forward her vision for the UK. Liz Truss was Secretary of State for International Trade and President of the Board of Trade. In 2016, Liz Truss became the first ever female Lord Chancellor. She has served as Conservative MP for South West Norfolk since 2010.

Title: The Dark and the Digital
Guests & Speakers: Ella Whelan, Janne Teller, Nigel Inkster, Yasmin Alibhai-Brown
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning journalist and commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown debates with Nigel Inkster, former Director of Operations and Intelligence at MI6, Ella Whelan, political commentator and co-convenor of the Battle of Ideas festival, and author and former UN macroeconomist Janne Teller.
Synopsis & Topics:
Most of us like to think that people are good, yet the anonymity of the internet has enabled an epidemic of abuse. Do we need the oversight of others to behave well? Was Hobbes right that humankind is at its core wicked and in need of constraint? Perhaps internet surveillance could create a better world, but is there an alternative where our essential goodness would flourish without us needing to be watched? 

Award-winning journalist and commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown debates with Nigel Inkster, former Director of Operations and Intelligence at MI6, Ella Whelan, political commentator and assistant editor at Spiked, and author and former UN macroeconomist Janne Teller.

Title: The Mathematics of Thought
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Minerva Fellow at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy, Silvia Jonas is in the Fast Track Program for outstanding female scientists by the Robert Bosch Foundation.
Synopsis & Topics:
What does mathematics have to do with the nature of human thought? How does it change how philosophers think of reality? Philosopher and author of 'Ineffability and its Metaphysics', Silvia Jonas explains how mathematics has come to shape our politics, ethics and our very idea of what the world is.

Minerva Fellow at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy, Silvia Jonas is in the Fast Track Program for outstanding female scientists by the Robert Bosch Foundation.

Title: The reality illusion
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Donald Hoffman, Maria Baghramian
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cognitive psychologist and author Donald Hoffman, professor of philosophy and expert on metaphysical relativism Maria Baghramian, and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson embark on a radical rethink of reality.
Synopsis & Topics: "Seeing is believing". "Seeing is the truth". Yet cognitive scientists seem to have uncovered these views as incorrect. Evolution led us to perceive what is best for survival and it turns out this has little to do with what we call 'reality'. Is reality then a creative construct that helps us to live but doesn't reflect the world? Are physical objects a useful hallucination? Or is the very idea of reality perhaps a mistake, and neuroscientists have just got it wrong? Cognitive psychologist and author Donald Hoffman, professor of philosophy and expert on metaphysical relativism Maria Baghramian, and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson embark on a radical rethink of reality.

Title: How does Uncertainty affect Business?
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eminent economist and author of Capitalism 4.0 , Anatole Kaletsky charts the road.
Synopsis & Topics: How might the current political uncertainty be affecting the economy in ways we cannot yet see? Is capitalism - felt by many to be failing - going to make it through the next few decades? Eminent economist and author of Capitalism 4.0, Anatole Kaletsky charts the road.

Title: The New Politics
Guests & Speakers: Vince Cable, Liz Truss, Richard Burgon
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cabinet Minister and Chief Secretary to the Treasury Liz Truss, Labour MP for Leeds East Richard Burgon, and former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable contest the importance of growth and seek plausible alternative goals.
Synopsis & Topics: "It's the economy, stupid" has been the political truth for decades. But the vote for Brexit and wide support for Corbyn suggest that many would sacrifice growth for social change. Has the economy become less important to us? Are we turning to broader, more socially radical political goals? Or is the weakness of the economy since 2008 the very reason for the shift away from the centre ground? Cabinet Minister and Chief Secretary to the Treasury Liz Truss, Labour MP for Leeds East Richard Burgon and former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable contest the importance of growth and seek plausible alternative goals.

Title: The Next Universe | Roger Penrose
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Sir Roger Penrose is an English mathematical physicist, mathematician and philosopher of science
Synopsis & Topics: What came before the Big Bang? What happens when our universe ends? Eminent theoretical physicist and Hawking collaborator, Roger Penrose, has a radical theory which proposes that another universe will follow our own.

Title: Tribal Identity and Tribal Conflict
Guests & Speakers: David Blunkett, Dawn Butler, Phillip Blond
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Political philosopher Phillip Blond, Labour MP Dawn Butler, and former Home Secretary David Blunkett seek answers to issues of identity and belonging in an increasingly divided society.
Synopsis & Topics: Identity politics has become ever more influential. While the left champions identities based on sexuality or race, the right reasserts the nation. Does our desire to belong to one tribe or another make conflict with others inevitable? Could we do away with tribal allegiances and see ourselves as part of the same human family? Or are group identities based on class, race, sexuality or nationality the only effective vehicles for political change?

Title: Clear Bright Future
Synopsis & Topics: How do we preserve what makes us human in this age of uncertainty? Broadcaster and author of Post-Capitalism Paul Mason covers markets, alogrithms, neuroscience and protest to put forward his new case for optimism, and how we can all be much more than cogs in a machine.

Title: Universes and fairy tales
Guests & Speakers: John Ellis, Mary-Jane Rubenstein, Cumrun Vafa
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Harvard String Theorist Cumrun Vafa, CERN physicist John Ellis, and author of Worlds Without End Mary-Jane Rubenstein dispute the possibility of universes outside of our own.
Synopsis & Topics: Should we recognise ours as the only universe and give up on others as fantasy science? Or is slipping through a worm hole into another universe a credible reality rather than a Hollywood fairytale? Harvard String Theorist Cumrun Vafa, CERN physicist John Ellis and author of Worlds Without End Mary-Jane Rubenstein dispute the possibility of universes outside of our own.

Title: On language and logic
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Saul Kripke has been described by many as the world's most influential living analytic philosopher and in the top 10 of the last 200 years. Timothy Williamson is the Wykeham Professor of logic at Oxford University - an institution that has played a major role in the development of the analytic tradition in the last century.
Synopsis & Topics: Saul Kripke and Timothy Williamson discuss why language has come to dominate their field, why logic matters, and the future of Anglo-American philosophy.

Title: A New Socialism
Guests & Speakers: Angela Eagle, David Aaronovitch, Jon Lansman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jon Lansman is founder of the 40,000-strong pro-Corbyn pressure group Momentum. Angela Eagle is a British Labour Party politician who has served as Minister of State for Pensions and Ageing Society and Shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury. David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and broadcaster. He writes a regular column for The Times which he has called "my war against stupidity".
Synopsis & Topics: What does Stalinism have in common with 21st century democratic socialism? Are modern forms of socialism merely adapted versions of capitalism? How can the ideals of communism, socialism and Marxism be used in politics today to create a fairer society? Jon Lansman, founder of momentum debates with Labour party politician Angela Eagle and journalist David Aaronovitch.

Title: Taking Humour Seriously
Synopsis & Topics: Is humour an essential form of subversion or a distraction from real dissent? Eminent literary critic and author of Humour, Terry Eagleton explores psyche and society to shed light on wit, irony and laughter.

Title: Decolonising Philosophy
Guests & Speakers: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, Nivi Manchanda, Timothy Williamson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Timothy Williamson is Wykeham Professor of Logic at the University of Oxford and world renowned philosopher of language and logic. Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy, a Fellow of the British Academy, and an expert in the history of Indian philosophy. Nivi Manchanda is a lecturer at the School of Politics and International Relations at Queen Mary University.
Synopsis & Topics: Many see the search for universal truths about the world as the noble aim of philosophy. Yet our universities largely dismiss non-Western philosophy, and critics argue that British students are taught a narrow analytic approach. Are great ideas independent of time, place and tradition? Do African conceptions of the self or Chinese Mohist logic offer equally valid insights? Do we need to wake up to Western prejudice, or is there only one right way to think?

Title: The Arc of Life: David Blunkett
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: David Blunkett : Former Home Secretary, David Blunkett was one of the most respected members of Tony Blair's cabinet. On top of the Home Secretary position, Blunkett also served as Education and Employment Secretary and Work and Pensions Secretary. In 2015, he was awarded a peerage and became Baron Blunkett.
Synopsis & Topics: David Blunkett: Former Home Secretary, David Blunkett was one of the most respected members of Tony Blair's cabinet. On top of the Home Secretary position, Blunkett also served as Education and Employment Secretary and Work and Pensions Secretary. In 2015, he was awarded a peerage and became Baron Blunkett.

Title: The Will of the People
Guests & Speakers: Anna Soubry, Jon Lansman, Michael Howard
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Jon Lansman is founder of the 40,000-strong pro-Corbyn pressure group Momentum . Lansman debates with former Conservative Party Leader and Brexiteer, Michael Howard, who supports the Eurosceptic pressure group, Leave Means Leave . Joining them is Anna Soubry, MP for Broxtowe and a member of the Independent Group . Having threatened repeatedly to leave the Conservative Party on account of its leadership's Brexit stance, Soubry defected to the newly-formed group in February 2019.
Synopsis & Topics: From Corbyn to Trump, populism has rejected established political elites. Some think a return to ideology and emotion is a dangerous backward step, others that this means the alternatives have failed. Is populism on both the left and the right something to be celebrated or feared? Can giving more power to the people bring about positive, lasting change? Or is the only safe way to make progress to give it all to those that know best?

Title: How To Spot Pseudoscience
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Professor of Philosophy at CUNY and founder of Rationally Speaking , Massimo Pigliucci's latest book is Answers for Aristotle . His recent work focuses on the boundaries between physics and metaphysics.
Synopsis & Topics: From climate change and evolution, why are beliefs that run counter to the scientific establishment so prolific? Philosopher of science and author of Nonsense on Stilts, Massimo Pigliucci looks at what causes people to hold these beliefs and how to separate the facts from fiction.

Title: What is the Power of Art?
Guests & Speakers: Colin MacCabe, Jennifer Scott, Paloma Strelitz
Synopsis & Topics: We think art opens minds . Yet from medieval cathedrals to today's oligarch collectors, art has always stuck close to wealth and power. Is art necessarily the plaything of the rich and privileged and, as John Berger argued, a means of cementing existing heirarchies? can we imagine a more diverse world where art is for all? Or are the rich the fallguys and art itself an empty bauble?

Title: The Great Economists
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Linda Yueh is an economist, broadcaster, and writer. She holds a number of positions, including Fellow in Economics at the University of Oxford and Adjunct Professor of Economics at London Business School, as well as presenting a number of programmes on the BBC.
Synopsis & Topics: Economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondant Professor Linda Yueh looks at the thinking of the great economists who changed the world and asks how their ideas can help us tackle issues such as Brexit, globalisatio and Trumpism as discussed in The Great Economists: How Their Ideas Can Help Us Today

Title: Has Brexit Broken British Politics?
Guests & Speakers: Anatole Kaletsky, Barry Gardiner, Leanne Wood, Mark Francois
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former leader of Plaid Cymru Leanne Wood debates with Shadow Secretary of State for International Trade and International Climate Change, Barry Gardiner, Conservative Party politician Mark Francois, and economist and writer, Anatole Kaletsky.
Synopsis & Topics: The European Elections have cast Britain into uncharted territory. And not just in a short term sense but in the longer term shift we are facing in our political and cultural environment. This debate focuses on how we navigate that uncertain future. Former leader of Plaid Cymru Leanne Wood debates with Shadow Secretary of State for International Trade and International Climate Change, Barry Gardiner, Conservative Party politician Mark Francois, and economist and writer, Anatole Kaletsky.

Title: Money For Nothing
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In a combative head-to-head debate, author of Basic Income: And How We Can Make it Happen Guy Standing goes head to head with leading libertarian economist Deidre McCloskey.
Synopsis & Topics: Once dismissed as a utopian fantasy, universal income has now hit the mainstream as a way to tackle inequality. With new technologies, support from across the political spectrum, it's no surprise people have begun to take the idea seriously. In a combative head-to-head debate, author of Basic Income: And How We Can Make it Happen Guy Standing goes head to head with leading libertarian economist Deidre McCloskey.

Title: Good and evil around the globe
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Cambridge anthropologist Joel Robbins tours the globe in search of the good.
Synopsis & Topics: From remote groups in Papua New Guinea to Pentecostal Christians, what can values and desires around the world tell us about the nature of morality? Is morality relative? Cambridge anthropologist Joel Robbins tours the globe in search of the good.

Title: Minds, Matter and Mechanisms
Guests & Speakers: Markus Gabriel, Raymond Tallis, Susanna Martinez-Conde
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Author of Aping Mankind Raymond Tallis, German philosopher and author of I am Not a Brain Markus Gabriel, and neuroscientist and author of Champions of Illusion Susana Martinez Conde seek answers to the mystery of consciousness.
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscientists believe that our minds and conciousness are no more than matter and mechanism. But if they are right, is all meaning, purpose and feeling illusory? Must we accept that we are just machines? Or do the secrets of experience require an alternative account of who we are? Author of Aping Mankind Raymond Tallis, German philosopher and author of I am Not a Brain Markus Gabriel and neuroscientist Susana Martinez Conde seek answers to the mystery of consciousness.

Title: The Mystery of the Good
Guests & Speakers: Paul Boghossian, Naomi Goulder, Michael Ruse
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this online debate, Fear of Knowledge author Paul Boghossian, philosopher of action Naomi Goulder and Philosophy after Darwin author Michael Ruse put good on trial.
Synopsis & Topics: What is good for one is not good for another – the suicide bomber and the pacifist have very different notions of the good. Does this mean that there is no ultimate meaning to good and evil? Is good only found in the practical outcome of one's actions? Fear of Knowledge Author Paul Boghossian, philosopher of action Naomi Goulder and Philosophy after Darwin author Michael Ruse put good on trial.

Title: Beyond Quantum
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: t'Hooft is the author of Time in Powers of Ten and In Search of the Ultimate Building Blocks.
Synopsis & Topics: Nobel Prize-winner Gerard 't Hooft examines Quantum Theory and its claims that reality is fundamentally uncertain and unknowable.

Title: Something and nothing
Guests & Speakers: Rupert Sheldrake, George Ellis, Amie Thomasson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Templeton Prize winning cosmologist George Ellis, metaphysician Amie Thomasson and author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake get to the bottom of nothingness.
Synopsis & Topics: The fundamental problem of philosophy, argued Heidegger, is 'why is there something rather than nothing?' Some scientists claim nothing doesn't exist and even the deepest space is full of virtual particles. Have we misunderstood the very idea of nothing? Is this little more than a logical mistake? Templeton prize winning cosmologist George Ellis, metaphysician Amie Thomasson and author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake get to the bottom of nothingness.

Title: Equal Is Unfair
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Director of the Ayn Rand Institute Yaron Brook explores the dark side of equality.
Synopsis & Topics: Equality is a goal most of us now share. But what if fighting against income inequality is misguided and dangerous? Director of the Ayn Rand Institute Yaron Brook explores the dark side of equality.

Title: After Post-Truth
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Rebecca Goldstein, Homi Bhabha
Synopsis & Topics: In a post-truth world, tribal agreement seems to have replaced reason and evidence. But is a world where our truths are tribal sustainable? Don't we need a shared framework of thought to prevent fragmentation and confrontation? Can we rely on evidence and reason whilst abandoning absolute truth, or do we need reality after all? Philosopher and novelist Rebecca Goldstein, post-colonial theorist Homi Bhabha and post-postmodern metaphysician Hilary Lawson confront the future of the post-truth world.

Title: Beyond Men and Women
Guests & Speakers: Angela Eagle, Finn Mackay, Patricia MacCormack
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this debate, radical feminist author Finn Mackay, Labour MP Angela Eagle and Professor of Continental Philosophy Patricia MacCormack examine the potential and pitfalls of a genderless world.
Synopsis & Topics: From Facebook's customisable gender option to popstars in drag, the traditional categories of male and female are now being challenged in the mainstream. Would a genderless world eradicate inequality or instead embed stereotypes? Should we keep gender and fight prejudice, or would a world beyond gender be both fair and free? In this debate, radical feminist author Finn Mackay, Labour MP Angela Eagle and Professor of Continental Philosophy Patricia MacCormack examine the potential and pitfalls of a genderless world.

Title: Revolution in Rojava
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Activist for the Kurdish women's movement, Sarican is the UK coordinator of the Kurdistan Students' Union.
Synopsis & Topics: In the shadow of ISIS, the community of Rojava is a flourishing experiment in direct democracy, gender equality and concerns about the environment. Now it's under attack. Back from Syria, Kurdish rights activist Elif Sarican tells this hopeful story. Activist for the Kurdish women's movement, Sarican is the UK coordinator of the Kurdistan Students' Union.

Title: Morality of the Tribe
Guests & Speakers: Peter Tatchell, David Miller, Natalie Cargill
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this debate, barrister and founder of Effective Giving UK Natalie Cargill, Oxford Political Theorist and author of 'On Nationality' David Miller and human rights activist Peter Tatchell examine the tribal nature of morality.
Synopsis & Topics: We think everyone should be treated equally. Yet we also think we are right to care most about our family, our friends and our lovers, and 82% of charitable donations in the UK are given to the causes closest to home. Should we embrace this, or go down Peter Singer and Effective Altruism's movement route? In this debate, barrister and founder of Effective Giving UK Natalie Cargill, Oxford political theorist and author of 'On Nationality' David Miller and human rights activist Peter Tatchell examine the tribal nature of morality.

Title: War and Peace
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mark Leonard, the director of the European Council on Foreign Relations, and British politician and broadcaster George Galloway take Trump to task.
Synopsis & Topics: Many think Trump a buffoon and a threat to world peace. But with IS weakened, and signs of progress in North Korea, perhaps his supporters can point to some initial successes. Could a belligerent approach to foreign policy make for a safer world? In this debate, founder of the European Council on Foreign Relations Mark Leonard and British politician and broadcaster George Galloway take Trump to task.

Title: Limits of language
Guests & Speakers: Stanley Fish, Hilary Lawson, Genia Schönbaumsfeld
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Eminent literary critic Stanley Fish, Wittgenstein expert Genia Schönbaumsfeld and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson scrutinise the limits of language.
Synopsis & Topics: We think that everything can be talked about. Yet, from metaphors to the mystical, there are many things we seem unable to directly express. Are the most important things in life beyond language? Or can we find the right words for everything? Eminent literary critic Stanley Fish, Wittgenstein expert Genia Schönbaumsfeld and post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson scrutinise the limits of language.

Title: Poisonous Speech
Synopsis & Topics: Historic hate speech was described as a "poison" at the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg. Then, they were talking about Nazi propaganda against Jewish people. Has hate speech become a poison again? Or does today's political and social context require total free speech? Cambridge Philosopher Rae Langton examines the offence and the harm of hate speech.

Title: Life, Beauty and Being
Guests & Speakers: Sam Roddick, Bence Nanay, Justine Kolata
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Founder of Coco de Mer Sam Roddick, philosopher and film critic Bence Nanay ad director of The Public Sphere Justine Kolata ask whether paintings have higher value than Kim Kardashian's bum.
Synopsis & Topics: Once beauty was about goodness and truth, now we think it means little more than models, products and outdated art. Have practical concerns and the economy of desire made aesthetics trivial and expendable? Is the goal of living beautifully a conceit of the privileged elite? In this talk, founder of Coco de Mer Sam Roddick, philosopher Bence Nanay and director of The Public Sphere Justine Kolata ask whether traditional art has higher value than Kim Kardashian's bum.

Title: Your Life in the Balance
Guests & Speakers: David Healy, Jacob Stegenga, Pallavi Bradshaw
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this debate, Pharmageddon author David Healy, Cambridge philosopher and author of Medical Nihilism Jacob Stegenga and Policy lead at the Medical Protection Society Pallavi Bradshaw rethink medical authority.
Synopsis & Topics: Clinical errors in the UK are responsible for six times as many deaths as road accidents. Is doctors' power dangerous and should we look elsewhere, perhaps to AI technology, to regain control? In this debate, Pharmageddon author David Healy, Cambridge philosopher and author of Medical Nihilism Jacob Stegenga and Policy lead at the Medical Protection Society Pallavi Bradshaw rethink medical authority.

Title: The Struggle for Social Justice
Synopsis & Topics: Britain is one of the wealthiest nations in the world, so why do so many feel short-changed? Labour MP and former minister Angela Eagle sees an urgent need to protect social cohesion and makes a case for radical economic reform, to trump inequality and create a fairer society.

Title: The Key to Creativity
