Synopsis & Topics: Quantum theorists claim their science reveals the existence of many worlds. Philosopher of physics James Ladyman on the multiverse theory

Title: Europe After the Reign
Guests & Speakers: Charles Saumarez Smith, Godfrey Barker, Theodore Dalrymple
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Royal Academy chief exec Charles Saumarez Smith, art critic and commentator Godfrey Barker, and Standpoint commentator Theodore Dalrymple debate the future of European culture.
Synopsis & Topics: All the signs are that Europe's economic dominance is over, as Asia continues its rise. Will Europe's global cultural influence decline as a consequence?

Title: The mind's eye
Guests & Speakers: David Malone, Nicholas Humphrey, Galen Strawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Philosopher Galen Strawson, evolutionary psychologist Nicholas Humphrey and award-winning documentary-maker David Malone investigate the all-seeing I.
Synopsis & Topics: Galen Strawson, Nicholas Humphrey, David Malone debate: For scientists and philosophers the idea of the soul has been out of fashion for 200 years. But can science explain consciousness without it? Or the experience of life?

Title: The Schlock of the New
Synopsis & Topics: Stephen Bayley tells the untold story of the truth about modern art: how giant art corporations became strangely vulnerable to the future

Title: Nature's Hidden Persuaders
Synopsis & Topics: Nicholas Humphrey examines studies on one of medicine's most mysterious phenomena, the placebo effect's role in psychology and human body

Title: Hawking vs philosophy
Guests & Speakers: Steve Fuller, Jonathan Derbyshire, Lewis Wolpert
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Provocative biologist and author Lewis Wolpert, postmodern sociologist of science Steve Fuller and New Statesman Culture editor Jonathan Derbyshire investigate the limits of science and philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Is philosophy dead? Was Stephen Hawking right? Biologist Lewis Wolpert, philosopher Steve Fuller and journalist Jonathan Derbyshire investigate the limits of science and philosophy.Derbyshire investigate the limits of science and philosophy.

Title: Empire Strikes Back
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Phillip Blond, Zoe Williams, David Marquand
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Times columnist David Aaronovitch, Oxford political theorist and former Labour politician David Marquand, Guardian columnist Zoe Williams and ResPublica director Phillip Blond question the new world order
Synopsis & Topics: Momentous decisions are increasingly driven not by national governments but by supranational and regional alliances. Is it the end of governments and nation-states?

Title: Economic Democracy
Synopsis & Topics: Peter Tatchell outlines his vision for a fair, successful and accountable economy: the theory and practice of economic democracy & democratic capitalism

Title: Our Hopeless Future & Other Comedy
Synopsis & Topics: Our Hopeless Future & Other Comedy is a talk by novelist and comics icon Warren Ellis on dystopian America, the space age and the power of Twitter

Title: On Humans and Animals
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Live from Melbourne, Australian philosopher, Princeton professor and author of Animal Liberation , Peter Singer joins the "UK's foremost scourge of scientific pretention" ( Guardian ) Mary Midgley to consider the future of bioethics. Roger Bolton makes sure the tough questions get answered.
Synopsis & Topics: Philosophers Peter Singer & Mary Midgley debate the future of bioethics in the light of human and animal rights & our attitudes to other forms of life

Title: The Theory of Everything
Guests & Speakers: John Ellis, Nicholas Maxwell, Frank Close
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: CERN theoretical physicist and coiner of the term "theory of everything", John Ellis, best-selling Oxford physicist Frank Close, and philosopher of science Nicholas Maxwell investigate the limits of knowledge.
Synopsis & Topics: Physicists John Ellis & Frank Close on the limits of knowledge, the quantum theory and the grand final theory of everything, unifying matter and the universe

Title: States of Play
Guests & Speakers: Harry Eyres, Chris Bateman, Don Paterson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning poet Don Paterson, Financial Times columnist Harry Eyres, and author and game designer and philosopher Chris Bateman find themselves at play with play.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning poet Don Paterson, FT columnist Harry Eyres, and author and game designer and philosopher Chris Bateman find themselves at play with play.

Title: Psychiatry and the Meaning of Pain
Synopsis & Topics: Mark Salter defends the value of sadness & depression – against the medicalisation of emotions - in this talk about psychiatry and the meaning of pain

Title: Meat, Metal, Code
Synopsis & Topics: Famed for pushing the boundaries of performance art and biotechnology, Stelarc previews startling new scientific developments set to transform our relationships to our bodies and our selves.

Title: Why Marx was right
Synopsis & Topics: Philosopher and critic Terry Eagleton makes the case for Marx's resurrection, challenging the standard critiques and explaining why the German philosopher's thought remains as relevant as ever.

Title: Myths for Modernity
Guests & Speakers: Justina Robson, Nicholas Royle, Jim Crace
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Whitbread award winning novelist Jim Crace, postmodern cultural theorist and writer Nicholas Royle, and science fiction author Justina Robson seek out new mythologies.
Synopsis & Topics: Novelist Jim Crace, cultural theorist Nicholas Royle and author Justina Robson examine the importance of reintroducing myths and mythologies in modern times

Title: Blinded by the Light
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Don Cupitt, Angie Hobbs, Simon Armitage
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In this debate, 'radical theologian’ Don Cupitt, leading poet Simon Armitage, and philosophers Angie Hobbs and Barry C. Smith examine the impact of metaphors of light & darkness on knowledge, truth and reality in philosophy.
Synopsis & Topics: Don Cupitt, Simon Armitage and philosophers Angie Hobbs & Barry Smith examine the role of metaphors of light & darkness on reality, knowledge and truth

Title: Enhancing Morality
Synopsis & Topics: Technology will soon have the power to forcibly 'improve' our moral behaviour. Bioethicists Julian Savulescu and John Harris consider what this means for the future of mankind

Title: The agony and the ecstasy
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Christopher Hamilton, Raymond Tallis, Havi Carel
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Physician Raymond Tallis, philosophers Christopher Hamilton and Barry C. Smith, and metaphysician Havi Carel, who has a terminal illness, question the purpose of pain.
Synopsis & Topics: We take it for granted that eradicating pain is desirable. But is it possible, and do we want, to eliminate agony or ecstasy or is it necessary to human life?

Title: Touching Cyberspace
Synopsis & Topics: Cyberspace is a world without laws or boundaries, and touch-screen technologies have made digital ideas tangible. Nick Harkaway asks where the physicalisation of the net is taking us.

Title: The Fantasy of Technology
Guests & Speakers: Kevin Warwick, Angela Saini, Luciano Floridi, Eva Aldea
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Leading cybernetics expert Kevin Warwick, cultural theorist Eva Aldea, science journalist Angela Saini, and philosopher of information Luciano Floridi take technology to task.
Synopsis & Topics: The fantasy of technology questions whether technological innovation viewed as a driver of progress or salvation isn’t clouding more meaningful human goals

Title: James Lovelock: Creativity in Science & Gaia Theory
Synopsis & Topics: James Lovelock on the origins of the Gaia Theory, being a lone scientist and creativity in science. With diplomat and environmentalist Crispin Tickell

Title: Reason and The Decline of Violence
Guests & Speakers: Andrew Copson, Steven Pinker, Roger Bolton, Judith Marquand
Synopsis & Topics: Steven Pinker's Theory Explored. Steven Pinker makes the case for the historical decline of violence. Roger Bolton, Andrew Copson and Judith Marquand cross-examine.

Title: Venus In Furs
Guests & Speakers: Minette Marrin, Rowan Pelling, Andrea Beckmann
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: In Venus in Furs, former editrice of the Erotic Review, Rowan Pelling, Sunday Times columnist Minette Marrin, and German psychosexual social theorist Andrea Beckmann consider the relationship between desire, violence and restraint.
Synopsis & Topics: Venus in Furs is a debate on sadomasochism, BDSM & the limits of sexuality. The role of the Internet in giving desire a new twist, with new ideas & examples

Title: The Eureka Moment
Guests & Speakers: Rupert Sheldrake, David Berman, James Wilk
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Independent scientist Rupert Sheldrake, theoretical physicist David Berman and Oxford philosopher James Wilk question the role of freedom in science.
Synopsis & Topics: Scientific advance is a roll call of eureka moments. Does the institutional character of big science research militate against these critical imaginative leaps?

Title: The Best of Times?
Guests & Speakers: Edward Mortimer, Meghnad Desai, Stephen D. King
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: HSBC Chief Economist Stephen D. King, diplomat and former FT columnist Edward Mortimer, and LSE economist and Labour peer Meghnad Desai explore the impact of the rise of the East.
Synopsis & Topics: The Best of Times: The Rise of India, modern China & the future of the West questions the impact of rampant consumerism and infinite economic growth

Title: Neuroscience and the Mystery of Music
Synopsis & Topics: Can neuroscience uncover the purpose of art or the philosophy of music? Raymond Tallis explains why our love for music remains beyond science's grasp

Title: Diane Abbott: Beyond Downton Abbey
Synopsis & Topics: Diane Abbott responds to Downton Abbey, presenting a less saccharine, refreshingly outspoken view of British history.

Title: Time's arrow
Guests & Speakers: Raymond Tallis, Angie Hobbs, Jim Al-Khalili, Craig Bourne
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Physician, poet and thinker Raymond Tallis, philosopher and broadcaster Angie Hobbs, theoretical physicist Jim Al-Khalili, and philosopher of time Craig Bourne go in search of time's direction.
Synopsis & Topics: What is time? A dimension, a place, a social construct, or something more mysterious? Philosophy meets physics to debate the reality & nature of time

Title: Pythagoras' Dream
Guests & Speakers: Peter Hacker, Hilary Lawson, Lee Smolin
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Theoretical physicist Lee Smolin live from Toronto, Oxford philosopher Peter Hacker and metaphysician Hilary Lawson dismantle the foundations of reality.
Synopsis & Topics: Pythagoras thought the key to universe was Mathematics. But even scientific realism questions the place of maths as the ultimate character of the world

Title: The Ultimate Map of Reality
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Giles Fraser, Adrian Moore, James Ladyman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: " Kantian or Lockean, it makes no difference! " - In this video, Nietzschean priest Giles Fraser puts himself in the firing line of three ardent metaphysicians. Post postmodernist Hilary Lawson and philosopher of physics James Ladyman clash over how to make sense of multiple realities, as Oxford philosopher Adrian Moore reveals: even this is metaphysics....
Synopsis & Topics: 20th Century thought and science seemed to render metaphysics obsolete, but could a revival be on the agenda? Should such talk be left to priests and mystics?

Title: After Capitalism
Guests & Speakers: Giles Fraser, Ben Harris-Quinney, Meghnad Desai
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: LSE economist Meghnad Desai, former St. Paul's Canon Chancellor and Oxford philosopher Giles Fraser, and Bow Group chairman Ben Harris-Quinney imagine the world's future.
Synopsis & Topics: Is capitalism the only viable economic system, or can we imagine a post-capitalist society? Debating a future based not on equality, but fairness.

Title: The Fifth Crime
Synopsis & Topics: Should ecocide – man-made environmental destruction - sit alongside genocide as a crime against humanity? Radical ecologist Polly Higgins makes a powerful case

Title: The Physical and Psychological Differences Between Men and Women
Synopsis & Topics:
Are the differences between men and women biological, psychological, or simply illusions?

Professor Lewis Wolpert, the renowned developmental biologist, looks for facts and scientific evidence underlying a controversial view of male and female biology and psychological and physical differences between men and women.

Author of Six Impossible Things and Malignant Sadness and Vice President of the British Humanist Association, Wolpert is known for his staunch defence of science and rational thought.

'Brilliant and persuasive' - Sunday Times

Title: The World in Our Hands
Guests & Speakers: Bjorn Lomborg, Nigel Lawson, Polly Higgins, Crispin Tickell
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Radical lawyer Polly Higgins and diplomat Crispin Tickell debate the rationality of climate change with former Chancellor Nigel Lawson and Bjørn Lomborg, one of Time ’s 100 Most Influential People.
Synopsis & Topics: Radical lawyer Polly Higgins and diplomat Crispin Tickell debate the rationality of climate change with former Chancellor Nigel Lawson and Bjørn Lomborg, one of Time’s 100 Most Influential People.

Title: The End of Ideals?
Guests & Speakers: David Aaronovitch, Nigel Lawson, David Blunkett, Jill Kirby
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Ritula Shah invites award-winning Times columnist and author David Aaronovitch to debate the role of ideals with Jill Kirby and former cabinet ministers David Blunkett and Nigel Lawson.
Synopsis & Topics: What is ideology now? Are we right to have become sceptical or would it be better to find new ideals to kindle our imagination and change our world?

Title: Uncharted Territory
Guests & Speakers: Ziauddin Sardar, Giles Fraser, Hilary Rose, Bjorn Lomborg
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Faced with Lomborg’s praise of our traditional, economic progress, Rose raises concern for the poverty and inequality still that continues. Amid her distinctions between types of progress, Fraser subverts the idea of aspiring for growth altogether, and Zardar envisages controversial new notions of progress needed in an era where world powers are shifting…
Synopsis & Topics: Is growth sustainable? Bjorn Lomborg, Hilary Rose, Giles Fraser, and Ziauddin Sardar debate the sustainability of economic growth.

Title: Cyborg Future
Synopsis & Topics: Microprocessors in the human brain. Nano-robots in your bloodstream. Real-life cyborg and scholar Kevin Warwick offers a glimpse into our cyborg future

Title: After Postmodernity
Synopsis & Topics: Ziauddin Sardar looks for answers in an uncertain world.

Title: My Avatar, Myself
Synopsis & Topics: When we extend ourselves into the virtual where do we, ourselves, end? With endless new capacities to animate our intentions beyond the body, leading anthropologist Henrietta Moore proposes this is far more than projection.

Title: The Ultimate Particle
Synopsis & Topics: CERN Director-General Rolf Heuer, post-postmodern thinker Hilary Lawson and writer Gwyneth Jones go in search of the ultimate particle.

Title: Taking Over the Asylum
Synopsis & Topics: BBC Night Waves presenter Rana Mitter keeps order as clinical psychologist and psychiatry critic Richard Bentall, Baroness Molly Meacher and controversial consultant psychiatrist Mark Salter debate the extent of madness.

Title: When China Rules the World
Synopsis & Topics:
What will it be like to live in a China-shaped world? Author of the global best-seller ‘When China Rules The World’, Martin Jacques argues that it will be profoundly different.
‘A tour de force’ - Independent

Title: Alchemy, Anarchy and Science
Synopsis & Topics: TED fellow and polymath Rachel Armstrong, sociologist Steve Fuller, and neuroscientist Baroness Susan Greenfield question the limits of science.

Title: Generation Wars
Synopsis & Topics: Laurie Penny distinguishes between respect for a generational group and respect for political consensus. With Anthony O'Hear. Julian Baggini chairs.

Title: X-Rated
Synopsis & Topics: Filmmaker Ben Moore wonders how porn affects the women who watch it.

Title: Banksy and the Media Barons
Synopsis & Topics: Controversial art historian and photographer Julian Stallabrass examines the trajectory of a new generation of artists from the margins of the system to art world's new favourites.

Title: The Killing Fields
Synopsis & Topics: Photojournalist Benjamin Dix recounts his experience of working as the liaison between the United Nations and the Tamil Tigers during the forgotten war of Sri Lanka.

Title: The Naked Truth
Synopsis & Topics: Can the sexually explicit have an artistic value? Is lust an acceptable material for artists? Eminent Leonardo Da Vinci scholar Martin Kemp and art historian Hans Maes discuss whether art and porn can coexist.

Title: Abstract Graffiti
Synopsis & Topics: Artist Cedar Lewisohn provides a vibrant account of the outer limits of street art and new graffiti ideas explored in London, Prague, Philadelphia and São Paulo

Title: The Limits of Art
Synopsis & Topics: Poet Raymond Tallis and art critic Julian Spalding are ready to unveil their new theory of art, the nature of artistic freedom & the dangers of the status quo

Title: Dancing with the Devil
Guests & Speakers: Matthew Stone, Raymond Tallis, Jake Chapman
Synopsis & Topics: Writers and artists have often treated the ethics of their time with contempt. Should art encourage an ethical framework or is morality a threat to creativity?

Title: American Surreal
Synopsis & Topics: Pursuing the art of the fantastic, Susan Hiller looks back on the philosophy that has driven her 40 year career at the forefront of contemporary art

Title: Nicolas Roeg
Synopsis & Topics: From his early involvement in Lawrence of Arabia to directing Performance and The Man who Fell to Earth, Nicholas Roeg became known for films that evaded traditional narrative and which have had a lasting impact on cinema. Roeg makes the case for a cinema defined by risks, accidents and misadventures.

Title: Becoming Human
Synopsis & Topics: In “Becoming Human”, Bracha Ettinger discusses the power of art to change who we are, the role of critical theory & creative practice with Griselda Pollock

Title: Awake in the Universe
Guests & Speakers: Bracha Ettinger, Joanna Kavenna, Julian Stallabrass
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Controversial art historian Julian Stallabrass, painter and psychoanalst Bracha Ettinger, and writer Joanna Kavenna debate how art and creativity make us alive.
Synopsis & Topics: Our 2011 opening debate addresses the festival’s theme ‘Awake in the Universe’ head on. What gives art the ability to raise us from emotional and intellectual slumbers and where is its edge currently to be found? Controversial art historian Julian Stallabrass, painter and psychoanalst Bracha Ettinger, and fresh from her retrospective at the Tate earlier this year, artist Susan Hiller debate how art and creativity make us alive.

Title: How To Change The World
Synopsis & Topics: Culture&Society;Politics & Economics;Philosophy;Richard Layard;Mark Williamson;HowTheLightGetsIn 2011;HowTheLightGetsIn;

Title: Towards A New Humanity
Synopsis & Topics:
Author and theorist Leela Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi's great-granddaughter, presents her postcolonial perspective on the future of political and intellectual change.

‘Outstanding’ - Dipesh Chakrabarti

Title: An Age of Transparency
Guests & Speakers: Annie Machon, Douglas Murray, Nigel Warburton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Former MI6 agent and whistleblower Annie Machon, neo-conservative commentator Douglas Murray, and Prospect journalist and philosopher Nigel Warburton question the limits of free speech.
Synopsis & Topics:
Julian Assange’s pursuit of transparency has left the world shaken. Does WikiLeaks represent democracy at its most pure or an assault on a legitimate need for governmental secrecy? Can there be limits to how far truth should be disseminated, or must we come to accept our new, radical freedoms?

Former MI6 agent and whistleblower Annie Machon, neo-conservative commentator Douglas Murray, and Prospect journalist and philosopher Nigel Warburton question the limits of free speech.

Title: The Great Escape
Guests & Speakers: Frank Furedi, Gwyneth Jones, Philip Pullman
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning novelists Gwyneth Jones and Philip Pullman and sociologist and philosopher Frank Furedi join Andrew Copson for a journey beyond reality. In association with the British Humanist Association.
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning novelists Gwyneth Jones and Philip Pullman and sociologist and philosopher Frank Furedi join Andrew Copson for a journey beyond reality.

Title: Neuro-Everything?
Synopsis & Topics: Are we on the verge of unlocking the secrets of the human brain? Colin Blakemore reveals neuroscience's profound new insights into human behaviour

Title: Writing the End Times
Synopsis & Topics:
Lars Iyer talks about his philosophical black comedy Spurious. 'It is near to the end of days, shortly before the appearance of a "stupid messiah." Two British men, somehow employed in academia, muse on their lack of success and incapacity for real thought while drinking too much gin...'

'A marvel' - Guardian

Title: Once Upon a Time the End
Guests & Speakers: Jesse Norman, Kabir Chibber, Lars Iyer
Synopsis & Topics:
From rolling news to Twitter, attention spans are shrinking, and substantive messages are sharpening into slogans. Will postmodernity see a distillation of literary meaning into fewer (better?) words, or will our ability to tell big, expansive stories be destroyed by glib brevity, leaving us at the mercy of blurbs, stings, tweets and zingers.

Politician and philosopher Jesse Norman talks fast and loose with philosopher-blogger Lars Iyer and PORT editor and New York Times writer Kabir Chibber.

Title: The Devil's Parties
Guests & Speakers: Lauren Booth, Rowan Pelling, Peter Hitchens
Synopsis & Topics:
The immediate pursuit of pleasure permeates our culture. If it provides the rush, we will sniff it, swallow it, spend it, and soak in euphoria. Could we be making a mistake? Is there more pleasure to be gained from constraint and restraint? Or should we be distancing ourselves from hedonism altogether?

Daily Mail columnist Peter Hitchens, journalist Lauren Booth, and writer and former "editrix" of the Erotic Review, Rowan Pelling, threaten to be good.

Title: Drug Culture
Guests & Speakers: Iain Edgar, Susan Blackmore, Edward Skidelsky, Peter Hitchens
Synopsis & Topics:
Whilst many eastern cultures, and our own predecessors, naturalised mind-altering drugs, the modern world has rejected and criminalized these very substances. Why? Is the state right to protect us from physical and psychological danger, or is the freedom of the individual paramount? Do drugs encourage us to accept pluralistic realities and thus undermine our security in the world, or simply open the imagination? Are we heading for a mass exodus from reality or opening up our eyes?

Psychologist Susan Blackmore, Daily Mail columnist Peter Hitchens, anthropologist Iain Edgar and philosopher Edward Skidelsky open the doors of perception.

Title: Global Futures
Guests & Speakers: Robert Skidelsky, Vince Cable, Will Hutton
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning historian Robert Skidelsky, 'Britain's most popular politician' ( Guardian ) Vince Cable and eminent economist Will Hutton examine the world's future.
Synopsis & Topics:
Two years on from one of the worst crises ever to hit the free market, what lies in store for the global economy? Are we steadfast on the road to recovery or does liberalism itself need to be rethought?

Award-winning historian Robert Skidelsky, 'Britain's most popular politician' (Guardian) Vince Cable and eminent economist Will Hutton examine the world's future.

Title: Vince Cable on the Financial Crisis
Synopsis & Topics: What can be done to get the economy back on track? Vince Cable presents the coalition’s vision for growth in a post-crunch era

Title: Plastic Fantasies and Disposable Gods
Guests & Speakers: Gerald Moore, Liz Jones, Sam Delaney
Synopsis & Topics: Celebrities are the gods of contemporary culture. Is this a consequence of a lack of genuine heroes and ideals, a harmless attachment to trivia, or a sign of the emptiness of our lives? Do the promises of fame and glamour make ordinary life more tolerable, or delude us into wanting something not worth having?

Title: Genes, Memes and Temes
Synopsis & Topics:
Are ideas, like the genes in our DNA, battling it out in a survival-of-the-fittest evolutionary race? Psychologist Susan Blackmore explores the science of ideas, and what it might mean if technology were able to replicate ideas, 'temes',  outside of human control.

'I am delighted to recommend her' - Richard Dawkins

Title: Childhood's End
Guests & Speakers: Frank Furedi, Gabriel Gbadamosi, Michael Hastings
Synopsis & Topics: Sociologist and author of Paranoid Parenting Frank Furedi on placing childhood at the centre of our lives. Have we made a fetish of it and is this good for them?

Title: The Sweetest Taboo
Guests & Speakers: Brett Kahr, Gerald Moore, Rowan Pelling
Synopsis & Topics:
We like to think we're a sexually liberated society. But are there still limits to sexual behaviour, or are there no taboos left to break? 200 years ago De Sade explored the limits of sexuality, have we learnt anything in the meantime?

Former Erotic Review 'editrice' Rowan Pelling, philosopher and critic Gerald Moore, and psychoanalyst Gerald Moore explore what sex is like at the edge.

Title: My Journey
Synopsis & Topics:
Journalist and broadcaster Lauren Booth reveals the choices that led her from a hedonistic libertarian lifestyle to her new life as a Muslim.

'Enlightening and provocative' - Mail on Sunday

Title: Freedom in Chains
Synopsis & Topics:
In the absence of clarity about the values that define society, leading sociologist Frank Furedi argues that political and cultural elites have built a network of procedures and codes in an attempt to eradicate risk. An outcome that has damaging consequences for our moral independence.

‘Thought-provoking’ - Times

Title: Buddhists in Suburbia
Guests & Speakers: Gay Watson, Jampa Thaye, Mark Vernon
Synopsis & Topics:
From yoga and meditation to celebrity followers, eastern spirituality is in vogue. Why?  Is it a desire to reintroduce mystery in a practical world? A dissatisfaction with the single God of western religions?  Or a temporary consumer fad?

Psychoanalyst and Buddhist Gay Watson, Lama Jampa Thaye and philosopher Mark Vernon debate the rise of eastern spirituality.

Title: Bad to the Bone
Guests & Speakers: Adjoa Andoh, Alex Voorhoeve, Michael Hastings
Synopsis & Topics:
From Bill Gates to George Soros, it seems you can't be in the rich list these days without setting up your own charity. Are these status symbols with personal benefit to the founders, or good deeds stemming from genuine selflessness? Can charity be a purely altruistic act or is it always compromised by personal and political goals?

Journalist and peer Michael Hastings, actress and humanitarian Adjoa Andoh, and LSE philosopher Alex Voorhoeve question our selfish genes. Mary Ann Sieghart chairs.

Title: The Never-ending Journey
Guests & Speakers: Ben Hammersley, Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Daniel Miller
Synopsis & Topics:
The world is on the move. But is travel a necessity or a luxury? Do we long for a home in which to settle, or is humanity nomadic at heart?

Independent columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, Wired UK editor and world Service reporter Ben Hammersley and anthropologist Daniel Miller talk to travel journalist and cultural commentator Anita Sethi.

Title: Gods and Monsters
Guests & Speakers: Gerald Moore, Lewis Wolpert, Mark Vernon
Synopsis & Topics:
In a scientific age faith seems to show no signs of dying off. Is it a fundamental part of the human state? Is the desire to trust that which can't be proven a source of wisdom or a curse of ignorance? And how does faith square with our increasingly relativistic age?

Critic Gerald Moore, scientist and author of Six Impossible Things, Lewis Wolpert, and philosopher and former priest Mark Vernon debate the need for faith.

Title: The Origin of Knowledge
Guests & Speakers: Chris Surridge, Kevin Warwick, Piers Corbyn
Synopsis & Topics:
Science is the truth of the modern age. But the very system that determines what counts as science, peer review, is itself under attack. Is it a powerful way of keeping corruption out of science, or itself a corrupt system? What counts as knowledge and who should decide?

Nature editor Chris Surridge, outspoken astrophysicist Piers Corbyn and cyborg and scholar Kevin Warwick question the scientific method.

Title: Tales of an Extravagant Stranger
Synopsis & Topics:
Journalist and political commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown explores her life-long love of Shakespeare. Her experience of playing Juliet as a teenager in ‘60’s Uganda sent shockwaves through her family and helped shape the emotional and political landscape of her life.

Commissioned and directed by the Royal Shakespeare Company.

‘Enlightening, funny and moving…beautifully performed’ - Colin Firth

Title: Limits to Liberty
Guests & Speakers: Frank Furedi, Lisa Appignanesi, Peter Tatchell, Robert Skidelsky
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Outspoken sociologist and author of The Culture of Fear , Frank Furedi, human rights advocate and campaigner Peter Tatchell, and historian Lord Robert Skidelsky freely debate the limits of freedom.
Synopsis & Topics:
From tabloid complaints about 'political correctness gone mad' to the banning of expressions of religious hatred, many believe our right to free speech is under threat. Can we reconcile liberal freedom with the right of others to feel offence?

Outspoken sociologist and author of The Culture of Fear, Frank Furedi, human rights advocate and campaigner Peter Tatchell, and historian Lord Robert Skidelsky freely debate the limits of freedom.

Title: How to be Agnostic
Synopsis & Topics:
Is there more to agnosticism than sitting on the fence? Philosopher, journalist, former priest and physicist Mark Vernon reveals how the agnostic spirit is a vital strand that runs through the fabric of belief - and indeed the best philosophy and science.

‘Thoughtful, accessible, lucid’ - Julian Baggini

Title: The Ultimate Particle
Guests & Speakers: Rolf  Dieter Heuer, Gwyneth Jones, Hilary Lawson
Synopsis & Topics: Billions are invested in search of the Higgs boson, or God particle. Some say we are on the cusp of uncovering the ultimate building blocks of the universe ...

Title: The Love of Things
Synopsis & Topics: What does it mean to possess, or indeed to be possessed? Drawing on conservations with figures as varied as Paddy Ashdown and Eartha Kitt, Anita Sethi dissects the profound entanglement between us and our 'things' with anthropologist Danny Miller.

Title: The Dark Side of Environmentalism
Guests & Speakers: Martin Palmer, Paul Kingsnorth, Piers Corbyn, Tamsin Omond
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist and top 'troublemaker' Paul Kingsnorth, meteorologist Piers Corbyn, activist Tamsin Omond and theological thinker Martin Palmer unpick environmental desire.
Synopsis & Topics:
From energy-saving light-bulbs to recycling bins, we are increasingly ecologically aware. But what motivates our newfound environmental consciousness? Are we driven by more than an economic desire to avoid disaster? A fundamental desire to reconnect with nature perhaps or atonement for relentless consumption?

Journalist and top 'troublemaker' Paul Kingsnorth, astrophysicist Piers Corbyn, activist Tamsin Omond and theological thinker Martin Palmer unpick environmental desire.

Title: Are Islam and Westernism compatible?
Guests & Speakers: Lauren Booth, Iain Edgar, Maryam Namazie
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Journalist, reality TV star and Muslim convert Lauren Booth, Islam scholar Iain Edgar and Director of the Ex-Muslim Council Maryam Namazie examine the reasons behind Islam's success.
Synopsis & Topics: Are Islamic values compatible with western liberalism or should we weary of? Lauren Booth, Ian Edgar & Myriam Namazie on the reasons behind Islam's success

Title: Jim Moray
Synopsis & Topics:
Inventive reimaginings of English traditional folk music blended with orchestral flourishes, guitars and electronics. A slew of album awards and major performances at Glastonbury, Cambridge Folk Festival and WOMAD all prepare him for…. Hay-On-Wye!

‘Ambitious and radical post-millennial takes on the genre’ - BBC

Title: Hannah Peel
Synopsis & Topics:
Elegant, beautiful, understated songs from one of the UK's rising folk stars. She's collaborated with Tunng, the Unthanks and Nitin Sawney and is one to watch for 2011.

‘Surprising boldness combined with cool restraint’ - Guardian

Title: Visions of Disaster and Perfection
Synopsis & Topics:
Paul Kingsnorth, Kevin Warwick. Andrew Copson chairs.

From Atlantis to 1984, visions of utopia once shaped the political landscape. What new visions, from technological golden age to environmental apocalypse, do today's thinkers foresee for the 21st century?

In association with the British Humanist Association.

Title: What are we Worth?
Synopsis & Topics: Spear's editor William Cash asks Oscar-winning screenwriter William Nicholson (Gladiator, Shadowlands) about the meaning of self-worth in today's money-driven society. Nicholson discusses wealth, happiness and virtue, as well as the 2008 Financial Crisis and his response to it in his new play Crash.

Title: The Old Gods: England's Mythic Past
Synopsis & Topics: Award-winning Hollywood screenwriter and Jerusalem playwright Jez Butterworth talks to environmentalist and poet Paul Kingsnorth and author of Bedlam Nell Leyshon about an older, darker and more authentic vision of this green and pleasant land.

Title: Rhyme and Punishment
Synopsis & Topics:
Chief Executive of the Koestler Trust for art by offenders Tim Robertson runs a discussion of themes and current issues for arts in prisons and other secure settings, illustrated with poems and visual arts to explore the relationship between confinement and creativity

In association with Lankelly Chase.

Title: Cultures of the Body
Guests & Speakers: Ben Hammersley, Gabriel Gbadamosi, Musa Okwonga
Synopsis & Topics:
Why are live music, theatre and festivals experiencing a resurgence in an age dominated by the virtual and disembodied? Does technology allow us to extend our consciousness worldwide, or does true culture need to be experienced through the body?

Broadcaster and journalist Mary-Ann Sieghart reaches out to performance poet and sportswriter Musa Okwonga, technophile war reporter Ben Hammersley and playwright Gabriel Gbadamosi.

Title: The Real Capitalism
Synopsis & Topics: When people attack Capitalism, what are they really attacking? Is it really just about greed and bonuses? Philosopher and Conservative MP Jesse Norman explores what Capitalism really means today, and why a true understanding of it may be our best hope for the future.

Title: Six Billion Characters in Search of an Author
Guests & Speakers: Jez Butterworth, Richard Schoch, Tim McInerny
Synopsis & Topics:
From the world stage to the parts we play in our own lives, is it human nature to see our own existence as a performance? While the theatrical metaphor may help us to build societies, do we risk losing touch with reality?

Scholar Richard Schoch, psychiatrist Tim McInerny and award-winning playwright Jez Butterworth strut and fret their hour upon the stage.

Title: The Myth of Being Happy
Synopsis & Topics: The myth of being happy explores the meaning of happiness, drawing from Socrates, and when it became a human right rather than the reward for a good life

Title: The Cinema of Ideas
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Playwright Gabriel Gbadamosi and Cardiff philosopher Jonathan Webber debate the effectiveness of thought on film.
Synopsis & Topics:
Can narrative film engage with the biggest questions in life? From Jean-Luc Godard to the Coen Brothers, can a real exploration of life, death, the universe and the human condition break through the demands of visual storytelling and the commercial imperatives of the industry?

Playwright Gabriel Gbadamosi and Cardiff philosopher Jonathan Webber debate the effectiveness of thought on film.

Title: Shooting Truth
Guests & Speakers: Hilary Lawson, Jerry Rothwell, Roger Graef
Synopsis & Topics:
From Fox to Al Jazeera, Bowling for Columbine to Loose Change, supposedly 'factual' film and TV has become ever more ideologically engaged with its subjects. Does narrative threaten to overwhelm objectivity, or is all reportage necessarily skewed?

Committed political documentarist Roger Graef, director of Deep Water and Heavy Load  Jerry Rothwell and philosopher and filmmaker Hilary Lawson take aim at reality.

Title: Order out of Chaos
Synopsis & Topics:
What links mental health and creativity? Does the act of writing help make sense of our lives, or draw us further into the mazes of the mind?

Psychiatrist Tim McInerny and playwright Nell Leyshon run creative writing workshops at the Royal Bethlem Hospital and are developing the use of creative writing in mental health settings. They are accompanied by two outsider-poets who will perform work.

In association with Lankelly Chase.

Title: The Screen Age
Guests & Speakers: George Barber, Justina Robson, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Award-winning video practitioner George Barber, post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson and speculative novelist Justina Robson look into their liquid-crystal ball at the future screen.
Synopsis & Topics: Projection and moving image are changing our architecture and the way we live and work. How will art respond to the rapidly evolving character of the screen age? Award-winning video practitioner George Barber, post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson and speculative novelist Justina Robson look into their liquid-crystal ball at the future screen.

Title: The If Machine
Synopsis & Topics: Find out why philosophy should be as fundamental to our education system as reading, writing and arithmetic. Peter Worley argues that exam culture has dulled our native and philosophical curiosity.

Title: Why we all need Big Ideas
Synopsis & Topics:
From Alain de Botton to Philosophy Bites, it seems that popular philosophy has never been more popular. What makes us hunger for the big ideas in life? Can any general introduction give us access to the benefits of philosophical wisdom, or is enlightenment difficult by definition?

Julian Baggini talks to academic Dr Peter Sedgwick, author Justina Robson and educational campaigner Peter Worley about whether big ideas can ever be bite-size.

Title: Dylan as Philosopher
Synopsis & Topics: Poet and editor Phil Bowen leads a celebration-cum-cross-examination of the work of Bob Dylan on the protean singer-songwriter’s 70th Birthday.

Title: Verses for Eternity
Synopsis & Topics:
Is the true nature of poetry philosophical, and should philosophy aspire to be poetic? Verse is thought to be the primal form of writing, so how did philosophy fall into the habits of logic and rigour, and who now will speak to us of mystery?

Prize-winning poet Ruth Padel speaks to thinker Jonathan Ree about the truth of poetry, and the mystery of philosophy.

Title: The Music of Revolt
Synopsis & Topics: Self-styled 'Militant Aesthete' and journeyman intellectual Ben Watson explores how music can respond, react to and take part in political upheaval, with examples from Adorno to Zappa to Tahrir Square.

Title: The Limits of Art
Synopsis & Topics: They met at Crunch 2010. Now physician, novelist and poet Raymond Tallis and controversial critic Julian Spalding are ready to unveil their new, radical and utterly compelling theory of art, the limits of artistic freedom, and the dangers of the status quo. Are formal constraints stultifying or liberating? Has the contemporary art world lost sight of necessary limits to artistic practice?

Title: Art Couture
Synopsis & Topics: From McQueen to McCartney, the fashion designer's cultural profile has never been higher. But is haute couture the same as high art? Can clothing have meaning? Does this dominant visual and mythic language of our time really have anything to say, or is it just empty glamour?

Title: The View From Outside
Synopsis & Topics: There has been a surge of art world interest in marginalised artists, platforming work by prisoners and the mentally ill. The author of Outsider Art from the Margins to the Marketplace David Maclagan asks art therapist Livy Powell whether the label of 'outsider art' downplays the achievements of these artists, and whether art-as-therapy can provoke truly powerful and original work. An art therapy workshop will follow the session.

Title: The New Beautiful
Guests & Speakers: Ben Watson, Godfrey Barker, Jonathan Ree
Synopsis & Topics: After the age of pickled sharks and dung, when Beauty was dismissed as shallow, kitsch and inauthentic, are we seeing the rise of a new aesthetics? Must art be grim and discordant to ring true, or have we painted ourselves into a dark corner?

Title: Spies, Lies and Life on the Run
Synopsis & Topics: Former M15 agent and whistleblower Annie Machon claims that spy agencies across the western world have been politicised to build a case for Middle Eastern wars. But what is the future for the intelligence infrastructure?

Title: Canon Under Fire
Guests & Speakers: Douglas Murray, Elleke Boehmer, Toby Young
Synopsis & Topics: From Gove's attempt to put a more patriotic version of British history in the curriculum to the rise of so-called 'soft subjects', the British education system has become a battleground between those who believe in a canon of knowledge and those who want to subvert it. Who has the right to determine what our children learn?

Title: What's Love Got To Do With It?
Synopsis & Topics:
Simon May

Is Love a new God or a false idol? Birkbeck philosopher Simon May challenges our infatuation with romance.

'An amazing tour de force' -  A.C. Grayling

Title: The Net Delusion
Synopsis & Topics: Could our obsession with digital protest backfire? Marshalling compelling evidence, Evgeny Morozov shows why “Internet freedom” might have disastrous implications for the future of democracy as a whole.

Title: After Democracy
Guests & Speakers: Bonnie Greer, David Aaronovitch, Robin Dunbar, Simon Glendinning
Synopsis & Topics: From the Russian mafia to global corporations, from Chinese leaders to Saudi princes, the world it would seem is run by oligarchies as much as democracy.  Should we be outraged or is democracy over-rated? Is there an ideal political framework or can Sparta be as valuable as Athens?

Title: The Return of Revolution
Guests & Speakers: Alex Callinicos, Cory Doctorow, Evgeny Morozov
Synopsis & Topics: Revolution is back on the agenda and many have claimed the internet has played a crucial role.  Are we seeing a means to convert grass-roots protest into powerful political movements or is the internet itself at the mercy of authoritarian intervention?

Title: Technology and Anarchy
Synopsis & Topics: With a 3D printer and laptop, does everyone have the tools they need to build a bio-weapon? Science fiction novelist, blogger and activist Cory Doctorow talks to Nigel Warburton about whether we can - or should - attempt to regulate subversive technology.

Title: The Politics of Terrorism
Guests & Speakers: Mark Littlewood, Ted Honderich, Yvonne Ridley
Synopsis & Topics: In the last decade terrorist acts have dominated the headlines like no other issue. Can the murder of civilians for a political goal ever be justified?

Title: In Love and War
Guests & Speakers: Alex Callinicos, David Lammy, Mark Littlewood
Synopsis & Topics: There's a new word on every politician’s lips, setting the agenda for everything from the budget to the electoral system. But what does fairness mean for politics, and is it a plausible goal? Does fairness require us to accept that we can’t all be winners, or is the only fair society an equal one?

Title: Saving Science
Synopsis & Topics: Laureate for the Women in Science awards, Athene Donald talks about the dangers of prejudice, gender stereotypes and why women are vital to the sciences

Title: Defeating Aging
Synopsis & Topics: Chief Science Officer of the SENS Foundation Aubrey de Grey believes we can defeat aging and that the power to make us immortal is just around the corner

Title: Why Society Drives You Mad
Synopsis & Topics:
From IQ to mental illness, genetics takes prime position in our thinking about psychology. Psychiatrists link schitzophrenia, depression and obsessive compulsion to different particular genes on a regular basis. Are the claims of geneticists exagerrated?

Clinical psychologist and vocal critic of psychiatry Richard Bentall reveals why social inequality, racism and the built environment have a far more significant role to play in mental illness than the biomedical establishment acknowledges.

Title: The Eagle and The Dragon
Guests & Speakers: Isabel Hilton, Gideon Rachman, Robert Bickers, Rana Mitter
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Oxford historian and broadcaster Rana Mitter, FT columnist Gideon Rachman, China commentator Isabel Hilton, and historian Robert Bickers weigh the consequences of the rise of a 21st century superpower.
Synopsis & Topics: China is the new god of global economics. With a population five times that of Europe and the US combined will we live in a China-shaped shadow?

Title: When Women Rule the World
Synopsis & Topics: Women are outpacing men at school and university alike, more are entering some professions than men as a consequence. Will this be sustained? What would a world where women were dominant be like, and  what will happen to masculinity in a modern, matriarchal society?

Title: The End of Abundance?
Guests & Speakers: Bonnie Greer, Christopher Hamilton, Gideon Rachman, Harriet Lamb
Synopsis & Topics:
Harriet Lamb, Christopher Hamilton, Bonnie Greer, Gideon Rachman. Simon Glendinning chairs.

For most of human history humans have had to contend with the scarcity of essentials. In the West we have had a relatively brief period of abundance. But scarcity was the word on everyone's lips at Davos this year. Is abundance now over and if so, what will this mean for our values and goals?

Title: Ana Silvera
Synopsis & Topics: The Liberal calls Silvera epic and intimate, with songs that offer us a landscape of the human heart. Hers is a tapestry carefully crafted, often woven with the fabric of mythic tales, told with tender insight and in wry, seductive tones.

Title: The Skin We're In
Guests & Speakers: Finn Mackay, Minette Marrin, Simon May
Synopsis & Topics: Whether it's the movies, advertising, or pornography, the body sells. We take it for granted that intellect or ability is prized and rewarded. Yet use of, and reward for, the body is often critized. Is this a prejudice of the intelligent over the beautiful? An appropriate moral stance? Or a necessary political goal?

Title: Taking Over the Asylum
Guests & Speakers: Molly Meacher, Richard Bentall, Mark Salter
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Night Waves presenter Rana Mitter keeps order as clinical psychologist and psychiatry critic Richard Bentall, Baroness Molly Meacher and controversial consultant psychiatrist Mark Salter debate the extent of mental illness. In association with the Maudsley Philosophy Group.
Synopsis & Topics: From ADHD to binge eating, celebrity worship syndrome to sex addiction, new types of mental illness are increasingly in the public eye. But what is mental illness?  Are we in danger of medicalising normal human behaviour or offering recognition and treatment to those whose suffering would once have been ignored?

Title: Creating Change
Synopsis & Topics: Chair of East London City & Mental Health Trust and formal Mental Health Act Commissioner Baroness Meacher discusses the future of arts provision in mental healthcare. In Association with Lankelly Chase.

Title: The Fountain
Synopsis & Topics: Life passes in a torrent of electronic communication and cultural change. Through the metaphor of the fountain, atheist theologian Don Cupitt proposes a deeply original means for reconciling ourselves to time and the transience of life.

Title: Metaphors of the Mind
Synopsis & Topics: Does metaphor hold the key to explaining consciousness? Radical philosopher Ted Honderich reveals his new theory of what it means to be a thinking, feeling human being.

Title: Peggy Sue
Synopsis & Topics: Sweet, soulful acoustic pop peppered with weird sounds and funny, unusual stories. Kate Nash loved them so much she brought them out on tour with her, and Mumford & Sons are huge fans.

Title: Happiness
Guests & Speakers: Jesse Norman, Richard Layard, Simon May
Synopsis & Topics:
Richard Layard, Simon May, Jesse Norman. Isabel Hilton chairs.

Nietzsche quipped:  “Humanity does not strive for happiness, only the English do.”  Now with Cameron’s ‘Happiness Index’ there is even talk that happiness of the individual could replace GDP as a national political goal.  But is it possible to measure happiness? And as a goal, is happiness an illusion? Or even desirable?

Title: Rescuing Morality
Synopsis & Topics: Belief in the literal existence of God is on the decline. But what will replace this moral framework if it disappears altogether? Mary Warnock makes a case for how we will survive morally in the changed world.

Title: On Having a Mind, Having a Body, and Being a Person
Synopsis & Topics: What precisely is a person? How is the person related to the mind and body? Philosopher Peter Hacker pieces together the puzzle that is the human being

Title: Generation Wars
Guests & Speakers: Anthony O'Hear, Laurie Penny, Aubrey de Grey
Synopsis & Topics: Our age idolises youth. But as lifespans extend what will come of our cult of youth? And as the population pyramid turns on its head will our values follow suit?  Is an escalation of inter-generational rivalry inevitable?

Title: Converging Cultures
Synopsis & Topics: Broadcaster, novelist and playwright Bonnie Greer explains why David Cameron , Angela Merkel, and Nicholas’ Sarkozy’s rejection of  multiculturalism is the  wrong analysis of the only ace that Britain and Europe have to play in the coming multi-polar world.

Title: Designing Life
Synopsis & Topics: Will our buildings of the future be alive? TED fellow Rachel Armstrong's radical 'metabolic materials' are changing how we see the future of the city.

Title: Rise of the Machines
Guests & Speakers: Alan Winfield, Hilary Lawson, Lilian Edwards, Peter Hacker
Synopsis & Topics: From 2001 to The Matrix, intelligent machines and robots have played a central role in our fictions. Some now claim they are about to become fact.  Is artificial intelligence possible or just a science fiction fantasy?  And would it be a fundamental advance for humankind or an outcome to be feared?

Title: The Solitary Self - Darwin and the Selfish Gene
Synopsis & Topics: Are neo-Darwinists right to reduce all human behaviour to self-interest? Moral philosopher Mary Midgley returns to Darwin's original writings…

Title: A Paradigm of Health
Guests & Speakers: Athene Donald, Dylan Evans, Lionel Milgrom, Steve Fuller
Synopsis & Topics: Even though the successes of western medicine are loudly applauded, alternatives from aromatherapy to raki, acupuncture to crystal healing, balloon in popularity. Is this evidence that the western model of health is flawed? Could any of these alternatives offer a genuinely new paradigm or are we seeing human gullibility at work?

Title: The Ego Trick
Synopsis & Topics: Is the self an illusion? The Philosopher's Magazine founder and author of Complaint Julian Baggini goes in search of the elusive ideas that make you 'you'.

Title: The Famine and the Feast
Guests & Speakers: Barry C. Smith, Joanna Kavenna, John Naish, Harriet Lamb
Synopsis & Topics: Food scarcity, at least in the West, is largely eradicated. Yet we are obsessed. Is the absence of hunger the problem, or our inability to contain desire? And what is the relationship between desire and constraint?

Title: Socrates vs. Jesus
Synopsis & Topics: Would either Socrates or Jesus attract a following today in the 21st century? Steve Fuller compares Socrates and Jesus as guides to contemporary life.

Title: Living Dangerously
Guests & Speakers: Dylan Evans, David Lammy, Douglas Murray
Synopsis & Topics:
Douglas Murray, David Lammy, Dylan Evans. Isabel Hilton chairs.

From GM foods to stranger danger, fear it would seem lurks round every corner in modern life. Yet statistically we are safer than we have ever been. Is our fear justified and beneficial, or misguided and debilitating?  Is it always right to seek safety, or is risk itself desirable?

Title: The Post-Nuclear Family Future
Guests & Speakers: Henrietta Moore, John Naish, Oliver James
Synopsis & Topics: The family is in transition. A generation is growing up with multiple parents and a host of half siblings. Are family structures falling apart or growing into exciting new possibilities? And is family essential to human well-being, and if so why?

Title: Mazes of the Mind
Guests & Speakers: Iain McGilchrist, Colin Blakemore, Bryan Appleyard
Synopsis & Topics: Neuroscience promises answers to philosophical questions, but can it account for issues as complex as the origins of consciousness and the nature of art?

Title: Kyla La Grange
Synopsis & Topics: Epic, widescreen pop with a keenly felt indie sensibility. Kyla's exquisitely smoky voice is laid over rich instrumentation to bewitching effect. Miss at your peril.

Title: Sensuality and deception
Guests & Speakers: Mary Warnock, Hilary Lawson, Mark Salter, Robert Rowland Smith
Synopsis & Topics: From the origins of western thought, we have been encouraged to value the sophistication and purity of the mind over the sensual experiences of the body. But could it be that the body is making a comeback? Might the richness of sensual experience provide the only truth in a world where the mind is a source of deception?

Title: A Spider in the Eye
Synopsis & Topics: Iain McGilchrist, consultant psychiatrist and author of The Master and His Emissary, presents a radical new consideration of the relationship between madness, art, and modernity. In association with Lankelly Chase.

Title: Animal Reason
Guests & Speakers: Colin Blakemore, John Harris, Mary Midgley, Tim Crane
Synopsis & Topics: Once we supposed that consciousness was unique to humans. Increasingly there are those who claim animals are conscious too. Are they? And if so, how does this change how we see ourselves and the nature of consciousness itself?

Title: Mind in the 21st Century
Synopsis & Topics:
AC Grayling

How is new technology set to change the nature of the mind? Humanist and public intellectual AC Grayling offers a radical new vision for being human.

Title: After postmodernity
Guests & Speakers: Ziauddin Sardar, Mary Warnock, Hilary Lawson
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Mary Warnock, Hilary Lawson, Ziauddin Sardar. Angie Hobbs chairs.
Synopsis & Topics:
Mary Warnock, Hilary Lawson, Ziauddin Sardar. Angie Hobbs chairs.

Postmodernism was the intellectual fashion of the turn of the millennium.  But what comes next?  Is there life after relativism or are we all lost in a world without certainties?  What are the new big ideas to sustain humanity and nurture the imagination? Three thinkers from across the intellectual spectrum reveal their visions of where we are and where we are heading.

Title: An Age of Tragedy?
Synopsis & Topics: Do we live in a tragic age? Christopher Hamilton's provocative, sceptical account of the modern world will resonate with anyone who seeks to see through the illusion of progress and moral order to which many cling.

Title: The New Romantics
Guests & Speakers: Iain McGilchrist, Peter Hacker, Joanna Kavenna
Synopsis & Topics:
Peter Hacker, Joanna Kavenna, Iain McGilchrist. Henrietta Moore chairs.

Should we be celebrating the end of rationality in favor of a more romantic sensibility? Or are we, in the words of J.G. Ballard, ‘re-primitivizing’ ourselves and entering an age of magic, unreason and romantic superstition?

Title: The World After Ideals
Synopsis & Topics: Have politics and big ideas and ideals become irreconcilably separated? Guardian columnist Polly Toynbee talks to Richard Sennett about whether grand ideas still have a place to play in our political life.

Title: The Global Aristocracy
Guests & Speakers: William Cash, Laurie Penny, Peter York, Jonathan Bailey
Synopsis & Topics: Across the globe the super-rich form a new global aristocracy. Should there be limits to their political and cultural power? Does wealth serve the greater good, or are we on a slippery slope to an age of oligarchy?

Title: Mind Change
Synopsis & Topics: New technologies are transforming our lives, the human mind is next on the list of unprecedented changes. “The crisis of a changing world”, Susan Greenfield

Title: The End of Ideas
Guests & Speakers: Christopher Hamilton, Peter Hacker, Jonathan Derbyshire
Synopsis & Topics: A century ago Freud and Einstein were at the height of intellectual activity. Can we create a new Enlightenment that matches the excitement of the past?

Title: Alchemy, Anarchy, and Science
Guests & Speakers: Rachel Armstrong, Susan Greenfield, Steve Fuller
Synopsis & Topics:
Science questions, but what does it mean to question science? Science is perhaps the defining triumph of the modern world. From Galileo to Quantum theory, scientific power was increasingly worshipped. Yet it is increasingly under attack both from those who fear its consequences and those who question its claims to unique authority. Is there any real alternative or are we just seeing the return of myth and superstition?

Susan Greenfield, Rachel Armstrong, Steve Fuller look at the value of science today. Bryan Appleyard chairs.

Title: When China Rules the World
Synopsis & Topics: Author of ‘When China Rules The World’, Martin Jacques on the rise of China, the Chinese government’s new world order and its consequences for our lives.

Title: Beyond good and evil
Guests & Speakers: Carol Diethe, Simon May, Anthony O'Hear
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: Carol Diethe, Anthony O'Hear, Simon May. Julian Baggini chairs.
Synopsis & Topics: Gone are the associations with the superman and the Nazis, in its place the new Nietzsche is the precursor of relativism and postmodernity.  Do we live in a Nietzschean world, and if so is this a fine or terrible thing?

Title: Why Humanism?
Synopsis & Topics: Do the doctrines of Dawkins, Hitchens and humanist atheists mimic or subvert the religious rituals they seek to destroy? Can we build a more tolerant world?

Title: Before the Beginning, After the End
Guests & Speakers: Don Cupitt, Carlos Frenk, Jo Dunkley
Synopsis & Topics:
Don Cupitt, Carlos Frenk, Jo Dunkley. Rachel Armstrong chairs.

From balloons to doughnuts, and string theory to multiverses, we seem to have as many models of the universe as we do cosmologists. Are we getting closer to answering what came before the universe's beginning and what lies beyond its end, or is a complete theory of the universe an illusion?

Title: Who Looks Back in the Mirror
Guests & Speakers: Henrietta Moore, Julian Baggini, Barry C. Smith, Simon May
Synopsis & Topics: In its focus on language and structure 20th century philosophy all but eradicated the need for the human subject. Now there are signs that the self is on its way back.  But are we any closer to understanding the self, and what makes each one of us who we are?

Title: My Avatar, Myself
Synopsis & Topics: When we extend ourselves into the virtual where do we, ourselves, end? With endless new capacities to animate our intentions beyond the body, leading anthropologist Henrietta Moore proposes this is far more than projection.

Title: What's the Big Idea?
Synopsis & Topics:
Without a big idea is art reduced to entertainment, decoration and the merely trivial? Should art primarily be a vehicle for ideas or are they secondary to its fundamental purpose?

On the lookout for a Eureka moment award-winning author AL Kennedy, Saatchi curator Patricia Ellis and psychiatrist and writer Iain McGilchrist.

Title: Ugly is over, Beauty is Back?
Synopsis & Topics:
For a century beauty has been out of fashion. Could it be on the way back? Some have argued that as the pessimism and brutality of the YBA era recedes, a new dawn of beauty is rising once again in British art. If so, is this indicative of a deep human desire for beauty, or a superficial antidote to the darkening external climate?
 
Artists Matthew Stone and Anj Smith debate the return of beauty with Godfrey Barker and Gabriel Gbadamosi.

Title: Seizing the Means of Production
Synopsis & Topics:
Brian Eno in conversation with Paul Morley.

From his earliest records to just-released new album Small Craft on a Milk Sea, musician, composer, producer and artist Brian Eno has been no stranger to tearing up tradition. Now Brian and legendary rock'n'roll journalist Paul Morley turn prophet, providing audiences with a preview of their new collaboration on the future collision of art, music and science.

Title: To the Ends of the Earth?
Synopsis & Topics: What motivates our attempts to protect the environment? We are part of the natural world but does this also provide us with a transcendental basis for ethics? Or are we seeking a meaningless catharsis to fulfil the human desire to value something beyond ourselves?

Title: The Point of Art
Synopsis & Topics: Since our ancestors marked cave walls thirty-two thousand years ago, the artistic impulse has been a facet of all human culture. But why? What is the point of art?

Title: The Individual: An Endangered Species
Synopsis & Topics: In the current economic climate there are widespread calls to limit individual excess, but where might a renewed focus on community lead and how might it change our culture? Are we individuals that need to be contained for the benefit of society, or herd animals that should be encouraged to venture forth? Provocative Times columnist and leader writer Oliver Kamm debates with Philip Blond and Geoff Mulgan. Rana Mitter chairs.

Title: The Great British Art Debate
Synopsis & Topics: Tate curator Cedar Lewisohn asks ICA Director Ekow Eshun, BBC Arts Editor Will Gompertz and Serpentine Director Julian Peyton-Jones what sort of art should be shown in our public galleries and museums? And more importantly, who gets to decide?

Title: The End of Privacy
Guests & Speakers: Frank Furedi, David Aaronovitch, Helena Kennedy, David Bond
Synopsis & Topics: Cameras watch our every move, internet databases hold the most private of information about us. But do we care, and does it matter? ;Times columnist and author of Voodoo Histories David Aaronovitch, author of Politics of Fear Frank Furedi, civil liberties champion Helena Kennedy QC, and filmmaker David Bond contemplate a world where nothing is entirely private.

Title: Sex machines
Guests & Speakers: Catherine Hakim, Michele le Doeuff, Mark Vernon, Simon Blackburn
Speaker Bios & Descriptions: LSE sociologist and 'Erotic Capital' theorist Catherine Hakim, author of Lust and Cambridge philosopher Simon Blackburn, leading French postmodernist Michèle le Doeuff and journalist and former priest Mark Vernon get serious about sex.
Synopsis & Topics:
Some would say we live in a sex obsessed age, but just how important is sexuality to our being? Should we along with Darwin and Freud see sex as central to our lives, or is it a passing hedonistic activity? And if it is central to what extent does our sexuality determine how we think and how we influence others?


LSE sociologist and 'Erotic Capital' theorist Catherine Hakim, author of Lust and Cambridge philosopher Simon Blackburn, leading French postmodernist Michèle le Doeuff and journalist and former priest Mark Vernon get serious about sex.

Title: Look back in angst
Synopsis & Topics: Former Liberal Democrat MP Lembit Opik bares all about his years in office, including a behind-the-scenes look at the general election and his predictions for the new coalition government. Expect humour and the melancholic sounds of his trusty harmonica.

Title: A change for culture
Synopsis & Topics: A new coalition government is in place and with it a new policy for culture and the arts. Rising star and minister with responsibility for arts and broadcasting in Cameron's government, Ed Vaizey, gives his vision of the future of culture in Britain.

Title: Art as gossip
Synopsis & Topics: Do we have to see art to appreciate it? Or can it exist as an idea, transferred to us via gossip, books or the media? Critic, curator and Saatchi collaborator Patricia Ellis challenges our assumptions about the ways we experience art.

Title: Awake in the universe (HTLGI 2010)
Synopsis & Topics: What allows mankind to confront the universe? Is imagination more important than knowledge? Join renowned physicist Sir Roger Penrose and author, playwright and commentator Bonnie Greer, as they explore how that most elusive of faculties – creativity – has helped us unlock the undiscovered country of the mind and the mysteries of the cosmos. Chaired by Andrew Copson.
